entries.heading: Sutlijaš (сутлијаш, сутлијач, благ ориз; milk rice pudding)
entries.what: Sweet dessert of rice cooked in milk, a regular dish in Macedonian cuisine; originates from Turkish sütlaç.

entries.heading: Sutlijaš (сутлијаш; rice pudding in milk)
entries.what: sweet rice dessert simmered in milk, sugar added near the end, served warm or cold; common in Serbian, Bosnian, Macedonian and Bulgarian cuisines.

entries.heading: Teh tarik
entries.what: A hot, frothy milk tea, most often found at restaurants, outdoor stalls and kopitiams; Brunei is named among countries where it is found.

entries.heading: Teh tarik (Jawi: تيه تاريق; teh ais, teh madu, teh halia, teh-C, teh madras as variants)
entries.what: A strong black tea sweetened and mixed with milk, frothed by pulling it between two vessels. The name means "pulled tea".

entries.heading: Teh tarik (pulled milk tea)
entries.what: strong tea mixed with milk and served hot, with a frothy top.

entries.heading: Tomme vaudoise (Tomme vaudoise; Tomme)
entries.what: A small round soft cheese, about 75 to 125 g, with a fine white-downed rind and a creamy paste that becomes runny as it ripens. Its traditional recipe is shared by the cantons of Vaud and Genève.

entries.heading: Tomme vaudoise
entries.what: small soft cheese from Vaud, typical of French-speaking Switzerland.

entries.heading: Tomme Vaudoise
entries.what: soft Swiss cheese of Canton Vaud, named in the Swiss cheese lists.

entries.heading: Trahana (dried yoghurt and grain)
entries.what: dried mix of wheat and fermented milk, rehydrated with milk into a soup; eaten at breakfast in rural areas

entries.heading: Trahanas (τραχανάς; Cypriot trachanas)
entries.what: A dried grain paste, a national specialty in Cyprus, served as a thick soup.

entries.heading: Trahanas (trahana, tarhana; xynohondros)
entries.what: a dried, fermented food of cracked wheat or couscous-like paste mixed with fermented milk or yogurt. Common in Greece and Cyprus (where it is often served with halloumi), and in Albania.

entries.heading: Trappe Échourgnac (curd made in Brittany)
entries.what: a commercial brand whose curd is made in Brittany and ripened in the Dordogne by Trappist nuns.

entries.heading: Trappe d'Échourgnac (Trappe Échourgnac; Le Timanoix variant)
entries.what: A monastic cheese sold under the Monastic collective mark, ripened by Trappist nuns at the Abbaye Notre-Dame de Bonne-Espérance in Échourgnac, Dordogne.

entries.heading: Trappe d'Échourgnac
entries.what: A cow's-milk cheese brand: made in an industrial dairy in Ille-et-Vilaine, then affinage by Trappist nuns at Notre-Dame de Bonne-Espérance, Échourgnac (Dordogne).

entries.heading: Trappista (Trapist; Trapist cheese; Trapisti)
entries.what: A semi-hard, mild, slightly sweet, cow's-milk cheese originating in France (Port-du-Salut); brought to Banja Luka by Trappist monks and widely eaten in Bosnia.

entries.heading: Trappista
entries.what: A semi-hard cow's-milk cheese first made by the Trappist monks of Port-du-Salut Abbey in France; also made in Belgium, Bosnia, Hungary.

entries.heading: Trappista
entries.what: a semi-hard, mild cheese that melts easily; originally made by French Trappist monks, and according to the Hungarian list the most popular cheese on the Hungarian market, with many companies making it.

entries.heading: Tres leches cake (pastel de tres leches)
entries.what: A sponge cake soaked in a three-milk mixture and topped with whipped cream.

entries.heading: Tres leches cake (pastel de tres leches)
entries.what: A moist sponge cake soaked in a mixture of three milks; topped with whipped cream and fruit or jam. Named in the source as the most popular cake in all of Mexico.

entries.heading: Tres leches cake
entries.what: a sponge cake soaked in evaporated, condensed and whole milk, topped with whipped cream, fruit and cinnamon. The English article's infobox gives Latin America, Mexico and Nicaragua as the region of origin, and says the history is debated.

entries.heading: Varenets (varenets)
entries.what: A baked fermented milk, similar to ryazhenka, with a caramel flavour and creamy colour. Russian in origin per its English article.

entries.heading: Varenets (варенец)
entries.what: Russian sour baked-milk drink close to ryazhenka, with caramel flavour and a creamy colour.

entries.heading: Varenets (варенець)
entries.what: Sour-milk product made from baked milk with a thermophilic starter. Close to ryazhenka.

entries.heading: Yak butter (酥油, sūyóu)
entries.what: Butter from yak milk, a staple and trade good for herders on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau; about twice the fat of cow's milk; tastes more like cheese than cream. Used in butter tea, cooking, pastries, ritual sculpture and lamps.

entries.heading: Yak butter
entries.what: Butter from yak milk, which has nearly twice the fat of whole cow's milk; used in Tibetan-Nepali cooking and butter tea. Thakali households usually buy it at market, as few own yaks because few own yaks.

entries.heading: Yak butter (Pamir)
entries.what: very creamy yak butter served at a yurt camp in the Murghab area of the Pamirs.

name: Zincarlin
names: Zincarlin da la Val da Mücc

entries.heading: Zincarlin da la Val da Mücc (Zincarlìn, Zincarlin; aged version a Slow Food Presidium)
entries.what: A pepper-spiced cheese from Val da Mücc on the Swiss side of Monte Generoso and the Valle di Muggio, based on a büscion-like acidified paste; its aged version was Switzerland's first Slow Food Presidium

entries.heading: Zincarlin (Cingherlino; Gingherlino)
entries.what: an alpine cheese from the Lombardy–Ticino border, flavoured with garlic, pepper and parsley.

entries.heading: Abbaye de Tamié (Tamié)
entries.what: trademark cheese of the Trappist monks of Tamié abbey, Bauges massif; about 1.5 kg, 51% fat.

entries.heading: Abbaye de Tamié
entries.what: A soft cheese made only by the monks of Tamié Abbey near Albertville in Savoie, similar in style to Reblochon.

entries.heading: Abondance (Abondance cheese)
entries.what: cheese from the Abondance valley; AOC 1990, AOP 1996.

entries.heading: Abondance
entries.what: A semi-hard, fragrant, raw-milk cheese from the Haute-Savoie department.

entries.heading: Acidofilní mléko (acidophilus milk)
entries.what: A fermented milk product listed for the Czech Republic.

entries.heading: Acidophilus milk (probiotic milk, US)
entries.what: Milk made with Lactobacillus acidophilus, a probiotic bacterium first isolated from infant faeces in 1900.

entries.heading: Acidophiline (acidophilin; Belarusian ацыдафілін, atsydafilin)
entries.what: A fermented milk product with Lactobacillus acidophilus, named in the Russia/Ukraine/Belarus group of the list. The Belarusian-language Wikipedia gives its Belarusian name as atsydafilin.

entries.heading: Acidophilin (ацидофилин)
entries.what: Soured pasteurised cow's milk made with Lactobacillus acidophilus, kefir grains and lactic streptococcus; Soviet-era drink, created in the Armenian SSR in the 1930s.

entries.heading: Afuega'l pitu (Afuega'l Pitu)
entries.what: PDO cheese from Asturias; made in Salas, Grado, Pravia and Tineo, Grado the largest producer. Made year-round.

entries.heading: Afuega'l pitu
entries.what: Cow's-milk cheese from Asturias, name roughly "strangle the chicken" in Asturian.

entries.heading: Agaran (ағаран)
entries.what: Fermented cream that forms on the surface of shubat and is collected.

entries.heading: Agaran (agaran; ағаран)
entries.what: A butter-like fat skimmed from the surface of chal. Turkmen cookbooks treat it as a separate dairy product.

entries.heading: Äidinmaito (human milk; rintamaito)
entries.what: Milk from the mammary glands, the infant's primary food in the first year and part of the diet afterwards. Composition varies by mother's diet. About 65 kcal per decilitre; about 47% of energy from fat, 46% from carbohydrate, 7% from protei

entries.heading: Human milk (breast milk sampled in Kuwait)
entries.what: Breast milk was among the samples analysed in a Kuwait aflatoxin study. This shows breast milk is sampled and tested in Kuwait, not that it is donated or sold.

entries.heading: Algunder Ziegenkäse (Formaggio di capra di Lagundo)
entries.what: A goat cheese from Lagundo (Burgraviato), about 1 kg per wheel, 10–12 cm across.

entries.heading: Algunder Ziegenkäse (formaggio di capra di Lagundo)
Anevato (Ανεβατό; Anevato)
entries.what: A PDO cheese named by the regional tourism site and the farms portal as a product of Grevena and Western Macedonia.

entries.heading: Anevato (Ανεβατό Γρεβενών και Νομού Κοζάνης; Π.Ο.Π.)
entries.what: Creamy cheese from Grevena and Kozani, Macedonia.

entries.heading: Anhydrous milk fat (grasa anhidra de leche; butteroil)
entries.what: nearly pure milk fat made from cream or butter, the Argentine term butteroil.

entries.heading: Anhydrous milk fat (AMF)
entries.what: Dried, almost pure milk fat, sold as an ingredient.

entries.heading: Anthotyros (Ανθότυρος)
entries.what: a Greek whey cheese, made in several regions including Crete (en Wikipedia lists Thrace, Macedonia, the Ionian Islands and Crete).

entries.heading: Anthotyros (Ανθότυρος)
entries.what: Traditional Greek whey cheese. Fresh type is white, soft to medium-firm and sweet, with no rind or salt. Dry type is hard, salty, can have a sherry-like smell; similar to mizithra.

entries.heading: Appenzeller Rässkäse (Räßkäse; "rezent (räss)")
entries.what: The sharper, longer-ripened quarter-fat variant of Appenzeller, sold as "Appenzeller Rässkäse". Traditionally made on farms in winter, when the cows give less milk and rely on hay feed, which intensifies the flavour.

entries.heading: Räßkäse (Appenzeller Räßkäse)
entries.what: naturally ripened Swiss/Vorarlberg cheese, a variant of Appenzeller, made in winter when cows give less milk; intensely flavoured from hay feeding.

entries.heading: Aqit (أقط; dried dairy)
entries.what: Named in the Dairy section of the Arabic Iraqi cuisine article as a dried dairy product.

entries.heading: Aqit (dried hard laban; iqt in the Wikipedia text)
entries.what: A hard, dried laban used as an ingredient in Najd dishes.

entries.heading: Arequipe (arequipe / dulce de leche)
entries.what: Colombia's version of dulce de leche, a milk caramel.

entries.heading: Arequipe (arequipe; Venezuelan dulce de leche)
entries.what: A caramelised milk-and-sugar spread; in Venezuela and Colombia the general dulce de leche term is "arequipe".

entries.heading: Arzúa-Ulloa (Queixo de Arzúa-Ulloa; also called queixo de Ulloa, queixo de Lugo, queixo de Chantada, queixo de Curtis locally)
entries.what: A cow's-milk cheese with DO status, made in 24 municipalities on both banks of the Ulla river, in A Coruña and the Ulloa comarca of Lugo. Typically 18–20 cm across, 6–8 cm high, 500–2,000 g.

entries.heading: Arzúa-Ulloa (queso Arzúa-Ulloa)
entries.what: Cow's-milk cheese from Arzúa and A Ulloa in Galicia.

entries.heading: Ayaka (Bonaire)
entries.what: A cornmeal dough, flavoured with salt, sugar and anise, with cheese, butter and milk, wrapped around a filling of chicken, pork, capers, raisins, olives and pickles, and wrapped in banana leaves.

entries.heading: Ayaka (Papiamento: ayaka)
entries.what: A savoury corn-dough parcel with grated cheese, butter and milk in the dough, filled with chicken or pork and capers.

entries.heading: Bagòss (Bagòss; also Bagoss, Bagòss di Bagolino)
entries.what: a hard, raw-milk cow's cheese made only in Bagolino, Caffaro Valley, Province of Brescia, with saffron added to winter cheeses.

entries.heading: Bagòss (Bagòss di Bagolino)
entries.what: a grana-style cheese coloured with saffron.

entries.heading: Balkaymak (балкаймак)
entries.what: Clotted-cream-like dairy product, rich and creamy, named in the atlas for Kyrgyzstan.

entries.heading: Balkaymak (балқаймақ; honey sour cream)
entries.what: Dessert of boiled sour cream sweetened with honey.

entries.heading: Formaggio bastardo del Grappa (Bastardo del Grappa)
entries.what: A cow's-milk cheese of the Grappa alpine pastures. Its name comes from its process, a half-way between Asiago pressato and Asiago d'allevo.

entries.heading: Tea with milk
entries.what: Tea brewed with milk added, served in cafés and at home, often with sugar, lemon or mint.

entries.heading: Bawarka (tea with milk)
entries.what: Tea with milk. The name means "Bavarian style."

entries.heading: Beaufort (Beaufort de Savoie; Beaufort fermier is a separate listed name)
entries.what: large cheese from eastern Savoie; AOC since 1968.

entries.heading: Beaufort
entries.what: A firm raw cow's-milk cheese of the gruyère family from the Alpine Savoie region (Beaufortain, Tarentaise, Maurienne).

entries.heading: Bebidas lácteas (milk-based drinks)
entries.what: milk-based drinks sold in Angolan retail. The report lists them among the most consumed dairy products.

entries.heading: Bebidas lácteas (dairy drinks)
entries.what: Commercial milk drinks sold by the dairy industry.

entries.heading: Beemster (Beemster kaas)
entries.what: Hard Dutch cheese associated with the Beemster polder in North Holland. Made by the CONO Cheesemakers cooperative (about 475 farmers, about 30,000 tons a year per source).

entries.heading: Beemster

entries.heading: Blancmange (blanc-manger)

entries.heading: Bleu d'Auvergne (Fourme du Mézenc listed under this article)

entries.heading: Bleu d'Auvergne

entries.heading: Bleu de Termignon

entries.heading: Bleu des Causses
entries.what: A French blue cheese from whole cow's milk; some see it as a mild variant of Roquefort.

entries.heading: Bleuchâtel (Bleuchâtel; the name combines "bleu" and Neuchâtel)

entries.heading: Bleuchâtel

entries.heading: Blue Rathgore (Blue Rathgore; no other names found)

entries.heading: Blue Rathgore
entries.what: blue goat's-milk cheese with a spicy flavour and crumbly, moist texture.

entries.heading: Bonchester (Bonchester cheese; cow's milk soft)

entries.heading: Bonchester
entries.what: A soft Scottish cheese from Bonchester Bridge, Roxburghshire.

entries.heading: Boursin

entries.heading: Boursin
entries.what: A French brand of soft, fresh Gournay-style cheese with herbs, sold as a spreadable cheese; the first flavour was garlic.

entries.heading: Bra (Bra DOP)

entries.heading: Bra

entries.heading: Brie de Meaux

entries.heading: Brie de Melun (Brie de Melun; Brie de Melun AOP)
entries.what: a small, stronger-flavoured Brie from the Melun area, aged longer than Brie de Meaux.

entries.heading: Brillat-Savarin
entries.what: A triple-cream cheese invented near Forges-les-Eaux (Normandy) and now mainly produced in Burgundy.

entries.heading: Brillat-Savarin
entries.what: a triple-cream bloomy-rind cheese first made near Forges-les-Eaux in Seine-Maritime, about 1890 (sold first as "Excelsior").

entries.heading: Brin d'amour (also fleur du maquis, petit corse)
entries.what: Small Corsican sheep cheese, about 10–12 cm and 500–700 g; created in the 1950s, produced at Furiani, Haute-Corse.

entries.heading: Fleur de maquis (Brin d'amour, Petit corse)
entries.what: A raw-milk cheese from Corsican ewe's milk created in the 1950s, branded "Brin d'Amour".

entries.heading: Brocciu (brocciu; brocciu passu, brocciu vechju)
entries.what: Corsica's most important cheese; eaten fresh or ripened. Fresh weighs 250 g to 3 kg, about 45% fat; produced October to June.

entries.heading: Brocciu
entries.what: A Corsican cheese made from whey and ewe's milk; a whey cheese used in place of ricotta.

entries.heading: Brousse du Rove (AOC/AOP Brousse du Rove)
entries.what: a fresh goat cheese made around Le Rove and the Marseille garrigues, named after the Rove goat breed.

entries.heading: Brousse du Rove
entries.what: A goat cheese made in the commune of Le Rove, Bouches-du-Rhône; a dossier for protection was filed by eight breeders in 2007.

entries.heading: Bruss (Bruss / Bruss da ricotta)
entries.what: strongly flavoured spread from Piemonte and Liguria.

entries.heading: Bruss (Brussu, Brös, Bruzzu, Bross, Brus, Bröss, Brôs; Liguria: Valle Arroscia)
entries.what: a creamy, very strongly flavoured spread. The Ligurian version is associated with the Valle Arroscia. The Piedmontese bruss is a different product, made from fermented leftover scraps of soft or semi-hard cheese with grappa.

entries.heading: Buttermilk powder
entries.what: Dried buttermilk, sold as an ingredient.

entries.heading: Buttermilk powder (dried and condensed buttermilk)
entries.what: Buttermilk dried or condensed for use as a solids ingredient.

entries.heading: Buxton Blue

entries.heading: Buxton Blue
entries.what: A blue cheese made in and around Buxton, Derbyshire.

entries.heading: Byaslag (Mongolian cheese, Inner Mongolia)
entries.what: A mild, unsalted, unaged Mongolian cheese served in milk tea.

entries.heading: Byaslag (бяслаг; byaslag, byasulag, byaslag)
entries.what: A firm, mild, slightly sweet and salty cheese eaten as a snack. Dried so it keeps while herders move.

entries.heading: Caboc (Caboc; cream cheese)

entries.heading: Caboc (Caboc)
entries.what: A Scottish cream cheese, made from double cream or cream-enriched milk.

entries.heading: Cabrales (queso de Cabrales; Asturian blue)
entries.what: traditional blue cheese from the Cabrales municipality and nearby villages in the Picos de Europa; PDO since 1981 per the source.

entries.heading: Cabrales (queso de Cabrales)
entries.what: Strong, pungent blue cheese from the Picos de Europa area of Asturias.

entries.heading: Caciocavallo (Caciocavallo silano; Caciocavallo podolico; Caciocavallo di bufala)
entries.what: a teardrop-shaped stretched-curd cheese; tastes like aged provolone. Name "horse cheese" likely from tying pairs over a stick to mature.

entries.heading: Caciocavallo (カチョカバロ, Nasu no Mori)
entries.what: An aged pasta filata cheese in the Italian style, from Nasu no Mori; name means "horse cheese" for its saddle shape.

entries.heading: Caciocavallo di bufala (semplice e affumicato) (PAT)
entries.what: A buffalo caciocavallo, Lazio.

entries.heading: Caciocavallo di bufala
entries.what: a buffalo-milk caciocavallo from Campania.

entries.heading: Caillebotte
entries.what: a soft, fresh curd from western France, eaten sweetened or lightly salted.

entries.heading: Caillebotte (fromage)
entries.what: A traditional curd dessert from western France, not fermented or drained. Warm milk to 30–35 °C, add a few drops of rennet, set in serving dishes within one or two hours. Keeps only a few hours.

entries.heading: Calcagno
entries.what: Listed among Sardinian cheeses.

entries.heading: Calcagno
entries.what: a Sardinian pecorino made from raw sheep's milk with peppercorns.

entries.heading: Camel milk powder (Camelait)
entries.what: Spray-dried camel milk sold by Al Ain Dairy under the Camelait brand, in 25 g and 400 g pouches and in 10 x 25 g multi-packs. The company calls it a prime export product with a one-year shelf life.

entries.heading: Camel milk powder (powdered camel milk)
entries.what: powdered camel milk offered to pastoralists in the Somali Region. In a sensory trial most preferred fresh milk, but the powder was still rated highly; urban pastoralists were more likely to prefer it.

entries.heading: Camel milk tea (camel tea)
entries.what: camel milk tea is a traditional preparation. It is also used as a base for soups and stews.

entries.heading: Camel milk tea
entries.what: tea made with camel milk.

entries.heading: Camel milk, raw (northern Kenya)
entries.what: camel milk drunk raw by pastoral and agro-pastoral communities in northern Kenya. In Isiolo and Marsabit, nearly all mothers introduced it, often raw, as a first food before one year of age.

entries.heading: Camel milk, raw
entries.what: Raw camel milk from the Laayoune-Sakia El Hamra region of Morocco, used in a study of Moroccan camel milk.

entries.heading: Camel-milk cheese (Rakhyut Cheese Factory; Arabic جبن الإبل)
entries.what: A camel-milk cheese introduced locally by Rakhyut Cheese Factory, according to a market report on Oman camel-milk products.

entries.heading: Camel-milk cheese (experimental, Saudi Arabia)
entries.what: The Camel and Range Research Center in Sakaka (Al-Jouf) conducted the first trial of milk pasteurization and cheese making in Saudi Arabia, in 2003.

entries.heading: Cancoillotte
entries.what: A soft, creamy spread from Franche-Comté eaten as a fondue or on bread.

entries.heading: Cancoillotte
entries.what: A runny French cheese made from metton; produced mainly in Franche-Comté, also in Lorraine and Luxembourg (known as Kachkéis there).

entries.heading: Cantal (fromage) (Cantal; fourme de Cantal; tomme de cantal for the pressed curd)

entries.heading: Fourme de Cantal

entries.what: A Brie-like soft cheese made from camel milk. It is made in Mauritania and is also sold and eaten in Senegal.

entries.heading: Carré de l'Est

entries.heading: Casizolu

entries.heading: Casolet (PAT)

entries.heading: Chevrette des Bauges

entries.heading: Chevrotin

entries.heading: Chloro Santorinis (χλωρό Σαντορίνης; Santorini)
entries.what: named as a Santorini cheese; no details found.

entries.heading: Chloro Santorinis (Χλωρό Σαντορίνης)
entries.what: Santorini cheese; no details.

entries.heading: Clover (spread)

entries.heading: Clover (Clover; dairy brand)
entries.what: a dairy brand reported as the most scanned dairy brand in Lesotho in a 2026 market-research post.

entries.heading: Comté (Comté; Gruyère de Comté)

entries.heading: Milk jam (confiture de lait)

entries.heading: Cornish Yarg

entries.heading: Cornish Yarg

entries.heading: Coutances

entries.heading: Coutances

entries.heading: Crémet d'Anjou

entries.heading: Queso Cremoso (Conaprole)

entries.heading: Crottin de Chavignol

entries.heading: Cuartirolo
entries.what: A Uruguayan cheese listed among the country's cheeses.

entries.heading: Cultured butter (زبدة رائبة; zibda raiba)
entries.what: a special soured butter used in one Bahraini rice dish (Al-Mudalal), added to finish the dish.

entries.heading: Cultured butter (syrnet smør)
entries.what: butter from cream with lactic cultures; a 1970s method in Denmark (per Danish article), with fuller aroma from diacetyl.

entries.heading: Dadih (dadiah)
entries.what: A traditional fermented buffalo milk from West Sumatra, eaten by the Minangkabau people, usually at breakfast with ampiang and palm sugar, or with rice and sambal.

entries.heading: Dadih (dadiah; traditional buffalo-milk yoghurt)
entries.what: A traditional fermented milk of the Minangkabau people, eaten with shallots and cucumber. Its name is linked by the article to Sindhi "dudh" (milk).

entries.heading: Dadih (Terengganu and Minangkabau fermented buffalo milk)
entries.what: Traditional milk fermented in a bamboo tube until it sets. Called dadiah in Minangkabau (West Sumatra, Indonesia).

entries.heading: Danbo (Danbo; Lillebror, Gamle Ole, Riberhus, King Christian are named variants)
entries.what: Denmark's most-produced and most-eaten cheese, sold as rectangular blocks; mild when young, sharp when aged.

entries.heading: Danbo (Uruguayan)
entries.what: A Uruguayan version of the Danish cheese danbo.

entries.heading: Derby (and Sage Derby)
entries.what: A mild, semi-firm British cheese with a smooth, mellow texture and buttery flavour; sweeter and firmer as it ages.

entries.heading: Derby (Sage Derby)
entries.what: A mild, semi-firm British cheese from Derbyshire.

entries.heading: Dhanaan (fermented camel milk)
entries.what: spontaneously fermented camel milk, the main fermented camel product in the Somali Regional State. Shelf life about five months. Also named as gariss or shubat in other countries.

entries.heading: Dhanaan (dhanaan; fermented camel milk)
entries.what: Fermented camel milk listed for Somalia in Table 3 of the camel-milk review, alongside garris.

entries.heading: Domiati (other names: jabna bayda, "the white cheese")
entries.what: An Egyptian white cheese named after Damietta.

entries.heading: Domiati (دمياطي; جبنه دمياطى; gebna beida / جبنة بيضا, "white cheese"; Dumyati; other names: Damietta cheese)
entries.what: The most common cheese in Egypt, a soft, white, salty cheese named after the seaport of Damietta.

entries.heading: Dumyati (Damietta cheese; Arabic name not in opened sources)
entries.what: A cheese produced today in the Damietta district. The Egyptian cheese article lists it separately from Domiati.

entries.heading: Dondurma (ice cream)
entries.what: a frozen product of cream, milk, sugar, flavourings and stabilisers. The Azerbaijani-language article says more than 50 varieties are made, in milk, cream, plombir, fruit and berry, and aromatic types.

entries.heading: Dondurma (Turkish ice cream)
entries.what: Turkish ice cream, usually made with milk, sugar, salep and mastic; its chewy texture comes from salep or starch.

entries.heading: Donor breast milk (proposed banking)
entries.what: donor breast milk and banking, described as a novel concept in Rwanda, not yet an established practice.

entries.heading: Donor breast milk (Milk Matters, Cape Town)
entries.what: A Cape Town-based programme that collects and distributes donor breast milk.

entries.heading: Dorset Blue Vinney
entries.what: Traditional English blue cheese, historically a by-product of butter-making using leftover skimmed milk.

entries.heading: Dorset Blue Vinney
entries.what: A traditional English blue cheese from Dorset.

entries.heading: Double Gloucester (and Single Gloucester)
entries.what: An English semi-hard cheese; Single is lighter and more crumbly, Double firmer and more savoury.

entries.heading: Double Gloucester
entries.what: A traditional English semi-hard cheese; Single and Double varieties.

entries.heading: Double skin milk (双皮奶, shuāngpínǎi)
entries.what: A Cantonese dessert from Shunde, Guangdong; velvety milk custard, somewhat like panna cotta. Chinese name 双皮奶.

entries.heading: Double-skin milk (雙皮奶)
entries.what: A Cantonese dessert of milk custard with two skins, somewhat like panna cotta, popular in Hong Kong.

entries.heading: Dovedale
entries.what: A soft, creamy blue cheese named after the Dovedale valley in the Peak District; the original is made at Hartington Creamery, Derbyshire; a version is also made by the Staffordshire Cheese Company in Cheddleton, Staffordshire.

entries.heading: Dovedale
entries.what: A soft, creamy, mild blue cheese from full-fat cow's milk, named after the Dovedale valley in the Peak District.

entries.heading: Dunlop (Traditional Ayrshire Dunlop; sweet-milk cheese)
entries.what: A mild Scottish sweet-milk cheese originating in Dunlop, East Ayrshire, resembling a soft Cheddar.

entries.heading: Dunlop
entries.what: A Scottish cheese from Dunlop, East Ayrshire.

entries.heading: Eezgii (roasted dried curd)
entries.what: Roasted, crumbly, lightly sweet Mongolian curd, also found among Manchu in NE China.

entries.heading: Eezgii (eezgii, eezgiy; Cyrillic spelling not found in sources)
entries.what: A dried, roasted curd eaten as a snack. Sweet and high in protein.

entries.heading: Eezgii (ээзгий; roasted dried curd)
entries.what: A long-keeping roasted curd, a steppe food, traditionally made from the first milk of spring and eaten dry or simmered back into milk.

entries.heading: Eidam (Eidamská cihla; Dutch-type natural cheese)
entries.what: the most common Czech round or brick cheese, mildly sweet, not very salty; made by about 15 Czech dairies.

entries.heading: Eidam (eidam; Edam-type; Slovak retail)
entries.what: sold in Slovak retail chains; tested with polooštiepok and parenica in a 2026 Foods paper.

entries.heading: Emmental français est-central
entries.what: Regional Emmental variant, listed as an IGP tagged to Franche-Comté, Lorraine and Rhône-Alpes.

entries.heading: Emmental français est-central
entries.what: The French Emmental (IGP), made in eastern-central France in the Swiss style, with holes (eyes).

entries.heading: Époisses
entries.what: A soft washed-rind cow's-milk cheese from the village of Époisses in the Côte-d'Or.

entries.heading: Époisses (Époisses de Bourgogne)
entries.what: A legally demarcated smear-ripened cheese from the village of Époisses, Côte-d'Or, between Dijon and Auxerre.

entries.heading: Etorki
entries.what: A cylindrical sheep cheese made by the Fromagerie des Chaumes in Mauléon-Licharre (former Soule, French Basque Country); a Savencia subsidiary, sold year-round, not a protected cheese.

entries.heading: Etorki
entries.what: A firm sheep's-milk cheese from the French Basque country, made at Mauléon-Licharre (Pyrénées-Atlantiques).

entries.heading: Faisselle
entries.what: A fresh curd cheese drained in a faisselle, listed for Poitou, Charentes, Touraine and Berry.

entries.heading: Faisselle
entries.what: A non-protected fresh curd cheese, named after the perforated mould in which it is strained; made in central France.

entries.heading: Firni (rice dessert)
entries.what: a rice dessert listed in Azerbaijani sweets; Azerbaijani article gives rice flour and sugar; the cuisine page says it is made from fresh milk, soured milk or qatıq.

entries.heading: Firni (phirni; rice pudding)
entries.what: Rice pudding of ground rice or cornflour cooked in milk, flavoured with cardamom, saffron, rosewater; served chilled in clay bowls (shikora).

entries.heading: Flan de leche
entries.what: a milk-based custard dessert, often topped with dulce de leche.

entries.heading: Flan de leche (Dominican crème caramel)
entries.what: A caramel custard made with evaporated and condensed milk and egg yolks.

entries.heading: Flor de Guía (Queso flor de Guía; Queso de Flor de Guía y Queso de Guía)
entries.what: A traditional Gran Canarian cheese from the Guía area, one of the island's symbols.

entries.heading: Flor de Guía (queso de Flor de Guía; Flor de Guía; Half Flor; Guía)
entries.what: A Canarian cheese from Gran Canaria with a rind imprinted with a flower pattern, in three varieties.

entries.heading: Fluid cow's milk (Australian milk; pasteurised and fresh)
entries.what: The main milk for drinking. Australia produces milk, cream, butter, cheese and yoghurt on an industrial scale.

entries.heading: Fluid cow's milk (pasteurised; grass-fed)
entries.what: fluid milk makes up about two-thirds of Canadian dairy output; Dairy Farmers of Canada names milk including grass-fed milk, which has a national DFC standard.

entries.heading: Formaggio di malga (Tipo malga friulano)
entries.what: Cheese from small mountain-hut (malga) dairies, made from milk of animals grazing high pasture; the paste varies by hut and season.

entries.heading: Formaggio di malga (di Triora, delle Alpi Marittime; alpeggio di Triora)
entries.what: a cow's-milk cheese from the summer pastures (alpeggio) of Triora and other Alpi Marittime pastures.

entries.heading: Mallorca cheese (Formatge de Mallorca; formatge mallorquí; Mallorquín)
entries.what: Semi-hard island cheese, made only on Mallorca, with a protected designation of origin. Eaten sliced with wine or beer, or with fruit and nuts; older cheeses are firmer.

entries.heading: Formatge Mallorquí (Mallorca cheese)
entries.what: Mallorcan cheese, PDO.

entries.heading: Fourme d'Ambert (Ambert)
entries.what: cylinder about 13 cm across, 19 cm high, 2–2.5 kg; first made around Ambert.

entries.heading: Fourme d'Ambert
entries.what: A semi-hard blue cheese, one of France's oldest, from the Auvergne (Ambert area); dates back to Roman times, per the article.

entries.heading: Fourme de Montbrison
entries.what: blue cheese from the Monts du Forez; AOC 1972, AOP 2009.

entries.heading: Fourme de Montbrison
entries.what: A cow's-milk cheese from Rhône-Alpes and Auvergne, named after Montbrison (Loire).

entries.heading: Fresh and pasteurised milk (რძე)
entries.what: standard milk products made in factories with standardised fat content; the Georgian article gives adult consumption at 250–500 g/day.

entries.heading: Fresh and pasteurised milk (industrial)
entries.what: Everyday liquid milk sold in Irish shops under dairy-company brands; Irish cuisine treats milk as a staple of all social classes in medieval Ireland, cow and goat milk ranked above sheep's.

entries.heading: Fresh raw milk (informal sale)
entries.what: Liquid milk sold unprocessed direct to consumers through informal channels by local producers; about 44% of locally produced milk is marketed informally versus 56% formally. Fresh liquid milk consumption fell from 357 mL per person per mont

entries.heading: Nom sot (นมสด, fresh raw milk)
entries.what: liquid fresh milk. The Thai term นมสด appears in the Thai Wikipedia condensed-milk article. In the 1990s about half of Thailand's liquid milk was fresh, the rest recombined.

entries.heading: Frico (fried cheese dish)
entries.what: Friulian dish of cheese (usually Montasio) fried until crisp, often with potato and onion.

entries.heading: Frico
entries.what: a Friulian dish of cheese (and potatoes, onions) fried or pressed until crisp; the cheese is the main ingredient, not a separate cheese.

entries.heading: Friese nagelkaas / Kanterkaas (Kanternagelkaas, kanterkaas; Friese nagelkaas)
entries.what: A spiced cheese from Friesland, flavoured with cloves (kruidnagel) or cumin (komijn). The protected version is called kanterkaas; its origin is given as Friesland and the Westerkwartier (the Westerkwartier is in Groningen, not Friesland, so

entries.heading: Kanterkaas (Kanternagelkaas; Kanterkomijnekaas)
entries.what: A Friesland cheese, the skimmed-milk relative of Friesian clove cheese. Plain Kanterkaas has no spice; Kanterkomijnekaas is spiced with cumin; Kanternagelkaas with cumin and cloves.

entries.heading: Friese nagelkaas (Friesian clove cheese)
entries.what: A Friesland wheel flavoured with cloves and cumin. The original was made from skimmed milk, which lacked flavour, so spices were added. Cloves helped it keep on long sea voyages.

entries.heading: Fromage frais
entries.what: A fresh, acid-coagulated cheese in the same article as fromage blanc; the Wikipedia article covers both.

entries.heading: Fromage frais (Luxlait)
entries.what: Smooth, mild fresh cheese sold by Luxlait ("onctueux et doux").

entries.heading: Frue (Frughe, Fiscidu)
entries.what: Curdled sheep's milk served in Sardinian meals. Served with Irgoli salami inland, and added at the end to the minestra de merca soup.

entries.heading: Fura da nono
entries.what: a Nigerian drink of millet and nono (fermented milk).

entries.heading: Fura da nono (millet balls in fermented milk)
entries.what: The famous northern Nigerian dish: spiced millet balls pounded into nono; served as a meal, drink, or weaning food, depending on thickness. Sold roadside and in markets.

entries.heading: Gammelost (gammalost, gamalost; "old cheese")
entries.what: a traditional, very pungent Norwegian cheese, over-matured. It is high in ACE-inhibiting peptides and is studied for blood-pressure effects.

entries.heading: Gammelost (historical Swedish name for fresh cheese)
entries.what: In Sweden, fresh cheese (färskost) was once called gammelost, to set it apart from cheese made with rennet, which took the name ost. Historical name only, not a separate product.

entries.heading: Gamonéu (Gamonedo; Queso de Gamonéu)
entries.what: blue cheese of the high Picos de Europa area of Asturias, PDO since 2003 per the source. Two varieties: Del Puerto (high mountain pastures, June–September, at least two milks, sheep and/or goat above 10% each) and Del Valle (lower valleys,

entries.heading: Queso de Gamonedo (Gamonéu)
entries.what: Asturian cheese, DO listing.

entries.heading: Gaperon (Limagne)
entries.what: small cheese from the Limagne plain, Auvergne; now about 30% fat.

entries.heading: Gaperon
entries.what: A cheese from the Auvergne made for over 1200 years, flavoured with cracked peppercorns and local pink garlic.

entries.heading: Garrotxa (Queso Garrotxa; Formatge Garrotxa)
entries.what: A small (~750 g), cylindrical, flat goat cheese with grey or blue-grey rind and an ivory, semi-firm interior; earthy and slightly acidic, revived in the Garrotxa by a cheesemakers' cooperative.

entries.heading: Garrotxa (formatge de la Garrotxa)
entries.what: Catalan goat's-milk cheese from the Garrotxa area, Pyrenees and Pre-Pyrenees.

entries.heading: Gelato (Italian-Eritrean)
entries.what: An Italian-style ice cream, listed among Italian-Eritrean dishes.

entries.heading: Gelato (gelato; Italian for ice cream)
entries.what: Italian frozen dairy dessert with lower butterfat than ice cream.

entries.heading: Ginger milk curd (姜撞奶; Macanese dessert, Macau)
entries.what: a custard-like dessert of sweetened milk set with ginger juice, listed among Macanese desserts and as a Macanese snack.

entries.heading: Ginger milk curd (薑汁撞奶; ginger milk pudding, 姜撞奶)
entries.what: A Chinese dessert of milk set with ginger juice and sweetened with sugar. Served in Hong Kong among several Guangdong and Macau places; instant packaged versions are sold.

entries.heading: Ginger milk curd (姜撞奶; Macanese "ginger milk")
entries.what: a warm, set milk pudding flavoured with ginger juice; sold in Macau and Hong Kong and in Guangdong.

entries.heading: Glarner Schabziger (Schabziger; Zigerstöckli; Sap Sago; Swiss Green Cheese)
entries.what: A very lean, hard, green-flecked cone made from skimmed milk curd, flavoured with blue fenugreek (Schabzigerklee), and produced only in the canton of Glarus. The sales names abroad are Swiss Green Cheese and, in the US, Sap Sago.

entries.heading: Schabziger (Glarner Schabziger)
entries.what: hard green cheese from Canton Glarus, flavoured with blue fenugreek (blue melilot).

entries.heading: Gourmelin
entries.what: described as a mild, creamy cheese with a subtle woody aroma.

entries.heading: Gourmelin
entries.what: Mild, creamy, subtly woody soft cheese; categorised as a Loire-Atlantique cheese.

entries.heading: Gratte Paille
entries.what: Cheese tagged to Champagne and Île-de-France on the list page.

entries.heading: Gratte-paille (Gratte Paille)
entries.what: a cheese listed for Champagne and Île-de-France.

entries.heading: Greek-style plain yoghurt (Greek Yogurt, 1 kg)
entries.what: Namibia Dairies' Greek-style plain yoghurt, sold in 1 kg tubs; a Woermann Central promotion at N$44.99 is shown on the homepage.

entries.heading: Greek yogurt (US strained yogurt)
entries.what: Yogurt strained or concentrated to a thick texture; a large US category.

entries.heading: Grießkoch (semolina pudding, Grießbrei)
entries.what: semolina cooked in milk (or a milk-and-water mix), served sweet or as a firmer base for Grießschmarren

entries.heading: Grießbrei (semolina pudding)
entries.what: porridge made from soft-wheat semolina (Weichweizengrieß), cooked in milk, slightly salted milk, or a mix of milk and water.

entries.heading: Gruyère français
entries.what: French gruyère; wheels about 42 kg, 53–63 cm across.

entries.heading: Gruyère français (Gruyère franc-comtois)
entries.what: A raw-milk pressed cheese, weighing about 42 kg per wheel, made in Franche-Comté, Jura and Doubs.

entries.heading: Hangop
entries.what: A thick, quark-like product from yoghurt or buttermilk, drained in a cloth; increasingly made commercially.

entries.heading: Hangop
entries.what: A dessert dairy product, a thick, quark-like yoghurt or buttermilk.

entries.heading: Harbourne Blue
entries.what: A spicy, assertive goat's cheese from Ticklemore Cheese Company, near Totnes, Devon, England.

entries.heading: Harbourne Blue
entries.what: A goat's-milk blue cheese from Devon.

entries.heading: Hard cheese (Sri Lankan market brands)
entries.what: 14 hard-cheese samples in the 2024 Sri Lankan market survey. Hard cheeses of brands A, D and G are named; the paper does not say which brands made the other hard cheeses.

entries.heading: Queso duro (hard cheese, brick-shaped)
entries.what: a strong-smelling, salty, dry-aged hard cheese in brick form, firmer than fresh Latin American cheeses and suited to crumbling or grating. Eaten on beans, bean soup, and Salvadoran enchiladas.

entries.heading: Havarti (cream Havarti / flødehavarti; dill, garlic, jalapeño and caraway flavours)
entries.what: a mild, creamy Danish cheese that can be sliced, grilled or melted.

entries.heading: Havarti (made in NZ)
entries.what: A Danish-origin cheese that the NZ cuisine article says some NZ farmers began making in the 1980s.

entries.heading: Herbstmilchsuppe (autumn milk soup)
entries.what: a soup of curdled milk, described as a typical farm breakfast

entries.heading: Herbstmilchsuppe (autumn sour-milk soup)
entries.what: a Bavarian peasant soup made from curdled milk.

entries.heading: Herve (Herve cheese; Limburger; Fromage de Herve; Limburgse kaas, Hervekaas; Land van Herve)
entries.what: A pungent, rind-washed cow's-milk cheese from the Herve area, east of Liège. Sold as a brick or cube. It is the cheese the English-language "Limburger" name points to, though the name is also used for the style made elsewhere.

entries.heading: Hervekaas (Limburgse kaas; Herfse kaas; fromage de Herve; rommedoe / Remoudou in Maastricht area)
entries.what: an old Limburg cheese from the Land van Herve, which the Dutch Wikipedia article gives as the Herve region in Belgium, but which was also made in Maastricht and its surroundings, where it is called rommedoe. Three varieties: mild (zachte),

entries.heading: Herzegovina "squeaking" cheese (škripavac; Hercegovački škripavi sir)
entries.what: A cheese from the Herzegovina region, named for the squeak it makes when eaten.

entries.heading: Škripavac (škripavac; "squeaky" farmers' cheese)
entries.what: a farmers' cheese from the Kordun and Lika regions

entries.heading: Horlicks (malted milk drink powder)
entries.what: sweet malted milk hot drink powder.

entries.heading: Horlicks (malted milk drink), including Horlicks Dinosaur
entries.what: British-origin malted milk powder drink; UK version prepared with hot milk, instant and chocolate versions with hot water.

entries.heading: Hvit geitost (hvitost; gulost; white goat cheese)
entries.what: a Norwegian white goat cheese, listed among Norwegian cheeses alongside Jarlsberg, Norvegia and Nøkkelost.

entries.heading: White goat cheese (Hijaz, in kunafah)
entries.what: Layered with butter and pine nuts in kunafah for Ramadan sweets in the Hijaz, then baked and soaked in rose-scented syrup.

entries.heading: Queso Ibores (queso de los Ibores; Spanish)
entries.what: a goat's-milk cheese from the Ibores and Villuercas mountains; sold with a natural, oiled or paprika-coated rind.

entries.heading: Ibores (queso Ibores)
entries.what: Goat's-milk cheese from the Ibores area of Extremadura.

name: Ice cream and frozen milk desserts

entries.heading: Ice cream and frozen milk desserts (雪糕, 冰淇淋, 冰酪, 酥山)
entries.what: Mainland China's terms for ice cream are 冰淇淋, 冰激凌 and 雪糕 (Hong Kong: 雪糕). Historical forms: 冰酪, a Tang-era cold drink of milk and fruit juice (Youyang Zazu); 酥山, a Tang-era cream-like frozen food. Modern products include Yili's Joyday ice c

entries.heading: Ice cream and frozen milk desserts (Luxlait glaces range)
entries.what: Luxlait's ice cream range: mochi, cones, sticks, tubs, miniatures, frozen yoghurt, cakes, "dame blanche" and water ices (water ices are not milk-based).

entries.heading: Imported supermarket cheeses (Gouda, Camembert, cheddar, soft bries and other imported types)
entries.what: Imported cheeses that dominate the market, ranging from soft bries to hard cheddars. The guide lists European types such as Gouda and Camembert, and American and regional Caribbean offerings.

entries.heading: Imported supermarket cheeses (mozzarella, cream cheese, sliced cheese)
entries.what: Imported Australian cheese products sold in the Maldives by a local trader. Not made in the Maldives.

entries.heading: Kalakand (कलाकंद)
entries.what: Firm milk-and-chhena fudge, firmer than milk cake and softer than burfi; sometimes called Indian cheesecake.

entries.heading: Kalakand (milk cake)
entries.what: Fudge-like sweet made from chhena, milk, sugar and ghee, cut into squares; listed under Pakistani desserts.

entries.heading: Kalathaki Limnou (Καλαθάκι Λήμνου; kalathaki)
entries.what: A white, brined sheep-and-goat cheese made on Lemnos, with small fat-filled holes and a taste similar to feta but less sour.

entries.heading: Kalathaki Limnou (Καλαθάκι Λήμνου; Π.Ο.Π.)
entries.what: Specialty of Lemnos; creamy cheese for spreads.

entries.heading: Karak chai (spiced milk tea)
entries.what: Strong, spiced milk tea popular across the Gulf Arab region, known as Chai Karak in Arabic (شاي كرك) and karak chai in Urdu (کڑک چائے).

entries.heading: Karak chai (milk tea)
entries.what: Spiced black tea with milk, sugar and spices; popular in the Gulf Arab region as "Chai Karak".

entries.heading: Kaskaval (kaskavál)
entries.what: a yellow semi-hard cheese across the Balkans, Turkey and the Levant; in Hungary the term kaskavál refers to this type, and the Hajdú brand is the best-known Hungarian kashkaval.

entries.heading: Kaşkaval
entries.what: Sheep's cheese, named from the Romanian cașcaval.

entries.heading: Katiki Domokou (Κατίκι Δομοκού, ΠΟΠ)
entries.what: a soft fresh cheese from Domokos in the Phthiotis prefecture.

entries.heading: Katiki Domokou (Κατίκι Δομοκού; Π.Ο.Π.)
entries.what: Creamy soft cheese from Domokos (Phthiotis), sold in many supermarkets; often served on toast, dakos or in salads.

entries.heading: Keshi yena (keshi yena, "kesh yena"; Papiamentu for cheese: keshi)
entries.what: a large round Gouda or Edam cheese rind stuffed with spiced meat, olives, raisins and chicken in modern versions; a national dish of Aruba and Curaçao

entries.heading: Keshi yena (keshi yená; "stuffed cheese")
entries.what: A Curaçaoan national dish of a whole Edam (originally leftover Gouda or Edam rinds) filled with spiced meat and baked or steamed. Also served at Curaçaoan weddings alongside stobá and a wedding cake.

entries.heading: Shubat / chal (шұбат; khoormog)
entries.what: Sour, sparkling fermented camel milk, a staple summer food of Kazakhs; hard to export because it is perishable.

entries.heading: Khoormog (хоормог; khormog, hoormog)
entries.what: A traditional fermented camel milk drink, sour, tangy and foamy, sold locally by herder households. Thicker than airag and does not separate into curd or yellow whey.

entries.heading: Klila (كليلة; Berber ikil/tiklitt; also Lagta, Lemjeben)
entries.what: The most popular traditional Algerian cheese, a fermented curd made by hand in several regions, mainly the east. Dried Klila is used rehydrated in cooking, and crushed as a condiment by nomads.

entries.heading: Klila (fresh cheese from lben curd)
entries.what: A fresh cheese made from the leftover curd of rayeb when it is not churned for lben.

entries.heading: Klila (dried lben curd)
entries.what: A dried, agglomerated white curd eaten for long storage, made from lben.

entries.heading: Koi lechi (Bonaire)
entries.what: A candy made from sweet milk, listed among the sweets of Bonaire's Kuminda Krioyo cuisine.

entries.heading: Ko'i lechi (koi lechi; K'oi lechi)
entries.what: A sweet of condensed milk and sugar, served at weddings and other special occasions.

entries.heading: Kollumer kaas (historic; discontinued)
entries.what: A factory cheese first made by Frico and later by Friesland Foods, named after the town of Kollum; not made in Kollum itself.

entries.heading: Kollumer kaas
entries.what: A factory cheese made by Frico and later Friesland Foods, described as the only factory cheese made from raw milk. Despite the name it was not made in Kollum.

entries.heading: Krasotyri Kou (κρασοτύρι Κω; Tyri tis Possias; PGI)
entries.what: a Kos cheese matured in wine lees, reddish rind.

entries.heading: Krasotyri Kou (Κρασοτύρι Κω; Π.Γ.Ε.)
entries.what: Kos cheese with PGI status.

entries.heading: Krempita (cream pie, custard-cream dessert)
entries.what: A cream dessert shown as "Cream pie" in the Bosnian cuisine article gallery.

entries.heading: Krempita (кремпита; cream pie)
entries.what: custard-filled puff pastry dessert, known in Serbia, Bosnia and Montenegro as krempita ("cream pie"); sometimes custard combined with meringue (šampita variant).

entries.heading: Kremšnita (kremšnita; Samoborska and Zagrebačka variants)
entries.what: A layered cream cake with a puff pastry base, custard and whipped cream filling, and a top of pastry or chocolate icing. In Croatia the two best-known versions are Samoborska and Zagrebačka.

entries.heading: Kremšnita (kremna rezina; cream slice)
entries.what: Four-layer dessert: puff pastry base, cooked vanilla custard, whipped sweet cream, puff pastry top dusted with icing sugar.

entries.heading: Milk toffee (kiri aluwa, කිරි ඇලුවා)
entries.what: A soft, crumbly toffee cut into small squares or diamonds, eaten cooled. Traditional Sinhalese New Year food.

entries.heading: Krówki (ciągutki mleczne, pomadki mleczne; milk toffee)
entries.what: Soft milk toffee candy with a chewy centre that becomes crumbly as sugar crystallises.

entries.heading: Kule-naoto (Maasai fermented milk)
entries.what: a traditional lactic fermented milk of the Maasai in Kenya and northern Tanzania. The review cites a consumption figure of about 2–3 litres per person per day.

entries.heading: Kule-naoto (Maasai fermented milk)
entries.what: a traditional lactic fermented milk of the Maasai, in Kenya and northern Tanzania.

entries.heading: Kvarg
entries.what: a Norwegian fresh cheese, similar to kesam; the en Wikipedia article is about German quark and lists Norwegian and Swedish "kvarg" as cognates.

entries.heading: Färskost (keso, kvarg, fresh cheese)
entries.what: Swedish fresh cheese family: färskost, keso (semi-liquid), kvarg (semi-liquid).

entries.heading: Kvarg (kesella)
entries.what: Smooth, creamy fresh cheese, sharper than keso, sold in several fat levels. Arla launched it in Swedish retail in 1985 under the name kesella. Its shelf life is about two weeks in a fridge.

entries.heading: Kwark (Dutch quark)
entries.what: A fresh cheese. Legally kwark is reserved for cow's-milk products under the Dutch Warenwet.

entries.heading: Kwark (plattekaas; maqueye)
entries.what: A fresh soft curd; originally a very fresh cheese, now treated as a dairy product under Dutch law. In Belgium known as plattekaas; the traditional Brabant product is "Brabantse plattekaas" or "Rotzelaer kaas", made by a dairy in Rotselaar.

entries.heading: Kwark
entries.what: A soft fresh curd. Historically a very fresh cheese, but the Dutch article classifies it as a dairy product (zuivelproduct) and dessert under dairy rules, and it is mostly eaten as a dessert, plain or with fruit.

entries.heading: L'Étivaz (L'Etivaz AOP)
entries.what: summer-only hard cheese from cows grazing alpine pastures in Vaud.

entries.heading: L'Etivaz
entries.what: hard Swiss cheese similar to Gruyère surchoix, made only in summer when cows graze Alpine pastures.

entries.heading: Ladotyri Mytilinis (Λαδοτύρι Μυτιλήνης; ladotyri)
entries.what: A PDO hard cheese from Lesbos (Mytilene), cylinders of about 10 cm across and high, around 1.5 kg; minimum fat over 40% of dry matter, maximum moisture 38%.

entries.heading: Ladotyri Mytilinis (Λαδοτύρι Μυτιλήνης; Π.Ο.Π. Lesbos)
entries.what: Hard cheese from Lesbos stored in extra virgin olive oil. The name means "oil cheese". Oil preservation was common until refrigerators became widespread in the 1960s–70s.

entries.heading: Lanark Blue (Lanark Blue; sheep's milk blue)
entries.what: A semi-hard, unpasteurised blue cheese from sheep's milk, named after the town of Lanark, Lanarkshire.

entries.heading: Lanark Blue
entries.what: A Scottish sheep's-milk blue cheese.

entries.heading: Lancashire (Creamy, Tasty, Crumbly; Beacon Fell Traditional Lancashire)
entries.what: A Lancashire cheese in creamy, tasty and crumbly forms; the creamy is traditionally paired with Eccles and Chorley cakes.

entries.heading: Lancashire
entries.what: An English cow's-milk cheese in three varieties.

entries.heading: Tettemelk (tjukkmjølk, tjukkmelk; Swedish långmjölk, långfil)
entries.what: a traditional Nordic soured milk that stays firm and does not separate into whey and curd. Rarely eaten in daily life today; the closest modern product is Tjukkmjølk from Rørosmeieriet, which is the first Norwegian farm product to receive a

entries.heading: Långfil (långmjölk)
entries.what: A very thick, stringy-textured soured milk, historically popular in Norrland and more common in northern Sweden; introduced by Arla in 1965.

entries.heading: Langres
entries.what: A cow's-milk cheese from the Langres plateau, mostly in Haute-Marne.

entries.heading: Langres
entries.what: A cow's-milk cheese from the Langres plateau (Champagne-Ardenne), AOC since 1991.

entries.heading: Latchiiri / dakkere (fermented milk eaten with couscous)
entries.what: Milk fermented into yoghurt, eaten with corn couscous, mixed or served apart.

entries.heading: Latchiiri / dakkere (yoghurt with corn couscous)
entries.what: fermented milk (yoghurt) eaten with corn couscous, under the names latchiiri or dakkere.

entries.heading: Leche fresca / pasteurizada (fresh and pasteurised cow milk)
entries.what: Cow milk is the main dairy product. Costa Rica produces more than 1,135 million litres of fluid milk a year, and consumption is above 210 litres per person.

entries.heading: Leche fresca pasteurizada (fresh pasteurised whole and skim milk)
entries.what: The standard drinking milk sold in Uruguay, whole or skimmed, pasteurised. The Uruguayan dairy co-operative Conaprole sells it as its basic product.

entries.heading: Leche nevada
entries.what: a cold sweet of meringue flakes poached in vanilla milk and set in a custard, dusted with cinnamon or chocolate.

entries.heading: Leche nevada (snow milk; custard with meringue flakes)
entries.what: A cold dessert the Spanish Wikipedia article calls typical of Chilean gastronomy, with French influence. Its earliest mention there is the 1913 "Manual de cocina a beneficio de Lourdes"; it also appears in "La Buena Mesa" (1935).

entries.heading: Leerdammer (Leerdammer kaas; Bel Leerdammer)
entries.what: a mild, nutty-sweet cheese sold as pre-packaged slices and rectangular blocks under the Leerdammer name, made by a large dairy group rather than farms.

entries.heading: Leerdammer
entries.what: A trademarked Emmental-style cheese, pale yellow, creamy, sweet and slightly nutty.

entries.heading: Leidse kaas (Leyden; Boeren-Leidse met sleutels)
entries.what: A cumin-spiced cheese from the Leiden area, traditionally made by farmers who turned surplus semi-skimmed milk into a low-fat cheese that kept better than Gouda. Young cheese has a red rind (annatto colouring).

entries.heading: Leyden cheese (Leidse kaas; Boeren-Leidse met sleutels PDO)
entries.what: A cumin-spiced cheese from the Leiden area. Historically a by-product of butter-making, from part-skimmed milk. The Dutch article calls it lower in fat than Gouda (40+, 30+ or 20+ fat in dry matter).

entries.heading: Limburger
entries.what: A soft, smear-ripened cheese named after the former Duchy of Limburg; brick-shaped and closely resembles Romadur.

entries.heading: Limburger (Hervekaas; Rommedoe)
entries.what: A soft cheese with a strong smell, made since the 15th century in the Herve area of the historical Duchy of Limburg. The Dutch Limburg name is Rommedoe (Maastricht) or Hervekaas.

entries.heading: Lincolnshire Poacher
entries.what: Hard cylindrical English cheese made by craft cheesemaker Richard Tagg at Ulceby Grange Farm near Alford, Lincolnshire.

entries.heading: Lincolnshire Poacher
entries.what: A hard, unpasteurised cow's-milk cheese from Alford, Lincolnshire.

entries.heading: Livarot (Livarot AOC/AOP)
entries.what: a Normandy washed-rind cheese from the Pays d'Auge, made from cow's milk.

entries.heading: Livarot
entries.what: A soft, pungent washed-rind cheese from Normandy, named after the commune of Livarot; AOC since 1975.

entries.heading: Lor
entries.what: Unsalted whey cheese made from whey left after kaşar or strained-yogurt production. Used in traditional dishes and desserts (ekşimik, höşmerim).

entries.heading: Lor (لور)
entries.what: A product named in the butter and kashk articles, made from buttermilk or from the liquid drained from fresh cheese.

entries.heading: Lymeswold
entries.what: A soft, mild English blue cheese, first produced at Cannington creamery, Somerset; developed at the Crudgington research centre in Shropshire; name from a public naming competition, possibly after the English place name Wymeswold.

entries.heading: Lymeswold
entries.what: An English blue cheese developed by the Milk Marketing Board.

entries.heading: Maaslander
entries.what: A Gouda-style cheese described as made in Huizen.

entries.heading: Maaslander
entries.what: A trademarked milder Gouda-type cheese (Westland Kaasspecialiteiten, Huizen), a wheel of about 12 kg, fat 30–50.

entries.heading: Mâconnais (goat cheese)
entries.what: A small goat cheese from Saône-et-Loire, in the Mâconnais.

entries.heading: Mâconnais
entries.what: A small cheese from Burgundy's Mâconnais, gained AOC in 2005.

entries.heading: Mafi (mafi; spontaneously fermented milk)
entries.what: a thick, spontaneously soured milk, the household fermented milk of Lesotho, named in Sesotho as mafi.

entries.heading: Mafi (Sesotho; sometimes called amasi)
entries.what: Fermented milk eaten with pap or on its own.

entries.heading: Mahón-Menorca (Queso Mahón; Menorcan Mahón)
entries.what: Menorca's protected cow-milk cheese, sold as soft, semi-cured or cured. Sold as "Mahón-Menorca" (protected name).

entries.heading: Mahón (Mahón-Menorca)
entries.what: Cow's-milk cheese from Menorca, orange-coloured from its rind treatment.

entries.heading: Majorero (Queso majorero; Queso Majorero DOP)
entries.what: A cylindrical goat cheese from Fuerteventura with a compact, creamy-to-semi-hard paste; mild when fresh, stronger and slightly spicy when cured.

entries.heading: Majorero (queso majorero)
entries.what: Hard goat's-milk cheese from Fuerteventura, Canary Islands.

entries.heading: Maroilles (Marolles; Vieux-Lille and Vieux Boulogne are variants)
entries.what: A soft washed-rind cow's cheese, AOC since 1976, named after the village of Maroilles; it has an orange-red rind and a strong smell. Sizes: standard about 13 cm square, 6 cm high, around 700 g; Sorbais (12–12.5 cm, 4 cm, 550 g), Mignon (11–

entries.heading: Maroilles (Marolles, Boulette d'Avesnes)
entries.what: A cow's-milk cheese from Picardy and Nord-Pas-de-Calais, named after the village of Maroilles; sold as rectangular blocks with a moist orange-red rind and strong smell.

entries.heading: Melichloro (μελίχλωρο; melipasto μελίπαστο)
entries.what: A traditional semi-hard cheese from Lemnos with a firm texture, rich taste and slightly sweet aroma; used in pasta, as a simple side, and for saganaki. The Lemnos article also names it alongside a yoghurt.

entries.heading: Melichloro (Μελίχλωρο Λήμνου; Lemnos and Chios)
entries.what: Local Lemnos cheese; Greek list also puts it under Χίου.

entries.heading: Metsovone (Μετσόβου / Metsovone; Metsovela, Foumarino, Boukovela are related Metsovo names)
entries.what: a smoked, stretched-curd cheese from the Aromanian village of Metsovo in the Pindus mountains of Epirus. It is the Metsovo cheese best known outside the area.

entries.heading: Metsovone (Μετσοβόνε; Π.Ο.Π.)
entries.what: Smoked cheese from Metsovo, Epirus, with Aromanian roots.

entries.heading: Metton
entries.what: The curd from which Cancoillotte is made.

entries.heading: Metton
entries.what: A runny cheese from Franche-Comté, mostly used as the base for cancoillotte.

entries.heading: Milchmischerzeugnisse (flavoured milk and milk-mix drinks)
entries.what: a legal term for products made of at least 70% dairy products and at most 30% other foods. Examples: Kakaotrunk, Erdbeermilch, whey-based milk-mix drinks, fruit yoghurt, drinking yoghurt, fruit buttermilk and fruit kefir.

entries.heading: Milk-mix products (Milchmischerzeugnisse, flavoured milk and yoghurt drinks)
entries.what: A product category the national dairy makes, defined as at least 70 percent dairy with at most 30 percent other ingredients. Typical examples in the German definition are cocoa drink, strawberry milk, drinking yoghurt and fruit kefir.

entries.heading: Milk punch
entries.what: cold drink of milk, brandy or whisky, sugar and vanilla, topped with nutmeg.

entries.heading: Ponche de leche (milk punch)
entries.what: a milk drink listed among Honduran drinks and sweets. Named only.

entries.heading: Mimolette (boule de Lille)
entries.what: A semi-hard, spherical, orange-coloured cheese originally from French Flanders around Lille; wheel about 2 kg. Young ones are soft; the extra-vieille (over 18 months) is very crumbly.

entries.heading: Mimolette (Boule de Lille, Vieux Hollande)
entries.what: A cheese produced around Lille, originally inspired by Dutch Edam.

entries.heading: Mishti doi (মিষ্টি দই; Bograr doi; Bogurar doi)
entries.what: sweetened fermented yoghurt from the Bengal region, sold as a famous Bogra sweet curd.

entries.heading: Mishti doi (মিষ্টি দই; mitha doi, meethi dahi)
entries.what: Sweet fermented curd from Bengal, popular in Bangladesh, West Bengal, Tripura and Assam's Barak Valley.

entries.heading: Mongolian milk skin (奶皮子, öröm)
entries.what: Rich fat skin from heated milk, a Mongolian dairy food; higher fat than ordinary milk, keeps longer.

entries.heading: Öröm (өрөм; urum; autumn clotted cream)
entries.what: A thick, foamy cream skimmed from boiled milk, mainly made in autumn (also summer per one source); eaten fresh, dried or frozen, and the base for butter.

entries.heading: Mont des Cats (Abbaye du Mont des Cats brand; La Bourle is a related lead)
entries.what: A trademark cheese made by the Trappist monks of the Abbaye du Mont-des-Cats, near Godewaersvelde in French Flanders (Nord). Made since 1826 on the abbey's land; the abbey buys milk from farms since 1970 and, since 2004, processes milk from

entries.heading: Mont des Cats
entries.what: Cheese made by monks of the Mont des Cats abbey in Nord, since 1890.

entries.heading: Monte Veronese (Monte Veronese DOP; Monte Veronese a latte intero; Monte Veronese d'allevo)
entries.what: A DOP cheese from the northern part of the Verona province (Lessinia and the Veronese Prealps). Two types: whole-milk (25–40 days) and partly skimmed "d'allevo" (aged).

entries.heading: Monte Veronese
entries.what: a PDO cheese from Veneto.

entries.heading: Queso de Murcia (Queso de Murcia DOP; queso de cabra murciano; other names: queso de Murcia fresco / curado)
entries.what: A fatty goat's-milk cheese from the Murcia region of south-east Spain, with a mild goat flavour and slight saltiness and acidity. The fresh type is unripened; the cured type is firm and white to light cream.

entries.heading: Murcia (queso de Murcia; Murcian cheese, goat)
entries.what: Goat's-milk cheese from Murcia; made as a fresh cheese and as a cured cheese.

entries.heading: Mutschli / Tomme du Valais (Mutschli, Tummeli, Tomme du Valais; Formagella related)
entries.what: A small semi-hard Swiss cheese, 0.5–4 kg (Valais Tomme usually 1–1.5 kg). The page links the name to the Romansh-speaking area.

entries.heading: Mutschli (Mutschli, Mutschli (Käse))
entries.what: A general term for small, usually mild cheeses rather than a strictly defined variety. Named as a Uri cheese in the Alpkäse article.

entries.heading: Neufchâtel (Neufchâtel AOC/AOP)
entries.what: a Normandy bloomy-rind cheese from the Bray country; the typical heart shape is sold as "cœur".

entries.heading: Neufchâtel
entries.what: A soft, slightly crumbly mould-ripened cheese from the Pays de Bray in Normandy, one of the oldest French cheeses; it resembles Camembert or Brie but is saltier and sharper.

entries.heading: Sheer chai (Afghan milk tea)
entries.what: tea with milk and sugar, drunk mostly in the morning and on special occasions; served with pastries and cookies.

entries.heading: Noon chai (Kashmiri pink tea; sheer chai)
entries.what: A pink, salty, milky tea from Kashmir, popular in Pakistan too.

entries.heading: Oštiepok (ovčí; Ostepek in review)
entries.what: Slovak sheep cheese; the review lists "Ostepek (sheep's milk)" on the Czech market.

entries.heading: Oštiepok (oštiepok; Slovak; cognate oscypek in Polish Goral areas)
entries.what: a Slovak smoked or unsmoked sheep or cow cheese made in mountain shepherd huts (salashe), shaped in hand-carved wooden moulds; the Wikipedia page lists it under stretched-curd cheeses.

entries.heading: Pampanella
entries.what: a cheese described on the disambiguation page as widespread in Abruzzo and Puglia.

entries.heading: Pampanella
entries.what: A fresh cheese, mildly flavoured, made in Puglia in the provinces of Taranto, Brindisi and Lecce; made since the 1700s on farmsteads (masserie). Named after the pampino or pampano fig leaf it is served on. A related goat cheese is made in A

entries.heading: Panna cotta (Italian-Eritrean)
entries.what: A cream dessert, listed among Italian-Eritrean dishes.

entries.heading: Panna cotta
entries.what: Italian dessert of sweetened cream, set with gelatine.

entries.heading: Pasteurised cow milk (factory)
entries.what: factory-pasteurised milk sold in retail. A three-region value-chain study sampled seven factories alongside raw milk from farmers and collectors.

entries.heading: Pasteurised cow milk (school supply)
entries.what: pasteurised milk supplied to primary schools in Maseru through the School Feeding Programme.

entries.heading: Patamulo (Pata de mulo)
entries.what: a named regional cheese, sold by several dairies in Teruel and Zaragoza.

entries.heading: Pata de mulo ("mule's leg")
entries.what: Sheep's-milk cheese from Tierra de Campos, Castile and León; aged version of Villalón cheese.

entries.heading: Pavé d'Auge (also called Carré d'Auge)
entries.what: a square Normandy cheese, about 12 cm a side, 6 cm thick, about 500 g.

entries.heading: Pavé d'Auge (Carré d'Auge, Pavé de Moyaux)
entries.what: A cow's-milk cheese of the historic Pays d'Auge, Normandy; names are AOC-style regional appellations.

entries.heading: Peanut punch (peanut milk drink; other names: peanut punch, peanut drink)
entries.what: A sweet Caribbean drink of peanuts or peanut butter, milk and sugar, often with spices.

entries.heading: Peanut punch (milk drink)
entries.what: a Caribbean drink of peanuts or peanut butter with milk, sugar and spices; in TT often sold in cartons and at punch carts.

entries.heading: Pecorino (pecorino marchigiano; pecorino del Vissano, historic)
entries.what: The regional pecorino, made across the whole region and most widely in the inland areas. The aged version is harder, with an oil-rubbed reddish rind. Visso and nearby areas historically used the now-rare sopravissana sheep; the cheese made

entries.heading: Pecorino (viterbese, ciociaro) (PAT)
entries.what: General pecorino from the Viterbo and Ciociaria traditions.

entries.heading: Pecorino della costa apuana (Apuan coast, La Spezia)
entries.what: a sheep's-milk pecorino of the Apuan coast, which reaches into La Spezia province.

entries.heading: Pecorino della Costa Apuana (Pecorino massese)
entries.what: pecorino from the Apuan coast, made with Massese sheep's milk.

entries.heading: Pecorino di Amatrice (PAT)
entries.what: Sheep pecorino from Amatrice (Rieti).

entries.heading: Pecorino di Amatrice
entries.what: a pecorino from Amatrice, Lazio.

entries.heading: Pecorino di Carmasciano
entries.what: a rare Irpinian sheep cheese from the Carmasciano hamlet, in the Ansanto valley.

entries.heading: Pecorino di Carmasciano
entries.what: a Campanian pecorino; PAT.

entries.heading: Pecorino di Filiano (sheep's milk; PDO)
entries.what: A hard-paste sheep's cheese from Basilicata, PDO since 2007, not pasteurised (en.wiki).

entries.heading: Pecorino di Filiano
entries.what: a hard pecorino from the Province of Potenza, Basilicata; PDO.

entries.heading: Pecorino di Osilo
entries.what: A pecorino named after the town of Osilo (Sassari province), listed among Sardinian cheeses.

entries.heading: Pecorino di Osilo
entries.what: a Sardinian pecorino; PDO.

entries.heading: Pecorino Sardo (Pecorino sardo; dolce and maturo)
entries.what: A DOP sheep cheese from the whole of Sardinia, in two types: dolce (ripened 20–60 days, 1–2.3 kg, white and soft with a sweet aroma) and maturo (over 2 months, 1.7–4 kg, straw-coloured with a sharper flavour and a rind darkening to brown).

entries.heading: Pecorino Sardo
entries.what: a firm sheep's-milk cheese from Sardinia, made from the local Sarda sheep.

entries.heading: Pecorino siciliano (picurinu)
entries.what: the most widespread cheese in Sicily; a hard sheep's-milk cheese, cylindrical with one slightly concave face, 4–12 kg per wheel.

entries.heading: Pecorino siciliano
entries.what: a Sicilian pecorino; PDO.

entries.heading: Pecorino umbro (ewe's milk, Umbria)
entries.what: A traditional pecorino from Umbrian farms. Made by small producers in the mountain and constrained areas of Umbria, under the name Pecorino umbro.

entries.heading: Pecorino umbro
entries.what: a pecorino from Umbria; dialect name Pecorino Subasio.

entries.heading: Pélardon
entries.what: A small goat cheese from the Cévennes and Languedoc, the "Pélardon des Cévennes" name is a sub-entry on the list page.

entries.heading: Pélardon
entries.what: A traditional goat's-milk cheese from the Cévennes (Languedoc-Roussillon), formerly paraldon or pélardou.

entries.heading: Peñamellera (Queso de Peñamellera)
entries.what: small artisan cheese made mainly in Peñamellera Alta, also in Peñamellera Baja.

entries.heading: Queso de Peñamellera
entries.what: Asturian cheese from Peñamellera.

entries.heading: Pérail
entries.what: A soft sheep cheese of the western southern Massif central.

entries.heading: Pérail
entries.what: A protected geographic indication sheep's-milk cheese made in the western part of the southern Massif central (Languedoc side).

entries.heading: Persillé de Tignes (tignard)
entries.what: farmhouse blue cheese from Tignes, Savoie (tarentaise valley); most production in a cooperative at Villaroger.

entries.heading: Persillé de Tignes (Tignard)
entries.what: A raw-milk cheese from Savoie made with goat and cow milk, named after Tignes in the Tarentaise valley.

entries.heading: Piave (Piave DOP; fresco, mezzano, vecchio, vecchio selezione oro, vecchio riserva)
entries.what: A DOP cheese named after the Piave river. The official product comes from the province of Belluno, Veneto. It is sold at five ages, from fresh to a grating cheese.

entries.heading: Piave
entries.what: a hard cooked-curd cheese from the Dolomites.

entries.heading: Pichtogalo Chanion (Πηχτόγαλο Χανίων; PDO)
entries.what: a soft cheese from the Chania prefecture of Crete, with yoghurt-like texture and a slightly sour taste.

entries.heading: Pichtogalo Chanion (Πηχτόγαλο Χανίων; Π.Ο.Π.)
entries.what: Chania (Crete) cheese; PDO.

entries.heading: Picodon
entries.what: a protected goat cheese of the Rhône-Alps and south; only part of it is in this region.

entries.heading: Picodon
entries.what: A goat's-milk cheese from the Rhône region of southern France; the name means "spicy" in Occitan.

entries.heading: Picón Bejes-Tresviso (Picón de Tresviso, queso picón de Bejes; nicknamed "Tres Leches")
entries.what: a cylindrical blue cheese from the Liébana valley, with a slightly spicy flavour and creamy blue-green veined paste; it weighs 0.7 to 2.8 kg.

entries.heading: Picón Bejes-Tresviso (Picón)
entries.what: Blue cheese from the Liébana valley in Cantabria, similar to Cabrales.

entries.heading: Pizza cheese (피자용 치즈; pizza cheese)
entries.what: A cheese produced by several Korean companies after pizza became popular in Korea.

entries.heading: Pizza cheese
entries.what: A cheese formulated for melting on pizza.

entries.heading: Ponche crema (ponche crema; Venezuelan origin, Trinidad and Tobago)
entries.what: a sweet, creamy drink served at Christmas and festive times in several Caribbean places

entries.heading: Ponche crema
entries.what: A cream liqueur from Venezuela, with a Christmas-season association; Trinidad and Tobago developed their own version (ponche de crème).

entries.heading: Port-Salut
entries.what: A trademark for a range of industrial pasteurised cheeses, now made in several European factories (owned by Bel Foodservice / Groupe Bel). Historically made by Trappist monks at Entrammes, Mayenne.

entries.heading: Port-Salut
entries.what: A semi-soft pasteurised cow's-milk cheese from Pays de la Loire, with an orange rind and mild flavour; originally made by Trappist monks at Port-du-Salut.

entries.heading: Potkæs (pot cheese)
entries.what: the Danish term for pot cheese.

entries.heading: Pot cheese (kuzeh; Persian پنیر کوزه; Kurdish پنیر کوپه / Pani Kupe)
entries.what: A traditional salty cheese from north-west Iran, named for the jar (kuzeh, "jug") in which it is buried for several weeks.

entries.heading: Provola (Provola)
entries.what: A provola listed for Calabria.

entries.heading: Provola (Sicilian)
entries.what: Provola dei Nebrodi, Provola delle Madonie, Provola ragusana, Provola siciliana and others from Sicily.

entries.heading: Provola affumicata
entries.what: a smoked stretched-curd cheese, a PAT product.

entries.heading: Provola affumicata (Campania)
entries.what: a smoked cow's-milk provola from Campania.

entries.heading: Provolone del Monaco (DOP)
entries.what: a large, melon-shaped aged stretched-curd cheese, the Agerola provolone; PDO.

entries.heading: Provolone del Monaco
entries.what: a PDO provolone from Campania.

entries.heading: Quartirolo Lombardo (Quartirolo Lombardo DOP)
entries.what: a soft cow's-milk cheese with Protected Designation of Origin status; production dates to the 10th century, originally seasonal (late summer, from milk of cows grazing on the third-cut grass), now year-round.

entries.heading: Quartirolo Lombardo
entries.what: a soft Lombard cheese, PDO.

entries.heading: Quesitos de Zuheros
entries.what: a small cheese from Zuheros, Córdoba province

entries.heading: Quesitos de Zuheros
entries.what: Small cheeses from Zuheros, Córdoba.

entries.heading: Queso Criollo (criollo cheese)
entries.what: a fatty, high-moisture cheese defined in the Argentine Food Code (article 626), with a compact, elastic paste and a few well-spread eyes.

entries.heading: Queso criollo (Taxco)
entries.what: A local cheese of Taxco, Guerrero.

entries.heading: Queso de Benabarre
entries.what: a goat cheese from Benabarre (Huesca), made on a family farm that began cheese-making in the 1990s.

entries.heading: Queso de Benabarre
entries.what: Aragonese cheese from Benabarre, Huesca.

entries.heading: Queso de Biescas
entries.what: a cheese named in the Aragón cheese lists; the Biescas autumn fair holds a cheese tasting (Cata Concurso de Quesos de Biescas) and the Jornadas de los Quesos de Aragón.

entries.heading: Queso de Biescas
entries.what: Aragonese cheese from Biescas, Huesca.

entries.heading: Queso de Fuente Palmera
entries.what: a cheese made near Fuente Palmera, Córdoba, in the Sierra Morena / Guadalquivir area

entries.heading: Queso de Fuente Palmera
entries.what: Andalusian cheese near Córdoba.

entries.heading: Queso de hoja (dominicano)
entries.what: A salted, mozzarella-like cheese whose name refers to its layered structure, which separates into peelable leaves ("hojas"). Listed in the Spanish cheese article as "dominicano".

entries.heading: Queso de hoja
entries.what: a cheese named in the highlands dish "Allullas con queso de hoja" (small sweet/savoury breads with leaf-cheese).

entries.heading: Queso de Las Alpujarras (Queso de la Alpujarra)
entries.what: a goat cheese of La Alpujarra, the mountain area south of Granada and west of Almería, in the Penibetic range.

entries.heading: Queso de las Alpujarras
entries.what: Cheese from the Alpujarras, Granada.

entries.heading: Queso de los Pedroches (Queso Pedroches)
entries.what: a cheese of Los Pedroches, the comarca of north Córdoba province.

entries.heading: Queso de los Pedroches
entries.what: Andalusian cheese, Los Pedroches, Córdoba.

entries.heading: Queso de Radiquero (Quesos de Radiquero cheeses)
entries.what: a family of artisan goat cheeses from Radiquero (Adahuesca, Huesca), founded in the late 1970s, known for creamy cheeses and award results.

entries.heading: Queso de Radiquero
entries.what: Aragonese cheese listed by name.

entries.heading: Queso de Sahún
entries.what: a cheese from Sahún (Huesca), in the Benasque valley; the guide lists the Benasqués dairy at Sahún.

entries.heading: Queso de Sahún
entries.what: Aragonese cheese from Sahún, Huesca.

entries.heading: Queso de Valdeón (Valdeón blue; León)
entries.what: a semi-soft blue cheese from Posada de Valdeón in the north-east of León province. Intensely blue, less sharp than Cabrales. Earlier local cheese made with goat's milk (en.wiki, pre-Roman origin claim).

entries.heading: Valdeón (queso de Valdeón)
entries.what: Blue cheese from the Valdeón valley in León, wrapped in maple or chestnut leaves before sale.

entries.heading: Queso Mozzarella (muzzarella, mussarela)
entries.what: a stretched-curd cheese defined in the Food Code.

entries.heading: Queso mozzarella (Peruvian mozzarella, cow's milk)
entries.what: Mozzarella made by Peruvian industry and small artisans; sold alongside fresh and matured cheeses.

entries.heading: Ragusano DOP (Ragusano; caciocavallo ragusano; cosacavaddu ragusano)
entries.what: a DOP cheese from the Iblean plateau in Ragusa, and partly Siracusa province; the Caciocavallo family's Ragusa version.

entries.heading: Ragusano
entries.what: a firm stretched-curd cheese from the whole milk of Modicana cows.

entries.heading: Raschera (Raschera DOP)
entries.what: PDO cheese from the Cuneo province; square or round wheels. The alpine type (d'alpeggio) is a Slow Food presidium.

entries.heading: Raschera
entries.what: a semi-hard cheese from the Cuneo area of Piedmont.

entries.heading: Raw cow's milk (fresh milk, unprocessed)
entries.what: milk drunk or sold raw or with minimal processing, moved through informal local value chains.

entries.heading: Raw cow's milk (no local name given in sources read)
entries.what: raw cow's milk sold in Libyan markets; the largest category in the market surveys.

entries.heading: Raw goat milk (sold at market)
entries.what: goat milk sold directly by sellers (Table 1 "Goat milk").

entries.heading: Raw goat milk (ħalib tal-mogħoż; fresh unpasteurised goat milk)
entries.what: Fresh goat milk drunk raw, as sold door to door in the towns and villages. Historically the commonest route of undulant fever (brucellosis) in Malta, the "Malta fever".

entries.heading: Reblochon (reblochon de Savoie; reblochon fermier)
entries.what: flat cylinder about 14 cm across, 450–550 g; petit reblochon 240–280 g.

entries.heading: Reblochon
entries.what: A soft washed-rind cheese from Haute-Savoie made from raw cow's milk; has its own AOC.

entries.heading: Red bean ice (紅豆冰)
entries.what: A cha chaan teng dessert of red bean with evaporated milk and ice.

entries.heading: Red bean ice (紅豆冰)
entries.what: a cold drink of red beans, evaporated milk and ice.

entries.heading: Red Leicester
entries.what: An English hard cheese originally made on farms in Leicestershire; named after Leicester or Leicestershire.

entries.heading: Red Leicester
entries.what: An English hard cheese similar to Cheddar but crumblier.

entries.heading: Requeijão (Requeijão cremoso / de corte / culinário)
