entries.what: a mildly salty spreadable cheese in three varieties: requeijão de corte (oldest, artisanal, solid), requeijão cremoso (most widespread, pasty), requeijão culinário (firmer, cottage-like, heat-stable).

entries.heading: Requeijão (requeijão; whey cheese)
entries.what: A Portuguese (and Brazilian) whey cheese, similar to ricotta, used for spreads.

entries.heading: Requeijão (requeijão de corte, requeijão cremoso, requeijão culinário, requeijão crioulo)
entries.what: Brazilian dairy product in two main forms. Requeijão de corte is an older, artisanal, solid, yellow product made from cow milk; common in Goiás, São Paulo, Minas Gerais and southern Bahia, predominant in North and Northeast. Requeijão cremo

entries.heading: Requeijão
entries.what: A salty, solid, white to yellowish dairy made from whey left over from cheese making, heated again. Up to 18% sheep or goat milk may be added to the whey. The page also calls it a type of cheese.

entries.heading: Ricota (Argentine ricotta)
entries.what: the fresh whey cheese known as ricota in Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay.

entries.heading: Ricota (Uruguayan ricotta)
entries.what: Ricotta is listed as dairy output in Uruguay and is used as the filling for sweet empanadas with raisins.

entries.heading: Ricotta di bufala campana (DOP, Lazio share)
entries.what: Buffalo-whey ricotta from the Mozzarella di bufala campana zone; the Lazio share is part of a multi-region PDO.

entries.heading: Ricotta di bufala campana (ricotta di bufala campana DOP)
entries.what: a fresh whey cheese made from buffalo whey, PDO.

entries.heading: Ricotta di pecora (Ricotta di pecora)
entries.what: Sheep's whey ricotta listed for Calabria.

entries.heading: Ricotta di pecora
entries.what: a sheep's-milk ricotta, typical of Sicily and other southern regions; widely used in Sicilian desserts.

entries.heading: Ricotta forte
entries.what: A soft, spreadable cheese from southern Italy, mainly Basilicata and Puglia, with a creamy, spicy and slightly bitter taste; made from whey and fermented by bacteria and yeasts, giving a strong aroma similar to aged pecorino.

entries.heading: Ricotta forte (whey cheese; fermented)
entries.what: A soft, spreadable whey cheese from southern Italy, especially Basilicata and Puglia, with a sharp, slightly bitter, strong aroma similar to long-aged pecorino.

entries.heading: Rigotte de Condrieu
entries.what: small goat cheese (4.2–5 cm across, 1.9–2.4 cm high) from the Pilat massif near Condrieu; AOC 2009, AOP 2013.

entries.heading: Rigotte de Condrieu
entries.what: A goat's-milk cheese from the Lyon region, named after the town of Condrieu.

entries.heading: Robiola (robbiola, robbiole; formagitt in Valle di Muggio)
entries.what: A small fresh cheese from the Sottoceneri, especially Valle di Muggio, where it was already made in the early 1900s and is now made across the canton

entries.heading: Robiola (Robiola di Roccaverano)
entries.what: soft cheese from the Langhe area, with many local forms.

entries.heading: Romadur (Romadour)
entries.what: originally Bavarian; sold and made in Czech Republic, with a yellow-orange smear.

entries.heading: Romadur
entries.what: A soft, stick-shaped cheese with a reddish, sticky rind; milder than Limburger. Originally Belgian; the German article cites Allgäu, where Carl Hirnbein introduced it in the 1830s.

entries.heading: Rompope (rompopo)
entries.what: a sweet, yellow, egg-and-milk drink. In Central America, especially El Salvador, Guatemala and Honduras, it is called rompopo; Salcajá (Guatemala) is named as a known version.

entries.heading: Rompope (Mexican eggnog-style milk drink)
entries.what: A yellow, emulsified drink of milk, egg yolk, sugar and vanilla, with rum. Cinnamon, nuts or strawberry are sometimes added. The Spanish word is said to derive from "rompón", and it is compared with eggnog.

entries.heading: Roncal (Queso de Roncal; Roncal cheese)
entries.what: The first Spanish cheese to receive a Denominación de Origen (1981), with EU PDO (DOP) status from 1996. Made only in the Valle de Roncal, Navarra, specifically in its seven villages of the Siete Villas association: Burgui, Garde, Isaba, Ro

entries.heading: Roncal (queso Roncal)
entries.what: Firm, creamy sheep's-milk cheese from the Roncal valley of Navarre.

entries.heading: Rotterdamsche Oude
entries.what: A trademarked (merk) Gouda-style cheese from the trader Velder, created by Rotterdam entrepreneurs as a "typical, traditional Rotterdam product"; reached the market around 2010 (the source flags this date as unverified).

entries.heading: Rotterdamsche Oude
entries.what: A trademarked long-aged hard Gouda, aged 36–100 weeks.

entries.heading: Saint Agur
entries.what: brand of Savencia Fromage & Dairy, made at Beauzac (Monts du Velay).

entries.heading: Saint Agur
entries.what: A blue cheese brand owned by Savencia, from the Monts du Velay, Auvergne (village of Beauzac).

entries.heading: Saint-marcellin
entries.what: small cheese of about 80 g; from the Dauphiné.

entries.heading: Saint-Marcellin
entries.what: A soft French cheese named after the town of Saint-Marcellin (Isère), from the former Dauphiné province.

entries.heading: Saint-nectaire (Saint-Nectaire)
entries.what: cylinder 20–24 cm (petit format 12–14 cm), from the Monts Dore and Cézallier volcanic grasslands.

entries.heading: Saint-Nectaire
entries.what: A cheese made in the Auvergne since at least the 17th century; once called "rye cheese" because it was matured on rye.

entries.heading: Sainte-Maure-de-Touraine (Sainte-Maure-de-Touraine; other names: Sainte-Maure)
entries.what: a truncated goat-milk log of about 250 g, grey-blue rind, creamy interior that dries and crumbles with age.

entries.heading: Sainte-Maure de Touraine
entries.what: A French goat cheese from Touraine (Indre-et-Loire), named after the town of Sainte-Maure-de-Touraine.

entries.heading: Salers (fromage de Salers)
entries.what: made April 15–November 15 on pastures; each farm its own; AOC 1961, AOP 1996 (intro) or 2003 (infobox); intangible heritage 2016.

entries.heading: Salers
entries.what: A semi-hard cheese from the volcanic Massif Central around Salers, in Cantal.

entries.heading: Salignun (Salignon, Salgnun)
entries.what: spicy ricotta-type cheese from Valle d'Aosta and northern Piemonte, especially Valsesia; P.A.T.

entries.heading: Salignon (Salignoun; Salignon di Valle d'Aosta)
entries.what: A spicy, creamy, fatty preparation made from leftover whey, enriched with milk or cream, mixed with grated toma, salt, pepper and chili (which turns it pinkish), and mountain herbs. Used to fill miasse (crispy cornmeal crêpes) and with pole

entries.heading: San Michali (Σαν Μιχάλη; Syros / Cyclades)
entries.what: named as a Cyclades cheese; no details found.

entries.heading: San Michali (Σαν Μιχάλη Σύρου; Π.Ο.Π. Syros)
entries.what: Cheese from Syros.

entries.heading: San Simón da Costa (Queixo San Simón da Costa)
entries.what: A DO cow's-milk cheese, pear-like in shape, rounded at the base and tapering at the top. Produced mainly in the Terra Chá comarca of Lugo province (Vilalba and nearby municipalities).

entries.heading: San Simón da Costa
entries.what: Smoked cow's-milk cheese from Galicia, the smoked counterpart to Tetilla.

entries.heading: Saudi Feta
entries.what: An Arabised version of Greek feta from Saudi Arabia; creamier and softer than Greek feta, and it does not crumble.

entries.heading: Saudi feta (Arabized feta, GCC cheese)
entries.what: An Arabized version of Greek feta, creamier and softer than the original and not crumbly; used as a spread and in salads. Described as popular in the GCC, with Saudi Arabia given as its origin.

entries.heading: Schiz
entries.what: A very fresh cow's-milk cheese of the Belluno province, a PAT product of Veneto. It is eaten warm.

entries.heading: Skúlamjólk (school milk)
entries.what: The same fresh milk in 250 ml packs, sold to schools for pupils' lunch boxes; MBM also funds a school-class support scheme with it.

entries.heading: School milk (นมโรงเรียน: raw, pasteurised, UHT)
entries.what: milk products that Thai schoolchildren drink. A 2026 study names raw, pasteurised and UHT school milk.

entries.heading: Schwyzer (Hartkäse) (Schwyzer Hartkäse; Schwyzer)
entries.what: A hard cheese of about 32–33 kg, aromatic and full-bodied, made in village dairies of the canton of Schwyz. Sold mainly regionally and in the Zurich area; about 730 tonnes a year.

entries.heading: Schwyzer (Hartkäse)
entries.what: full-fat hard cheese, close to Gruyère but smoother, made in several valley dairies in Canton Schwyz.

entries.heading: Seirass di latte (Seirass, Sairass, Ricotta piemontese)
entries.what: traditional ricotta-like cheese made across Piemonte.

entries.heading: Seirass (Sérass / Seras)
entries.what: Piedmont whey cheese with sub-types del Fen, di siero di pecora; Seras in Aosta Valley since 1267.

entries.heading: Selles-sur-Cher (Selles-sur-Cher)
entries.what: a flat truncated-cone goat cheese of about 150 g with a very thin dark blue-grey rind dusted with charcoal ash.

entries.heading: Selles-sur-Cher
entries.what: A French goat-milk cheese from Centre-Val de Loire; named after the commune of Selles-sur-Cher, where it was first made in the 19th century.

entries.heading: Shaneeneh (شنينة, shanina)
entries.what: A salty-sour aged goat-milk yogurt, served cold; the Jordanian cuisine article presents it as a drink.

entries.heading: Shanina (Shineena; Arabic script not given in source)
entries.what: A homemade fermented yoghurt beverage drunk daily in Iraq. Iraqi shanina has garlic added, which the review says is unique to Iraq among the versions made in the region (Ayran in Turkey, Doogh in Iran).

entries.heading: Shanklish (شنكليش, شنغليش; shankleesh, chancliche, sorke, eddesh)
entries.what: A pungent, aged cheese made from fermented yogurt curd, shaped into balls and coated in za'atar, sumac, thyme, Aleppo pepper or chili. Eaten as a table or mezze cheese.

entries.heading: Shanklish (شنكليش; also shankleesh, chanclich, sorke/sürke, surke, eddesh)
entries.what: A Levantine cheese made from strained, fermented yogurt curd, shaped into balls and aged. Syria's coastal plain around Tartus is praised for it, and a Syrian shanklish set a Guinness record for heaviest piece (2008).

entries.heading: Shishbarak (ششبرك)
entries.what: dumplings cooked with jameed

entries.heading: Shishbarak (شيش برك)
entries.what: small dough dumplings cooked in a yoghurt sauce; a Palestinian dish listed on Wikipedia.

entries.heading: Silter (Silter DOP)
entries.what: a hard cheese from Val Camonica and the Province of Brescia, made in summer at high alpine pastures (malghe), with EU PDO since 2015.

entries.heading: Silter
entries.what: a PDO cheese from Lombardy (Silter della Val Camonica).

entries.heading: Smažený sýr (fried cheese, smažák)
entries.what: Czech and Slovak fried cheese dish, served with tartar sauce and potatoes or bread.

entries.heading: Vyprážaný syr (vyprážaný syr, smažený syr; Slovak fried cheese)
entries.what: a Slovak fried cheese, listed on the Slovak cuisine page as vyprážaný syr (also smažený syr).

entries.heading: Smen (سمن)
entries.what: Aged, salted, fermented butter used in Moroccan, Algerian and Tunisian cooking; aged smen is said to taste like blue cheese.

entries.heading: Smen (samn, samna; also sman, semn, semneh, samneh, sminn)
entries.what: Salted, fermented clarified butter, aged until it develops a strong, blue-cheese-like aroma. The older it is, the more valued.

entries.heading: Smen (d'hen; salted fermented butter)
entries.what: Salted, fermented butter, stored for months, used as a seasoning. Found in Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia and Yemen.

entries.heading: Smoked Cheese (Kurashima Dairy)
entries.what: A cheese slowly smoked over cherry wood, individually wrapped, from Kurashima Dairy Co., Ltd., Hokkaido.

entries.heading: Smoked cheese (La Joya, Veracruz)
entries.what: A smoked pressed cheese from a small area around La Joya, Veracruz; served with ham, chili, epazote and jalapeños.

entries.heading: Soft serve (ソフトクリーム, sofuto kurīmu)
entries.what: Soft-serve milk-based frozen dessert from a commercial mix (powder or liquid), dispensed from a soft-serve freezer. Commonly sold at dairy-farm shops.

entries.heading: Soft serve
entries.what: Ice cream with much more air, dispensed from a spigot into a cone or dish.

entries.heading: Speiseeis (ice cream), Austrian types: Vollmilcheis, Magermilcheis, Topfeneis, Magertopfeneis
entries.what: named ice cream types in the Austrian Lebensmittelkodex (Kapitel B2): Vollmilcheis (at least 2.1 % milk fat, about 60 % whole milk), Magermilcheis, Topfeneis, Magertopfeneis, Nusseis, Oberseiscreme and Málaga-Eis (with wine)

entries.heading: Speiseeis (ice cream: Cremeeis, Eiscreme, Rahmeis, Milcheis, Quarkeis, Spaghettieis, Eis am Stiel)
entries.what: German legal categories with minimum milk content: Cremeeis at least 50% milk and egg; Eiscreme at least 10% milk fat; Fruchteiscreme at least 8% milk fat; Rahmeis/Sahneeis at least 18% milk fat; Milcheis at least 70% milk; "-Eis" from a mi

entries.heading: Sperrin Blue
entries.what: A blue cheese from Dart Mountain Cheese, County Londonderry.

entries.heading: Sperrin Blue (Dart Mountain Cheese, Co. Londonderry)
entries.what: Blue cheese from Dart Mountain Cheese, Co. Londonderry.

entries.heading: Spressa delle Giudicarie
entries.what: A DOP cheese from the Giudicarie area and Val Rendena.

entries.heading: Spressa delle Giudicarie
entries.what: a PDO cheese from Trentino.

entries.heading: Squacquerone di Romagna
entries.what: A fresh, creamy, soft cow's-milk DOP cheese from Romagna (provinces of Ravenna, Forlì-Cesena and Rimini). Mainly used to fill piadina and cappelletti.

entries.heading: Squacquerone di Romagna
entries.what: a spreadable, creamy fresh cheese with an ivory colour and a sweet-sour, lactic taste.

entries.heading: Staka (Στάκα)
entries.what: a Cretan sour cream from spontaneously fermented sheep (or sheep and goat) milk.

entries.heading: Staka (Cretan buttery cream)
entries.what: a buttery cream from Crete, mixed with flour and served with poached or fried eggs in the dish "staka me ayga".

entries.heading: Stichelton
entries.what: An English blue cheese made in small batches at a dairy in Cuckney, on the northern edge of Sherwood Forest, Nottinghamshire.

entries.heading: Stichelton
entries.what: An English blue cheese similar to Stilton, made from unpasteurised milk.

entries.heading: Stinking Bishop
entries.what: A smooth, creamy English semi-soft cheese made at Hunts Court Farm.

entries.heading: Stinking Bishop
entries.what: An English washed-rind cheese.

entries.heading: Stolwijker (Goudse boerenkaas from Stolwijk and Haastrecht)
entries.what: The farmhouse Gouda made on farms in the region around Stolwijk and Haastrecht in the Krimpenerwaard, sold under this name.

entries.heading: Stolwijker
entries.what: The name under which farm-made Goudse boerenkaas from the Krimpenerwaard (near Stolwijk and Haastrecht) is sold.

entries.heading: Stosuppe (Milchsuppe, milk soup)
entries.what: an Austrian milk soup, a meat-free fasting dish

entries.heading: Milchsuppe (milk soup)
entries.what: a dish that is now mostly sweet and often served to children; formerly it could be a savoury meal.

entries.heading: Stosuppe (sour-milk soup, Austria)
entries.what: a simple Austrian soup of sour milk, sour cream, water and flour; known in Bavaria as Herbstmilchsuppe and in Poland as Polewka.

entries.heading: Stracciata
entries.what: a fresh stretched-curd cheese from Molise (PAT).

entries.heading: Stracciata (stracciata di Agnone / stracciata molisana; Italian "stracciata")
entries.what: A fresh cow's-milk cheese from Molise, Italy. The Italian Wikipedia article says the Pope sources it from a Molise dairy and that it is an important reference for the Pope's menu and for Vatican City.

entries.heading: Stracciatella (stracciatella di bufala)
entries.what: A fresh dairy product from southern Italy, particularly Puglia, made by mixing shredded stretched-curd cheese with fresh cream. It is essentially the filling of burrata served on its own.

entries.heading: Stracciatella
entries.what: fresh cheese of shredded stretched mozzarella curd, mixed with cream; the filling of burrata.

entries.heading: Sulguni (Sulquni; Georgian; listed as popular in Azerbaijan)
entries.what: A Georgian cheese from Samegrelo, named in the Azerbaijani popular cheese list.

entries.heading: Sulguni (სულგუნი; სულუგუნი; Mingrelian სელეგინი; also ქართული "მეგრული სულგუნი", "სვანური სულგუნი" in Georgian Wikipedia)
entries.what: A flat disc of brined cheese, sour and moderately salty, with an elastic, dimpled texture; one of Georgia's best-known cheeses, often deep-fried and served in wedges.

entries.heading: Sussex Slipcote
entries.what: A fresh sheep's cheese from High Weald Dairy, West Sussex, England; made since the Middle Ages according to the source; bronze award at the 2008 British Cheese Awards.

entries.heading: Sussex Slipcote
entries.what: A fresh ewe's-milk cheese from West Sussex.

entries.heading: Swaledale
entries.what: A hard cheese made in Richmond, Swaledale, North Yorkshire, by the Swaledale Cheese Company (founded 1987 by David and Mandy Reed; original recipe from Mrs Longstaff).

entries.heading: Swaledale
entries.what: A hard cheese from Richmond, Swaledale, North Yorkshire.

entries.heading: Swiss cheese (queso suizo; imported, used in the sandwich cubano)
entries.what: Imported Swiss-style cheese used as the melted layer in the Cuban sandwich (sandwich cubano), pressed with roast pork, ham, pickles and mustard.

entries.heading: Swiss cheese (North America) (American Swiss; Emmental-type)
entries.what: Any variety that resembles Emmental, a yellow, medium-hard cheese from the Emmental area of Switzerland; the term is generic and does not mean the cheese is made in Switzerland.

entries.heading: Ta komart (Tuareg local name, Latin spelling as in source; Tamasheq script not sourced; other names: none found)
entries.what: a Tuareg cheese named in the Wikipedia article on the Tuareg, alongside tona (a thick yogurt) and akh (milk).

entries.heading: Ta komart (Tamasheq; "ta komart")
entries.what: A cheese made from goat and camel milk, named as a Tuareg food in the Tuareg people article.

entries.heading: Teh C (teh si; Malay "teh C")
entries.what: A milk tea made with unsweetened evaporated milk; common in Malaysia and listed in Brunei's drinks.

entries.heading: Teh-C (tea with evaporated milk)
entries.what: a variant of teh tarik made with unsweetened evaporated milk instead of condensed milk.

entries.heading: Teleme (tele, Ru теле)
entries.what: a soft, curd-like cheese; eurasia.travel compares it to cottage cheese.

entries.heading: Teleme (Turkish listing)
entries.what: Named in Template:Turkish cheeses; the Wikipedia article covers the cheese generally, not its Turkish production.

entries.heading: Tête de Moine (Tête de Moine AOP; Mönch-kopf in German)
entries.what: A cylindrical raw-milk cow's cheese from the Bernese Jura and the canton of Jura, known for being shaved into rosettes with a girolle rather than sliced.

entries.heading: Tête de Moine
entries.what: cylindrical Swiss cheese, its name means "monk's head"; originally made by canons at Bellelay Abbey.

entries.heading: Tetilla (Queixo de Tetilla; Queixo Tetilla)
entries.what: A cow's-milk cheese from southeast A Coruña province, with DOP status. Breast-shaped pieces of about 1 kg.

entries.heading: Tetilla (queso de tetilla)
entries.what: Small conical Galician cheese whose name means "small breast", for its nipple-like top.

entries.heading: Teviotdale (Teviotdale; cow's milk hard)
entries.what: A full-fat (at least 48%) hard cheese from Jersey cows' milk, made around Teviotdale on the Scotland–England border within 90 km of Peel Fell in the Cheviot Hills; cylindrical, white-coated, smooth yellow paste, salty.

entries.heading: Teviotdale
entries.what: A hard cheese from the Teviotdale border region of Scotland and England.

entries.heading: Toma piemontese (Toma piemontese DOP)
entries.what: PDO round toma with flat faces, 15–35 cm across, 1.8–8 kg, from high valleys and mountains.

entries.heading: Toma piemontese
entries.what: a Piedmontese toma with many local forms; toma di capra is goat's milk from Piedmont and Lombardy.

entries.heading: Tome des Bauges (Tomme des Bauges)
entries.what: cylinder 18–20 cm, 3–5 cm high, 1.1–1.4 kg; AOC 2002, AOP 2007, mountain protection 1993.

entries.heading: Tomme des Bauges
entries.what: A raw-milk cow's cheese from the Bauges massif in Savoie; name derives from "toma", a Savoyard word for cheese made in the high pastures.

entries.heading: Tome fraîche (Cantal tomme fraîche, IGP 2023)
entries.what: IGP since 23 October 2023; from the curd of Laguiole, Cantal or Salers production (Aubrac and Haute-Auvergne).

entries.heading: Tome fraîche
entries.what: A fresh-curd-style tomme of the Aubrac, made from the Laguiole, Cantal or Salers process before salting.

entries.heading: Tomme de Montagne (tomme d'Auvergne)
entries.what: cylindrical tomme, about 4.5 cm high and 17.5–20 cm across.

entries.heading: Tomme de Montagne (Tomme d'Auvergne)
entries.what: A cow's-milk tomme from Auvergne, historically from the Loire and Puy-de-Dôme.

entries.heading: Tomme de Savoie (Tomme de Savoie IGP)
entries.what: tomme of about 1.6 kg; IGP in the EU since 1996.

entries.heading: Tomme de Savoie
entries.what: An upland tomme from Savoy: mild, semi-firm, beige paste under a thick brownish-grey rind.

entries.heading: Tomme des Pyrénées
entries.what: A tomme from the Pyrénées, named in the 2024 regional contest.

entries.heading: Tomme des Pyrénées
entries.what: A Pyrenean tomme in several varieties, fruity and slightly tangy.

entries.heading: Tomme du Jura
entries.what: A pressed cheese from the Jura mountains, mostly sold locally.

entries.heading: Tomme du Jura
entries.what: A cow's-milk tomme from the Jura mountains in Franche-Comté; circulates mostly locally.

entries.heading: Torta del Casar (torta del Casar; Spanish)
entries.what: a sheep's-milk cheese curdled with wild cardoon pistils; spreadable and eaten on bread.

entries.heading: Torta del Casar
entries.what: Creamy sheep's-milk cheese from the Casar area of Extremadura, eaten by scooping out the soft centre.

entries.heading: Tosela (Tosèla, Tosella)
entries.what: A fresh cheese originally made in mountain pastures (malga) from small milkings. Usually grilled; can be breaded and fried or toasted.

entries.heading: Tosella (Tosela in Trentino)
entries.what: A fresh cow's-milk cheese made in Trentino-Alto Adige and in Veneto. Veneto version is a PAT product named "Tosella".

entries.heading: Trappe de Timadeuc (Trappiste de Timadeuc; Timanoix variant)
entries.what: an industrial, pasteurised cow's-milk cheese of about 18–20 cm diameter, 4–5 cm thick, about 1.8 kg, rind fine and straw-yellow, paste ivory and fairly elastic.

entries.heading: Trappe de Timadeuc (Abbaye de Timadeuc)
entries.what: Trappist cheeses from the Timadeuc abbey in Brittany: "Trappe de Timadeuc" and "Le Timanoix" (affined in nut liqueur).

entries.heading: Tre Valli
entries.what: A Trentino cheese named after three valleys. PAT.

entries.heading: Tre Valli
entries.what: Local cheese name from the Pordenone area ("Tre Valli" suggests three valleys).

entries.heading: Trèfle
entries.what: a cheese named for Eure-et-Loir and Loir-et-Cher.

entries.heading: Trèfle
entries.what: Named in the list of French cheeses; the list ties it to Sarthe and Pays de la Loire among other regions.

entries.heading: Tricorne de Marans
entries.what: A triangular cheese from the town of Marans, Charente-Maritime (infobox also lists Vendée).

entries.heading: Tricorne de Marans
entries.what: A soft cheese from Charente-Maritime, shaped like a three-cornered hat; can be eaten fresh or aged.

entries.heading: Trifolait
entries.what: A raclette-style cheese made in Valais and introduced in 2017, made from a blend of cow, sheep and goat milk.

entries.heading: Trifolait
entries.what: raclette-type cheese from Valais made since 2017.

entries.heading: Tsalafouti Karpenisiou (Τσαλαφούτι Καρπενησίου, ΠΟΠ)
entries.what: a PDO cheese named for Karpenisi (Evrytania).

entries.heading: Tsalafouti Karpenisiou (Τσαλαφούτι Καρπενησίου; Π.Ο.Π.)
entries.what: Karpenisi cheese; PDO.

entries.heading: Tyrogiliata of Agrinio (Τυρογιλιάτα Αγρινίου; tyrogiliata)
entries.what: A local cheese from Agrinio, the main town of Aetolia-Acarnania

entries.heading: Tyrogiliata (Τυρογιλιάτα)
entries.what: a cheese named on the list page with the region Agrinio.

entries.heading: UHT (long-life) milk
entries.what: shelf-stable milk sold in Guatemala. Guatemala has its own UHT milk factories, and about half of the UHT milk consumed is imported from Costa Rica.

entries.heading: UHT (shelf-stable) milk
entries.what: Shelf-stable milk, sold in small pouches.

entries.heading: Vacherin Fribourgeois AOP (Vacherin Fribourgeois; Freiburger Vacherin)
entries.what: A Swiss cheese from the canton of Fribourg, with several varieties under one AOP.

entries.heading: Vacherin Fribourgeois
entries.what: Swiss semi-hard cheese from Canton Fribourg, with six varieties; key ingredient in some fondue recipes.

entries.heading: Valençay (Valençay; Pyramide de Valençay)
entries.what: a soft goat cheese of about 220 g (a 110 g size also exists), coated in food-grade vegetable charcoal and grey-blue rind.

entries.heading: Valençay
entries.what: An unpasteurised goat-milk cheese from the Berry (Indre), with a truncated pyramid shape.

entries.heading: Valtellina Casera (Valtellina Casera DOP)
entries.what: a cheese from the Province of Sondrio, dating to the 16th century, used in Valtellina cooking, especially pizzoccheri (buckwheat pasta) and sciatt fritters.

entries.heading: Valtellina Casera
entries.what: a PDO cheese from Valtellina, Lombardy.

entries.heading: Vastedda della Valle del Belice (vastedda; vastedda del Belìce)
entries.what: a fresh stretched-curd cheese from the Belice valley, traditionally a summer cheese made now year-round.

entries.heading: Vastedda (Vastedda della Valle del Belice; Vastedda palermitana)
entries.what: a Sicilian cheese; the article opened covers mainly the bread and the fried version used in pani câ meusa.

entries.heading: Vezzena (Vezzena di Lavarone)
entries.what: A granular, yellowish semi-fat cheese with a slightly bitter, spicy flavour; three ages (mezzano, vecchio, stravecchio).

entries.heading: Vezzena (Vèzzena; Vezzena di Lavarone sapori di malga)
entries.what: A cheese made mostly on the Vezzena plateau in Trentino, with a part of Vicenza province (Enego) in Veneto. It is a PAT product; the Lavarone version is a Slow Food presidium. A DOP application was filed in 2005 but not granted at the time

entries.heading: Viili (viili; fil in Swedish)
entries.what: A mesophilic fermented milk. Left unmixed it is "long" (ropy) in texture. Surface growth of Geotrichum candidum gives a velvet-like skin. English Wikipedia's list says it is originally from Sweden and "a Finnish specialty".

entries.heading: Viili
entries.what: A fermented milk with a ropy, "long" texture when left unstirred and a velvet-like surface from a fungus. Listed as Nordic in origin; most common in Finland and Sweden. The fermented-milk comparison lists it as originally from Sweden and as

entries.heading: Vlaflip
entries.what: A 1963 product combining fruit syrup, yoghurt and vla (custard), created to improve the image of vla.

entries.heading: Vlaflip
entries.what: A 1963 combination of fruit syrup, yoghurt and vla, in one dessert.

entries.heading: Wasserbüffelmilch (water buffalo milk)
entries.what: buffalo milk has about 8% fat, twice the fat of cow milk, and a longer shelf life. Milk breeds (Murrah, Nili-Ravi, Mehsana, Italian Mediterranean) are rising in number.

entries.heading: Water buffalo milk (susu kerbau, fresh)
entries.what: Buffalo milk produced on farms in Peninsular Malaysia; the study describes its composition and safety.

entries.heading: Wensleydale
entries.what: A medium cheese with a slight honey aroma; now mostly made in large commercial creameries across the UK.

entries.heading: Wensleydale
entries.what: A cheese from Wensleydale, North Yorkshire, with a slight honey aroma.

entries.heading: West African soft cheese (WASC; wagashi, wagasi, warankasi family; the local Burkina name is not confirmed in my sources)
entries.what: A soft white cheese traditionally made across West Africa. The review names Burkina Faso among the countries where it is made, citing O'Connor (1993), and notes it is common to most West African countries.

entries.heading: West African soft cheese (WASC; wagashi / wagasi / warankasi family)
entries.what: A family of West African soft cheeses that share a name root and a process across many countries. The review lists Togo among the countries where it is produced, but gives no Togolese local name and no Togo-specific description. The Togo-sp

entries.heading: Yakult (ヤクルト)
entries.what: A sweetened probiotic milk drink from Yakult Honsha, Tokyo, fermented with Lacticaseibacillus casei Shirota.

entries.heading: 야쿠르트 (Yakult; drinkable lactic-acid drink)
entries.what: Korea Yakult (한국야쿠르트, founded 1969) launched 야쿠르트 in Korea in 1969 under a technical tie-up with Yakult Honsha. Sold door to door through 야쿠르트 아줌마 from August 1971.

entries.heading: Yuenyeung (鴛鴦)
entries.what: Coffee mixed with Hong Kong-style milk tea. Traditional Chinese medicine treats coffee and tea as opposites, so mixing them is considered a balance.

entries.heading: Yuenyeung (鴛鴦; coffee and milk tea mix)
entries.what: a mix of brewed coffee and Hong Kong-style milk tea, served hot or iced.

entries.heading: Zamorano (queso zamorano; Zamora)
entries.what: hard Spanish sheep cheese from the province of Zamora, with a zigzag pattern on the rind, comparable to Manchego in taste and look.

entries.heading: Zamorano (queso zamorano)
entries.what: Hard sheep's-milk cheese from Zamora, Castile and León, dark from oil-rubbed rind.

entries.heading: Zebda (fresh butter)
entries.what: Fresh, unpreserved butter used in everyday cooking, the counterpart of smen.

entries.heading: Zebda (zebda beldia; artisanal butter)
entries.what: The fat fraction separated from rayeb by churning, described as an artisanal butter with a short shelf life.

entries.heading: Žinčica (žinčice; sheep whey drink)
entries.what: A kefir-like drink made as a by-product of brynza (sheep cheese). Named Slovak žinčica and Polish żętyca; the word comes from Romanian jîntiţa.

entries.heading: Žinčica (žinčica; žincica; Zyntyca in Goralic; Żętyca in Polish; Jintiță in Romanian)
entries.what: A sour drink made from the whey left after sheep-milk cheese (bryndza) is made. Fermented by lactic bacteria (Lactobacillus casei, L. plantarum, Lactococcus lactis, Leuconostoc mesenteroides, per the English article). Traditionally served i

entries.heading: Zrig (milk or yoghurt drink with roasted maize flour or yoghurt)
entries.what: a rich, sweet, refreshing drink served at iftar.

entries.heading: Zrig (زريق, زرق)
entries.what: A drink made by mixing soured milk (lait caillé) with milk or water, plus sugar. Served to guests with mint tea, as a breakfast or daytime drink, and at iftar during Ramadan.

entries.heading: a+ (formerly Súrgað Mjólk, soured milk with Acidophilus)
entries.what: A soured milk product, renamed a+ in 2026 to stress its Acidophilus cultures. Eaten at breakfast, as a snack, or in baking. Per 100 g: 49 kcal, 3.3 g protein, 1.5 g fat. Sopi and Summarskál also carry Acidophilus cultures. Packaging has "Fl

entries.heading: Aarts (aarts; Cyrillic spelling not found in sources)
entries.what: A semi-solid curd drained from yoghurt. Kept cool or frozen and eaten, or boiled into a hot drink; also the base for khuruud.

entries.heading: Aarts (аарц; curd)
entries.what: The soft, pressed curd that is the base for aaruul; also eaten, frozen, or boiled into a hot drink in winter and put into tea.

entries.heading: Āb havīj bastani (آب هویج بستنی; carrot ice cream float)
entries.what: Carrot juice with ice cream as a float, garnished with cinnamon, nutmeg or other spices; listed under Iranian cuisine.

entries.heading: Abbaye de Belloc
entries.what: A Basque/Béarn sheep's-milk cheese from Belloc abbey, Pyrénées-Atlantiques; an Ossau-Iraty cheese under AOC.

entries.heading: Abbey Cheese Company (Abbey Blue Brie, Abbey Smoked Brie, St Canice, Paddy Jack)
Abertam (Abertamský sýr)
entries.what: irregular ball with a thin yellow-orange rind; table or melting cheese.

entries.heading: Ábrystir (colostrum set custard)
entries.what: A traditional Icelandic dish, classed as spónamatur (food eaten with a spoon), made from colostrum. Surplus ewe colostrum was used in the sheep-milking era.

entries.heading: ÅCA butter (Åland butter)
entries.what: Butter made by the ÅCA dairy, sold in supermarkets, used by restaurants, and exported to mainland Finland, where it is described as creamy. It is also spread on black bread, which the aland.travel page recommends with cheese.

entries.heading: ÅCA milk (Ålandsmejeriet ÅCA, including organic milk)
entries.what: The milk sold by ÅCA (Ålandsmejeriet), the islands' cooperative dairy, in all supermarkets. Most restaurants use ÅCA as their main dairy supplier. The range includes organic milk.

entries.heading: Achocolatado (Toddy, Nescau)
entries.what: Chocolate powder dissolved in milk to make a chocolate milk drink. Brands: Toddy and Nescau. Powder contains about 70% sucrose and 30% cocoa; no milk powder "for conservation reasons"; may include glucose, malt extract, vitamins and mineral

entries.heading: Acidified and cultured milk (US standards)
entries.what: US standardised acidified milk and cultured milk products.

entries.heading: Ädelost
entries.what: Swedish blue-green mould cheese, described as a Swedish version of Roquefort.

entries.heading: Adobera
entries.what: A cheese named as derived from queso fresco; sold in Guerrero markets.

entries.heading: Adyghe cheese (адыгейский сыр; Adyghe матэкъуае; also черкесский сыр)
entries.what: Mild, lactic-acid-flavoured fresh cheese from the Republic of Adygea, named after the Adyghe people; the name is protected to Adygea.

entries.heading: Æbleskiver (Danish pancake balls)
entries.what: fried round cakes made of wheat flour and a liquid of buttermilk, milk or cream, with eggs, sugar, salt; served with jam and icing sugar.

entries.heading: Afyon manda yoğurdu (Afyon water buffalo yoghurt)
entries.what: a yoghurt from the Afyon region's water buffalo, with a GI application listed in the review.

entries.heading: Äggost (egg and milk curd dish)
entries.what: A typical Bohuslän dish made from milk and eggs, with vinegar, filmjölk or gräddfil, cooked until it curdles and then drained in a star-shaped mould. Historically a feast-food on smörgåsbord or breakfast; now mainly a dessert with sugar, ci

entries.heading: Aghoughlou
entries.what: A cheese from Kabylie made by curdling with fig latex, eaten fresh.

entries.heading: Agrì di Valtorta (PAT)
entries.what: a fresh, delicate, soft cheese from the Alta Valle Brembana, Province of Bergamo; Slow Food presidium per the milanofree table.

entries.heading: Aguadulce con leche (sugar-cane drink with milk)
entries.what: Aguadulce, a sweetened drink, made with or without milk.

entries.heading: Aho
entries.what: Named with Golot and Telli as a traditional Black Sea cheese; well known for its unique flavour and artisanal method.

entries.heading: Aiguille d'Orcières
entries.what: a mild cow's-milk cheese of the Champsaur.

entries.heading: Airan / Ayran (айран)
entries.what: Cold salty yoghurt drink of Turkic, Caucasian and Balkan peoples; Russian name айран, with Kalmyk/Mongolic-influenced variant chalap/shalap; Cossack variant iryan made from suzma.

entries.heading: Ais kacang (milk-topped shaved-ice dessert)
entries.what: A shaved-ice dessert topped with syrups, beans and milk.

entries.heading: Aisy cendré
entries.what: A soft cow's-milk cheese rolled in vine-shoot ash, named after Aisy (Aisy-sous-Thil or Aisy-sur-Armançon).

entries.heading: Aitim tat (ไอติมตัด)
entries.what: rectangular ice cream bars in various flavours, sliced by the vendor. Popular around 1986.

entries.heading: Akasan (AK 100)
entries.what: A thick, sweet corn drink with anise, vanilla and cinnamon. Served warm or cold, often at breakfast; also eaten as a dessert.

entries.heading: Akh (goat and camel milk, Tuareg)
entries.what: the common dairy foods of the Tuareg, called akh.

entries.heading: Aklak (аклак)
entries.what: A curd made by thickening milk with sour milk.

entries.heading: Al-rashoof (الرشوف)
entries.what: a winter meal of wheat flour, lentils and yoghurt

entries.heading: Åland pancake (Ålandspannkaka; Swedish: Ålandspannkaka; English: Åland pancake)
entries.what: An oven-baked semolina pancake flavoured with cardamom, eaten warm or cold with prune jam and whipped cream. Popular across the islands, especially with cycling tourists.

entries.heading: Åland Special Cheese (Åland Special Cheese; ÅCA dairy product)
entries.what: An ÅCA cheese that won a gold medal in a Finnish cheese-making competition.

entries.heading: Aletria dourada (golden aletria)
entries.what: A sweet made with aletria pasta, condensed milk and eggs. The standard aletria doce uses sugar and eggs, not milk.

entries.heading: Algunder Bauernkäse halbfett (Formaggio contadino semigrasso di Lagundo)
entries.what: A semi-fat farm cheese from Lagundo. PAT.

entries.heading: Allegretto (La Sarre, Abitibi, Quebec)
entries.what: A sheep's-milk cheese from the Abitibi region of Quebec, where the cold, northern climate is said to give the grass more sugar and sweeter milk.

entries.heading: Allgäuer Bergkäse
entries.what: A mountain cheese from the Allgäu, with loaves smaller and lower than Emmentaler's; ripened at least four months, flavour mild-aromatic and nutty, stronger with age.

entries.heading: Allgäuer Emmentaler
entries.what: The Allgäu version of Emmentaler, with about 45% fat in dry matter; at least 3 months ripening under its rules.

entries.heading: Allgäuer Weißlacker
entries.what: A rindless, pale, slightly crumbly semi-hard cheese invented in 1874 in Wertach, southern Allgäu.

entries.heading: Almendras de leche (Nariño)
entries.what: Sweets made from milk and cinnamon from Nariño.

entries.heading: Almond milk (not an animal milk)
entries.what: almond milk offered to a guest at someone's home in Libya.

entries.heading: Alouda (alouda; milk drink)
entries.what: A sweet, cold drink made with milk, tukmaria (basil seeds) and slices of coloured agar-agar jelly. The source says it comes in almond and vanilla flavours.

entries.heading: Alouette (Alouette Crème de Brie)
entries.what: A brand of French-style cheeses made by the French company Savencia Fromage & Dairy and sold throughout the US; products include spreadable cheese, crème de Brie, baby Brie, crème fraîche and crumbled cheese.

entries.heading: Alpazul (Conaprole)
entries.what: A cheese sold by Conaprole under the name Alpazul.

entries.heading: Alpkäse (Formaggio di alpeggio)
entries.what: A cheese made on alpine pastures, Bolzano province. PAT.

entries.heading: Alpmutschli
entries.what: A Mutschli made on an alp in the Berner Oberland. The 2023 Alpkäsemeisterschaft named an Alpmutschli winner: Familie Zumbrunnen, Boltigen, Alp Neuenberg (Schiltenegg).

entries.heading: Alt Urgell i la Cerdanya (Formatge de l'Alt Urgell i la Cerdanya; Urgèlia)
entries.what: A cylindrical, flat, pale-ivory cheese from the Alt Urgell and Baixa Cerdanya, sold whole and cut at retail. It is the only cheese from Catalonia with a PDO.

entries.heading: Altenburger Ziegenkäse (g.U.)
entries.what: A cylindrical soft cheese, about 11.5 cm across and 3 cm high (typically 250 g), with optional caraway; a local speciality named for its goat-milk content.

entries.heading: Aludttej (aludttej; "tej" family)
entries.what: Raw milk that clots at room temperature by the action of lactic acid bacteria with no added culture; cream rises as it stands.

entries.heading: Aluwa (අළුවා)
entries.what: Flat, cookie-like Sinhalese sweet cut into diamonds or squares with a wooden mould, eaten cooled. Variants pani, seeni and meegamu aluwa.

entries.heading: Alzitone
entries.what: Corsican cheese listed on the French cheese list.

entries.heading: Amabere amaruranu (Kisii fermented milk)
entries.what: a traditional spontaneously fermented bovine milk of the Kisii community of western Kenya. Spread to urban areas with migration.

entries.heading: AmaBlu (Caves of Faribault blue)
entries.what: One of the blues made by the Caves of Faribault; mould and yeasts on the cave ceilings are left in place.

entries.heading: Amarula (cream liqueur) and springbokkie
entries.what: Amarula is a South African cream liqueur at 17% ABV, containing cream and sugar with marula fruit. Springbokkie is a shooter made with Amarula and crème de menthe.

entries.heading: Amateregua (Kirundi; amateregwa spelling also possible)
entries.what: a household-made Burundian milk product named alongside urubu and amavuta in the review abstract.

entries.heading: Ambarees (also Serdalli / Serdale; Arabic script not given in the sources read)
entries.what: A traditional Lebanese goat cheese, made in the Bekaa Valley (northern and West Bekaa) and the Shouf Mountains (as Serdalli), kept for winter. Used in making kishk.

entries.heading: Ambrosia creamed rice
entries.what: British brand best known for custard and rice pudding; first product was a dried milk powder for infants.

entries.heading: American cheese (processed)
entries.what: The sliced, individually wrapped processed cheese, usually made from Colby or cheddar.

entries.heading: Ami du Chambertin
entries.what: A trade-marked washed-rind cheese made at a dairy in Brochon, Côte-d'Or.

entries.heading: Amon soja (fromage de soja; soy cheese)
entries.what: A soy cheese described as typically Beninese and highly valued locally; fried in peanut oil, or cooked in boiling water, and used in soups across West Africa. Name from Fon/Gbe and Yoruba; French "fromage de soja".

entries.heading: Amul cheese (Amul brand, Gujarat cooperative)
entries.what: Cheese sold under the Amul cooperative brand; the Amul article cites a report calling it "the world's biggest vegetarian cheese brand", exporting to the Middle East, Singapore and Hong Kong, with about 600 tonnes of sales estimated for 2005

entries.heading: Anari (Αναρί; "Nor" in the Wikipedia navigation box)
entries.what: A mild, crumbly, islandwide whey cheese. Fresh anari is eaten sliced with honey or carob syrup; dry anari is salted and grated over pasta and giouvetsi.

entries.heading: Anchor butter (English; brand name)
entries.what: Packaged butter, on the food survey's dairy item list.

entries.heading: Anchor full-cream milk powder (English; brand name)
entries.what: Powdered full-cream milk in a 250 g pack, on the food survey's list of dairy items.

entries.heading: Anchor liquid milk (English; brand name)
entries.what: Packaged liquid milk sold in shops and markets, tracked as a food price during COVID-19.

entries.heading: Anchor Milk Powder (other names: Anchor milk powder)
entries.what: The milk powder of the New Zealand Anchor brand, sold in Guyana and Ethiopia as a major product of the brand in some developing countries.

entries.heading: Anebabero
entries.what: layered injera soaked in butter mixed with berbere.

entries.heading: Angelico del Grappa (Formaggio dell'Angelo)
entries.what: A soft, creamy cheese with a white, velvety bloomy rind, made by the Centro Veneto Formaggi at Cavaso del Tomba, in the Pedemontana del Grappa.

entries.heading: Angelot
entries.what: named in the French Normandy cuisine article as a Normandy cheese. The English Pont-l'Évêque page says Angelot was an earlier name for Pont-l'Évêque.

entries.heading: Angou (cream dessert)
entries.what: A dessert named "Angou (crème)" in French Guianese cuisine.

entries.heading: Anijsmelk
entries.what: Warm milk traditionally boiled with aniseed, typically Dutch and especially in the northern provinces, usually drunk in winter. Sugar optional.

entries.heading: Ankole ghee (Banyankole ghee)
entries.what: Ghee made and sold by smallholder Banyankole farmers in south-western Uganda; the study records ghee-making yields and ghee sales as a household income line.

entries.heading: Anneau du Vic-Bilh
entries.what: A ring-shaped cheese of the Béarn and Gascogne (Vic-Bilh).

entries.heading: Anthotyro / Thilykotyri (Ανθότυρο / Θηλυκοτύρι)
entries.what: the mild "female" counterpart to arseniko, listed among Naxos whey cheeses.

entries.heading: Anyajia
entries.what: A thickened, sour fermented milk drink, served plain in a clay cup or sweetened with honey and cardamom.

entries.heading: Apetina (Arla white cheese, formerly sold as feta)
entries.what: Danish white brined cheese; Arla Foods renamed its white cheese products Apetina after Denmark lost its legal challenge to the EU feta name.

entries.heading: Api con leche (api; milk version)
entries.what: A traditional hot drink of maize, cinnamon and sugar, which the English article says is made with milk.

entries.heading: Aqit / Jameed (أقط, جميد; dried curd)
entries.what: A dried curd used in Najdi (central Saudi) dishes: mixed into مريس الأقط (mariss al-aqit) in المليحية (al-Muliha), used instead of flour in the variant الشعثة (Sha'atha) called العبيط (al-Abeet), and called "hard dry laban" in the Sha'atha

entries.heading: Aragatsyan panir (Aragatsyan panir; Aragatsotn)
entries.what: A semi-hard cheese with a mild nutty flavour and soft texture, less salty than brined cheeses, with a fat content stated as 50% or higher.

entries.heading: Araki (аракы, reindeer milk vodka)
entries.what: Milk vodka made from reindeer milk; the Russian article names Altai and Tuvan people as the producers.

entries.heading: Arany galuska (golden dumplings with vanilla custard)
entries.what: Dough balls rolled in butter and served with vanilla custard.

entries.heading: Arazhani (არაჟანი)
entries.what: lactic-fermented cream, similar to crème fraîche but less thick and less sour; unlike Western crème fraîche it does not curdle in hot dishes, per the Georgian article. Highest grade 36% fat, first grade 30%.

entries.heading: Ardrahan (and smoked Ardrahan)
entries.what: semi-soft farmhouse cheese, earthy with a zesty tang, deep-yellow interior, firm but slightly chalky; smoked version also made.

name: Ardsallagh soft and hard goat's cheese, Ardsallagh smoked

entries.heading: Ardsallagh soft and hard goat's cheese, Ardsallagh smoked
Areesh (اريش; جبنة قريش; gebna arish; cottage-type)
entries.what: A traditional Egyptian soft, white, crumbly fresh cheese, sometimes called cottage cheese. Also the base for mish.

entries.heading: Areesh / Arish
entries.what: A dried, aged curd used to make shanklish.

entries.heading: Arla Foods milk ingredients (whey protein, lactose, milk protein, permeate)
entries.what: milk-based ingredients for the food industry: milk proteins, phospholipids, minerals, permeate, lactose; a wholly owned plant is in Denmark (joint ventures in Argentina and Germany, incl. whey protein with DMK).

entries.heading: Armenian grain kashk (dried yoghurt grain mix)
entries.what: Strained yoghurt mixed into grain, fermented, dried in the sun and rubbed to a coarse powder. The English Kashk article links this method to Armenian, Arab and Turkish cooking.

entries.heading: Armexia (αρμέξια; Andros)
entries.what: named as an Andros cheese; no details found.

entries.heading: Armexia Androu (Αρμεξιά Άνδρου)
entries.what: Andros cheese; no details.

entries.heading: Armogalo Samou (Αρμόγαλο Σάμου)
entries.what: Samos cheese; no details.

entries.heading: Armyrotyri (αρμυρότυρι; Karpathos)
entries.what: a salty firm cheese from Karpathos.

entries.heading: Armyrotyri Karpathou
entries.what: a firm, intensely salty cheese from Karpathos.

entries.heading: Arnautski sir (Travnik cheese; Albanian name)
entries.what: the Bosnian Vlašić (Travnik) cheese; the Albanian cuisine article lists "Arnautski sir" as an Albanian dairy item and links it to Vlašić cheese.

entries.heading: Arnégui
entries.what: A cheese of the Pays basque.

entries.heading: Arrera (arerra; defatted sour milk / buttermilk)
entries.what: thin, defatted sour milk left after butter is churned. Colour like ergo, thicker than fresh milk, smooth, pleasant aroma and taste. Widely consumed across the country.

entries.heading: Arrigny
entries.what: A cheese tagged to Champagne-Ardenne on the list page.

entries.heading: Arroz com iogurte (badadji) — rice with yoghurt
entries.what: A rice dish made with plain yoghurt, often served with palm oil.

entries.heading: Arroz doce
entries.what: Portuguese rice pudding of rice cooked in milk with sugar, cinnamon and often egg yolk.

entries.heading: Arseniko (Αρσενικό Νάξου; PDO)
entries.what: a sharp, salty, mature yellow cheese from Naxos.

entries.heading: Arseniko Naxou (Αρσενικό Νάξου; Π.Ο.Π.)
entries.what: Naxos cheese; PDO.

entries.heading: Arthon (fromage)
entries.what: named as a cheese of the Centre.

entries.heading: Artisanal fresh cheese (unnamed in source; Tunisia)
entries.what: Artisanal fresh cheese sold unpackaged at unorganised retail points in northern Tunisia.

entries.heading: Artisanal yoghurt (Far North)
entries.what: Artisanal yoghurt made by women in the Far North Region, named as a common product of local fermentation practice alongside pendidam and kindirmou.

entries.heading: Arupiara and Cariri (goat cheeses, Paraíba)
entries.what: premium goat cheeses from Taperoá that have won awards.

entries.heading: Arz (арз; double-fermented milk liquor)
entries.what: A double-fermented milk liquor of about 30% alcohol.

entries.heading: Asadero (queso asadero)
entries.what: A melting white cheese of northern and other parts of Mexico, used for queso fundido.

entries.heading: Aschbacher Magerkäse (Aschbach magro)
entries.what: A "lean" cheese that is semi-fat, from Lagundo (hamlet Aschbach / Rio Lagundo). About 5 kg, about 25 cm across.

entries.heading: Ash Blue (King Island Dairy, Tasmania)
entries.what: A King Island Dairy blue listed as "Ash Blue".

entries.heading: Ash-e doogh (آش دوغ; ash-e mast)
entries.what: A yogurt soup in Azerbaijan, Shiraz and other parts of Iran; the yogurt or doogh is the main liquid, with herbs, vegetables, lamb meatballs or a vegetarian version; topped with fried mint in oil.

entries.heading: Asìno (Formaggio asìno)
entries.what: Soft-paste cheese named after Monte Asio, similar to Carnic salted cheese.

entries.heading: Atlama (qatıq ayran, cooling drink)
entries.what: cooling drink from Azerbaijan, drunk after meals, on hot days, at weddings and feasts; similar to ayran and called "qatıq ayranı". Also used to make doğramac.

entries.heading: Atleet
entries.what: best-known brand of block cheese from Võru Juust (Valio), sold in Estonia and Russia.

entries.heading: Atmet (atmit; oat and barley porridge drink)
entries.what: a drink of barley and oat flour cooked with water and sugar, with kibe, thick like eggnog. Given to nursing women as a comfort drink. A separate Wikipedia article describes a fortified form with oats, nonfat dried milk, sugar and micronutri

entries.heading: Atol de leche (atol con leche; atole)
entries.what: atole is a maize-based hot drink. The Spanish article lists Nicaragua in its territory (Mexico, Nicaragua, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, Costa Rica) and says atole is also often made with milk instead of water.

entries.heading: Atsidofilin (atsidofilin; acidophilin qatiq)
entries.what: A qatiq made with acidophilus bacteria. Sweeter than plain qatiq; 3.2% fat. Given as diet food in medicine and widely used in veterinary practice for calves. Acidophilus milk and paste are also made industrially.

entries.heading: Aukstā zupa (cold soup)
entries.what: Cold soup made with kefir or soured milk, beetroot, radish, cucumber, boiled egg and herbs, eaten in spring and summer.

entries.heading: Aulnay-de-Saintonge
entries.what: A cheese of the Aulnay area, Charente-Maritime (Saintonge).

entries.heading: Aura (Finnish blue cheese, Valio)
entries.what: A Finnish blue cheese named after the Aura river; Aura Gold is the same recipe aged 12 weeks.

entries.heading: Aushari (أوشاري; Aushari, Kurdish; script not given in source)
entries.what: A traditional Kurdish cheese from the mountains of northern Iraq, made mainly by Kurdish tribes and very popular with Kurds. It has a yellowish colour and a strong, sharp aroma from long ageing and added herbs.

entries.heading: Avdiivka kasha (Авдіївська каша; gonorova kasha, Gahai kasha)
entries.what: Traditional sweet dish from Avdiivka, Donetsk oblast, rich in butter and eggs and served hot with melted butter and raisins or cherries. Added to Ukraine's national intangible cultural heritage list in 2022 (per source).

entries.heading: Avena caliente (Dominican hot oat drink)
entries.what: A hot drink of milk, water and rolled oats spiced with cinnamon, cloves and nutmeg, sweetened with brown sugar.

entries.heading: Avena con leche
entries.what: an oat drink made with milk, listed among Nicaraguan drinks. The English avena article is general and mainly Colombian: oatmeal simmered in water and/or milk with sugar and spices such as cinnamon and clove.

entries.heading: Avocado cream
entries.what: Household dessert, often offered in restaurants, of avocado, sugar and cream.

name: Awal Dairy yoghurt, milk and cheese

entries.heading: Awal Dairy yoghurt, milk and cheese (Awal; Awal Dairy Company W.L.L.)
entries.what: a Bahrain-based company's dairy line. Its profile lists milk, yoghurt and cheese among its products.

entries.heading: Awassi sheep milk
entries.what: Milk from the Awassi fat-tailed sheep, the main milk and red meat breed of Syria.

entries.heading: Axsaq oğlaq (garlic yoghurt with hot oil)
entries.what: dish of garlic qatıq mixed with hot oil.

entries.heading: Ayib (ayibe, ayeb, ayib; Amharic/Gurage name, Ethiopian cottage cheese)
entries.what: A traditional Ethiopian cottage cheese, mild and crumbly, eaten widely across ethnic groups and often served beside spicy dishes (kitfo, kocho) to soften their heat. Described as a staple and a cheap, affordable product.

entries.heading: Ayran laban (salted laban drink)
entries.what: A salted laban drink sold in Saudi Arabia, with the lowest pH of the products tested (about 4.1).

entries.heading: Ayrani (αϊράνι; Cypriot ayran)
entries.what: A traditional yoghurt drink, a cold salted dilution of yoghurt.

entries.heading: Ayryan (айрян, айран) — ayran
entries.what: a cold, salted yoghurt drink; popular across the Balkans and in restaurants in Bulgaria

entries.heading: Azul de Búnker (blue sheep cheese, Villanúa)
entries.what: a large blue sheep cheese from Villanúa (Huesca), named after a Civil War bunker at El Carrascal where it was once ripened; 8 to 10 kg pieces, sold portioned.

entries.heading: Babribyol sharbat (Kashmiri sweet milk drink)
entries.what: Sweetened milk drink with rosewater or Rooh Afza and basil seeds, from Kashmir.

entries.heading: Baby Organic yoghurt (Glenisk)
entries.what: Organic yoghurts for babies from six months.

entries.heading: Babybel (Mini Babybel)
entries.what: A small individually wrapped snack cheese from the Bel Group, with roots in the Jura; made in Mayenne (per French list).

entries.heading: Bạc xỉu (white coffee, Saigon style)
entries.what: Milky coffee made with a mix of condensed milk and fresh milk and only a splash of coffee.

entries.heading: Bachensteiner
entries.what: Austrian cheese named in the English list.

entries.heading: Backslopping mabisi
entries.what: a type in which a portion of one batch is kept as starter for the next, repeated over many cycles. Ranked third in popularity in the national survey.

name: Bactrian camel milk and camel milk powder

entries.heading: Bactrian camel milk and camel milk powder
entries.what: A review says pasteurised milk, fermented beverages and dehydrated camel products are readily available on the Chinese market, and that powder has carried camel milk to urban consumers across China. China's camel herd was about 579,700 in 2

entries.heading: Bagaces (queso Bagaces; queso seco tipo Bagaces)
entries.what: A dry, salty, smoked cheese from the Bagaces area of Guanacaste, central part of the province; important to the cattle-ranching dairy culture of the region. Used as a filling for tanelas (corn empanadas with panela) and to bake a cheese bag

entries.heading: Bakoura
entries.what: An Algerian version of the Figou cheese, often filled with local fig jam.

entries.heading: Bakšteinas (Bakštein-type cheese, made in Lithuania before WWI)
entries.what: A cheese type made in Lithuania before WWI, about 3.4 % of output.

entries.heading: Bal de Broto cheeses (cow, washed and natural rind)
entries.what: a set of raw-milk cow cheeses from Broto (Huesca), named after former prisoners of the medieval Broto jail.

entries.heading: Balaninu (Balagne)
entries.what: A Corsican cheese named after Balagne, listed in the typical products of Corsican cuisine.

entries.heading: Balaton cheese
entries.what: a mild, yellow, semi-hard cheese named after Lake Balaton's region.

entries.heading: Balkánský sýr (Balkan cheese)
entries.what: Czech version of Balkan white cheese, salty, grainy, sold in blocks or cubes.

entries.heading: Ballyblue (Ballyblue soft blue)
entries.what: A soft blue cheese in the brie style, said to be the first blue cheese developed in Ireland.

entries.heading: Ballybrie (Ballybrie Irish brie)
entries.what: An Irish brie-style soft cheese made by Fivemiletown Creamery.

entries.heading: Ballyoak (Ballyoak smoked brie)
entries.what: A smoked brie-style cheese, described as the first smoked brie in Europe.

entries.heading: Balqaymaq (balqaymaq; Kazakh balqaimaq, Kyrgyz balkaymak)
entries.what: Described in the atlas paper as "a dairy product similar to clotted cream, rich and creamy in texture", with the Uzbek name Balqaymaq.

entries.heading: Balsfjordost
entries.what: a Norwegian goat cheese, part of the Norske Ostespesialiteter series; introduced in the early 1980s.

entries.heading: Banagher Bold
entries.what: A washed-rind cheese from Dart Mountain Cheese, County Londonderry.

entries.heading: Banco de Leche, Roosevelt Hospital (human donor milk bank, Guatemala City)
entries.what: a nonprofit human donor milk bank run by the Banco de Leche of Roosevelt Hospital in Guatemala City, described in a 2019 Journal of Human Lactation paper.

entries.heading: Bandel cheese (Bandel)
entries.what: Smoked cheese introduced in Bengal by the Portuguese; made in Bandel, a former Portuguese colony near Kolkata.

entries.heading: Bánh flan (caramel custard)
entries.what: Steamed caramel custard made from eggs and milk; sold as a city dessert or snack; also called bánh lăng or ca-ra-men.

entries.heading: Bar One sauce
entries.what: A sauce of melted chocolate and cream, usually poured over vanilla ice cream.

entries.heading: Baramili (براميلي; "barrel cheese")
entries.what: A white Egyptian cheese whose name means "barrel cheese".

entries.heading: Barberey (troyen cendré)
entries.what: Troyen cendré tagged to Champagne on the list page.

entries.heading: Bardhoke (cheese, named origin, pasteurised milk)
entries.what: a named traditional origin sampled after manufacture for hygiene.

entries.heading: Barfi / burfi (बर्फ़ी)
entries.what: Fudge-like sweet, widespread in North India and Pakistan.

entries.heading: Barotse mabisi
entries.what: named after Barotseland, the old name for the Western province, where it is mainly made. Second in popularity in the national survey, and most popular in Western province.

entries.heading: Barousse
entries.what: A Pyrenean cheese from the Barousse valley with a strong hay-like smell.

entries.heading: Basa (basa; basa pomješa; posna basa)
entries.what: a soft white cheese from Lika (Croatia) and parts of Bosanska Krajina (Bosnia); a regional speciality

entries.heading: Basils Original Rauchkäse
entries.what: a naturally ripened semi-hard cut cheese with a hearty flavour, named after the company's founder, Basil Weixler.

entries.heading: Bastani (بستنی; incl. bastani-e sonnati and saffron variant)
entries.what: Traditional Iranian ice cream made with milk, egg yolk, sugar, rose water, saffron, vanilla and pistachio, often with flakes of frozen clotted cream and sometimes salep. Its saffron form (bastani-e zaferani, bastani sonnati zaferani) is a n

entries.heading: Bastilicacciu (Bastelica)
entries.what: A Corsican cheese named after Bastelica, listed in the typical products of Corsican cuisine.

entries.heading: Basundi (बासुंदी; basundi)
entries.what: Sweetened thick milk dessert from western and southern India; a northern equivalent is rabri.

entries.heading: Batido (batido de guanábana, batido de trigo)
entries.what: A milkshake in Cuban cuisine, with flavours such as guanábana (soursop) and trigo (wheat).

entries.heading: Batidos (fruit milk drinks)
entries.what: Creamy fruit drinks made with fruit and milk, sold in juice bars.

entries.heading: Batidos de leche (milk and fruit shakes)
entries.what: milk blended with fruit, listed among Honduran drinks.

entries.heading: Bavaria blu (Weiß-Blau-Käse)
entries.what: a German brand of the Bergader Privatkäserei in Waging am See, introduced in 1972. It combines a white camembert-type rind with a blue-marbled interior. 70% fat in dry matter; ideal ripeness four to six weeks. The article gives it a 13% sha

entries.heading: Bayard Gourmand (Bayard Gourmand)
entries.what: a cheese listed under Île-de-France.

entries.heading: Bear Brand (Nestlé Bear Brand; sterilised milk)
entries.what: A milk brand produced by Nestlé Philippines, sold as a powdered milk and as a ready-to-drink sterilised milk in tin cans and Tetra Pak cartons. Fortified versions exist, such as Bear Brand Gold. Sold across much of Southeast Asia and East A

entries.heading: Beara Blue (Knockatee Cheese, Co. Kerry)
entries.what: Traditional blue cheese in the Stilton style from Knockatee Cheese, Co. Kerry.

entries.heading: Beaumont (tomme de Beaumont)
entries.what: flat disc about 20 cm across, 4 cm thick, 1.5 kg; created 1881 by Jérémie Girod in Saint-Julien-en-Genevois.

entries.heading: Bebè di Sorrento
entries.what: a small stretched-curd cheese shaped like a baby in swaddling clothes (the name), from Sorrento.

entries.heading: Bebida láctea
entries.what: A dairy drink made of whey and milk with at least 51% dairy content by mass. Legal standard: Instrução Normativa nº 16 (2005) of Brazil's agriculture ministry.

entries.heading: Béchamel (béchamel; French: béchamel; Spanish: bechamel)
entries.what: A white sauce used as a topping in fideos al horno, a baked macaroni dish, where it melts and binds the dish during baking.

entries.heading: Béchamel sauce (on cardu at Christmas)
entries.what: A béchamel, a white sauce made from milk, is the sauce in which cardu (cardoon) is served at the Christmas meal.

entries.heading: Beddo
entries.what: alpine cheese from Biellese, Piemonte, made at Pralungo and the Oropa valley (Biella province).

entries.heading: Beder yoghurt (camel milk yoghurt, Mogadishu)
entries.what: Yoghurt made from camel milk, described as the first niche yoghurt dairy in the country, sold in supermarkets in Mogadishu.

entries.heading: Beetroot and orange drinking yoghurt (experimental)
entries.what: a drinking yoghurt fortified with beetroot pulp and orange juice; the authors have Bangladeshi names, but the study location was not checked and this is a lab formulation, not a product on sale.

entries.heading: Bëggia
entries.what: traditional sheep cheese from the mountain areas of Cuneo and Torino (originally two side valleys of the Valle Gesso).

entries.heading: Beijing Grey (北京灰, industrial/artisanal)
entries.what: Mild, creamy, Camembert-style cheese made by local Chinese producers.

entries.heading: Bel Paese
entries.what: a cheese from Lombardy whose name is a poetic name for Italy, inspired by Antonio Stoppani's 1876 book.

entries.heading: Beleghman (balls of roasted barley flour with dairy)
entries.what: balls made from roasted barley flour bound with dairy, eaten at iftar.

entries.heading: Beli sir na žaru (grilled white cheese)
entries.what: a traditional Đerdap dish of brined white cheese; often served as an appetiser

entries.heading: Belicino
entries.what: a pecorino-type cheese with pitted olives added (Nocellara del Belice).

entries.heading: Belizean cheese dip (dish, made with the processed cheese above)
entries.what: A blended dip of processed white cheese, evaporated milk, salsa casera and optional pickled jalapeño, served chilled with fried corn tortilla chips. Named as the signature cheese dish in travel sources.

entries.heading: BellaVitano
entries.what: A cheese listed among American soft cheeses.

entries.heading: Belle des champs
entries.what: An industrial cylindrical soft cheese with a bloomy rind, about 2 kg, made in the Aisne department from 1973 by the Bongrain group (now Savencia); production is said to have stopped in the 1990s.

entries.heading: Bellingham Blue
entries.what: firm blue-veined cheese with a strong, salty finish.

entries.heading: Belper Knolle
entries.what: A small raw-milk cheese from Belp, south of Bern in the Bern-Mittelland. Named for its knobbly shape, like a potato or truffle. The fresh form is creamy and melting, with a slightly sour taste; the hard form is grated as a seasoning.

entries.heading: Bergader Edelpilz
entries.what: a blue cheese developed by Basil Weixler in the 1920s, similar to Roquefort but made from cow milk. After he lost a court case over the name "Bayerischer Gebirgs-Roquefort", the cheese was sold as Bergader Edelpilz. The article says it has

entries.heading: Bergbaron (Schärdinger / Berglandmilch brand)
entries.what: a cheese brand listed for both Schärdinger (1970s) and Berglandmilch

entries.heading: Bergenost (Yancey's Fancy)
entries.what: A mild, smooth, slightly tangy cheese.

entries.heading: Bergues (fromage de Bergues)
entries.what: A washed-rind farmhouse cheese from the French Blootland around Bergues near Dunkirk; about 20 cm in diameter, 20–25% fat, yellow to ochre or pinkish rind, strong smell.

entries.heading: Bernardo (PAT)
entries.what: a soft, fat cheese from the Valle Seriana, Province of Bergamo, with a compact yellow or orange paste.

entries.heading: Berner Alpkäse and Berner Hobelkäse
entries.what: alpine cheese from the Bernese Oberland and nearby areas, made on approved alpine farms in the alpine season; Hobelkäse ("planing cheese") is aged at least two years and planed.

entries.heading: Berner Alpkäse AOP (Berner Alpkäse; Coeur des Alpes as a named cheese)
entries.what: A raw-milk alp cheese made in the summer pastures of the Berner Oberland and some adjacent alps. The cheese is made only in recognised alp dairies during the alp season, from about mid-May to the end of September, and sold as young semi-har

entries.heading: Berner Hobelkäse AOP
entries.what: An Alpkäse aged for at least two years and planed (Hobel) into shavings. It is the most widely available form of Berner Alpkäse.

entries.heading: Bethmale
entries.what: A Pyrenean farm cheese from the Vallée de Bethmale, Couserans, Ariège.

entries.heading: Bettelmat (Bettelmatt)
entries.what: traditional alpine cheese made in high summer pastures above 1,800 m in Ossola (upper Val Formazza and Valle Antigorio / Valle di Devero).

entries.heading: Beurre blanc
entries.what: A hot emulsion of lightly salted butter with a reduction of white wine, vinegar and shallots, from the Loire region around Nantes; usually served with fish.

entries.heading: Beurre clarifié (beurre fondu, Normandy)
entries.what: Butter melted and skimmed so mostly fat remains; traditional French preservation method, notably in Normandy, where it was called beurre fondu.

entries.heading: Beurre d'Ardenne (AOP butter)
entries.what: A butter from the Belgian Ardennes; the only Belgian product with an EU Appellation d'Origine Protégée (AOP), granted 1996; Belgian recognition by royal decree of 18 December 1984.

entries.heading: Beurre d'Isigny AOP
entries.what: A Normandy butter with a protected name, made from slowly matured cream.

entries.heading: Beurre de Bresse AOP
entries.what: A sweet butter made by churning cultured cream from Bresse cows, with a protected name.

entries.heading: Beurre des Charentes-Poitou AOP
entries.what: A cultured-cream butter from western France (Charente, Charente-Maritime, Deux-Sèvres, Vienne, Vendée); a protected name.

entries.heading: Beurre traditionnel (traditional butter; French "beurre", Peul dairies)
entries.what: Butter made by Peul women from the cream of the milk.

entries.heading: Bhola / Noakhali artisanal buffalo curd (traditional buffalo milk curd)
entries.what: artisanal buffalo milk curd from Bhola, Bangladesh, with natural (spontaneous) fermentation. Studies name Leuconostoc and Bifidobacteria in it; the buffalo review says yoghurt from Bhola and Noakhali is in demand.

entries.heading: Biancomangiare
entries.what: milk or cream and sugar set with a thickener, often with almonds; the Italian form of blancmange.

entries.heading: Biancospino
entries.what: Listed among Sardinian cheeses.

entries.heading: Bienmesabe (bienmesabe; rice and milk dessert)
entries.what: A dessert of rice, milk and cane honey, named in the Panamanian lexicon column.

entries.heading: Biezpiena sieriņš (curd snack)
entries.what: A cottage-cheese-based snack and dessert; the brand Kārums was voted Latvia's favourite product in 2012 with 20% of votes.

entries.heading: Big Woods Blue
entries.what: A complex, spicy blue.

entries.heading: Bilozhar (Білозар)
entries.what: Ukrainian cheese in the country section of the List of cheeses.

entries.heading: Bird's custard powder
entries.what: cornflour-based custard powder, made into a custard-like sauce with milk.

entries.heading: Bishop Kennedy (Bishop Kennedy; cow's milk soft)
entries.what: A soft, round, brie-like Scottish cheese with a yellowish runny interior, listed on the Scottish cuisine dairy list.

entries.heading: Bite d'âne
entries.what: named as a Loir-et-Cher cheese.

entries.heading: Bito sirene / branza (Бито сирене, Брънза; "brânza" term)
entries.what: a Bulgarian cheese type named on the Bulgarian Wikipedia cheese-list page; "Rodopska brânza" (Rhodope brânza) appears as a recipe name.

entries.heading: Bjurholms blåmögelost (moose blue cheese)
entries.what: Blue-mould cheese made from moose milk at Bjurholm, Västerbotten.

entries.heading: Blå Gotland
entries.what: Blue-wrapped, cube-shaped cheese with pale yellow paste, similar in texture to Emmentaler but stronger in taste.

entries.heading: Blaand (bland)
entries.what: a fermented milk product made from whey, acidic with very low alcohol.

name: Black and white yuenyeung and malted-milk drinks

entries.heading: Black and white yuenyeung and malted-milk drinks (Ovaltine, Horlicks)
entries.what: Ovaltine and Horlicks served as drinks, and mixed together as a children's version of yuenyeung ("black and white yuenyeung").

entries.heading: Black Bomber
entries.what: A very strong cheddar variety named in the cookbook overview of Welsh cuisine.

entries.heading: Black Danbo
entries.what: a Danish-style cheese listed as made in Kenya.

entries.heading: Black tea with milk (Sudanese tea)
entries.what: black tea served with milk, sold on the street by "tea ladies" in Sudan.

entries.heading: Blak (soured milk drink)
entries.what: A sour, fresh-tasting milk drink, also used in cooking and baking. Per 100 g: 0.5 g fat, 3.3 g protein. Keeps 2–3 days chilled once opened.

entries.heading: Blanc-manger coco (créole; blanc-manger à la noix de coco, Antilles)
entries.what: A coconut blanc-manger listed among the creole versions of blanc-manger. The French Wikipedia article names it as the creole version, not specifically Martinique.

entries.heading: Blaťácké zlato
entries.what: Czech soft cheese, golden-orange rind, mild milky taste with nutty notes.

entries.heading: Blatnički sir (Blatnica cheese)
entries.what: A white cheese from Vučija planina and Blatnica, in western Bosnia.

entries.heading: Bleu Bénédictin (Saint-Benoît-du-Lac, Quebec)
entries.what: A semi-soft whole-milk blue cheese made by the monks of the Benedictine Abbey of Saint-Benoît-du-Lac, Quebec.

entries.heading: Bleu d'Élizabeth (Sainte-Élizabeth-de-Warwick, Quebec)
entries.what: A semi-firm blue cheese, process inspired by French blues such as Fourme d'Ambert and Bleu d'Auvergne.

entries.heading: Bleu de Bresse
entries.what: A blue cheese first made in Bresse after World War II; creamy interior like Brie with blue patches.

entries.heading: Bleu de Chèvre
entries.what: A blue goat's-milk cheese; unlike most French blues it is made from goat's milk.

entries.heading: Bleu de Costaros
entries.what: small, hand-made cheese from Costaros, Velay (Haute-Loire).

entries.heading: Bleu de Langeac
entries.what: blue cheese named after Langeac, Haute-Loire.

entries.heading: Bleu de Loudes (bleu du Velay)
entries.what: cylinder 12 cm across, 12–15 cm high, 600 g–1 kg; Velay, Haute-Loire.

entries.heading: Bleu de Thiézac
entries.what: blue cheese of Thiézac, Cantal; made like bleu d'Auvergne, exclusively artisanal.

entries.heading: Bleu des Basques (Le Bleu des Basques)
entries.what: A blue-veined sheep cheese from the Pays basque.

entries.heading: Bleu du Quercy
entries.what: A French blue cheese from cow's milk made in the Lot (Quercy).

entries.heading: Bleu du Queyras
entries.what: a blue-veined cheese from the Queyras, made from alpine-pasture milk.

entries.heading: Bleu Ticines (Ul Bleu Ticines)
entries.what: A goat's blue cheese from Fattoria del Faggio in Sonvico, which has won several awards; it is soft, melts easily and has a mildly sweet taste between spicy and piquant

entries.heading: Blue Brie (King Island Dairy, Tasmania)
entries.what: A King Island Dairy product listed as "Blue Brie".

entries.heading: Blue Castello (Castello; White Castello as a related product)
entries.what: a soft, creamy Danish blue cheese from the Castello brand (Arla Foods, Viby, Aarhus; established 1893 by Rasmus Tholstrup).

entries.heading: Blue Cheddar (King Island Dairy, Tasmania)
entries.what: A King Island Dairy product listed as "Blue Cheddar".

entries.heading: Blue Cheshire (King Island Dairy, Tasmania)
entries.what: A King Island Dairy product listed as "Blue Cheshire".

entries.heading: Bóc
entries.what: a cottage cheese dumpling associated with the Csángó people of Moldavia and Transylvania (Hungarian-speaking communities).

entries.heading: Bocadillo (bocadillo; milk candy)
entries.what: A firm, square sweet made from milk, listed among Panamanian sweets.

entries.heading: Bocconcini
entries.what: small fresh cheeses; Bocconcini of buffalo milk in Campania.

entries.heading: Boeber
entries.what: A Cape Malay sweet milk drink, sometimes called a pudding.

entries.heading: Boer'n Trots (Boer'n Trots; cheese trademark, Q27978495)
entries.what: A Dutch cheese brand made at Landgoed Kaamps, an estate in Deurningen, Twente, with cow's milk from its own herd and goat's milk for some varieties. Made since 1985 according to the Wikipedia article; distributed by Vandersterre Groep.

entries.heading: Boerenkaas (farmer's cheese)
entries.what: A protected category of Dutch farmhouse cheese, most of it handmade from raw (unpasteurised) milk. At least half the milk comes from the farm where the cheese is made. May contain cumin, other seeds, herbs or spices.

entries.heading: Bog butter
entries.what: Butter, or animal fat, packed in a wooden vessel and buried in a peat bog to keep it. Practice dates to the 1st century AD in Ireland.

entries.heading: Bogobe jwa lerotse (sorghum and cooking-melon dish with sour milk)
entries.what: A sorghum dish with cooking melon (lerotse) prepared with sour milk, served at weddings.

entries.heading: Bogobe jwa logala / sengana (sorghum porridge cooked with milk)
entries.what: A traditional Setswana dish of sorghum porridge cooked with milk.

entries.heading: Bohinjski sir (Bohinj cheese)
entries.what: Hard cheese from Bohinj, based on the Swiss Emmental (ementalec) technique.

entries.heading: Boïga (Casa Raubert matured cheese)
entries.what: A matured cheese from Casa Raubert.

entries.heading: Boiled cow milk
entries.what: fresh milk boiled before use, the most common form in Jimma households.

entries.heading: Boilie (Boilie Irish Cheese Pearls; Boilie Irish Goat's Cheese)
entries.what: A soft cream cheese shaped into small balls and steeped in sunflower oil infused with herbs and garlic. Sold as cow's milk "Boilie Irish Cheese Pearls" and goat's milk "Boilie Irish Goat's Cheese". Sizes 150 g, 200 g and 1 kg.

entries.heading: Boisseau (Boisseau)
entries.what: a cheese listed under Île-de-France.

entries.heading: Bojar (yoghurt and related, Berglandmilch)
entries.what: a Berglandmilch brand in the yoghurt range

entries.heading: Bolo di manteka (butter cake)
entries.what: A pound-cake-style cake where butter is a main ingredient, with flour, sugar and many eggs in roughly equal weights.

entries.heading: Bonassai
entries.what: A soft caciotta listed among Sardinian cheeses.

entries.heading: Bondard
entries.what: named in the French Normandy cuisine article as a Normandy cheese. No description opened.

entries.heading: Bondon
entries.what: named in the French Normandy cuisine article; the bung shape (bondon) is also a Neufchâtel shape per fr.wikipedia.

entries.heading: Bonèt (bunet)
entries.what: Piedmontese custard of eggs, milk, cocoa, sugar and amaretto, sometimes rum, cooked over caramel.

entries.heading: Bongo
entries.what: A traditionally fermented dairy beverage from Uganda, studied in Lyantonde district and in commercially produced form.

entries.heading: Bonne Bouche
entries.what: A goat cheese dusted with poplar ash.

entries.heading: Bons mayennais
entries.what: Named on the list of French cheeses with origin Mayenne, Pays de la Loire.

entries.heading: Borani (yogurt-based dish with spinach)
entries.what: A yogurt-based dish combined with spinach and other ingredients.

entries.heading: Borasaame (Sidama)
entries.what: cooked mixture of wassa and butter, sometimes eaten with mustard greens or beans.

entries.heading: Bordall (lactic cheese, Es Pinaró de ses Monges)
entries.what: Named product of Es Pinaró de ses Monges, Mallorca.

entries.heading: Borhani (বোরহানি)
entries.what: a savoury drink made from sour doi, served as a digestive or appetiser.

entries.heading: Bosnian Gruyère cheese
entries.what: A Gruyère-style cheese made in Bosnia, recognised by the producers' association.

entries.heading: Bosnian smoked cheese (Suhi dimljeni sir; Suhi sir)
entries.what: A very dry, piquant, low-fat smoked cheese with a dark skin and white interior, in a small round shape.

entries.heading: Boterbroodje (hand-moulded butter)
entries.what: Traditional hand-made butter pressed into small wooden moulds and decorated.

entries.heading: Boterroomcrème (butter cream filling)
entries.what: A butter cream used as the filling joining two almond biscuits in baisers (Belgian meringue-type pastry).

entries.heading: Bouca
entries.what: Named in the list of French cheeses with origin "Val de Loire", which spans several regions.

entries.heading: Bouchon charentais
entries.what: A small cheese of the Charentes.

entries.heading: Bouchon de Sancerre (also bouchon de chèvre)
