entries.what: a small goat cheese named for its bottle-stopper shape and the town of Sancerre.

entries.heading: Bougatsa krema (semolina custard pastry)
entries.what: the cream version of bougatsa, a pastry of filo with a semolina custard. It is the most popular version and is sweet.

entries.heading: Bouhezza
entries.what: A traditional fermented soft-ripened cheese from eastern Algeria, made by hand; kneaded with red pepper at the point of eating.

entries.heading: Bouille
entries.what: named in the French Normandy cuisine article as a Normandy cheese. No description opened.

entries.heading: Bouine
entries.what: A Sarthe speciality made from leftover cheeses, with crème fraîche, garlic and parsley, mixed with a fork. Described as a strong cheese from the Sarthe.

entries.heading: Boulet de Cassel
entries.what: A round farmhouse cheese, about 500 g, with an orange-tinted paste, sold under a trademark belonging to Marie Christine Dubois; in existence since 1991.

entries.heading: Boulette d'Avesnes
entries.what: A small conical, hand-shaped soft washed-rind cheese from the Avesnois, about 250 g, made from fresh white Maroilles scraps and downgraded Maroilles.

entries.heading: Boulette de Cambrai
entries.what: A small cone-shaped fresh cheese, about 200 g, flavoured with pepper, tarragon and parsley, with no rind; from Cambrai in the Nord.

entries.heading: Boulette de la Pierre-qui-Vire
entries.what: A small cheese made by the Pierre-qui-Vire abbey in Burgundy; the name is a registered brand.

entries.heading: Bouq Émissaire (Châteauguay, Quebec)
entries.what: A raw-milk goat cheese with an ash-covered rind; the name is a misspelling of the French term for "scapegoat."

entries.heading: Bouton de Culotte
entries.what: A small farm goat cheese from the Mâconnais and Haut-Beaujolais, sold under a brand owned by a group of around ten farm producers.

entries.heading: Bouyi (bouye; Serer mbudaay-baak; baobab juice)
entries.what: A baobab-fruit drink with milk and sugar, drunk cold or at room temperature. Frozen, it is sold as "ice" on streets and beside buses.

entries.heading: Bouza (sorghum dessert cooked in milk)
entries.what: A sorghum dessert with dried fruit, named in the Tunisian cuisine article.

entries.heading: Bovški sir (Bovec cheese; bovški sir, Formaggio di Plezzo vero)
entries.what: Sheep-milk cheese from the Bovec area in the upper Soča valley; compact, elastic, aromatic and slightly piquant.

entries.heading: Boyne Valley Blue (Glyde Farm Produce, Co. Louth)
entries.what: Blue cheese from Glyde Farm Produce, Co. Louth.

entries.heading: Brădet (cașcaval)
entries.what: A Romanian cașcaval variety named in the Romanian cașcaval list; no description given.

entries.heading: Brændende kærlighed (burning love)
entries.what: mashed potatoes made with butter and milk or cream.

entries.heading: Brăila (hard buffalo cheese)
entries.what: A Romanian hard cheese named in the buffalo article's list of buffalo-milk cheeses.

entries.heading: Brânză (brined sheep's-milk cheese; brynza in Russian)
entries.what: Brined white cheese, the everyday cheese of Moldova. In Romanian "brânză" is the general word for any cheese, so the Moldovan use is a brined sheep's cheese.

entries.heading: Brânză de coșuleț (coșuleț)
entries.what: A cheese made only from sheep's milk, specific to Romania; it is named for the basket (coșuleț) it is moulded in.

entries.heading: Brânză de Suhaia
entries.what: A cheese from the commune of Suhaia (Teleorman county), matured in brine.

entries.heading: Brânza lui Vodă
entries.what: A semi-hard mountain cheese tied to a legend about medieval ruler Prince Radu Mihnea; still made in the Romanian mountains.

entries.heading: Brânză topită
entries.what: The generic Romanian name for processed cheese, an industrial product.

entries.heading: Branzi (PAT)
entries.what: a historic Alpine cheese of the Alta Valle Brembana; the fresh version is eaten young, the aged one grated.

entries.heading: Bread and butter pudding
entries.what: buttered bread and dried fruit baked in an egg custard made with milk or cream.

name: Breakfast cheese, Brie and other styles

entries.heading: Breakfast cheese, Brie and other styles (Marin French Cheese Company)
entries.what: A small-batch creamery making over 40 styles.

entries.heading: Breakfast-shop milk tea (早餐店奶茶)
entries.what: A standard milk tea sold at traditional and modern breakfast shops, made with black tea and creamer rather than fresh milk.

entries.heading: Breast-milk ice cream (Baby Gaga, London 2011)
entries.what: breast-milk ice cream sold in London's Covent Garden in February 2011 by The Licktators.

entries.heading: Breastmilk (human milk), with breastmilk substitutes in use
entries.what: Breastmilk is the normal first food for infants in the Pohnpei Mand community; infant formula is used alongside or instead of it, mostly among families with low incomes.

entries.heading: Brebiblu
entries.what: a soft sheep's-milk blue cheese inoculated with Penicillium roqueforti.

entries.heading: Brebidor
entries.what: a soft sheep's-milk cheese.

entries.heading: Bredsjö Blå
entries.what: Swedish sheep blue cheese from Bergslagen.

entries.heading: Bregenzerwälder Alpkäse (Bregenzerwälder Bergkäse)
entries.what: Alpine cheese from the Bregenzerwald in Vorarlberg. The Bergkäse article does not name it.

entries.heading: Bresse Bleu
entries.what: blue cheese from the Bresse (Ain), first made by the Servas cooperative.

entries.heading: Brick cheese (Brick)
entries.what: A medium-soft cheese named for its brick shape, from when real bricks were used to press it.

entries.heading: Brie de Melun bleu (Brie de Melun bleu)
entries.what: a blue version of Brie de Melun named in the English Brie article.

entries.heading: Brie de Montereau (Brie de Montereau ou Ville-Saint-Jacques; ville-saint-jacques)
entries.what: a Brie-type cheese of Île-de-France, similar in size to Coulommiers and in taste to Brie de Melun.

entries.heading: Brie de Nangis (Brie de Nangis)
entries.what: a Brie-type cheese named after Nangis, a commune of Seine-et-Marne.

entries.heading: Brie de Nasu (ブリー・ド・那須)
entries.what: A creamy white-mould cheese modelled on French brie, from Nasu no Mori in Tochigi.

entries.heading: Brie de Provins (Brie de Provins)
entries.what: a Brie-type cheese from the Provins area; created in 1979 and given a registered trademark of the same name.

entries.heading: Brie fermier (Brie fermier)
entries.what: a farm-made Brie listed under Seine-et-Marne, Île-de-France.

entries.heading: Brie noir (Brie noir; Vieux-Brie)
entries.what: a darker, stronger Brie aged for many months, described as Île-de-France in origin; the source says a Brie aged about 6 months resembles Comté and one aged a year resembles Parmesan.

entries.heading: Brie petit moulé (Brie petit moulé; petit brie de Coulommiers)
entries.what: a small Brie-type cheese, related to Coulommiers and sometimes called "petit brie de Coulommiers".

entries.heading: Brie Piton des Neiges (Brie Péi Piton des Neiges)
entries.what: A brie-style cheese with a bloomy rind from highland cow's milk.

entries.heading: Brie-style cheese (Jindi Cheese, Victoria)
entries.what: Jindi Cheese is named as one of three Australian makers of brie-style cheese.

entries.heading: Brie-style cheese (High Valley Mudgee Cheese Co, NSW)
entries.what: High Valley Mudgee Cheese Co is named as one of three Australian makers of brie-style cheese.

entries.heading: Brie-style cheeses (Mainland; craft makers such as Grinning Gecko)
entries.what: Brie-style cheeses made in NZ: the Mainland brand's Creamy, Double Cream and Blue varieties, and brie-style cheeses from craft cheesemakers such as Grinning Gecko.

entries.heading: Brigadeiro
entries.what: Typical Brazilian sweet made from condensed milk, cocoa powder and butter, coated with chocolate sprinkles. Known as "negrinho" in Rio Grande do Sul.

entries.heading: Brighton Blue
entries.what: a yellow, semi-soft blue cheese named after Brighton, East Sussex.

entries.heading: Brique de Lisieux
entries.what: named in the French Normandy cuisine article as a Normandy cheese, from the Lisieux area. No description opened.

entries.heading: British rice pudding
entries.what: pudding rice cooked slowly in milk with cream or butter and sugar, topped with nutmeg.

entries.heading: Brjóstamjólkurís (ice cream made from breast milk)
entries.what: An ice cream made from breast milk, offered for tasting at Kjörís's Ísdagurinn (Ice Day) in Hveragerði as one of several experimental flavours (mustard, BBQ, marshmallow, ash).

entries.heading: Broddmjólk (colostrum)
entries.what: The milk produced late in pregnancy and in the first days after birth, rich in substances that help newborns develop and resist disease.

entries.heading: Brookside dairy products (Kenyan company, sold in Tanzania)
entries.what: products of Brookside Dairies, a Kenyan dairy processor whose products are distributed in Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda.

entries.heading: Brossa (Brossa; brossa)
entries.what: A PAT-recognised preparation listed for Valle d'Aosta with sheep, goat and cow milk.

entries.heading: Brossat (brull)
entries.what: A very low-fat, high-protein fresh whey cheese, white and flaky; eaten the same day, not pressed, salted or matured.

entries.heading: Brothchán
entries.what: A gruel of water or milk and meal, served to monks as a staple.

entries.heading: Brotzu (Brocciu)
entries.what: Listed among Sardinian cheeses.

entries.heading: Brukina (Brukina; spelled "burkina" in some titles)
entries.what: A fermented beverage of milk and millet, popular in Ghana and other West African countries, sold in markets.

entries.heading: Brull (brossat)
entries.what: A very soft, fresh cheese of the Maestrat and Terres de l'Ebre, equivalent to mató.

entries.heading: Brunost (brunost; mysost; "brown cheese")
entries.what: the general name for Norway's sweet brown whey product. The en Wikipedia article calls it "not a true cheese". FAO and WHO do not count it as cheese (no.wiki Geitost).

entries.heading: Brussels cheese (Brusselse kaas; fromage de Bruxelles; (h)ettekeis)
entries.what: A traditional Brabant cheese named after the Brussels market. Smooth and sharp, with a strong, salty bite; nicknamed "stinkkaas". Traditionally eaten on bread at breakfast with strong coffee or Oude Geuze.

entries.heading: Brutto ma buono di Brugnato (Brugnato, La Spezia)
entries.what: a cheese from Brugnato named in the sources, with no description.

entries.heading: Bryndza Podhalańska (bryndza podhalańska)
entries.what: The Polish protected variety of bryndza from the Podhale region of the Tatra foothills.

entries.heading: Brynza, lowland and regional (Бринза; Vinnytsia, Chernivtsi)
entries.what: the general Ukrainian brynza, a brine-ripened white cheese, also called bryndza in English and common in Ukrainian, Moldovan, Romanian and Slovak cooking.

entries.heading: Bubble milk tea (珍珠奶茶; pearl milk tea, boba milk tea)
entries.what: Black tea with milk and sugar, served with chewy cooked tapioca pearls (粉圓). Some versions add pudding, nata de coco or grass jelly. Taiwan marks 30 April as national bubble tea day.

entries.heading: Buča (Буча; Buča)
entries.what: a Montenegrin cheese listed in the cheese section of Montenegrin cuisine.

entries.heading: Bûche du Poitou
entries.what: A log-shaped cheese of Poitou and Limousin.

entries.heading: Buda (Budské sýry)
entries.what: named Czech cheese from the Krkonoše mountains, produced for decades.

entries.heading: Budz (бундз, буц)
entries.what: fresh Hutsul sheep cheese made on mountain pastures (polonyna); also made in Poland.

entries.heading: Buffalo blue cheese (Laos Buffalo Dairy)
entries.what: blue cheese made from water buffalo milk in Luang Prabang.

entries.heading: Buffalo brie (Laos Buffalo Dairy)
entries.what: brie made from water buffalo milk in Luang Prabang. The Nat Geo article says that before the dairy "it was impossible even to find a local brie".

entries.heading: Buffalo camembert (Laos Buffalo Dairy)
entries.what: camembert made from water buffalo milk in Luang Prabang.

entries.heading: Buffalo cheesecake
entries.what: cheesecake made with water buffalo milk, a higher-fat version of cow-milk cheesecake.

entries.heading: Buffalo feta (Laos Buffalo Dairy)
entries.what: feta made from water buffalo milk in Luang Prabang.

entries.heading: Buffalo ice cream (lemongrass and tamarind flavours)
entries.what: ice cream made from water buffalo milk in lemongrass and tamarind flavours.

entries.heading: Buffalo milk curd (Bhola district, Charfassion Upazila; artisanal)
entries.what: traditional artisanal buffalo-milk curd from Bhola district, Bangladesh, studied as a source of bifidobacteria (per the paper titles); Leuconostoc citreum and L. falkenbergense strains have been isolated from it.

entries.heading: Buffalo mozzarella (Laos Buffalo Dairy)
entries.what: mozzarella made from water buffalo milk in Luang Prabang, one of the cheeses the dairy makes for locals and visitors.

entries.heading: Buffalo ricotta (Laos Buffalo Dairy)
entries.what: ricotta made from water buffalo milk by the Laos Buffalo Dairy.

entries.heading: Buffalo yoghurt (Laos Buffalo Dairy)
entries.what: yoghurt made from water buffalo milk, noted as richer than cow-milk yoghurt.

entries.heading: Bukovynskyi (Bukovyna cheese)
entries.what: hard Ukrainian cheese from Bukovyna (Chernivtsi area), per the List of cheeses.

entries.heading: Bukstiņputra (barley porridge with milk)
entries.what: Barley grits cooked with milk, potatoes and speck.

entries.heading: Bulgarian white brined cheese (Бяло саламурено сирене; sirene, сирене; Bulgarian sirene, "white brine cheese"; Serbian sir; Macedonian сирење; Albanian djathë i bardhë; English "white cheese")
entries.what: the Bulgarian national white cheese, the one Bulgarians mean by "сирене", used in shopska salad. It is the second most consumed traditional dairy product after yoghurt.

entries.heading: Bulgarian white cheese (industrial; Libanlait, Dairy Khoury)
entries.what: Libanlait lists "Bulgarian White Cheese"; Dairy Khoury lists "Bulgarian".

entries.heading: Bulgarian yoghurt (Namibia Dairies)
entries.what: A yoghurt listed in Namibia Dairies' yoghurt range.

entries.heading: Bulgarian yogurt
entries.what: A yogurt type introduced to Israel by Bulgarian Jewish Holocaust survivors. It is used to make tarator and other dishes.

entries.heading: Bündner Bergkäse (Bündner Bergkäse; Bergkäse, Alpkäse in German)
entries.what: A Graubünden mountain cheese named in the Swiss Bergkäse article. The page says it is made only in village dairies at altitudes above 1000 m.

name: Bündner Bergkäse, Röthenbacher Bergkäse, Glarner Alpkäse, Mutschli, Chällerhocker, Scharfe Maxx, Gala, Belper Hirn, Belper Knolle, Malakoff, Tomme

entries.heading: Bündner Bergkäse, Röthenbacher Bergkäse, Glarner Alpkäse, Mutschli, Chällerhocker, Scharfe Maxx, Gala, Belper Hirn, Belper Knolle, Malakoff, Tomme
entries.what: named Swiss cheese types from the lists; no production details were found for these in the pages opened.

entries.heading: Bundz (bundz; Polish)
entries.what: A mild sheep's-milk cheese from the Carpathian region of Poland and Ukraine, sharing its first steps with oscypek.

entries.heading: Burrata
entries.what: a fresh cheese with a solid mozzarella shell around a filling of stracciatella and cream.

entries.heading: Burrata di Andria (burrata, Burrata di Andria PGI)
entries.what: A fresh cheese with a mozzarella-like shell around a filling of stracciatella and cream. Originated in Puglia; the en.wikipedia article credits Lorenzo Bianchino of Piana Padura farm with developing it in 1956.

entries.heading: Burrata di bufala (PAT)
entries.what: A buffalo burrata listed as Lazio PAT.

entries.heading: Burrell' (scamorza con burro all'interno) (PAT)
entries.what: A scamorza with butter inside.

entries.heading: Burren Gold
entries.what: Gouda-style cheese; rounds hand-waxed; flavours include cumin, nettle and garlic, black pepper, piri piri and smoked.

entries.heading: Burrini di bufala (burrini e burrata di bufala)
entries.what: a Campanian buffalo cheese: a stretched-curd sheet wrapped around a ball of butter; burrini are more elongated, burrata has no top knot.

entries.heading: Burro centrifugato (centrifuged butter)
entries.what: butter from cream separated by centrifuge.

entries.heading: Burro composto (compound butter)
entries.what: softened butter mixed with herbs, garlic or anchovies.

entries.heading: Burro da siero (whey butter)
entries.what: butter from the fat remaining in whey from cheese making.

entries.heading: Burro di affioramento (cream-rise butter)
entries.what: most common Italian butter, made by letting cream rise from milk.

entries.heading: Burro di bufala (buffalo butter)
entries.what: butter from buffalo milk, a typical Campanian product.

entries.heading: Burro tradizionale (traditional butter, EU category)
entries.what: EU-defined category of butter made only from pasteurised cream; label in Italy is voluntary and needs authorisation.

entries.heading: Büscion (Büsciòn, Büsción)
entries.what: The Valle di Muggio's fresh cheese, kept somewhat longer than robiola; the name comes from a dialect word traced to French "bouchon" (cork), referring to its shape

entries.heading: Bush Pepper Cheddar (King Island Dairy, Tasmania)
entries.what: A King Island Dairy cheddar listed as "Bush Pepper Cheddar"; the name suggests a native pepper-berry flavouring (Tasmanian pepperberry), but the page does not say so.

entries.heading: Bushwacker (cocktail with milk or half-and-half)
entries.what: A creamy, chocolate-style blended cocktail. Dark rum, Kahlúa, dark crème de cacao and cream of coconut, with milk or half-and-half, plus ice.

entries.heading: Butter and butter oil (beurre; cow)
entries.what: Butter and butter oil made by a small share of milk-producing households in the Dakar, Thiès and Fatick survey (4% of participants produced other milk products such as butter, cheese or butter oil). Butter is also served with white rice in

name: Butter and condensed-milk toast; butter pineapple bun

entries.heading: Butter and condensed-milk toast; butter pineapple bun
entries.what: toast or buns eaten at cha chaan teng diners; toast is spread with butter or with condensed milk and butter/peanut butter; pineapple buns can be served with an optional slab of butter inside.

entries.heading: Butter and margarine on bread (consumed; origin unclear)
entries.what: Butter or margarine spread on bread, asked about as a food-frequency item in the questionnaire. The questionnaire names the brand Meadowlea as an example of a margarine.

name: Butter and milk-curds in early Khmer diet

entries.heading: Butter and milk-curds in early Khmer diet
entries.what: The Book of Sui's account of the 7th-century Chenla diet mentions a lot of butter and milk-curds.

entries.heading: Butter and other milk fats (imported)
entries.what: Butter and other fats and oils derived from milk, imported into Bermuda, valued at US$2.17 million from the United States in 2025.

entries.heading: Butter and smen (clarified butter)
entries.what: butter and smen (preserved clarified butter) are staples at Ramadan tables.

entries.heading: Butter crumble pastry (大甲奶油酥餅; Dajia butter crumble)
entries.what: A pastry from Dajia whose name refers to butter (奶油). Listed in the dessert section.

entries.heading: Butter spread
entries.what: A soft spread made from butter softened with canola oil (Anchor Spreadable); Westland also lists a butter-margarine blend spread.

entries.heading: Butter tart (tarte au beurre)
entries.what: a Canadian pastry, primarily eaten in English-speaking provinces; the filling is mainly butter, brown sugar, maple syrup and egg in a pastry shell, with raisins, walnuts or pecans often added.

entries.heading: Butter, industrial (масло сливочное)
entries.what: Factory butter and milk spread, separate from home-made sary may.

entries.heading: Butterkäse
entries.what: A mild, slightly tangy yellow semi-hard cheese; reportedly first produced in 1928 at the Staatliche Molkerei Weihenstephan; derived from the Italian Bel Paese.

name: Cà phê sữa chua, cà phê cốt dừa, cà phê bơ, cà phê lá dứa and sinh tố cà phê

entries.heading: Cà phê sữa chua, cà phê cốt dừa, cà phê bơ, cà phê lá dứa and sinh tố cà phê (milk-coffee variants)
entries.what: Newer café drinks that combine coffee with yoghurt, coconut cream, avocado, pandan or ice cream and condensed milk.

name: Cà phê sữa đá and cà phê sữa nóng

entries.heading: Cà phê sữa đá and cà phê sữa nóng (milk coffee with condensed milk)
entries.what: Robusta coffee brewed through a metal phin filter over a layer of sweetened condensed milk, stirred and poured over ice (iced) or with hot water (hot).

entries.heading: Cà phê trứng (egg coffee)
entries.what: Robusta coffee topped with a foam of egg yolk and condensed milk; from Hanoi.

entries.heading: Caano jallaato (milk ice pop)
entries.what: Mogadishu's version of jallaato, a milk-based ice pop made with milk and sugar.

entries.heading: Cabacinha
entries.what: a traditional stretched-curd cheese made in Minas Gerais (Pedra Azul, Cachoeira do Pajeú, Comercinho, Medina, Itaobim, per the review).

entries.heading: Cabécou du Périgord (cabécou)
entries.what: A small round goat cheese of the Périgord and the wider Massif central (Quercy, Rouergue, Haute-Auvergne, Bas-Limousin); the Périgord version is a collective-brand cheese.

entries.heading: Cabrinu
entries.what: Corsican cheese listed on the French cheese list.

entries.heading: Čačanski sir (Čačak cheese)
entries.what: a soft cheese from the Čačak area

entries.heading: Cacao con leche
entries.what: a cocoa drink made with milk, listed under drinks in the central region.

entries.heading: Cacciatello (cacciatello; Italian-language name, San Marino dessert)
entries.what: a dessert made from milk, sugar and eggs, described as similar to crème caramel.

entries.heading: Cachaille
entries.what: a strong fermented cheese from southeastern France, especially Puimichel, Provence and the Alpes du Sud; Reillanne is also named in its history.

entries.heading: Cachat (fort du Ventoux; Cachat du Comtat)
entries.what: a strong cheese from the Comtat Venaissin, on the foothills of Mont Ventoux (Vaucluse).

entries.heading: Cacio di fossa
entries.what: a pit cheese similar to pecorino.

entries.heading: Cacio di Genazzano (PAT)
entries.what: A sheep cacio from Genazzano (Roma).

name: Cacio di nonno Nino di Montalto di Castro

entries.heading: Cacio di nonno Nino di Montalto di Castro (PAT)
entries.what: A sheep cacio from Montalto di Castro (Viterbo).

entries.heading: Cacio figurato
entries.what: a Sicilian stretched-curd cheese, formed into decorative shapes.

name: Cacio figurato / Cacio ubriaco / Cacio ubriaco

entries.heading: Cacio figurato / Cacio ubriaco / Cacio ubriaco (Tuscany)
entries.what: named Italian cheese types; Cacio ubriaco in Tuscany.

entries.heading: Cacio fiore (PAT)
entries.what: A sheep cheese listed as Lazio PAT.

entries.heading: Cacio in forma di limone
entries.what: A Marche cheese given a lemon shape (cacio a forma di limone), listed as a traditional product.

entries.heading: Cacio magno (semplice e alle erbe) (PAT)
entries.what: A sheep cheese in plain and herb versions.

entries.heading: Cacio-ricotta (Molise proposal)
entries.what: A cheese-ricotta hybrid name ("cacio-ricotta") listed for Molise in the national table of traditional products.

entries.heading: Caciocapra
entries.what: A goat's-milk cheese of the Asiago plateau and Lusiana (Vicenza), a PAT product of Veneto. Made from the local tradition of goat herding (Alpine and Saanen breeds).

entries.heading: Caciocavallo abruzzese
entries.what: the Abruzzo entry in the table of traditional Italian agri-food products for caciocavallo.

entries.heading: Caciocavallo affumicato
entries.what: smoked caciocavallo made across inland Campania.

entries.heading: Caciocavallo di Agnone (caciocavallo di Agnone; Italian)
entries.what: A pear-shaped stretched-curd cheese made year-round in Molise, mainly in the comune of Agnone, and also in Abruzzo. It is recognised as a traditional food product (PAT) and in the Slow Food Ark of Taste; it has no DOP.

entries.heading: Caciocavallo di Castelfranco
entries.what: a stretched-curd cheese from the Miscano valley, named for the cheeses hung across wooden poles.

entries.heading: Caciocavallo di Ciminà (caciocavallo di Ciminà)
entries.what: A local caciocavallo named after the town of Ciminà, listed for Calabria.

entries.heading: Caciocavallo di Supino (PAT)
entries.what: A cow's-milk caciocavallo from Supino (Frosinone).

entries.heading: Caciocavallo palermitano (caciocavallo di Godrano; caciocavaddu palermitanu)
entries.what: a caciocavallo from the Palermo area, made mainly from native Cinisara cows; in its aged form it is grated over dishes, and it can be eaten fresh after about two weeks.

entries.heading: Caciocavallo siciliano (caciocavallo; caciocavaddu)
entries.what: an aged stretched-curd cheese from Sicily, historically spread across the former Kingdom of the Two Sicilies. Sold as several varieties, of which the palermitano and ragusano are the main Sicilian ones.

entries.heading: Caciocavallo vaccino (semplice e affumicato) (PAT)
entries.what: A cow's-milk caciocavallo.

entries.heading: Caciocchiato
entries.what: a semi-hard oval stretched-curd cheese from the Ariano Irpino area, Avellino.

entries.heading: Caciofiore (Caciofiore di Foggia; Caciofiore aquilano; Caciofiore della campagna romana)
entries.what: cheese curdled with a flower-based vegetable rennet; three named versions, from Puglia, Abruzzo and Lazio.

entries.heading: Caciofiore aquilano
entries.what: a cheese of the L'Aquila area in Abruzzo.

entries.heading: Cacioricotta caprino del Cilento
entries.what: a Cilento goat cheese, eaten fresh or aged for 3–4 months.

entries.heading: Cacioricotta di bufala (PAT)
entries.what: A buffalo cacioricotta, Lazio.

entries.heading: Caciotta al tartufo (truffle caciotta)
entries.what: A caciotta with truffle, made in Umbria.

entries.heading: Caciotta cepranese (PAT)
entries.what: A cow's-milk caciotta from the Ceprano area.

entries.heading: Caciotta degli Elimi
entries.what: a Sicilian semi-cooked sheep's-milk cheese from the Valle del Belice, named after the Elimi people of western Sicily; cylindrical with flat faces and a convex edge.

entries.heading: Caciotta dei Monti della Laga (PAT)
entries.what: A caciotta from the Monti della Laga, Lazio and Abruzzo border area.

entries.heading: Caciotta della Lunigiana
entries.what: caciotta from cow's milk, named for the Lunigiana.

entries.heading: Caciotta della Sabina (PAT)
entries.what: A sheep caciotta from the Sabina area.

entries.heading: Caciotta di Brugnato (Liguria, middle Val di Vara, province of La Spezia)
entries.what: a cylindrical cow's-milk cheese from the middle Val di Vara and throughout the province of La Spezia; produced year-round.

entries.heading: Caciotta di bufala Pontina (PAT)
entries.what: A buffalo caciotta from the Pontine plain, Latina province.

entries.heading: Caciotta di capra (Caciotta caprina)
entries.what: Goat caciotta made in Friuli Venezia Giulia.

name: Caciotta di latte di capra dell'Isola di Capraia

entries.heading: Caciotta di latte di capra dell'Isola di Capraia
entries.what: goat-milk caciotta from the island of Capraia (Tuscan archipelago).

entries.heading: Caciotta di mucca (PAT)
entries.what: A plain cow's-milk caciotta.

entries.heading: Caciotta di pecora
entries.what: sheep-milk caciotta.

entries.heading: Caciotta di vacca (Abruzzo)
entries.what: a cow's-milk caciotta listed among the Abruzzo cheeses.

entries.heading: Caciotta di vacca ciociara (semplice e aromatizzata) (PAT)
entries.what: A cow's-milk caciotta from the Ciociaria area (Frosinone).

entries.heading: Caciotta dolce (vacchino dolce)
entries.what: sweet caciotta from cow's milk.

entries.heading: Caciotta genuina romana (PAT)
entries.what: A cylindrical sheep's-milk caciotta, sweet when young and sharper when aged. Traditionally produced from October to June.

entries.heading: Caciotta mista ai bronzi (PAT)
entries.what: A mixed-milk caciotta from the Bronzi area.

entries.heading: Caciotta mista della Tuscia (PAT)
entries.what: A mixed caciotta from the Tuscia area of Viterbo, mildly sweet and newer in its tradition than Pecorino.

entries.heading: Caciotta mista ovi-vaccina del Lazio (PAT)
entries.what: A mixed sheep-and-cow caciotta made across the whole Lazio region.

entries.heading: Caciotta misto pecora
entries.what: A PAT cheese of Veneto made from mixed milk.

entries.heading: Caciotta Sarda
entries.what: Listed among Sardinian cheeses.

entries.heading: Caciotta stagionata (mucchino, vacchino)
entries.what: aged caciotta from cow's milk, also called mucchino or vacchino.

entries.heading: Caciotta vaccina al caglio vegetale
entries.what: A Montefeltro cheese in the Pesaro e Urbino province, made with vegetable rennet from artichoke or cardoon flowers. It is thought to be more digestible because plant enzymes break down protein more during ripening.

entries.heading: Caciottina canestrata di Sorrento
entries.what: a small cheese from the Sorrento peninsula, shaped in rush baskets (canestri), which give it its name.

entries.heading: Caciottina di bufala di Amaseno (semplice e aromatizzata) (PAT)
entries.what: A small buffalo caciotta from Amaseno, Frosinone.

entries.heading: Caciottina Montanara (Innichner Butterkäse, Formaggio al burro di San Candido)
entries.what: A small (about 600 g) butter-style table cheese with a thin edible straw-yellow rind and ivory paste with very small eyes.

entries.heading: Caciotto di Cirella di Platì (Caciotto di Cirella di Platì)
entries.what: A small cow's milk cheese from Cirella di Platì, listed for Calabria.

entries.heading: Caciottone di Norcia
entries.what: A caciotta-style cheese named after Norcia.

entries.heading: Cacık (yoghurt-cucumber dish)
entries.what: a cold meze of yoghurt with cucumber, olive oil, mint or dill, served in Türkiye and across former Ottoman lands; very close to Greek tzatziki.

entries.heading: Cadolet di capra (PAT)
entries.what: a goat cheese in a rectangular block, for table use and starters; production is limited.

entries.heading: Caerphilly (Caerffili)
entries.what: A hard, crumbly, mild, almost white cheese from the Caerphilly area of Wales, with a slight sour tang.

entries.heading: Café com leite
entries.what: Coffee with milk, described as a typical drink of Portugal and Brazil; widely drunk in the morning. Rural colonists mixed whole cow milk with brewed coffee. Industrial versions use powdered milk and instant coffee, and a ready-to-use produc

entries.heading: Caffè latte
entries.what: espresso with a larger volume of steamed milk, served in a glass (about 230 ml).

entries.heading: Cagliu
entries.what: Listed among Sardinian cheeses.

entries.heading: Cahill's (Ballintubber, Plain Porter, Ballinwood Smoked Cheddar)
entries.what: Ballintubber Cheese with Chives (black wax, chives); Plain Porter (brown wax, flavoured with Guinness); Ballinwood Smoked Cheddar; Vintage Cheddar.

entries.heading: Caillebotte Aunis
entries.what: A fresh curd cheese of Aunis, also listed for Brittany and Poitou.

entries.heading: Cajeta (cajeta de Celaya; goat-milk dulce de leche)
entries.what: A thick, caramel-coloured milk-and-sugar confection. In Mexico and some Central American countries, dulce de leche made with goat's milk is called cajeta. Cajeta de Celaya is named as a well-known Mexican version.

entries.heading: Cajeta de leche
entries.what: a milk sweet listed in the Nicaraguan desserts list. Cajeta is goat-milk dulce de leche in Mexico and some Central American countries.

entries.heading: Calinzanincu (Calenzana; Calinzanincu vecchju)
entries.what: Farmhouse cheese of the Calenzana area and neighbouring Balagne; about 400 g per unit; sharp, similar in character to Niolo cheeses; an older-style version is called Calinzanincu vecchju.

entries.heading: Callu (kid rennet)
entries.what: Kid's rennet made by filling a cleaned kid's stomach with its mother's milk, which curdles from enzymes in the stomach wall. Used to set cheese milk.

entries.heading: Calpis (カルピス)
entries.what: A Japanese probiotic milk drink sold as a concentrate, mixed with water or sometimes milk. Light, slightly milky and acidic, like plain or vanilla yogurt. Sold as Calpico in North America. Made by Calpis Co. (Asahi group).

entries.heading: Calpis Kids (カルピスキッズ)
entries.what: A milk-based lactic drink from Calpis, named as an example of the lower-dairy category; the source says it was formerly sold.

entries.heading: Cambozola
entries.what: a German blue cheese with a rich, creamy texture and a mild blue flavour, milder than Gorgonzola piccante. Patented by the German company Hofmeister-Champignon and produced since 1983; the name evokes the protected name Gorgonzola.

entries.heading: Camel cheese (experimental)
entries.what: cheese made from camel milk. In Ethiopia it is "largely experimental"; no traditional camel cheese was found.

entries.heading: Camel milk ice cream
entries.what: Camelait Premium Ice Cream from Al Ain Dairy, sold in 125 ml and 1-litre tubs in select UAE retail outlets, in six flavours: date, saffron, cardamom, chocolate, caramel and lite raspberry vanilla.

entries.heading: Camel milk products (fresh, fermented, powder, cheese; Arabic حليب الإبل)
entries.what: Camel milk products sold in Oman. A market report puts fresh camel milk at about 37% of camel-milk revenue, fermented camel milk at about 14% and powder at about 8%. It also names Watani Camel Milk (packaged fresh milk in Muscat retail outl

entries.heading: Camel milk, processed (Tiviski camel dairy)
entries.what: Camel milk produced and processed by the Tiviski dairy in Mauritania, described as one of the earliest camel milk dairy plants globally. Known mainly for camel cheese (Caravane), which is excluded here.

entries.heading: Camel yoghurt (Kenya, small-scale)
entries.what: small-scale camel-milk yoghurt, listed among Kenya's processed camel-milk products.

entries.heading: Camel-milk feta-type cheese (low-fat, 15% and 30% camel milk; research)
entries.what: Low-fat feta-type cheese made from bovine milk blended with camel milk. The 30% camel blend had higher moisture (61.50%, against 54.86% for bovine alone after 14 days' ripening). Camel-blend cheeses differed in texture and rheology, and the

name: Camel-milk laban with pectin or sodium alginate

entries.heading: Camel-milk laban with pectin or sodium alginate (research)
entries.what: Drinkable laban made from camel and bovine milk, with pectin (0.1–0.3%) or sodium alginate (0.1–0.5%) added. Camel labans were more acidic than bovine labans. Pectin did not change the camel laban's rheology; sodium alginate raised viscosit

entries.heading: Camel's milk (as drink)
entries.what: Camel's milk named as a traditional drink in Kyrgyzstan.

entries.heading: Camembert and smoked cheese (Strauss)
entries.what: Cheeses made by the Strauss Group, which turned surplus milk into cheese and made cheese its main business focus. In 1967 Strauss won awards for Camembert and smoked cheese at an Israeli food exhibition.

entries.heading: Camembert de Normandie (Camembert de Normandie AOC/AOP)
entries.what: a bloomy-rind cheese from Normandy, made under the protected name Camembert de Normandie.

entries.heading: Camembert-style cheese (monks' factories)
entries.what: A soft French-style cheese listed among the products of the Belgian monks' cheese factories in Masisi.

entries.heading: Campo de Montalbán
entries.what: A semi-hard pressed cheese from La Mancha with a blend of three milks, similar to Manchego in texture and flavour but with more noticeable goat and cow notes.

entries.heading: Canadian cheddar (Ontario and Quebec; cheddar as a Canadian style)
entries.what: Canadian cheddar, which grew after a mid-19th-century wheat midge outbreak pushed many Ontario farmers into dairying.

entries.heading: Canestrato di Moliterno (sheep and goat milk; PGI)
entries.what: A cheese from Moliterno in the province of Potenza, made from sheep and goat milk from free-range pasture animals. Name derives from Latin mulcternum, a place where milk was milked and coagulated.

entries.heading: Canestrato Fresco
entries.what: a historic Sicilian cheese, documented from the early 15th century, made by factories and small dairies; cylindrical, 1–2 kg, uniform texture, ivory-white.

entries.heading: Canestrato Pugliese (DOP)
entries.what: The PDO sheep cheese of Puglia, aged in traditional rush baskets, which leave the name and rind marks.

entries.heading: Canestrato vacchino
entries.what: a Sicilian hard cheese made mainly from cow's milk, produced throughout Sicily.

entries.heading: Canillitas de leche
entries.what: a sweet made with milk and shaped into thin sticks about 1 cm thick.

entries.heading: Cantabrian cream cheese (Queso de nata de Cantabria)
entries.what: Mild cow's-milk cheese from Cantabria, cream-style in character.

entries.heading: Cantal Entre-deux
entries.what: A variant of Cantal aged in the medium range ("entre-deux" means between the young and the old).

entries.heading: Capeta
entries.what: A cocktail with skim milk, named in the English Wikipedia "Brazilian cuisine" article.

entries.heading: Cappuccino
entries.what: espresso topped with equal parts steamed milk and milk foam.

entries.heading: Capreggio
entries.what: Swiss goat cheese whose name comes from the Italian word for goat.

entries.heading: Capricciu
entries.what: Corsican cheese listed on the French cheese list.

entries.heading: Capricho del Vispe
entries.what: a soft mould-rind cheese from Tarazona (Zaragoza), praised for its creamy texture.

entries.heading: Capricious
entries.what: An aged goat's-milk cheese.

entries.heading: Caprilo
entries.what: a cheese named on the Croatia list

entries.heading: Caprino a coagulazione lattica (Caprino a coagulazione lattica; PAT Lombardy)
entries.what: a very fresh, creamy goat cheese of 100–200 g from raw whole goat's milk, made in many Lombard provinces, recognised in the Lombardy traditional food list (PAT).

entries.heading: Caprino a coagulazione presamica (Caprino a coagulazione presamica; PAT Lombardy)
entries.what: a fresh, soft, sticky white goat cheese made with rennet, eaten with herbs, tomatoes, oil and salt.

entries.heading: Caprino al latte di fico
entries.what: A goat cheese in which fig latex (the milky sap of the fig tree) is used, listed as a traditional product.

entries.heading: Caprino da grattugia (Liguria; also Emilia-Romagna)
entries.what: a goat's cheese for grating, listed for Liguria and also for Emilia-Romagna.

entries.heading: Caprino dell'Aspromonte (Caprino dell'Aspromonte)
entries.what: Goat cheese from the Aspromonte mountains, listed for Calabria.

entries.heading: Caprino della Carnia
entries.what: Goat cheese from Carnia in hard and soft-paste forms.

entries.heading: Caprino della Val Vigezzo
entries.what: small cylinder, 300 g to 1 kg, from the Val Vigezzo, with a thin rind (ivory fresh, reddish or brown when aged).

entries.heading: Caprino della Valbrevenna (Val Brevenna, Genoa)
entries.what: a goat's cheese from the Valbrevenna valley, Genoa province. It is listed as a Ligurian PAT.

entries.heading: Caprino di capra / Ircano / Morello
entries.what: Ircano (Sardinian goat's-milk cheese); Morello (Tuscan ewe's-milk cheese with live lactic cultures).

name: Caprino di malga delle Alpi Marittime

entries.heading: Caprino di malga delle Alpi Marittime
entries.what: a goat's cheese from the Alpi Marittime mountain pastures, listed as a Ligurian PAT.

entries.heading: Caprino nicastrese (Caprino nicastrese)
entries.what: Goat cheese from the Nicastro area, listed for Calabria.

entries.heading: Caprino presamico (di latte vaccino) di Supino (PAT)
entries.what: A fresh cheese from Supino made with rennet.

entries.heading: Caprino stagionato
entries.what: Aged goat cheese from Friuli Venezia Giulia.

entries.heading: Caprino vaccino (Caprino vaccino; also Robiolino, Formaggino, Formaggella)
entries.what: a fresh, soft cheese made from cow's milk with lactic cultures and rennet, sold in 80–160 g cylinders; despite the name it contains no goat milk. Made in three versions: light, aged and fresh.

entries.heading: Capron
entries.what: a cheese named on the Croatia list

entries.heading: CAPSA dairy brands (Larsa, Ato, Innova, Vega de Oro)
entries.what: Brands of Corporación Alimentaria Peñasanta (CAPSA), a dairy group in Asturias.

entries.heading: Carabao (water buffalo) fresh milk
entries.what: Carabao milk is richer and creamier than cow or goat milk, with higher fat and protein and about twice the phosphorus of cow milk. Drunk as a drink, and sometimes poured over rice with other ingredients for breakfast or merienda.

entries.heading: Caramel au beurre salé (salted butter caramel sweet)
entries.what: A Breton confection of caramel made with lightly salted butter and nuts, invented in Quiberon in 1977.

entries.heading: Cardamom-spiced milk
entries.what: A glass of milk spiced with cardamom, often drunk before sleep.

entries.heading: Carlow Cheese (Edam-style washed curd, Carlow Farmhouse)
entries.what: Edam-style washed-curd cheese, some flavoured to go with the farm's sheep cheeses.

entries.heading: Carlow Farmhouse goat Tomme-style
entries.what: A new Tomme-style goat's cheese from the farm.

name: Carlow Farmhouse sheep cheddar-type and pecorino-style

entries.heading: Carlow Farmhouse sheep cheddar-type and pecorino-style
entries.what: Hard cheddar-type and pecorino-style cheeses from the farm's dairy sheep, matured up to two years.

entries.heading: Carmelo (carmadelo)
entries.what: A carabao-milk candy from Milagros, Masbate.

entries.heading: Carnia (cheese)
entries.what: Cheese named after the Carnic Alps area.

entries.heading: Carrageen pudding (Scotland)
entries.what: milk pudding thickened with seaweed (carrageen).

entries.heading: Carraig Bán
entries.what: A fresh goat's cheese from Dart Mountain Cheese, County Londonderry.

entries.heading: Carré d'Aurillac
entries.what: trademark cheese made in Saint-Flour, Cantal, by Les Fromageries occitanes (Toulouse-based company); name refers to Aurillac but was not produced there.

entries.heading: Carré de Bray
entries.what: named in the French Normandy cuisine article as a Normandy cheese, from the Bray area. No description opened.

entries.heading: Carré de Lavande (Mirasaka summer goat)
entries.what: A summer goat cheese from Mirasaka Fromage, topped or scented with lavender.

entries.heading: Carré de Rouez
entries.what: A Carré-named cheese from Sarthe, which the article says has disappeared.

entries.heading: Caș (caș; caș dospit; caș de păpuși in Negrilești, Vrancea)
entries.what: The base cheese of Romanian cheesemaking. Eaten fresh, or kept in brine it becomes telemea, and it is also the raw material for brânză de burduf and cașcaval.

entries.heading: Casa Grande de Xanceda yoghurt (yogur Casa Grande de Xanceda)
entries.what: Organic yoghurt from a farm in Mesía, A Coruña (Galicia).

entries.heading: Casàda (Casada)
entries.what: A fresh product from Primiero: tenza version tops a piece of fresh curd with semi-whipped cream; poina version uses fresh ricotta in place of the curd.

entries.heading: Casale de Elva (Tumo de Caso)
entries.what: fresh or aged cheese from Elva, Piedmont; resembles Castelmagno when aged.

entries.heading: Casareccio di Gorreto (Gorreto, Genoa)
entries.what: a farmhouse cheese of Gorreto, province of Genoa.

entries.heading: Casatella trevigiana (Casatella trevigiana DOP)
entries.what: A fresh, soft DOP cheese from the Treviso province, traditionally made by farm housewives in winter with the richest milk.

entries.heading: Casatta di Corteno Golgi (PAT)
entries.what: a straw-yellow cow's cheese from Corteno Golgi, Val Camonica, Province of Brescia, eaten with polenta.

entries.heading: Cașcavea
entries.what: A smoked cheese made from caș, linked to cașcaval.

name: Cascio pecorino lievito / pecorino fresco al latte crudo

entries.heading: Cascio pecorino lievito / pecorino fresco al latte crudo
entries.what: A traditional Marche sheep cheese made from raw milk, with a fresh version named in the list; the name combines the leavened and fresh forms.

entries.heading: Casecc
entries.what: A name in the regional list of traditional Marche cheeses. Nothing else is known from the sources I opened.

entries.heading: Casein and caseinates
entries.what: Milk protein used as an ingredient; sold by Fonterra's NZMP and Westland.

entries.heading: Caséine (casein)
entries.what: The main milk protein, precipitated from skimmed milk and sold as an industrial ingredient.

entries.heading: Casgiu merzu (casgiu marzu; lagrima)
entries.what: A Corsican fermented cheese in which fly larvae (Piophila casei) break down the fats, leaving a soft, tunnelled paste; the liquid it releases is called lagrima.

entries.heading: Cashel Blue (J&L Grubb, Co. Tipperary)
entries.what: hand-made semi-soft blue cheese with a creamy texture and mild, slightly acidic blue veining.

entries.heading: Cassava semolina with sweetened milk (couac et lait sucré)
entries.what: Toasted cassava meal (couac) served with sweetened milk, a dish named in French Guianese cuisine.

entries.heading: Casu axedu
entries.what: A traditional fresh cheese from rural Sardinia that its papers describe as recognised as a PAT product (MASAF, 2025). It is coagulated and fermented in its retail container, and the whey it releases stays in the pack and is eaten with the c

entries.heading: Casu Conzeddu
entries.what: Listed among Sardinian cheeses.

entries.heading: Casu de cabreddu
entries.what: Listed among Sardinian cheeses.

entries.heading: Casu Friscu (fresh cheese)
entries.what: A fresh goat cheese listed among Sardinian cheeses.

entries.heading: Casu furriau (melted cheese with saffron)
entries.what: A melted cheese with saffron, used on malloreddus.

entries.heading: Casu spiattatu
entries.what: Listed among Sardinian cheeses.

entries.heading: Cathare
entries.what: A goat cheese from Saint-Félix-Lauragais, Haute-Garonne, sold under the Cathare trademark of a farm company.

entries.heading: Cathedral City Cheddar
entries.what: a Cheddar cheese brand.

entries.heading: Cattle milk (Beninese indigenous breeds)
entries.what: milk from Beninese indigenous cattle, farmers describe it as appreciable; the dairy sector is low-productivity and depends on imports.

entries.heading: Catupiry
entries.what: one of the most popular brands of requeijão in Brazil; spread for toast, crackers, bread; filling for pizza, coxinha, pão de queijo, pastéis.

entries.heading: Caudle
entries.what: thick, sweet, usually alcoholic hot drink given to invalids and new mothers, from the Middle Ages to Victorian times.

entries.heading: Çaycuma manda yoğurdu (Çaycuma water buffalo yoghurt)
entries.what: a buffalo-milk yoghurt from Çaycuma, Zonguldak.

entries.heading: Cayolar
entries.what: A pastoral cheese of the Pyrénées-Atlantiques, named after the cayolar (mountain shelter).

entries.heading: Cazelle de Saint-Affrique
entries.what: A small soft sheep cheese from the Saint-Affrique area, processed in Saint-Affrique.

entries.heading: Cebreiro (Queixo do Cebreiro)
entries.what: A DO cheese made in Galicia's mountain municipalities around O Cebreiro (Baralla, Becerreá, Folgoso do Courel, Cervantes, Navia de Suarna, As Nogais, Triacastela, Pedrafita do Cebreiro). Pieces weigh 0.5–2 kg; output is about 20–28 tonnes a

entries.heading: Cendré de Champagne
entries.what: Ash-rind cheese from the Marne, listed on the list page.

entries.heading: Cendré de Niort
entries.what: An ash-coated cheese of the Niort area, Deux-Sèvres.

entries.heading: Centrale milk (industrial)
entries.what: Milk sold under the "Centrale" brand, one of the products of Centrale Danone, a Moroccan dairy company founded as Centrale Laitière.

entries.heading: Cer cheese (cerski sir)
entries.what: a cheese from the Cer mountain region

entries.heading: Cervelle de canut (claqueret, tomme daubée)
entries.what: Lyonnais spread from the silk-worker area, of the same family as sarasson.

entries.heading: Cetinski sir
entries.what: a cheese from the Cetina region (Dalmatia)

entries.heading: Cevrin di Coazze (Cevrin)
entries.what: alpine cheese from summer pastures in Val Sangone, Orsiera-Rocciavrè Natural Park, Torino province, Piemonte; March–September production.

entries.heading: Chaas / chhach / mattha / taak / ghol (छाछ, मट्ठा)
entries.what: Thin, lightly salted yoghurt drink made by churning dahi with cold water in a madhani. Its name comes from Sanskrit chacchika, churned yoghurt with butter removed. Sweet versions are close to lassi. Chaas is much more diluted than lassi (ar

entries.heading: Chabis
entries.what: A cheese of Poitou and Charentes.

entries.heading: Chagaa (чагаа; fermented curd)
entries.what: A fermented curd made from yellow whey, the step before aarts.

entries.heading: Chajá (postre chajá; cream-and-meringue cake)
entries.what: Layered dessert of meringue, sponge cake (bizcochuelo), cream and fruit (usually peaches or strawberries). Named after the chajá bird, its origin is Uruguay.

entries.heading: Chaka / chakka / chakida (sour cream or strained yogurt)
entries.what: a thick sour dairy product used to top dishes; Meiji calls it thickened doogh.

entries.heading: Chakka / chaka (Tajik чака; also suzma)
entries.what: thick sour curd eaten with flatbread at the start of a meal, eaten alone or as a condiment; drained-yoghurt family (suzma/strained yogurt).

entries.heading: Chalap / tan (чалап)
entries.what: A fizzy drink made from ayran (also sold as "tan"). The Ayran wiki lists "chalap" as an alternative name, and a Kyrgyz-language link titled "Чалап" exists.

entries.heading: Chalay (Mantaro de Huancayo, "Quesos de Autor")
entries.what: A matured cheese from Mantaro de Huancayo coated in powdered paprika.

entries.heading: Chalop (chalap, chalob; Kyrgyz chalap, Kazakh shalap)
entries.what: A chilled dairy drink made from qatiq or suzma, eaten as a light dish or beverage. In Uzbek preparations vegetables are added, which makes it look like a cold soup.

entries.heading: Chamcham (চমচম)
entries.what: a chhana-based sweet; Banglapedia attributes it to Tangail.

entries.heading: Chami
entries.what: A traditional Emirati cottage-style cheese, eaten with ghee and dates.

entries.heading: Champ (brúitín)
entries.what: Mashed potatoes with spring onions (or nettles or dillisk), butter and milk; customary with first new potatoes of harvest; eaten at Samhain.

entries.heading: Champorado (chocolate rice porridge)
entries.what: A sweet chocolate porridge made with sticky rice, eaten hot or cold at breakfast or merienda, often with salted dried fish such as daing or tuyo. A drizzle of milk or coconut milk is added with sugar.

entries.heading: Champurrado (chocolate atole, made with milk or water)
entries.what: A warm, thick chocolate drink made from masa or corn flour, served with churros in the morning and at Day of the Dead and Las Posadas with tamales.

entries.heading: Chanakh (Չանախ)
entries.what: A white, mild, brittle cheese with small holes, kept in brine and sold as a salty cheese.

entries.heading: Chancletas de güisquil
entries.what: halves of güisquil (chayote) filled with their own pulp mixed with milk, sugar, raisins, cinnamon, egg and crushed champurradas, then baked until golden.

entries.heading: Chanco (queso Chanco; Chanco cheese)
entries.what: A Chilean cheese from the Chanco farm and town in the Maule Region, now made across south-central Chile. Spanish Wikipedia says it is one of the most sold cheeses in Chile, after gouda-type cheeses, and mostly industrial now; English Wikipe

name: Chanco-style cheese with cow and goat milk

entries.heading: Chanco-style cheese with cow and goat milk (research, 2019)
entries.what: A study of Chanco-style cheese, "a traditional variety from Chile and produced with pasteurized cow milk", made with increasing shares of goat milk to test its effect on composition, texture and sensory properties.

entries.heading: Chandamour
entries.what: Named in the list of French cheeses with origin Loire-Atlantique, Pays de la Loire.

entries.heading: Changua
entries.what: A hearty breakfast soup of the Colombian Andes, a popular late-night meal and hangover remedy.

entries.heading: Channel Island (Jersey and Guernsey) gold-top milk
entries.what: milk from Jersey and Guernsey cows, sold in the UK as "gold-top milk" after its bottle cap.

entries.heading: Chapo (plantain drink)
entries.what: A drink of boiled sweet plantain blended into water, from the Shipibo and Matsés of the Peruvian Amazon. The Wikipedia version has no milk; a La República recipe adds one cup of milk.

entries.heading: Château-Blâmont
entries.what: A cheese tagged to Lorraine on the list page.

entries.heading: Chaudeau (chaudeau; Guadeloupean eggnog)
entries.what: A rich, eggnog-style drink made with milk or cream, served on special occasions. The Guadeloupean version is paired with a whipped sponge cake (génoise).

entries.heading: Chaumes
entries.what: A cow's-milk cheese made traditionally at Saint-Antoine-de-Breuilh in Périgord; name means stubble in French.

entries.heading: Chausudake (Japanese name not in sources; ash-dusted goat cheese)
entries.what: A goat cheese from Ima Farm in the Nasu Highlands, Tochigi, dusted with ash and pyramid-shaped.

entries.heading: Chaux d'Abel
entries.what: A hard cow's-milk cheese made in the village of Chaux-d'Abel at the foot of the Franches-Montagnes.

entries.heading: Cheddar and gouda (factory-made, Jakar)
entries.what: Western-style cheeses made at a factory called Swiss Cheese Factory in Jakar, or imported from India.

entries.heading: Cheese and curd (imported, general)
entries.what: Cheese and curd imported into Vanuatu, recorded in UN COMTRADE trade statistics; the category is not split by type.

entries.heading: Cheese cubes and sliced cheese (Luxlait Fromage en cubes, Fromage en tranche)
entries.what: Cheese cubes for appetizers and sliced cheese for sandwiches and hot or cold snacks, both sold by Luxlait.

entries.heading: Cheese lollipop (Fonterra fruit cream cheese)
entries.what: Fruit-flavoured cream cheese lollipop made in China by Fonterra from New Zealand cream cheese.

entries.heading: Cheese Okaki (チーズおかき, cheese rice cracker)
entries.what: A rice-cracker snack made with cheese, named this way by some Japanese makers.

entries.heading: Cheese on breakfast baguette (melted cheese)
entries.what: Melted cheese on breakfast baguette slices, presented in Wikipedia as a French-influenced dish.

entries.heading: Cheese roll (cheese-filled bread roll, a dish)
entries.what: A New Zealand snack, popular in Otago and Southland on the South Island, sold at cafeterias and food outlets, often with soup in winter; rarely found north of the Waitaki River.

entries.heading: Cheese roti prata (roti prata with cheese filling)
entries.what: Roti prata, the fried flatbread of Singapore, is often sold with a cheese filling, one of several sweet and savoury variants alongside onion, banana, red bean, chocolate, mushroom and egg.

entries.heading: Cheese Stand fresh cheeses (Cheese Stand, Shibuya)
entries.what: Fresh cheeses made in front of customers at Cheese Stand, a shop in Shibuya, Tokyo.

entries.heading: Cheese tea (cheese foam tea; 奶盖茶 / naigai cha)
entries.what: Cold brewed tea (green or black) topped with a salted or sweetened whipped cream-cheese foam, like a mascarpone-style cap.

entries.heading: Cheeses cured in olive oil (aceite)
entries.what: a preparation found in several Aragonese dairies.

entries.heading: Chef-Boutonne
entries.what: A cheese of the Chef-Boutonne area, Deux-Sèvres (Poitou).

entries.heading: Chemin de fer (roll cake with vanilla cream)
entries.what: a rolled cake filled with vanilla cream and covered in red-coloured sugar.

entries.heading: Chere (saay)
entries.what: A Serer millet dish, described as a favourite Serer food, eaten for breakfast with fermented milk, or with cream and sugar, much like a cereal.

entries.heading: Cherni Vit (Зелено сирене "Черни Вит"; green cheese, Cherni Vit cheese)
entries.what: a green cheese from the village of Cherni Vit, Teteven municipality, Lovech province, north-central Bulgaria.

entries.heading: Chèvre (Phukamyao)
entries.what: fresh goat cheese made by a family goat farm in northern Thailand. The article names it among the farm's fresh products from June 2016.

entries.heading: Chèvre du Mont-Ventoux
entries.what: a small goat cheese from the foot of Mont Ventoux.

entries.heading: Chèvre du Poitou
entries.what: A goat cheese of the Poitou.

entries.heading: Chèvre noir (Chesterville, Quebec)
entries.what: A goat's-milk firm cheese in the style of cheddar, made by Fromagerie Tournevent.

entries.heading: Chèvreton
entries.what: cheese of the Massif central, sold at local markets.

entries.heading: Chevrotin des Aravis
entries.what: A goat cheese variant of Chevrotin from the Aravis area in Haute-Savoie.

entries.heading: Chevru (Chevru)
entries.what: a cheese of the Brie area that was nearly vanished by the 1950s; the Fougerus article describes it as the model for that cheese.

entries.heading: Chhana murki / chhena murki (छेना मुरकी)
entries.what: Cubes of chhena (paneer) simmered in syrup, then dried and coated with sugar.

entries.heading: Chhena poda (ছেনাপোড়া; ଛେନାପୋଡ଼)
entries.what: Odisha's baked chhena sweet, named "burnt cheese" in Odia.

entries.heading: Chhurpi, hard (छुर्पी; durkha, chogo/chugo; other names: chhurpi cheese)
entries.what: A hard cheese traditionally made from the buttermilk left after butter-making in the Himalayan regions of Nepal, Bhutan, Tibet and parts of NE India. Today also made commercially; mostly sold as cubes and sticks, largely as dog chews, and e

entries.heading: Chicha de arroz (chicha de arroz; chicha de pasta)
entries.what: A sweet white drink with the consistency of eggnog, served as a refreshing beverage; not fermented.

entries.heading: Chicheme (chicheme; maize drink with milk)
entries.what: A drink of maize with milk and sugar, flavoured with spices.

entries.heading: Chigee (чигээ; Inner Mongolian name for mare's milk drink)
entries.what: The Inner Mongolian (China) name for a fermented mare's milk drink, closely related to airag. The sources studied are from Xilin Gol, China, not from the Mongolian state.

entries.heading: Chilean kefir beverage (kefir from Chile)
entries.what: Kefir beverages from Chile, studied as household-origin grains from the Valparaíso Region; the beverage is made by fermenting milk with kefir grains, separated by percolation.

entries.heading: Chilled dairy desserts (fromage frais, quark)
entries.what: Chilled dairy desserts and fromage frais and quark, sold as chilled snacks.

entries.heading: Chimay (Grand Cru; Chimay with beer; Grand Classic; Old Chimay)
entries.what: Cheeses made by the Trappist monastery at Scourmont Abbey (Chimay) since 1876. Four varieties offered as of 2010, including a beer-washed cheese and a hard, aged "Old Chimay".

entries.heading: Chimombe Long Life Milk (Dairibord)
entries.what: A Dairibord milk product listed as "Chimombe Long Life Milk".

entries.heading: Chipinge factory cheese (name not recorded; Chipinge, Manicaland)
entries.what: Cheese made in factories at Chipinge: two cheese factories were in operation by 1931, a third opened in 1945 and was amalgamated the same year into one large factory, and cheese production there continued until 1976.

entries.heading: Chiquián (queso chiquián)
entries.what: A named Peruvian cheese type listed among the 50 varieties at the 2023 Lima cheese salon, with no description.

entries.heading: Chistabín (queso chistabino)
entries.what: a cheese from the Chistau valley (Gistaín, Huesca), named in the regional guide as one of the best-known Aragonese cheeses.

entries.heading: Chitrali cottage cheese (local name not given in sources)
entries.what: The cottage cheese used as the main filling in Chitrali and Kho (Khowar) flatbreads. It is the base of ghalmandi and phenak tikki.

entries.heading: Chöbögö / tybyt (чөбөгө, тыбыт)
entries.what: Sediment that forms when butter is boiled; protein-rich. Sometimes honey or sugar is added. Some regions call it tybyt. Kyrgyz Wikipedia (Курут) says tybyt (chöbögö) is added to kurut.

entries.heading: Chocolate a la taza (chocolate a la taza; chocolate espeso)
entries.what: A thick hot chocolate drink made from a chocolate tablet with flour (rice or corn starch) added for body.

entries.heading: Chocolate caliente / chocolate santafereño (hot chocolate with cheese)
entries.what: Hot chocolate made with milk and water and semi-sweet chocolate bars; in Bogotá (chocolate santafereño) served with cheese (queso) on the side or in the cup.

entries.heading: Chocolate de maní (peanut chocolate drink)
entries.what: A hot drink of peanut, milk, corn, sugar, spices and sometimes rum.

entries.heading: Chocolate milk and flavoured milk
entries.what: Milk sweetened and flavoured with cocoa or other flavours; in US schools a long-running issue.

entries.heading: Chocolate tea (hot chocolate, called "tea")
entries.what: In Jamaica, hot chocolate is called "tea", because the morning drink is called tea there.

entries.heading: Chocomel
entries.what: A trademarked chocolate milk, sold mainly in the Netherlands. "Chocomel" is often used in everyday speech for chocolate milk in general.

entries.heading: Chogi (ჩოგი)
entries.what: a piquant, yellowish sheep cheese from Tusheti, made mainly in July and August; up to 60% moisture, at least 50% fat in dry matter, 2–4% salt; keeps over 12 months at up to +12 °C.

entries.heading: Cholob (Tajik чолоб)
entries.what: katyk diluted in cold boiled water with ice cubes and apple pieces.

entries.heading: Chongos zamoranos (chongos zamoranos)
entries.what: A Mexican dessert of curdled milk, giving a soft, cheese-like curd in a sweet brown milky syrup; its origin is attributed to colonial-era convents in Zamora, Michoacán.

entries.heading: Chorotani (ჩოროთანი)
entries.what: curd (khacho) formed from boiled whey, served with leftover boiled butter.

entries.heading: Chortan (չորթան; also kashk in Armenian-cuisine references)
entries.what: The Armenian name for dried yogurt or dried curd, the Caucasus form of kashk. Dry, hard and white; formed into balls, strips or chunks.

entries.heading: Chortan (չորթան; chort'an, charathan)
entries.what: Dried balls kept as a winter food. Armenian name, in the Armenian dairy list and in the Wikipedia infobox. Called a form of kashk on English Wikipedia.

entries.heading: Choukalig (Musa Dagh)
entries.what: A traditional cheese made from curds, from the Musa Dagh (Armenian village community in the Hatay region, now Turkey).

entries.heading: Chugum (Tibetan dried curd beads)
entries.what: Tiny, very hard dried curd kernels, strung like beads, eaten as a travel snack.

entries.heading: Chukkoo (Oromo sweet whole-grain dish)
entries.what: sweet whole-grain dish seasoned with butter and spices.

entries.heading: Chukulati di pinda (Bonaire)
entries.what: A peanut-and-chocolate drink, listed as a drink in Bonaire's Kuminda Krioyo cuisine.

entries.heading: Chukwi (chukuwi; camel or cow milk)
entries.what: A cheese popular in northern Nigerian states bordering Niger; eaten with dates in some places and considered nourishing (protein, calcium, fat). Recommended for children under 15 and people who want to gain weight, not those trying to lose

entries.heading: Chülü (чүлү)
entries.what: Jam of kurut and dried apricot, found mainly in Batken oblast. Locals tell stories of its health properties.

entries.heading: Chura (general term, 曲拉 family)
entries.what: The general name for Tibetan nomadic cheeses, made each summer by adding acid to milk and dried to last the year.

entries.heading: Chura kampo (Tibetan hard cheese)
entries.what: Tibetan hard cheese, mentioned in the cuisine article.

entries.heading: Chura loenpa (Tibetan buttermilk curd, also ser)
entries.what: Soft curds like cottage cheese made from buttermilk.

entries.heading: Churgot (чургот)
entries.what: described as a sour product made by fermentation; nothing further in sources read.

entries.heading: Chuship (Tibetan dri yak cheese)
entries.what: Crumbly yak cheese from Tibet, mixed with tsampa and tea or added to noodle soup.

entries.heading: Chuto (Nepali yak cheese product)
entries.what: One of the yak cheese products listed by the Nepal yak-milk review alongside chhurpi and hapiruto.

entries.heading: Ciambella di Morolo (PAT)
entries.what: A cow's-milk ring cheese from Morolo (Frosinone).

entries.heading: Cicvara (цицвара)
entries.what: a cornmeal dish in which kajmak is the main fat and flavour; served hot, sometimes with honey.

entries.heading: Cijeli sir (whole cheese; Цијели сир)
entries.what: "whole cheese" (cijeli sir), a Montenegrin cheese listed in the cheese section of Montenegrin cuisine.

entries.heading: Cilentana goat cheese (formaggio caprino del Cilento; study cheese)
entries.what: a goat cheese from a Cilento dairy farm, studied for its composition and microbiology.

entries.heading: Cincar cheese (Cincarski sir)
entries.what: A cow's-milk cheese from the Cincar and Livno areas, recognised by the producers' association.

entries.heading: Cincho (fresh cheese)
entries.what: a fresh Aragonese cheese type (Cincho), made in Sieso and El Burgo de Ebro; La Val makes a cured variant with truffle paté.

entries.heading: Cioccolata calda (Italian thick hot chocolate)
entries.what: thick, creamy hot chocolate; tradition says it dates to about 1560 in Turin.

entries.heading: Citronfromage and romfromage
entries.what: Danish lemon custard topped with whipped cream; rum variant romfromage.

entries.heading: Civray
entries.what: A cheese from the Civray area of the Vienne.

name: Clarified butter and curd in Angkorian Cambodia

entries.heading: Clarified butter and curd in Angkorian Cambodia
entries.what: Cows and their dairy, including curd and clarified butter, appear often in Angkorian inscriptions. They were used as sacred offerings, in royal and funerary rites, and in medicine.

entries.heading: Clonmore
entries.what: hard goat's-milk cheese with a beige waxed rind; mild and sweet when young, stronger with age.

entries.heading: Cocada com leite condensado (cocada branca; cocada de colher)
entries.what: Brazilian white cocada is grated coconut with sugar and water, sometimes with condensed milk, sold in bar form or as a spoon sweet ("de colher"). Variants elsewhere use egg yolks, whole milk or coconut milk.

entries.heading: Cocadas (condensed-milk coconut candy)
entries.what: A coconut candy rolled and made with a condensed-milk base.

entries.heading: Cocido (raw-milk cocido cheese)
entries.what: A raw-milk fresh cheese of Sonora family makers with a cooked curd; had low microbial load in the survey.

entries.heading: Cocido con leche (mate cocido with milk)
entries.what: Mate cocido, a hot infusion of yerba mate and sugar, drunk with milk.

entries.heading: Cocoa tea (local name not found; condensed milk)
entries.what: A hot drink made from cocoa, with condensed milk, spices and sugar.

entries.heading: Coconut ice cream (Kriol dessert)
entries.what: a coconut-flavoured ice cream listed among Kriol coconut desserts

entries.heading: Coconut tart (condensed milk filling)
entries.what: a shortcrust pastry filled with grated coconut, condensed milk, nutmeg, vanilla and sugar, then baked until golden

entries.heading: Cœur de Neufchâtel
entries.what: The heart-shaped form of Neufchâtel from the Pays de Bray; AOC since 1969.

entries.heading: Cœur du Berry
entries.what: named as a Berry (Centre) cheese.

entries.heading: Cofanetto
entries.what: a square block cheese from the Trapani province, named after Monte Cofano and not its shape.

entries.heading: Coffee cream (crème à café)
entries.what: Cream sold by Luxlait for softening and reducing the bitterness of coffee.

name: Coffee with butter or niter kibbeh

entries.heading: Coffee with butter or niter kibbeh (buna)
entries.what: Gurage coffee served with butter; in parts of Ethiopia niter kibbeh replaces sugar or salt in coffee. Ghee is served with coffee and tea to guests.

entries.heading: Çökelek
entries.what: Dried cottage cheese with many regional varieties.

entries.heading: Colby (Colby; Longhorn for the traditional cylindrical form)
entries.what: A mild cheddar relative with an open, washed-curd texture that melts well.

entries.heading: Colby-Jack (Co-Jack, Cojack, marble jack)
entries.what: A marble cheese made by combining Colby and Monterey Jack; mild, with a two-week ageing period per the infobox.

entries.heading: Cold pack cheese
entries.what: A spread made from cheese with spices, fruits, vegetables or nuts added; the infobox dates it to c. 1930.

entries.heading: Coleraine Cheddar (Coleraine Cheddar; Coleraine Mature White, Medium and Mild White Cheddar; Royal Canadian Mature Cheddar)
entries.what: A hard, pasteurised cheddar from cow's milk, named after the town of Coleraine, County Londonderry. Ages about three to four months, depending on variety.

entries.heading: Colorado Blackie
entries.what: A Western US cheese, as listed.

entries.heading: Colostrum and lactoferrin
entries.what: Bioactive ingredients from colostrum (first milk) and lactoferrin, used in nutrition products.

entries.heading: Çömlek peyniri (çömlek cheese)
entries.what: A typical artisanal cheese of Central Anatolia.

entries.heading: Commercial cheese, Sylhet (twelve brands, types not named)
entries.what: twelve commercially available cheese brands bought in ten batches from retail outlets in Sylhet, sampled for Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) in a 2026 study.

name: Commercial sour milk and sour cream

entries.heading: Commercial sour milk and sour cream
entries.what: Sour milk, sour cream and other modern milk variants sold in South African supermarket dairy sections. Sour milk is described as somewhat like yoghurt and a dietary staple before refrigeration.

entries.heading: Commissiekaas (Dutch Mimolette)
entries.what: A Dutch ball-shaped cheese, orange to orange-red, the origin of the French Mimolette. Weighs 3–4.5 kg.

name: Communal milk at the end of meals

entries.heading: Communal milk at the end of meals
entries.what: at the end of traditional meals a communal vessel (guerba) containing spring water or milk passes around those eating.

entries.heading: Component-adjusted, low-fat and non-fat milk (成分調整牛乳, 低脂肪乳, 無脂肪乳)
entries.what: Milks whose fat or solids are changed. 成分調整牛乳 (component-adjusted) has some components removed or concentrated, with non-fat solids at least 8%; low-fat is 0.5–1.5% fat; non-fat is under 0.5%. Created as a category in 2002; 2–3% fat version

entries.heading: Compromiso de Caspe
entries.what: a named cheese from Caspe (Zaragoza), made by Quesos Los Arcos.

entries.heading: Comtesse de Vichy
entries.what: commercial brand from the Montagne bourbonnaise.

entries.heading: Conciato di San Vittore (PAT)
entries.what: A sheep cheese from San Vittore (Frosinone).

entries.heading: Conlloc (Casa Raubert mature cheese)
entries.what: One of the three mature cheeses from Casa Raubert, named with Orri and Pletiu.

name: Consumer milks: standardmjölk, mellanmjölk, lättmjölk, minimjölk

entries.heading: Consumer milks: standardmjölk, mellanmjölk, lättmjölk, minimjölk (heat-treated)
entries.what: The standard Swedish drinking milk is 3% fat (3.5% in the rest of the EU); the oldest type, introduced during the Second World War to give more cream for butter. Lower-fat grades are mellanmjölk (green pack), lättmjölk (blue pack) and minim

entries.heading: Cooked mabisi
entries.what: a type that is cooked after sieving. One of the seven national types, under 5 per cent of respondents.

entries.heading: Coolea
entries.what: hard, sweet, caramel-flavoured Gouda-type cheese with a smooth texture, coated in a thick wax rind.

entries.heading: Cooleeney Farmhouse Cheese
entries.what: soft, smooth farmhouse cheese made by the Maher family.

entries.heading: Coquetdale
entries.what: A Northumberland cheese.

entries.heading: Coquito
entries.what: A creamy, spiced Christmas drink made with coconut and canned milks and rum, which the source says originated in Puerto Rico.

entries.heading: Corfu sheep-and-goat brine cheese (retail sample)
entries.what: soft brine cheese from Corfu, bought at a Greek retail outlet and analysed for composition in a survey of non-PDO Greek cheeses.

entries.heading: Corn pilhi (corn and sweet potato bake, polenta cooked in milk)
entries.what: A baked corn and sweet potato dish that the SBS recipe page says comes from Norfolk Island. The mixture is cooked in milk and set with cheddar, then baked until crisp.

entries.heading: Cornilly
entries.what: named as a Centre cheese.

entries.heading: Cornish Blue
entries.what: A blue cheese from Cornwall.

entries.heading: Cornish ice cream
entries.what: ice cream that originated in Cornwall, traditionally made with clotted cream.

name: Cornmeal porridge with milk and condensed milk

entries.heading: Cornmeal porridge with milk and condensed milk (local name not found)
entries.what: A breakfast porridge made from fine cornmeal (polenta-like) with milk, sweetened condensed milk and sugar.

entries.heading: Cortadito (cortadito)
entries.what: A sweetened Cuban espresso "cut" with steamed milk, a pre-sweetened cortado; popularised by Cuban immigrants in South Florida.

entries.heading: Cortado de leche (dulce de cortado)
entries.what: A sweet made from curdled milk ("cortado"); in Bucaramanga metro area "cortados de leche", in Cúcuta a goat-milk version ("cortados de leche de cabra"); Valle del Cauca has "dulce de cortado".

entries.heading: Cosacavaddu ibleo (cosacavaddu rausanu; caciocavallo ibleo)
entries.what: a traditional cheese of the Iblean area, the same type as Ragusano but not made to the DOP specification.

entries.heading: Cossol (Casa Raubert fresh cheese)
entries.what: A fresh cheese from Casa Raubert, named among its fresh cheeses.

entries.heading: Costeña
entries.what: A cheese of Guerrero that tastes of fresh or slightly soured milk.

entries.heading: Cotija (queso Cotija, Cotija de Montaña)
entries.what: A hard grating cheese from the mountains of Michoacán and Jalisco; compared to Parmesan when aged, to feta when young.

entries.heading: Cougar Gold
entries.what: An aged sharp cheddar sold in cans.

entries.heading: Couhé-Vérac
entries.what: A cheese of the Couhé-Vérac area, Vienne.

entries.heading: Coulommiers fermier (Coulommiers fermier)
entries.what: a farm-made Coulommiers listed on the French list of cheeses under "pays briard".

entries.heading: Country butter (farmhouse butter)
entries.what: Hand-made butter once made in nearly every farmhouse with cows, usually by the farmer's wife; revived as premium "country butter."

entries.heading: Country cheese (Wase and Wawa/Zange grazing reserves; Plateau and Bauchi States)
entries.what: A hard cow's-milk cheese introduced by a UNDP/FAO rural-development project in grazing reserves; listed in FAO's cheese catalogue as a Nigerian country cheese.

name: Country Goodness sour cream dips and butter-margarine spread

entries.heading: Country Goodness sour cream dips and butter-margarine spread
entries.what: Consumer dairy products under the Country Goodness brand in NZ, listed in the Fonterra article.

entries.heading: Country Life and Utterly Butterly (butter)
entries.what: UK butter brands named in the Dairy Crest article.

entries.heading: Couronne lochoise
entries.what: named as a Loches (Indre-et-Loire) cheese.

entries.heading: Coussignous
entries.what: a strong, pungent cheese originally made in Signes, Var.

entries.heading: Cousteron
entries.what: Named in the list of French cheeses; the entry mixes Sablé (Sarthe) and Cléry (Meuse).

name: Cow milk and butter from historic herd cattle

entries.heading: Cow milk and butter from historic herd cattle (unnamed)
entries.what: The Falklands cattle-history page says that some herd cows were kept for milk production, and that the milk was made into cheese and butter. No milk product is named and no date or place is given.

entries.heading: Cow milk, UHT (shelf-stable)
entries.what: cow's milk sold as UHT, one of the top milk items in the diets of young children in rural Lao PDR.

entries.heading: Cow-milk feta-type brined cheese (Albanian product)
entries.what: a feta-type brined cheese made in Albania from pasteurised cow milk, sampled in a 2026 hygiene study. Only the sampled product is known; no name is given beyond the feta-type category.

entries.heading: Cow's milk from farm herds (historical; Longyearbyen, Pyramiden, Barentsburg)
entries.what: Milk from dairy cattle kept on the settlement farms of Svalbard. The herds were a small-scale local supply that ended with the farms.

name: Cow's milk given to infants as a supplement

entries.heading: Cow's milk given to infants as a supplement (Jonglei, pre-lacteal and after 6 months)
entries.what: Cow's milk is the most common supplement given to infants in the first six months, alongside water and cereal porridge. Given early in place of, or alongside, breastmilk.

entries.heading: Cow's milk, raw (farm and informal)
entries.what: Unpasteurised milk bought from farms or informal sellers, the most common milk in a Morocco brucellosis survey.

name: Cracker Barrel, Mersey Valley and CHEER cheddars

entries.heading: Cracker Barrel, Mersey Valley and CHEER cheddars (Saputo brands)
entries.what: Cheddar cheeses sold under the Cracker Barrel, Mersey Valley and CHEER brands of Saputo Dairy Australia.

entries.heading: Cranachan
entries.what: traditional Scottish dessert of whipped cream, toasted oats soaked in whisky, honey and raspberries.

entries.heading: Cream butter (сметанковае масла; vyarshkovae masla)
entries.what: A butter made by separating or churning the cream of cow's milk. Sour cream butter is made from soured cream; sweet cream butter from fresh cream.

entries.heading: Cream in brandaminciun (crème, used in cooking)
entries.what: Cream is one of the ingredients of brandaminciun, a traditional salted-cod dish.

entries.heading: Cream soda with milk (忌廉溝鮮奶)
entries.what: A drink popular in the 1970s in Hong Kong, combining cream soda and fresh milk.

entries.heading: Cream tea (cream with scones)
entries.what: Scones served with cream and jam, which the NZ cuisine article says were served in tearooms until the 1990s and have since gone out of fashion.

name: Cream, clotted cream and cream tea

entries.heading: Cream, clotted cream and cream tea (Devonshire tea)
entries.what: Cream served with scones and jam in a "cream tea" (Devonshire tea). Cream teas spread to southern Australia with early immigrants from Cornwall and Devon.

entries.heading: Cream: single, double, whipping (UK fat grades)
entries.what: the standard British cream types, sold by fat content.

entries.heading: Creamer (coffee whitener)
entries.what: Coffee whitener sold in the Cambodian dairy market.

entries.heading: Creamjam (ক্রিমজাম)
entries.what: sweetmeat named in the 2025 Bogura survey; priced BDT 700/kg.

entries.heading: Creamy mabisi
entries.what: a type that keeps cream in the product. It is one of the seven national method types but found only in small proportion (less than 5 per cent of respondents).

entries.heading: Crema a l'andorrana (Andorran-style cream)
