entries.what: A milk custard with lemon and cinnamon, topped with sugar that is burnt with a hot iron. Presented on visitandorra.com as the Andorran version of crème brûlée.

entries.heading: Crema Dania (Crema Danica)
entries.what: a rich Danish soft cheese, nearly high enough in fat to be called a triple cream.

entries.heading: Cremă de zahăr ars (burnt sugar cream)
entries.what: A dessert made from eggs, sugar and milk, with caramel; the Romanian article gives the origin as France but lists it among Romanian sweets.

entries.heading: Crema del Friuli (Crema del Cuc)
entries.what: Cream cheese made in Friuli; "Crema del Cuc" is a variant name on the EN list.

entries.heading: Crema pasticcera (Italian pastry custard)
entries.what: thick custard of milk, egg yolks, sugar and usually vanilla or lemon, used in cakes and desserts.

entries.heading: Crema volteada (flan-style milk custard, "turned cream")
entries.what: A Peruvian caramel custard close to flan, made with evaporated and condensed milk and eggs; it is turned out of its mould after chilling. Compared to a quesillo or condensed-milk flan.

entries.heading: Crème anglaise (custard sauce)
entries.what: A sweet, pourable milk-egg custard flavoured with vanilla, lemon or orange; origin French or English per the source.

entries.heading: Crème brûlée
entries.what: A baked custard with a hardened caramel top.

entries.heading: Crème caramel (crème renversée)
entries.what: A baked custard served with a clear caramel sauce.

entries.heading: Crème catalane (Catalan cream, Roussillon)
entries.what: A custard flavoured with lemon zest and cinnamon, with a caramelised sugar top; called a traditional dessert of French Catalonia (Languedoc-Roussillon).

entries.heading: Crème d'Isigny AOP
entries.what: A Normandy cream with a protected name (AOP since 1986 per the source), made by slow traditional maturation and sold thick or fluid.

entries.heading: Crème de Bresse AOP
entries.what: A thick or semi-thick crème fraîche from the Bresse area with a protected name.

entries.heading: Crème de Chapelain
entries.what: A local processed cheese specialty of Luxembourg, named in the Luxembourg section of the List of cheeses.

name: Crème double, crème épaisse, crème fleurette

entries.heading: Crème double, crème épaisse, crème fleurette (creams sold by fat level)
entries.what: French cream grades by fat content: crème double (thick, high fat), crème épaisse, and fluid crème fleurette, used whipped or in cooking.

entries.heading: Crème fleurette
entries.what: A liquid pasteurised cream used by professionals; not matured or sterilised.

entries.heading: Crème fraîche fluide d'Alsace (IGP)
entries.what: A fluid crème fraîche with a protected geographical name from Alsace.

entries.heading: Crème pâtissière (pastry cream)
entries.what: A thick milk-egg-sugar custard used as a French pastry base in éclairs, mille-feuilles and tarte tropézienne; attributed in the source to François Massialot (1691).

entries.heading: Crémet nantais
entries.what: A fresh cheese from the pays nantais, eaten cold, often with fruit or compote. Variants add lemon and mint, or fines herbes. Close in composition to the crémet d'Anjou.

entries.heading: Crémeux du Puy
entries.what: A cow's-milk cheese from Auvergne (Haute-Loire), with a cendré rind and persillé soft paste.

entries.heading: Creole cream cheese
entries.what: A Louisiana dairy cheese associated with New Orleans.

entries.heading: Crispy Cheese (Niseko Fromage)
entries.what: A cheese sold by Niseko Fromage, listed in a Hokkaido product roundup.

entries.heading: Crottin de Berry
entries.what: a Berry (Centre) crottin.

entries.heading: Croupet (Croupet)
entries.what: a cheese listed for Seine-et-Marne, Île-de-France.

entries.heading: Crozier Blue
entries.what: sheep's-milk blue cheese made by the Grubb family's daughter, Sarah Furno, at the same farm as Cashel Blue.

entries.heading: Cuajada / quesillo (curd dessert with honey, Loja)
entries.what: a curd served as a dessert with honey (miel) in the southern Loja Province; the Wikipedia cuisine page calls it "quesillo" or "cuajada".

entries.heading: Cuallà (cuajada de Morella)
entries.what: A curd served as a dessert at Corpus Christi and Virgen de Agosto celebrations in Morella (Castellón).

entries.heading: Çuç di mont
entries.what: Friulian mountain cheese named "Çuç di mont" (the "cuç" is a dialect word; the EN list gives the name as "Çuç di mont").

entries.heading: Cuincir
entries.what: Local Friulian cheese name.

entries.heading: Culture Collection Oshitaka (Oshitaka; other names: Oshitaka Vanilla)
entries.what: A Namibia Dairies brand in its "Culture Collection" range, with a limited-edition 500 g Vanilla flavour and new packaging.

entries.heading: Cup cheese
entries.what: A Pennsylvania Dutch spread; a variation of German Kochkäse.

entries.heading: Curau
entries.what: A Brazilian dessert combining a European pudding and a Tupi drink, made from fresh corn cream, sugar and cinnamon in cow milk or coconut milk. Also called papa de milho / mingau de milho (Southeast, Centre-West, South), canjica (Northeast,

entries.heading: Curd and whey (eaten with grains)
entries.what: Curd and whey are listed in the Guinea-Bissau cuisine article as foods eaten with cereal grains, milk, and each other.

entries.heading: Curdled fresh milk (name not confirmed)
entries.what: a curdled product made from fresh milk, sold at markets; the paper gives the English name only.

entries.heading: Cured cheeses (El Batall)
entries.what: The main speciality of El Batall, a cheese shop with its own dairy in Santa Coloma. No individual cheese names are given.

entries.heading: Cusa masqool (goat-milk fermented drink)
entries.what: An alcoholic drink made from fermented goat's milk, found mainly in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq.

entries.heading: Cuscionu (Zicavo valley)
entries.what: A Corsican cheese named for the Zicavo valley, listed in the typical products of Corsican cuisine.

entries.heading: Custard block (ice block; other names: custard block, ice block)
entries.what: A frozen treat sold in Guyana, listed beside ice cream and custard.

entries.heading: Custard slice / custard square
entries.what: A layered puff pastry slice with a custard filling and icing, called a custard square or slice in NZ.

entries.heading: D'ora ligure (Liguria)
entries.what: a Ligurian cheese named in the English list, with no description read.

entries.heading: Dachsteiner (Berglandmilch brand)
entries.what: a cheese brand in the Berglandmilch cheese list

entries.heading: Dadih dessert (modern Malaysian dadih)
entries.what: A modern set milk pudding sold as dadih in Malaysia; it is not fermented.

entries.heading: Dahen (buttermilk made with fig latex)
entries.what: buttermilk made by adding fig latex to fresh milk. The wild-plant paper says two drops of Ficus palmata latex turn the milk into buttermilk (dahen).

entries.heading: Dahi bhalla (dahi baray; vada soaked in yoghurt)
entries.what: Fried urad lentil vadas soaked in thick beaten dahi, served as a chaat. Originated on the subcontinent, now associated with Pakistan.

entries.heading: Dahi chhana
entries.what: Reddish-brown cheese from traditional buttermilk, listed for the Cuttack region of Odisha.

entries.heading: Dahi sharbat (Manipur, Nagaland)
entries.what: A sweet-sour curd drink from north-east India.

entries.heading: Dahi vada (दही वड़ा)
entries.what: Lentil dumplings soaked in thick, beaten curd; a street-food dish in Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Hyderabad.

entries.heading: Daigo (醍醐)
entries.what: A dairy product made alongside so in ancient Japan.

entries.heading: Daigo (醍醐, だいご)
entries.what: A rich, milky, mildly sweet product that became a byword for the best flavour. Its production method has been lost.

entries.heading: Daigomi and Daigoso (Calpis precursors, romanised as given in the English source)
entries.what: Two early products by the founder of Calpis, both named after daigo: Daigomi, a cultured cream (1916), and Daigoso, a cultured skimmed milk. Both are discontinued.

entries.heading: Dairy buffalo milk (นมควาย)
entries.what: milk from buffalo. The 1996 paper describes a crossbreeding programme that mixes Indo-Chinese riverine buffalo, which are selected for milk, with native Thai swamp buffalo.

entries.heading: Dairy products eaten in Palau (unspecified kind)
entries.what: The only confirmed reference is that dairy products are part of adults' diets in Palau. A 2026 study of adults in Palau found dairy intake was somewhat more common in urban than rural areas, though the difference was not statistically signi

name: Dairy residues in Early Bronze Age pottery

entries.heading: Dairy residues in Early Bronze Age pottery (archaeological evidence of dairying)
entries.what: Lipid analysis of 179 pottery vessels from southeastern Arabia (northern Oman and the UAE) found dairy residues in local and imported vessels from Hili 8, Mukhtru and Salut-ST1, c. 3000–2000 BC.

entries.heading: Dairy-containing ready-to-use supplementary food (RUSF), Guinea-Bissau trials
entries.what: Ready-to-use supplementary foods containing dairy, tested in three cluster-randomised trials in Guinea-Bissau in preschools, primary schools and villages, for children 6 to 59 months, 5 to 19 year olds, and mothers.

entries.heading: Dakéré (fermented milk and cassava semolina)
entries.what: A mixture of fermented milk and cassava semolina, named among the Adamawa dairy products by Edima et al. 2014.

entries.heading: Dalaostar
entries.what: A cheese brand listed by the Icelandic dairy cooperative Mjólkursamsalan.

entries.heading: Dali ni horbo (dali; bagot in horbo)
entries.what: A traditional food of the Batak Toba people of the Tapanuli region, North Sumatra; sold in local markets across Tapanuli.

entries.heading: Damascus goat milk
entries.what: Milk from the Damascus goat, a dairy breed named after Damascus and reared for milk and meat.

entries.heading: Dambalkhacho (დამბალხაჭო)
entries.what: A semi-soft, crumbly, spicy, strongly aromatic mould-ripened cheese; one of the oldest and most expensive Georgian cheeses according to the Georgian cuisine article.

entries.heading: Dame blanche
entries.what: A dessert of ice cream topped with whipped cream and molten chocolate; listed in the English Belgian cuisine article as a Belgian dessert.

entries.heading: Dampali kveli (დამპალი ყველი)
entries.what: A rare Georgian cheese with a butter filling inside.

entries.heading: Danablu (Danish Blue Cheese)
entries.what: a sharp, salty Danish blue-veined cheese, developed early in the 20th century by Marius Boel to imitate Roquefort-style cheese.

entries.heading: Dangke (dangke; local-language name not given in sources)
entries.what: A traditional soft white cheese from Enrekang Regency, South Sulawesi, Indonesia, eaten fresh or cooked (grilled, stir-fried, or in crackers).

entries.heading: Dani (pudding)
entries.what: Strauss's most popular pudding brand, sold within its range of puddings and individual packaged dairy desserts; Milky (above) followed about 15 years later.

entries.heading: Danish Blue (King Island Dairy, Tasmania)
entries.what: A King Island Dairy blue, listed as "Danish Blue".

entries.heading: Danish white cheese (Danish feta)
entries.what: a Danish white brined cheese sold as feta-style.

entries.heading: Danone Réunion organic yoghurt ("Le Bio de Danone Réunion")
entries.what: organic plain and Bourbon-vanilla yoghurts, free of colourings and preservatives, with a soft texture; launched May 2021.

entries.heading: Dara (Tibetan buttermilk / yoghurt drink)
entries.what: Tibetan word for buttermilk, referring to a yoghurt drink; also used for lassi.

entries.heading: Darfiyeh (درفية; Arabic script not given in the sources read)
entries.what: A seasonal goat cheese from the northern villages of Ehden and Bcharre, matured in a salted goat skin ("darf").

entries.heading: Dates ice cream (Maltese ice cream with dates)
entries.what: A Maltese ice cream flavour named as a typical local sweet.

entries.heading: Datshi (dar-tshi, Dzongkha; also datsi)
entries.what: The everyday cottage cheese of Bhutan, eaten as a curry ingredient in main meals; the most common dairy product produced in the country.

entries.heading: Dauphin (also baguette laonnaise, baguette de Thiérache, losange)
entries.what: A soft washed-rind cow's cheese related to Maroilles, made in the historic Thiérache (Avesnois) in the Nord and Aisne departments. Milder than Maroilles according to a 17th-century origin account.

entries.heading: De Fryske (Friese Goudse kaas)
entries.what: A Frisian Gouda-style cheese on the market since 2017, presented as the Frisian Goudse kaas; a brand of a farm family's own dairy brand.

entries.heading: Dègè (souroundou)
entries.what: a millet couscous dish made with yoghurt or curdled milk.

entries.heading: Délice de Bourgogne
entries.what: An industrial soft cheese made by Fromagerie Lincet in the Yonne.

entries.heading: Délice de la Sicalait
entries.what: Described by the producer as the oldest cheese made on the island; light and very creamy.

entries.heading: Demi-sel
entries.what: named in the French Normandy cuisine article. No description opened.

entries.heading: Demineralised whey (Dairygold)
entries.what: A main Dairygold product, sold to makers of infant formula and protein powder.

entries.heading: Denizli yanık kokulu yoğurt (Denizli smoked yoghurt)
entries.what: a yoghurt with a smoky, burnt taste from Denizli.

entries.heading: Derbyshire (Red Highland)
entries.what: an English-style cheese listed as made in Kenya under the name Red Highland.

name: Dessert cream from cream-cheese spread and baobab powder

entries.heading: Dessert cream from cream-cheese spread and baobab powder
entries.what: a cream the chef made to serve with pain perdu, from processed cream-cheese spread mixed with baobab powder (milky texture, tart flavour).

entries.heading: Devondale butter (imported, Australian; sold in the Maldives)
entries.what: Australian packaged butter sold through Maldivian retail; an imported product, not made in the Maldives.

name: Dgig lmegli with milk and fruit

entries.heading: Dgig lmegli with milk and fruit (suhoor drink)
entries.what: roasted barley flour (dgig lmegli) mixed with milk and fruit, eaten at suhoor to provide fibre and reduce dehydration during the fast.

entries.heading: Dhaka paneer (ঢাকা পনির; Astogram paneer)
entries.what: a traditional Bangladeshi cheese named for Dhaka, which the source says is made in Astogram village, where some families have made it for about 100 years using a protocol they keep secret. It is sold and used within one month of making.

entries.heading: Dhallë (dhalla, salted yoghurt drink)
entries.what: a summer drink of diluted yoghurt, often salted, served cold; one of the easiest drinks to make at home

entries.heading: Dhau (Newari curd, incl. juju dhau)
entries.what: A yoghurt made mainly by the Newar people of the Kathmandu Valley, traditionally set in clay pots, sweetened and served with chopped fruit.

entries.heading: Dickmilch (Setzmilch, Stockmilch; Sauermilch in common use)
entries.what: milk thickened by lactic acid, either from natural fermentation of raw milk or from added lactic bacteria on pasteurised milk. The base for quark and sour-milk cheese.

entries.heading: Dickmilch / Sauermilch (soured milk)
entries.what: milk that has soured and thickened as casein coagulates; in German usage it is called Dickmilch, Setzmilch or Stockmilch

entries.heading: Dimsi
entries.what: a cheese named on the Croatia list

entries.heading: Dinarski sir
entries.what: a Dinaric-region cheese

entries.heading: Dinarski sir iz maslinove komine
entries.what: a Dinaric cheese made with olive pomace (maslinova komina)

entries.heading: Dippin' Dots (beaded ice cream)
entries.what: Small beads of ice cream sold in franchised outlets, stadiums, malls and zoos.

entries.heading: Djathë i Sharrit (Sharr cheese; shared with Kosovo)
entries.what: a Kosovar hard cheese from the Šar Mountains, listed in the Albanian cuisine article under its Albanian name djathë i Sharrit.

entries.heading: Djeben el Kafs affiné (Djeben el Kafs, "cheese in a cage")
entries.what: A soft cheese from Boussaâda (M'sila), coated in local herbs and sold in Algiers (Said Hamdine quarter).

entries.heading: Djurgot / thick yoghurt (Tajik дуг / маст style)
entries.what: thick sour yoghurt served in the appetizer spread with flatbread; also the sour base for chakka.

entries.heading: Dobilas (organic dairy line; Žemaitijos pienas)
entries.what: the organic line of Žemaitijos pienas. Products listed include natural yoghurt (300 g and 125 g), yoghurts with apple and grains, with pineapple, mango and peach, with vanilla, and with banana and pear; drinking yoghurts (banana, peach, nat

entries.heading: Dobrodar (Добродар)
entries.what: Ukrainian hard cheese in the List of cheeses.

entries.heading: Dobroe (Dobroe, Derevenskoye; industrial brand)
entries.what: A local Uzbek dairy brand, present on the Uzbek market since 2011. Products on the page: Greek yoghurt, labneh, suzma, ayran, cottage cheese and glazed curd bars, kaymak, sour cream, kefir and Kefir Pro, drinking yoghurt, katyk and Turkish

entries.heading: Dobrogea (cașcaval)
entries.what: A Romanian cașcaval variety named in the Romanian cașcaval list; no description given.

entries.heading: Doce de leite (cajeta-like milk sweet; in Brazil also called doce de leite)
entries.what: A sweet made from milk and sugar, traditional in Brazil and other Latin American countries. Two textures: soft spreadable and firm bars/pieces.

entries.heading: Dodol susu (milk dodol)
entries.what: A milk version of dodol, named on the Indonesian Wikipedia dodol page, with a photo captioned "Dodol susu" from Pangalengan, Bandung.

entries.heading: Doğramac (cold yoghurt soup)
entries.what: Azerbaijani cold soup, national dish; a version of Russian okroshka, related to dovğa. Also called ovduq or bozdamaş.

entries.heading: Dolaz peyniri (Dolaz cheese)
entries.what: a traditional Turkish cheese of the Lakes region, associated with the Yörük nomadic groups (Karakoyunlu, Hayta, Honamlı, Sarıkeçili).

entries.heading: Dolce di Macomer
entries.what: Listed among Sardinian cheeses, named after the town of Macomer.

entries.heading: Dolce sardo
entries.what: Listed among Sardinian cheeses.

entries.heading: Dolcelatte
entries.what: a Gorgonzola-related blue cheese made for export.

entries.heading: Dolianova Funtana Noa
entries.what: One of 16 lesser-known Sardinian cheeses, made by the Unione dei Pastori di Nurri.

entries.heading: Dolomiti (formaggio)
entries.what: A white, soft, not creamy cheese with a pale rind; fresh or aged, sharper with ripening. Cylindrical, 3–7 kg.

entries.heading: Donair sauce ("sweet milk sauce")
entries.what: a very sweet sauce of condensed or evaporated milk, sugar, vinegar and garlic, served on the Halifax donair (a beef kebab).

entries.heading: Donor milk / human milk (ドナーミルク, 母乳バンク)
entries.what: Breast milk donated by mothers with surplus, pasteurised and stored in medical freezers, then supplied to preterm and very low birth weight infants (under 1,500 g) in neonatal units.

entries.heading: Doogh / shomleh / shlombeh / shromba (Persian دوغ; Pashto شړومبه; Kabul "triwai")
entries.what: a chilled, salted, savoury drink of yogurt and water, often flavoured with dried mint and sometimes cucumber or lime; sometimes carbonated. Served with bolani, picnic foods and meals.

entries.heading: Doolé (fortified thiakry for school children)
entries.what: A fortified version of thiakry made for school children and sold in shops and supermarkets in Dakar and regional towns.

entries.heading: Double Brie (King Island Dairy, Tasmania)
entries.what: A King Island Dairy brie product, listed as "Double Brie".

entries.heading: Dovğa (yoghurt soup, national dish)
entries.what: described as Azerbaijan's national dish; yoghurt soup with herbs, rice, and sometimes chickpeas and meatballs (dindili küftə); usually served after the main course, warm in winter or cold in summer. Variants: ayranaşı (made with ayran), qat

entries.heading: Dragon's Breath Blue (Upper Economy, Nova Scotia)
entries.what: A Canadian blue cheese from Nova Scotia, in a black wax coating.

entries.heading: Dreitill (vitamin D-fortified low-fat milk)
entries.what: A milk-drop character used by Mjólkursamsalan for vitamin D-fortified léttmjólk, advertised heavily in primary schools to help children take in vitamin D.

entries.heading: Dried camel milk powder (industrial, export)
entries.what: Camel milk dried into powder for export, mainly to China and Inner Mongolia, and to Saudi Arabia (dry milk negotiation).

entries.heading: Dried milk paste (historical)
entries.what: A dried milk paste that was stirred into a drink when needed, as reported by Marco Polo around 1300 (via a food-history page).

entries.heading: Drinking milk (Milch, pasteurised and raw)
entries.what: Drinking milk; about 400,000 tonnes went into drinking milk in 2011, and about 500,000 tonnes into butter. Raw-milk products are sold (raw-milk yoghurt discussed).

name: Drinking milk types: sødmælk, letmælk, minimælk, skummetmælk

entries.heading: Drinking milk types: sødmælk, letmælk, minimælk, skummetmælk
entries.what: standard Danish milk grades by fat — sødmælk (whole, about 3.5%, oldest type), letmælk (1.5%, on market since 1973), minimælk (0.5%, introduced February 2001), skummetmælk (skim, 0.1%, at most 0.5%; formerly "futmælk").

entries.heading: Drinking yoghurt and UHT/pasteurised milk (Dutch Lady and similar)
entries.what: packaged UHT and pasteurised milk, low-fat and 0% fat drinking yoghurt, and fruit yoghurt, sold in Singapore.

entries.heading: Drinking yogurt (飲むヨーグルト, nomu yōguruto)
entries.what: Fermented yogurt broken up into a liquid, sold as a drink.- How it is made: Fermented yogurt is finely broken up to a liquid after fermentation (per the Japanese yogurt article).

entries.heading: Drinkyoghurt (Yogho! Yogho!; drinkyoghurt)
entries.what: Fruit-flavoured drinkable yoghurt; the Dutch yoghurt drink Yogho! Yogho! is named as an example. Related drinks named as ayran and lassi.

entries.heading: Dry milk powder (сухое молоко)
entries.what: Milk dried to powder; Russian and Soviet production under GOST 4495-87 and GOST R 52791-2007.

entries.heading: Dubliner
entries.what: hard, sweet, granular cheese meant to combine mature cheddar sharpness with a buttery sweetness like Parmigiano; may contain calcium lactate crystals.

entries.heading: Dubrovački sir
entries.what: a cheese from the Dubrovnik area

entries.heading: Dulce de leche / cajeta
entries.what: Dulce de leche is listed as its own dessert and used as a filling for pastries and cajetas. Cajetas come in dulce de leche, chocolate, coffee and milk versions.

entries.heading: Dulce de leche cortada
entries.what: Listed among the desserts of Lara state.

entries.heading: Dulce de leche de cabra
entries.what: A dulce de leche made from goat's milk, listed among the desserts of Falcón state.

entries.heading: Dulce de leche en tabla (milk fudge)
entries.what: A milk-based fudge cut in slabs, listed among Dominican sweets.

entries.heading: Dulce de zapallo loche (Lambayeque squash sweet)
entries.what: A squash dessert from Lambayeque, made with zapallo loche (a squash with designation of origin since 2010), functioning as a mazamorra; evaporated milk is added late in the cooking.

entries.heading: Dulce gatas
entries.what: A liquid milk spread from Negros Island, made with carabao milk and muscovado sugar, similar to pastillas in ingredients but not a candy.

entries.heading: Dulces abrillantados
entries.what: Mérida's best-known sweets, made from milk and coated in sugar; the article says they were first made by the nuns of the Mérida convent and are now sold to tourists as souvenirs.

entries.heading: Dulya pudding (bread pudding)
entries.what: Bread-pudding-like dessert, served on special occasions.

name: Dunbarra, Smoked Gubbeen, Dromana, Cashel-style and other list-only cow cheeses

entries.heading: Dunbarra, Smoked Gubbeen, Dromana, Cashel-style and other list-only cow cheeses
Durda (durda; Uzbek Latin, Cyrillic not shown)
entries.what: A traditional Uzbek dish of butter and qatiq. The top forms golden lumps and a brown layer forms below. Sour, pleasant, eaten with bread and sometimes added to dishes. The Uzbek article gives "durda" first as the residue left when butter is

entries.heading: Durrus
entries.what: round washed-rind cheese, pale interior with pinkish-yellow-grey rind; mild and creamy when young, stronger and fruitier with age.

entries.heading: Dutch goat cheese (geitenkaas, Goudse type)
entries.what: Goat-milk cheeses made in the Dutch style, with semi-hard Goudse-type cheeses ripening faster than cow cheese.

entries.heading: Dutch Lady (Dutch Lady Malaysia; sterilised and chilled milk, fruit yoghurt, growing-up milk)
entries.what: The Malaysian arm of Dutch Lady Milk Industries Berhad, a FrieslandCampina subsidiary, selling milk, yoghurt and growing-up milk in Malaysia and Brunei.

entries.heading: Duvanjski sir (Duvno cheese)
entries.what: A hard cheese from Duvno (Tomislavgrad) in western Bosnia.

entries.heading: Dwida (salted concentrated milk soup)
entries.what: A soup of salted, peppered concentrated milk, sometimes with fresh cheese added.

entries.heading: Džiugas (Džiugas; Lithuanian: Džiugas sūris)
entries.what: A medium-fat Lithuanian hard cheese from the Telšiai region of Samogitia, ripened for 12 to 60 months. By 2019 it was the only Lithuanian hard cheese with EU PGI status.

entries.heading: Echo y Ansó (Queso Echo y Ansó)
entries.what: a cheese from the Echo and Ansó valleys (Huesca), named in the English Wikipedia list.

entries.heading: Édel de Cléron
entries.what: A soft cheese from the village of Cléron in the Loue valley, sold in a spruce box.

entries.heading: Eesti Juust (Estonian cheese)
entries.what: a semi-hard Dutch-type cheese in the Estonian cheese list.

entries.heading: Egg cream
entries.what: A New York City soda-fountain drink of chocolate (or other) syrup, milk and soda water, with a foam top third. Contains neither egg nor cream.

entries.heading: Egg custard tart
entries.what: pastry tart filled with milk or cream custard set with eggs.

entries.heading: Egg nog (seasonal, non-alcoholic)
entries.what: A creamy, vanilla-flavoured drink with rum aroma, non-alcoholic, sold for the end-of-year holidays; adults may add a few drops of rum.

entries.heading: Egg nog (Luxlait, 200 ml)
entries.what: Egg nog in a 200 ml carton, shown among Luxlait's new products on its home page.

entries.heading: Eghajira (Tuareg festival drink)
entries.what: a festival drink served at celebrations.

entries.heading: Eiskaffee (iced coffee with ice cream and cream)
entries.what: cold coffee drink; the Viennese form is equal parts ice cream, coffee and whipped cream

entries.heading: El Burgo (queso de El Burgo de Ebro)
entries.what: fresh and cured cheeses from El Burgo de Ebro (Zaragoza), made by Villacorona.

entries.heading: Elaiki (ελαΐκι; Kasos)
entries.what: a Kasos myzithra sealed in jars under melted local butter for long keeping.

entries.heading: Elaiki Kasou
entries.what: a salty myzithra from Kasos, sealed in jars under a layer of melted local butter.

entries.heading: Elba (Kuwaiti milk pudding)
entries.what: A Kuwaiti milk pudding flavoured with saffron and cardamom, listed under desserts.

entries.heading: Elmas Caprino Santa Maria Aquas
entries.what: One of 16 lesser-known Sardinian cheeses, made by Caseificio Deidda.

entries.heading: Emasi emabele (ground sorghum with sour milk)
entries.what: a Swazi dish of ground sorghum (emabele) mixed with sour milk.

entries.heading: Emasi etinkhobe temmbila (ground maize with sour milk)
entries.what: a Swazi dish of ground maize mixed with sour milk.

entries.heading: Ementáli (Hungarian)
entries.what: the Hungarian version of Emmental, with large holes from ripening and a fat content of about 45% in dry matter.

entries.heading: Emirdağ yoğurdu (Emirdağ sheep yoghurt)
entries.what: a high-fat sheep-milk yoghurt from Emirdağ, Afyonkarahisar.

entries.heading: Emme (Hindmarsh Valley Dairy, South Australia)
entries.what: A raw-milk goat's cheese made in the style of Emmentaler by Denise Riches at Hindmarsh Valley Dairy, near Victor Harbour on the Fleurieu Peninsula.

entries.heading: Emmental de Savoie
entries.what: wheels of about 75 kg, 75 cm across; PGI registered in the EU 1996 (regional Savoie label 1978).

entries.heading: Emmental français
entries.what: a national French industrial version of Emmental, listed as produced across the territory.

entries.heading: Emmental râpé (grated Emmental, Luxlait)
entries.what: Grated Emmental for melting or gratinating; Luxlait says it is made from "lait 100% Luxembourgeois de première qualité", with a tender, fruity, creamy paste.

entries.heading: Empriu (Casa Raubert spreadable cheese)
entries.what: A spreadable cheese from Casa Raubert.

entries.heading: Energo Cheddar (block cheese, Frisian Flag with PT Dairygold Indonesia)
entries.what: A Frisian Flag block cheese, Energo Cheddar, launched with the cheese producer PT Dairygold Indonesia.

entries.heading: English custard
entries.what: milk or cream thickened with egg yolks, sugar and vanilla (cornflour sometimes added).

entries.heading: Ennstaler Steirerkäse (Steirerkäse, Ennstal variety; g.U. trademark)
entries.what: Styrian sour-milk cheese from the Enns valley, a regional variety of Steirerkäse.

entries.heading: Entrammes
entries.what: A Mayenne cheese named in the list of French cheeses (its Wikipedia title is a redirect to Port-Salut).

entries.heading: Enyucado (enyucado; cassava cake with coconut, butter and cheese)
entries.what: A cassava (yuca) cake with coconut, sugar and anise, made with butter and cheese.

entries.heading: Ereğli yoğurdu (Ereğli sheep yoghurt)
entries.what: a smoky, high-fat sheep-milk yoghurt from Ereğli.

entries.heading: Ergo (ergo; sour milk; also called ensira in the smoked-vessel sense)
entries.what: thick, set-yoghurt-like fermented milk, white, smooth and mildly sour, eaten plain or with spices. Most widely consumed fermented milk in Ethiopia. Flavour and texture vary by ethnic group, spices and smoking material.

entries.heading: Ericino
entries.what: a mixed-milk Sicilian cheese from the Erice area.

entries.heading: Erzurum küflü peynir (mould-ripened Erzurum cheese)
entries.what: Named in the review as an Erzurum mould-ripened cheese.

entries.heading: Es krim (ice cream), including colonial-era Batavia production
entries.what: Ice cream is made from milk-based ingredients mixed with sweetener and flavouring, then stirred while cooling.

entries.heading: Es krim dadih (buffalo-milk dadih ice cream, study product)
entries.what: A probiotic ice cream made with dadih, tested in a 2025 study; 30 untrained panelists preferred the version with 15 % dadih.

entries.heading: Es puter (es dung dung, es tung tung)
entries.what: An Indonesian ice-cream-like dessert made with coconut milk rather than milk.

entries.heading: Esbareich
entries.what: A Barousse cheese from Hautes-Pyrénées.

entries.heading: Eshabwe
entries.what: A traditional butter-based sauce widely prepared in south-western Uganda.

entries.heading: Eshel
entries.what: A yogurt named alongside leben in the Israeli cuisine article, with no further detail.

entries.heading: Eşmekaya yoğurdu
entries.what: a sheep-milk yoghurt from Eşmekaya, using its own culture.

entries.heading: Esrom
entries.what: a pale yellow, semi-soft Danish cheese with a pungent aroma and sweet, full flavour; used as a table or melting cheese.

entries.heading: ESSI (ESSI; industrial brand)
entries.what: Uzbek dairy brand. Products on the page: kefir and bio-kefir, sour milk, cottage cheese, sour cream, kaymak, curd snacks, cheese, drinking yoghurt, natural fruit yoghurts.

entries.heading: Etken chay / süt chay (Uyghur milk tea)
entries.what: Black tea boiled with an equal amount of milk and salt, sometimes with butter, sour cream or spices; süt chay means "milk tea" in Uyghur. Said to have reached China from India via the Silk Road.

entries.heading: Étkezési tehéntúró (table cow curd)
entries.what: a fresh, unripened cow curd used in desserts.

entries.heading: Eton mess
entries.what: strawberries, meringue and whipped cream.

entries.heading: Evaporated and condensed milk (HOMPI plant, San Pedro, Laguna)
entries.what: The Wikipedia article on this company (which it names HOMPI) says the company first made canned liquid milk, evaporated and condensed, from a first plant in San Pedro, Laguna that began operations in September 1972. It later added dried mil

name: Evaporated canned milk in tea and coffee

entries.heading: Evaporated canned milk in tea and coffee
entries.what: Canned evaporated milk used with sugar to prepare tea and coffee.

entries.heading: Ewe lump cheese (ovčí hrudkový syr; Slovak "ewe lump cheese", traditional specialty-guaranteed)
entries.what: a traditional Slovak sheep lump cheese made by many small producers across Slovakia; the 2025 J Dairy Sci study frames it as a traditional specialty-guaranteed cheese for which national specifications are being developed.

entries.heading: Ewe's-milk hard cheeses (Croatian raw ewe's milk cheese types, unnamed in source)
entries.what: three artisanal Croatian raw ewe's-milk cheese types from two production sites, studied for their microbiology

entries.heading: Excelsior
entries.what: the first brand name of Brillat-Savarin, created about 1890 near Forges-les-Eaux. Named in the French Normandy cuisine article.

entries.heading: Family powdered milk (Dutch Lady) and milk powder in Milo
entries.what: powdered milk sold for family use; milk powder is also an ingredient in Milo.

entries.heading: Fan ice cream (Fanice, FanGold, FanChoco, FanDango, Fanmaxx)
entries.what: Fan Milk's frozen dairy products sold in Ghana, including ice lollies. Fanice is a 150 mL pouch.

name: Fan yoghurt and frozen dairy desserts

entries.heading: Fan yoghurt and frozen dairy desserts (Fan Milk)
entries.what: Fan Milk's yoghurt and ice-cream range (FanYogo, Fanice and others); the company has operated in West Africa.

entries.heading: Fantasia di Capra
entries.what: One of 16 lesser-known Sardinian cheeses, made by Caseificio Argei (Gergei).

entries.heading: Far breton (Breton batter pudding)
entries.what: A Breton baked batter pudding with eggs, flour, sugar, butter and milk, traditionally with prunes.

entries.heading: Farci-provola (Farci-provola)
entries.what: A provola-type cheese listed for Calabria.

entries.heading: Fåreost (sheep cheese)
entries.what: the Danish term for sheep cheese.

entries.heading: Farine lactée Henri Nestlé (milk-based infant food; infant formula)
entries.what: Milk-based baby food developed by Henri Nestlé and marketed from Vevey from 1867 under the name Farine lactée Henri Nestlé. The company kept the name until 1905 after Nestlé retired in 1875.

entries.heading: Farm ice cream (Mattas gårdsmejeri)
entries.what: Ice cream made on the Mattas farm and sold at its summer café in Sund.

entries.heading: Farmer cheese
entries.what: Cottage cheese pressed to remove water.

entries.heading: Färsk bredbar fårost (fresh spreadable sheep cheese)
entries.what: A fresh sheep's-milk spreadable cheese flavoured with truffle, horseradish or herbs, named in the Swedish Fårost article in the same paragraph as the Gotland cheeses.

entries.heading: Fat skimmed from fermented milk (northern Kenya)
entries.what: fat extracted from fermented milk and rubbed on children's tongues after about six months to help digestion; reported by fathers in Marsabit (Gabra) and Isiolo (Sakuye).

entries.heading: Fatteh with yoghurt (الفتّة)
entries.what: bread topped with strained yoghurt, chickpeas and olive oil

entries.heading: Felciata (Felciata)
entries.what: A goat cheese listed for Calabria under the name felciata.

entries.heading: Fereni (فرنی; rice-milk pudding)
entries.what: A rice-flour and milk pudding from the phirni family; a fixture of iftar tables in Gorgan (northern Iran).

entries.heading: Fermented goat milk (used in veterinary practice)
entries.what: goat milk left to ferment, named in Sahrawi veterinary remedies alongside camel milk and butter.

entries.heading: Fermented zebu milk curds (caillé)
entries.what: Curds made by fermenting zebu milk. In the arid south and west, pastoral families may eat these instead of rice.

entries.heading: Fermented zebu-milk curd (caillé de lait de zébu fermenté; no local Malagasy name found)
entries.what: a curd made by fermenting zebu milk, eaten by pastoral families in the arid south and west, where it can take the place of rice.

entries.heading: Fernea / feereny (milk and cornstarch dessert)
entries.what: a very sweet dessert, mainly milk and cornstarch, similar to rice pudding without rice.

entries.heading: Feta Cheese Original 125 g (Obour Land; Arabic name not in opened sources)
entries.what: Obour Land's original feta, sold in 125 g packs. The same white-cheese range also lists a 500 g "lovely feta" and a 500 g low-salt cheese.

entries.heading: Feuille de Dreux (Feuille de Dreux)
entries.what: a disc of about 300 g, 14 cm across, decorated with a chestnut leaf.

entries.heading: Feuille du Limousin
entries.what: A regional collective-brand cheese of the Limousin; named in the 2024 regional cheese contest.

entries.heading: Figou
entries.what: A cheese of the Limousin.

entries.heading: Figue (Périgord)
entries.what: A cheese named Figue, listed for the Périgord.

entries.heading: Filbunke (fil in Finland-Swedish and some Swedish dialects)
entries.what: A breakfast dish of soured milk with a pudding-like texture, served chilled, plain or with fruit and berries; known in Sweden since at least the 1600s.

entries.heading: Filled milk (blend of skimmed milk and soybean oil)
entries.what: A blend of skimmed milk and soybean oil that some cafes use in milk tea in place of whole milk or evaporated milk.

entries.heading: Filmjölk (fil; surmjölk in Central Sweden; kulturmelk/surmelk in Norway; skyr on Gotland formerly; filbryta/filbruttu in parts of Norrland)
entries.what: Traditional Swedish soured milk, common across the Nordic countries, thickened by lactic acid bacteria. Sold industrially since 1931 (Arla); now mostly unflavoured, flavoured and probiotic versions.

entries.heading: Fin de siècle
entries.what: named in the French Normandy cuisine article as a Normandy cheese. No description opened.

entries.heading: Fior delle Dolomiti
entries.what: A PAT cheese of the Dolomites area of Veneto.

entries.heading: Fiordilatte (PAT)
entries.what: Plain cow's-milk fior di latte.

entries.heading: Fiordilatte dell'Agro Pontino (PAT)
entries.what: A cow's-milk fior di latte from the Agro Pontino (Latina).

entries.heading: Fiore Sardo (Fiore sardo; Barbagia "fiore")
entries.what: A hard sheep's-milk DOP cheese from Sardinia, shaped as a double truncated cone of about 1.5–4 kg with a yellow or dark brown rind. It is eaten as a table cheese, or grated when aged over 6 months.

entries.heading: Fiorone della Valsassina (PAT)
entries.what: a fat cheese from the Valsassina, Province of Lecco, whose curd opens like a flower when broken.

entries.heading: Firm and semi-rigid industrial cheese (Kalleh Dairy, Amol)
entries.what: Cheese lines of Kalleh Dairy, an Iranian dairy company in Amol. The article lists firm cheese, semi-rigid cheese and diet cheese; its cheese is sold nationally.

entries.heading: Fiskesuppe (milk-based fish soup)
entries.what: a white soup based on milk with vegetables (usually carrots, onion, potato) and various fish; creamed seafood soups are common along the coast.

entries.heading: Fit-fit / chechebsa (butter-berbere dishes)
entries.what: breakfast dishes made with niter kibbeh and berbere.

entries.heading: Fitt (high-protein drinking yoghurt)
entries.what: A drinking yoghurt with 10 g protein and 0.9 g fat per 100 g. Flavours strawberry, blueberry and vanilla.

entries.heading: Fium'Orbo (Fium'Orbu)
entries.what: Corsican cheese listed on the French cheese list.

entries.heading: Fiurit (PAT)
entries.what: a fresh, lean, soft, creamy white cheese; the name means "flower of ricotta".

entries.heading: Fivemiletown Cheddar range (Fivemiletown Cheddar; Fivemiletown Creamery)
entries.what: A cheddar range from mild to extra mature, made by Fivemiletown Creamery.

entries.heading: Flam (flan, with or without cream)
entries.what: A baked custard of milk, eggs and sugar, cooked in moulds in a bain-marie over caramel. Named in the 2017 survey as a typical dessert "with or without cream" (1.8% of respondents).

name: Flan de coco / flan de guayaba / flan de calabaza

entries.heading: Flan de coco / flan de guayaba / flan de calabaza
entries.what: Flan in several Cuban flavours listed in Cuban cuisine.

entries.heading: Flan pâtissier (custard tart)
entries.what: A pastry tart filled with a milk-and-egg custard, also called flan parisien.

entries.heading: Flaó (cheese tart; Ibiza and Menorca)
entries.what: Ibiza flaó is a tart with a sheep- or goat-milk fresh cheese filling, slightly flavoured with peppermint leaves and aniseed. Menorca's flaó uses Maó cheese, and Menorca flaons should be very puffy in the middle.

entries.heading: Flavoured and chocolate milk drinks (Cowbell, Miksi)
entries.what: Chocolate-flavoured milk drinks made from sachet powdered milk, sold as Cowbell chocolate milk and Miksi chocolate.

entries.heading: Flavoured and spreadable butters (Beurre ail et fines herbes, Beurre Rose, beurre frigo-tartinable)
entries.what: Luxlait lines: garlic and parsley butter for barbecue and meat dishes; "Beurre Rose", made with the know-how of the company's master butter makers; and a spreadable butter that is soft straight from the fridge.

entries.heading: Flavoured and UHT milk (vanilla, chocolate, mango, strawberry)
entries.what: UHT milk, vanilla milk, chocolate milk and mango milk were sampled from commercial outlets in south-west Bangladesh (2024–25); processed liquid milk was about 5% of consumption in the 2004 paper, which gave 185,000 litres a day from process

entries.heading: Flavoured camel milk (Camelait)
entries.what: Flavoured camel milk sold by Al Ain Dairy under the Camelait brand, part of its camel range alongside fresh camel milk and camel laban.

entries.heading: Flavoured milk drinks (Milka Krem)
entries.what: Chocolate milk ("choco milk") and coffee milk, sold as fresh flavoured milk at the Milka Krem outlet, Philippine Carabao Center.

entries.heading: Flavoured yoghurt (Dairibord)
entries.what: A chilled Dairibord yoghurt for "anytime snack, meal"; the product page says always keep chilled.

entries.heading: Fleur bleue (Fleur bleue)
entries.what: a cheese listed near Rambouillet, Yvelines.

entries.heading: Flødekager (cream cakes) including lagkage and gåsebryst
entries.what: cakes made with generous whipped cream; lagkage is a layer cake with berries and cream or custard; gåsebryst is a cream cake with prune jam, whipped cream, wrapped in marzipan.

entries.heading: Floreffe (triple-cream)
entries.what: A Belgian triple-cream cheese, traditionally 200 g. The article says it is close to Remoudou and Crâmeû, and that there is no connection to Floreffe Abbey despite the shared name.

entries.heading: Flors
entries.what: Friulian cheese named "Flors".

entries.heading: Fløtemysost (fløte mysost; cream whey cheese)
entries.what: a traditional Norwegian brown whey cheese, the milder brunost made without goat's milk. About 30% of brunost sold is fløtemysost.

entries.heading: Fodom (Formaggio Fodom)
entries.what: A cheese of Livinallongo del Col di Lana (Fodom in Ladin), in the upper Cordevole valley, Belluno. Made only by the Latteria cooperativa di Livinallongo since 1983, along with the Renaz and Contrin cheeses.

entries.heading: Fontainebleau (Fontainebleau; fromage Fontainebleau)
entries.what: a cream-and-curd dessert, about 10 cm across and 60 % fat, with an airy white mousse on top; served cold; the cream-only form keeps only two days.

entries.heading: Fontal
entries.what: A Trentino cheese, named on the register list. PAT.

entries.heading: Formadi cjoc (formaggio ubriaco)
entries.what: Cheese wheels steeped in grape must.

entries.heading: Formadi frant
entries.what: Scraps and ends of other cheeses crumbled together and aged as a spreadable mix.

entries.heading: Formaela (Φορμαέλα Αράχωβας; Π.Ο.Π.)
entries.what: Strong, sharp cheese, usually grilled or fried for saganaki.

entries.heading: Formaela Arachovas (Φορμαέλα Αράχωβας, ΠΟΠ)
entries.what: a hard cheese produced in Arachova, grilled or fried (often as saganaki).

entries.heading: Formagella della Val di Scalve (PAT)
entries.what: a Formagella from the Val di Scalve, Province of Bergamo, with origins in the 12th century.

entries.heading: Formagella della Val Sabbia (PAT)
entries.what: a soft cheese from the Val Sabbia, Province of Brescia, for table use.

entries.heading: Formagella di Menconico (PAT)
entries.what: a soft cheese from Menconico in the Oltrepò Pavese, Province of Pavia, served with bread and light white wines of the area.

entries.heading: Formagella di Tremosine (PAT)
entries.what: a soft cheese from Tremosine near Lake Garda, recognised by a cross incised on one face.

entries.heading: Formaggella (formagella; chiasörin in Leventina, crenga in Blenio, maioca in Biasca, mota or motigni in Vallemaggia, fromagela in Verzasca)
entries.what: A cheese made across the canton and now also in the lowlands; its character varies by valley with pasture, ripening, milk and producer

entries.heading: Formaggella del Luinese (Formaggella del Luinese DOP)
entries.what: a DOP cheese from the pre-Alps north of Varese, described as the only DOP goat cheese from Lombardy and the only Italian DOP cheese made only from goat milk.

entries.heading: Formaggelle di capra (aged goat cheese, Fattoria del Faggio)
entries.what: An aged goat cheese made at Fattoria del Faggio in Sonvico, alongside the Bleu Ticines and fresh büscion

entries.heading: Formaggetta (valley varieties: Val Graveglia, Bonassola, Vàise, alta Valle Scrivia, alta Valle Stura, Val di Vara, Valle Argentina, Arroscia)
entries.what: a family of small local cheeses named after their valleys. The Liguria table lists about seven valley versions; no individual method was read on a page.

entries.heading: Formaggetta savonese (Formaggetta di Stella San Giovanni; Stella, Imperia to Savona)
entries.what: a small fresh cheese made from Imperia to Savona, mainly in the comune of Stella; small method variations exist between zones.

entries.heading: Formaggi caprini della Maremma (caprini freschi o aromatizzati)
entries.what: goat cheeses from the Maremma, fresh or flavoured.

entries.heading: Formaggio acidino
entries.what: A fresh goat's-milk cheese typical of the Sette Comuni plateau (mainly Vicenza), a PAT product of Veneto.

entries.heading: Formaggio agordino di malga
entries.what: A summer cheese from the alpine pastures of the Agordino (Belluno). Local names include "Casél", "Nostrano" and "Formai". It is a regional traditional product (PAT).

name: Formaggio al latte crudo di Posina

entries.heading: Formaggio al latte crudo di Posina
entries.what: A raw-milk PAT cheese of Posina (Vicenza).

entries.heading: Formaggio Busche
entries.what: A PAT cheese of Veneto.

entries.heading: Formaggio caprino dell'Alto Mugello
entries.what: goat cheese from the Alto Mugello.

entries.heading: Formaggio caprino della Limina (Formaggio caprino della Limina)
entries.what: Goat cheese from the Limina area, listed for Calabria.

entries.heading: Formaggio caprino delle Apuane
entries.what: goat cheese named for the Apuane.

entries.heading: Formaggio caprino morbido
entries.what: Soft goat cheese from Friuli Venezia Giulia.

entries.heading: Formaggio casato del Garda
entries.what: A PAT cheese associated with Lake Garda in Veneto.

entries.heading: Formaggio casel bellunese
entries.what: A Belluno cheese on the PAT list. "Casél" is also a local name for the Formaggio agordino di malga.

entries.heading: Formaggio Cesio
entries.what: A PAT cheese of Veneto.

entries.heading: Formaggio Comelico
entries.what: A PAT cheese of the Comelico valley (Belluno).

entries.heading: Formaggio Contrin
entries.what: A cheese of Livinallongo del Col di Lana, made by the same co-operative as the Fodom cheese.

entries.heading: Formaggio d'Alpe misto (PAT)
entries.what: a mixed cow and goat alpine cheese from high pastures across Bergamo, Brescia, Como, Lecco, Pavia, Sondrio and Varese; hard to find.

entries.heading: Formaggio d'alpe ticinese
entries.what: AOP alpine cheese of Canton Ticino.

entries.heading: Formaggio d'Alpe Ticinese DOP (Formaggio d'Alpe; varieties Piora, Sorescia, Pontino, Pesciüm, Camadra, Pertusio, Campo la Torba, Fümegna)
entries.what: The canton's first DOP, registered in 2002; made on alpine pastures in the alpine season and ripened in cellars. Young cheese is sweet and aromatic; older cheese is sharper

entries.heading: Formaggio di capra (PAT)
entries.what: Goat cheese listed as Lazio PAT.

entries.heading: Formaggio di capra siciliana
entries.what: a cylindrical goat's-milk cheese about 3 kg, with flat or slightly concave faces, oily rind marked with the rush-basket pattern, spicy taste; known since Homer, per the article.

entries.heading: Formaggio di capra umbro (on-farm goat cheese, Umbria)
entries.what: Goat cheese made on Umbrian farms, from the same study as the pecorino above.

entries.heading: Formaggio di colostro ovino
entries.what: A cheese made from sheep colostrum, listed among Sardinian cheeses.

entries.heading: Formaggio di Fagagna (Latteria di Fagagna)
entries.what: Cheese named after the town of Fagagna (Udine).

entries.heading: Formaggio di fossa di Sogliano
entries.what: A traditional cheese from Sogliano al Rubicone and other municipalities in Romagna and the Marche, protected under DOP since 2009 (Reg. CE n. 1183 del 30.11.09).

name: Formaggio di malga dell'Altopiano dei Sette Comuni

entries.heading: Formaggio di malga dell'Altopiano dei Sette Comuni (allevo di malga)
entries.what: A Veneto alpine cheese of the Sette Comuni plateau (Asiago). Its aged version (stravecchio, 19 months or more) is a Slow Food presidium.

entries.heading: Formaggio di montagna friulano
entries.what: Mountain cheese from Friuli, named in the EN list.

entries.heading: Formaggio di Pietracatella
entries.what: A Molise cheese from Pietracatella (CB) listed in the national table of traditional products.

name: Formaggio di Santo Stefano di Quisquina

entries.heading: Formaggio di Santo Stefano di Quisquina
entries.what: a cylindrical sheep's-milk cheese of about two kilograms, from the central Monti Sicani around Santo Stefano Quisquina.

entries.heading: Formaggio Dolomiti
entries.what: A PAT cheese of the Dolomites area of Veneto.

name: Formaggio e caciotta di pecora sott'olio

entries.heading: Formaggio e caciotta di pecora sott'olio (PAT)
entries.what: Sheep cheese or caciotta preserved in oil.

entries.heading: Formaggio latteria di Sappada
entries.what: A dairy cheese from Sappada (Belluno), on the PAT list.

entries.heading: Formaggio malga bellunese
entries.what: A summer alpine cheese of the Belluno Prealps and Dolomites. A recent study said only one malga in six in the Belluno province still makes it by tradition; it is at serious risk of disappearing. Slow Food presidium for the aged version.

name: Formaggio misto pecora fresco dei Berici

entries.heading: Formaggio misto pecora fresco dei Berici
entries.what: A fresh mixed-milk PAT cheese from the Berici hills (Vicenza).

entries.heading: Formaggio montemagro
entries.what: A PAT cheese of Veneto.

entries.heading: Formaggio nostrano veronese
entries.what: A local farm cheese of Verona province, on the PAT list.

entries.heading: Formaggio pecorino dei Berici
entries.what: A sheep's-milk PAT cheese from the Berici hills (Vicenza).

entries.heading: Formaggio Renaz
entries.what: A cheese of Livinallongo del Col di Lana, made by the same co-operative as Fodom.

entries.heading: Formaggio salato (Salato duro friulano; Salato morbido del Friuli)
entries.what: Salted cheese made in Friuli in a hard and a soft version.

entries.heading: Formaggio saltarello
entries.what: Friulian cheese named "saltarello".

entries.heading: Formaggio Valmorel
entries.what: A PAT cheese of Veneto.

entries.heading: Formaggio zigher
entries.what: A PAT cheese of Veneto (Zigher is a Ladin-area name).

entries.heading: Formaggio Zumelle
entries.what: A PAT cheese of Veneto, named after the Zumelle area.

entries.heading: Formai de Livign (PAT)
entries.what: an alpine cheese from Livigno, Province of Sondrio, made in summer in the alpine pastures.

entries.heading: Formai de Mut (Formai de Mut dell'Alta Valle Brembana)
entries.what: a Val Brembana cheese; PDO for the Alta Valle Brembana version.

name: Formai de Mut dell'Alta Valle Brembana

entries.heading: Formai de Mut dell'Alta Valle Brembana (Formai de Mut DOP)
entries.what: a DOP cheese from the Alta Valle Brembana, Province of Bergamo, made at 1,200–2,500 m across about 21 municipalities.

entries.heading: Formai del cìt (Formaggio del cit)
entries.what: Local cheese name; the "cìt" is a Friulian dialect word.

entries.heading: Formai nustran
entries.what: A PAT cheese of Veneto listed under its local name.

name: Formatge de l'Alt Urgell i la Cerdanya

entries.heading: Formatge de l'Alt Urgell i la Cerdanya
entries.what: Catalan cheese from the Alt Urgell and Cerdanya, Pyrenees.

entries.heading: Formella del Friuli
entries.what: Regional cheese named "formella".

entries.heading: Fôte des bergères
entries.what: A sheep cheese from the Limousin, one of five cheeses named in the 2024 regional cheese contest.

entries.heading: Foudjou (foujou)
entries.what: strong cheese of Drôme and Ardèche, spelled "foujou" around Crest.

entries.heading: Fougerus (Fougerus)
entries.what: a brie-type cheese resembling Coulommiers, wrapped in fern, created by the fromager Rouzaire in 1957 to echo the nearly vanished Chevru.

entries.heading: Fourme d'Asco
entries.what: Fourme-type cheese from Corsica, listed on the French cheese list.

entries.heading: Fourme d'Yssingeaux
entries.what: a French cheese made in the Yssingeaux area, sub-prefecture of Haute-Loire.

entries.heading: Fourme de Rochefort-Montagne
entries.what: from Rochefort-Montagne, Puy-de-Dôme.

entries.heading: Főzött sajt (főzősajt)
entries.what: a Hungarian cooked (processed) cheese, made from melted rennet curd or túró, with salt, caraway, cream and butter added.

entries.heading: Frachet
entries.what: traditional cheese from the Valsesia, province of Vercelli, made from scraps of cheese or ricotta.

entries.heading: Frasia Kythirwn (Φράτσια Κυθήρων)
entries.what: Kythira cheese; no details.

entries.heading: Freixneda goat cheeses (raw and pasteurised)
entries.what: a family of goat cheeses from La Freixneda (Teruel) from a single goat farm.

entries.heading: Fresa
entries.what: Listed among Sardinian cheeses (the Ittiri Slow Food presidium cheese may be a different product; see Unconfirmed leads).

entries.heading: Frescos con leche (fruit drinks with milk)
entries.what: Fruit drinks made with milk or water, including banana, papaya and vanilla cream versions.

entries.heading: Fresh (raw) cow milk
entries.what: most milk sold in Tanzania as raw milk through an informal market.

entries.heading: Fresh and heat-treated cow milk (raw, boiled, sold at ambient temperature)
entries.what: Unprocessed cow milk sold in Korhogo and Abidjan, with some vendors boiling milk before sale.

name: Fresh and industrial types named in the Swiss list

entries.heading: Fresh and industrial types named in the Swiss list (no production detail)
Fresh and spreadable cheeses (El Batall)
entries.what: Fresh and spreadable cheeses from El Batall. This resolves the dairy-file lead on El Batall's "fresh dairy products".

entries.heading: Fresh buffalo milk (Egyptian)
entries.what: Buffalo milk produced in Egypt; Egypt is listed fourth among top water buffalo milk producers (2020 FAO estimate, 1,747,641 tonnes).

entries.heading: Fresh camel milk (тэмээний сүү)
entries.what: Fresh camel milk, mostly drunk fresh and also supplied to factories; Mongolia's government named camel milk a priority product.

entries.heading: Fresh cheese, 100 % New Caledonian milk (made in Païta)
entries.what: Fresh cheeses made by Isabelle Leblanc, a cheesemaker in Païta, from milk the article describes as "lait 100 % calédonien".

entries.heading: Fresh cow and goat milk (local drinking milk)
entries.what: Milk from small local herds, produced mainly for fresh drinking rather than processing. Local cattle and goat herds are small; sheep are kept too but no source names sheep milk as a product.

entries.heading: Fresh cow milk, raw (local name not confirmed)
entries.what: Milk from smallholder dairy and cattle herds. Some households drink it raw. A Malawi KAP survey of dairy and cattle farmers names drinking or eating raw milk and raw meat as a risk practice, and not drinking raw animal products as a good pr

entries.heading: Fresh cow's milk and yoghurt (lait frais, yaourt de la Ferme de Lait-Quateur)
entries.what: Fresh milk and yoghurt from a dairy farm, "La Ferme de Lait-Quateur", sold in Guianese supermarkets and small shops. A fresh white cheese (fromage blanc) is also named and excluded here.

entries.heading: Fresh cream: crème fraîche liquide
entries.what: Liquid fresh cream sold by Luxlait, described as "fraîcheur et légèreté".

entries.heading: Fresh goat cheese, rural processing (queso de cabra fresco rural, Chile, 1988)
entries.what: Fresh goat cheese made in small rural dairies in two villages in Chile, studied for hygiene and process quality over two seasons.

entries.heading: Fresh goat's milk
entries.what: Goat's milk, drunk fresh, one of the most-liked dairy items in a Cypriot survey.

entries.heading: Fresh milk flavoured with dates (lait frais aromatisé aux dattes)
entries.what: Fresh milk flavoured with dates.

entries.heading: Fresh mozzarella (industrial; Dairy Khoury)
entries.what: Dairy Khoury lists "Fresh Mozzarella" and "Fresh Mozzarella Cerise" (cherry-size).

entries.heading: Fresh raw and pasteurised milk
entries.what: Raw milk is sold and consumed; pasteurised milk is also sold, and the 2019 study lists it among the best-known milk products.

entries.heading: Fresh raw cow milk (market milk)
entries.what: Raw cow milk sold in calabashes or containers from herds to retailers and households; the main form of dairy sold in northern markets.

name: Fresh raw milk sold in Bamako

entries.heading: Fresh raw milk sold in Bamako
entries.what: raw milk sold in Bamako and other Malian markets, often without cold chain.

name: Fresh unaged cheese from goat or cow milk

entries.heading: Fresh unaged cheese from goat or cow milk (small experiments, no local name)
entries.what: Small-scale experimental fresh cheeses. The guide says they have not developed into a recognised local tradition.

name: Fresh whole milk in milk tea

entries.heading: Fresh whole milk in milk tea (全脂奶)
entries.what: Whole milk offered as an alternative to evaporated milk in the base Hong Kong-style milk tea recipe.

entries.heading: Frico balacia
entries.what: Listed as a Friulian frico variant on the EN list.

entries.heading: Frijj (flavoured milkshake)
entries.what: a milkshake brand sold mainly in the UK, in strawberry, chocolate, banana, fudge brownie and cookie dough, with limited editions such as Jaffa Cake and banoffee pie.

entries.heading: Frinault (Frinault cendré, Frinault bleu, Frinault sec)
entries.what: a disc about 10 cm across and 2 cm thick, 120 g; ash version 50 g heavier.

entries.heading: Frischkäse (German fresh cheese)
entries.what: a fresh cheese used as a spread, in dips and creams, and in baking. German cheese rules give it a group of its own: water over 73% of the fat-free cheese mass, so it keeps only briefly and must be chilled. Made in all fat grades and sometim

entries.heading: Friulano (Canada; Italian-named cheese, "Italian Cheddar")
entries.what: A creamy, salty Canadian cheese named after Friuli in Italy and meant to imitate Montasio; it is not made in Italy and is not cheddared.

entries.heading: Fromage aux artisons (Velay)
entries.what: Velay cheese ripened with cheese mites (Acarus siro), lemon-like flavour.

entries.heading: Fromage blanc and petit-suisse (made locally; second pass)
entries.what: Fresh white cheese, sold plain or sweetened or with fruit; the petit-suisse is a smoother, richer version. The 2019 release defines it as a non-ripened smooth fresh cheese with 4 % fat or less on the whole weight, 20 % or less of dry matter

entries.heading: Fromage blanc sur fruit (Luxlait fresh cheese dessert)
entries.what: Creamy fresh cheese served on a bed of fruit, sold by Luxlait under desserts lactés with the tagline "Une tendresse inégalable".

entries.heading: Fromage Bleu (Atelier de Fromage)
entries.what: A blue cheese modelled on southern French blues, made by Atelier de Fromage (Shigeo and Yoko Matsuoka), Nagano Prefecture, founded 1982.

name: Fromage caillé frais de la Manche

entries.heading: Fromage caillé frais de la Manche
entries.what: a fresh curd cheese from the Manche department, named in the French Normandy cuisine article. No description opened.

entries.heading: Fromage de Bagnes (Bagnes)
entries.what: A semi-hard cheese from the Val de Bagnes in Valais, first mentioned in the 14th century. It is suited to raclette and fondue and can be eaten raw.

entries.heading: Fromage de Mirasaka (Japanese name not in sources)
entries.what: A soft-ripened cow's-milk cheese made by Mirasaka Fromage, a family farm in the mountains of Hiroshima Prefecture.

entries.heading: Fromage de Mirasaka Chèvre (Mirasaka goat soft-ripened)
entries.what: The goat-milk version of Fromage de Mirasaka, from the same Hiroshima farm; made only from March to November.

entries.heading: Fromage de Troyes
entries.what: Cheese from the Aube and Champagne tagged on the list page.

entries.heading: Fromage de vache brûlé
entries.what: A cow's-milk cheese of the Pyrénées-Atlantiques (Béarn/Pays basque).

entries.heading: Fromage des Plaines (nature; pasteurisé; ail et fines herbes)
entries.what: A fresh cheese from the plains of Réunion, sold plain, pasteurised and with garlic and herbs.

entries.heading: Fromage fermier de Corse
entries.what: A generic farm cheese from Corsica, listed on the French cheese list.

entries.heading: Fromage fort de la Croix-Rousse
entries.what: spread from Lyon's Croix-Rousse quarter, also known in the Dombes and Beaujolais.

name: Fromage Gouda de bière du Battin

entries.heading: Fromage Gouda de bière du Battin (Gouda made with Battin beer)
entries.what: A local Luxembourg version of Gouda, described in the List of cheeses as inspired by Belgian monastery cheeses and influenced by Flemish cheesemakers who came to Luxembourg.

entries.heading: Fromage sinistré (canned block cheese, "survivor's cheese")
entries.what: A large golden-canned block of cheese sold on Haitian streets, nicknamed "fromage sinistré" (roughly "a survivor's cheese"). The author recalls it from the 1994 embargo period.

entries.heading: Frozen custard
entries.what: A denser, slightly warmer frozen dessert than ice cream, made with egg yolks, cream and sweetener.

entries.heading: Frozen yoghurt (Taste Trends, UK; owned by Lakeland Dairies)
entries.what: Frozen yoghurt from Taste Trends Ltd, a UK producer that Lakeland Dairies acquired in 2015.

entries.heading: Frozen yoghurt ice cream (Yogurt Factory, Libreville)
entries.what: an ice cream made from yoghurt, sold by the Yogurt Factory chain in Libreville and customisable with toppings. Example mix: plain yoghurt with mango, coconut and salted butter caramel.

entries.heading: Frozen yogurt
entries.what: A frozen dessert made with yogurt cultures; tarter and lower in fat than ice cream in its tart form.

entries.heading: Fruit and yoghurt smoothie (local name not found)
entries.what: A smoothie blended from fruit and yoghurt, sold by street vendors alongside fried chicken and fish.

entries.heading: Fruit milk (フルーツ牛乳, furūtsu gyūnyū)
entries.what: Milk flavoured with fruit (strawberry, banana, mango, mandarin, pineapple, melon, apple), sold as a bathhouse drink; a close relative of coffee milk.

entries.heading: Frumagit di Curiglia (PAT)
entries.what: a fresh goat cheese from Curiglia; the unsalted version is eaten for breakfast, as an antipasto or in salad.

entries.heading: Frumenty-like dish (cracked wheat and heated milk)
entries.what: A fermented mix of cracked wheat and heated milk, possibly with egg yolks, that could be dried and stored over winter.

entries.heading: Fuarag (Scotland)
entries.what: oats mixed with cold milk.

entries.heading: Fudge or barfi (local name not confirmed)
entries.what: a fudge-like sugar and milk sweet; the Grenadian mention is listed alongside fudge.

entries.heading: Fula milk cheese, unnamed (Fula/Fulbe; Sierra Leone name not given)
entries.what: A cheese made by Sierra Leonean Fula (Fulani) women and taken to local markets to sell or trade, per the Wikipedia article on the Fula of Sierra Leone. The article gives it no name.

entries.heading: Fulani fresh milk (kossam / miraɗam)
entries.what: Fulfulde term "kossam" is the general word for milk, and "miraɗam" for fresh milk; milk is central to Fulbe identity.

entries.heading: Fura (dônou, furah, chobbal, tidda)
entries.what: a drink of millet flour balls dissolved in milk or yoghurt, very popular across ethnic groups in Niger.

entries.heading: Furmagg de Sègia (PAT)
entries.what: a semi-hard cheese layered with salt and pepper in a sègia (a wooden vessel), which tends to become sharp.

entries.heading: Furmaìn (Furmain)
entries.what: A cow's-milk caciotta from the Emilia area, the ancestor of Formadio, described on the source page as a predecessor of Parmigiano Reggiano. Local names: Furmaìn (Emilian).

entries.heading: Fynbo
entries.what: a semi-hard Danish cheese named after the people of Funen (Fyn); formerly called "Danish Gouda".

entries.heading: Gagauz colostrum pies (name not confirmed)
entries.what: sweet pies made from the first milk of a cow that has just calved, eaten by the Gagauz.

entries.heading: Gailtaler Almkäse (g.U.)
entries.what: Alpine cheese from the Gailtal valley in Carinthia, protected by g.U.

entries.heading: Gailtaler Almschotten (Schotten, Molkenkäse; Carinthia)
entries.what: whey cheese from the Gailtal in Carinthia, listed in the German article on Schotten as an example of Molkenkäse

entries.heading: Gais (Γαΐς)
entries.what: A Pontic cheese named together with Parcharotyr in the Greek Macedonian cuisine article, said to be famed mainly in Kilkis, Veria, Katerini and Ptolemaida.

entries.heading: Gajraila (carrot milk dessert)
entries.what: Carrots boiled in milk with sugar, cream and green cardamom, topped with nuts and dried fruit.

entries.heading: Galaktoboureko (γαλακτομπούρεκο)
entries.what: a custard baked between filo sheets, served plain or with syrup. Its origin is Byzantine-era western Asia Minor (Smyrna), per tradition.

entries.heading: Galão
entries.what: A hot drink of espresso and milk foam, served in a tall glass. About a quarter coffee, three quarters milk foam.

entries.heading: Galatopita (milk pie)
entries.what: a milk cake or pie.

entries.heading: Galaxy (speciality cheese)
entries.what: A speciality cheese brand listed under New Zealand in the Fonterra article.

entries.heading: Galenis Kritis (Γαλένι Κρήτης)
entries.what: Cretan fresh cheese; no details in the source.

entries.heading: Galet de la Loire
entries.what: Named in the list of French cheeses with origin Maine-et-Loire.

entries.heading: Galet solognot
entries.what: a Sologne (Centre) cheese.

entries.heading: Galil (גליל)
entries.what: A creamy Israeli semi-hard cheese named after the Galilee, used on pizza and in sandwiches.

entries.heading: Galomyzithra (Γαλομυζήθρα)
entries.what: a home-made Cretan cheese, not sold commercially, made by the simplest process: milk curdled by natural souring.

entries.heading: Galomyzithra Kritis (Γαλομυζήθρα Κρήτης)
entries.what: Cretan fresh cheese; no details in the source.

entries.heading: Galotyri (Γαλοτύρι; Π.Ο.Π. Epirus and Thessaly)
entries.what: Creamy spread-like product from late-lactation ewes' milk.

entries.heading: Gamle Ole (Old Ole)
entries.what: a strongly pungent, long-aged Danish cheese, eaten on rye bread (rugbrød) with onion and aspic; sometimes rum is dripped on it.

entries.heading: Gappal
entries.what: A locally made dairy product named in the 2019 study and in the 2023 survey, which lists it among six local dairy products. Its exact nature is not described in what I opened.

entries.heading: Gari soakings with milk
entries.what: Gari (roasted dried cassava) soaked with sugar, groundnut and milk; a modern favourite.

entries.heading: Garis / shubat (camel fermented milk; gariss; other names not confirmed)
entries.what: a traditional fermented camel milk, documented in pastoral communities in Sudan. The review lists it among the "shubat-type" fermented camel milk products of Sudan.

entries.heading: Garoobey (oat porridge in milk)
entries.what: A porridge of oats soaked in milk and flavoured with cumin or other spices, eaten as a breakfast food.

entries.heading: Garris (gariss; fermented camel milk)
entries.what: Traditional naturally fermented camel milk in Somalia, listed alongside dhanaan as a documented Somali product; eaten fresh or mixed with cereals.

entries.heading: Gatyk (gatyk; gatygy)
entries.what: A thick drinking yoghurt similar to kefir, served with breakfast. It is also used as a condiment on börek and manty in place of sour cream.

entries.heading: Gaymont's yoghurt (Lacthosa brand)
entries.what: a creamy yoghurt with pieces of fruit and jelly, sold as a Honduran brand.

entries.heading: Gazdovský sýr
entries.what: named in the review as a Czech market cheese.

entries.heading: Gaztazarra (Gaztazaharra; Gazta Zaharra)
entries.what: A traditional Basque-Navarran cheese. The Spanish article calls it "un queso fermentado elaborado en el País Vasco" (a fermented cheese made in the Basque Country); the Basque article lists Gipuzkoa, Araba, Nafarroa and Bizkaia as its regio

entries.heading: Ġbejna (ġbejniet; ġbejna t'Għawdex; ġbejna tan-nagħaġ as the registered GI name)
entries.what: A small round Maltese cheeselet, served in several forms, most associated with Gozo. Fresh ġbejniet are called friski or tal-ilma; sundried ones are moxxa, bajda or t'Għawdex; the salt-cured variety is maħsula; the peppered variety is tal-b

entries.heading: Ġbejna t'Għawdex (sundried ġbejna; also moxxa, bajda)
entries.what: The sundried variety of ġbejna, named after Gozo (Għawdex). Also called moxxa and bajda.

entries.heading: Ġbejna tal-bżar (peppercorn-coated ġbejna)
entries.what: A ġbejna coated in crushed black pepper.

entries.heading: Gebzhalia (გებჟალია)
entries.what: A cold dish of cheese rolled or coated in a mint sauce, served with cornmeal (mchadi or ghomi).

entries.heading: Geheimratskäse (Berglandmilch brand)
entries.what: a cheese brand in the Berglandmilch cheese list

entries.heading: Geitenmelk (goat milk products)
entries.what: Goat milk is made into products in the Netherlands, with much of the output exported. Goat milk powder goes mainly to Asian countries. Goat milk can be an infant formula base (EU-approved 2014).

entries.heading: Geitost (geitost, gjetost, ekte geitost)
entries.what: the goat-milk brunost. "Ekte geitost" (true goat cheese) is the strict version. The brown type is Norway's national symbol (no.wiki).

entries.heading: Gelundener Käse (Lüneberg cheese)
entries.what: Cheese from Vorarlberg's mountain valleys, named in the English list as Lüneberg cheese.

entries.heading: Genfo (ga'at, marca)
entries.what: stiff porridge of barley or wheat flour and water, shaped into a mound with a well in the centre filled with niter kibbeh and berbere.

entries.heading: Gerémezi (Γκερεμέζι Ηπείρου και Αίγινας)
entries.what: Cheese from Epirus and Aegina; no details in the source.

entries.heading: Germantas Gouda (Germantas Gouda; Gouda)
entries.what: a semi-hard Gouda-type cheese sold under the Germantas brand by Žemaitijos pienas, listed at 45 % fat in dry matter. The page calls it one of the world's oldest and most popular cheeses, with regular, evenly spaced eyes in the cut.

entries.heading: Germantas Tilsit (Germantas Tilsit; Tilsit type)
entries.what: a Tilsit-type cheese sold under the Germantas brand by Žemaitijos pienas, bright yellow, soft, slightly sour, with irregular eyes and a crumbly texture; listed at 45 % fat in dry matter.

entries.heading: Gervais Liptov
entries.what: named in the review as still on the Czech market.

entries.heading: Getmessmör / getmesost (goat whey cheese)
entries.what: Goat's-milk variant of messmör/mesost.

entries.heading: Gevinah (גבינה, ancient) and Marvad (מרבד, ancient)
entries.what: Ancient cheeses of the Land of Israel as described in the list page.

entries.heading: Gheu / mar (Sikkim, Arunachal Pradesh)
entries.what: Crude butter from the high-altitude naturally fermented milk of Sikkim (gheu) and Arunachal Pradesh (mar), made alongside chhurpi.

entries.heading: Ghol / chaas (ঘোল)
entries.what: buttermilk drink; the Solop village in Sirajganj District is named for it.

entries.heading: Ghreyba (butter cookies)
entries.what: a Libyan butter cookie.

entries.heading: Giaourtopita (yogurt pie)
entries.what: a yogurt cake soaked in syrup.

entries.heading: Gibna bayda (jibna bayda; Arabic white soft cheese)
entries.what: the most consumed cheese in Sudan by per-capita figures in one source, ahead of muddaffara. Also called a soft white cheese in the Wikipedia cuisine article.

entries.heading: Gidino (γκιντίνο)
entries.what: named on the Naxos page without description.

entries.heading: Gigha (Gigha cheese; Dunlop-style)
entries.what: A Dunlop-style cheese long produced on the Isle of Gigha, Argyll, listed on the Scottish cuisine dairy list.

entries.heading: Gij (kebdzoudz baneyr) (Musa Dagh)
entries.what: A salted cheese of curd mixed with dried thyme, kept in a jug.

entries.heading: Gilboa (גלבוע)
entries.what: A kosher cheese from the Gilboa mountains with a slightly lemony flavour.

entries.heading: Gioda
entries.what: traditional cheese developed in 1928 by Prof. Alessandro Gioda; cylinder about 20 cm across, 1.8–2.5 kg.

entries.heading: Gioddu
entries.what: Listed as a sheep cheese on the Italian Wikipedia list.

entries.heading: Girenbader Chöpfli
entries.what: semi-hard Swiss cheese from the Girenbad dairy near Hinwil (Zürcher Oberland).

entries.heading: Giuncatella abruzzese
entries.what: an Abruzzo variant of giuncata, listed under giuncata on the cuisine page.

entries.heading: Gjizë (gjizë; "Albanian ricotta", salted curd cheese)
entries.what: a fresh curd cheese, called "Albanian ricotta" in the fërgesë section and "salted curd cheese" in the papare section of the cuisine article. Used as a filling in papare and lakror, with leek or tomato and onion.

entries.heading: Glarner Alpkäse (AOP) (Landkäse)
entries.what: A full-fat semi-hard alp cheese from the canton of Glarus, weighing 5 to 9 kg, 28 to 32 cm across, with no eyes. It is also called Landkäse ("country cheese") because of its link to the canton. It has been a protected AOP since 2014.

entries.heading: Glass (ice cream and milk ice cream)
entries.what: Swedish ice cream in several legal categories: hushållsglass (home dessert, 0.5–2 litres), mjölkglass (at least 3% fat, sometimes called lättglass), gräddglass (at least 8% milk fat), saftis, sherbet and sorbet. Swedish ice cream has no leg

entries.heading: Glebe Brethan (Co. Louth)
entries.what: Comté-style cheese from Glebe Brethan, Co. Louth.

entries.heading: Goat cheese, fresh and aged (fromage de chèvre frais et affiné)
entries.what: Fresh and aged goat cheeses made on a farm at Montsinéry and sold at markets and shops in Kourou, Cayenne and nearby areas.

entries.heading: Goat lump cheese (kozí hrudkový syr; Slovak farm-produced "lump goat cheese")
entries.what: a Slovak farm goat lump cheese; the 2024 study (PMC11241544) tested 145 fresh and vacuum-packed samples from Slovak farms.

entries.heading: Goat mabisi
entries.what: mabisi made from goat milk. Rare; in the foodscape study goat milk was not common in any of the three study areas. Some Tonga people milk goats; many Lozi respondents said it was not part of their practice.

entries.heading: Goat milk ice cream (US standard)
entries.what: A US standardised frozen dessert made from goat milk.

entries.heading: Goat milk products (ヤギ乳, yagi-nyū)
entries.what: Small-batch goat-milk products in Japan, including goat yogurt (said to be lower in lactose than cow yogurt), fortified goat milk drinks, goat milk ice cream and cookies, butter and milk powder, and goat-milk lattes and smoothies sold in To

entries.heading: Goat yoghurt (Bulgarian White Dairy Goat milk)
entries.what: a goat-milk yoghurt used in a Trakia University pilot trial in type 2 diabetes patients, with added Aronia melanocarpa juice

entries.heading: Goat-milk liqueur, Fuerteventura (licor de leche de cabra)
entries.what: A liqueur made from goat milk.

entries.heading: Goat-milk white cheese (Otjizondu cheese and yoghurt plant)
entries.what: White cheese made at a cheese and yoghurt plant of 300 litres a day in the rural Otjizondu region, built with Turkish TİKA support to process local goat milk.

entries.heading: Goat-milk-based infant formula
entries.what: Goat-milk-based formula used for infantile colic. A 2026 Saudi survey of pediatricians reports increased availability and marketing of it in Saudi Arabia.

name: Goat's milk as an infant supplement and a milk source

entries.heading: Goat's milk as an infant supplement and a milk source (Jonglei; Toposa)
entries.what: Goat's milk given to infants in Jonglei as a supplement; goats are kept by the Toposa and others for milk.

entries.heading: Goat's milk on Miquelon-Langlade (lait de chèvre; chèvre)
entries.what: Goat milk produced by small farms on Miquelon-Langlade, the commune on the Miquelon island group. The farming is described as serving the local population and passing sailors, and as including dairy and cheese production for the local marke

entries.heading: Goat's milk, Comarca Lagunera (Durango and Coahuila)
entries.what: Milk of goats kept in the Comarca Lagunera, on the border of Durango and Coahuila in northern Mexico, sampled in a 2026 study.

entries.heading: Goat's-milk cheese (сыр з казінага малака)
entries.what: Cheese made from goat's milk, which the source says was more common in the past than today.

entries.heading: Goat's-milk yoghurt (yaourt de lait de chèvre)
entries.what: Yoghurt made from goat's milk on a farm at Montsinéry; the farm's entire milk output goes into yoghurts and cheeses. Cheese is excluded here.

entries.heading: Goldenburg
entries.what: named in the review as a Czech market cheese, 60% dry matter.

entries.heading: Gołka (gołka; Polish)
entries.what: A cylindrical Polish smoked cheese, made from cow's milk where oscypek is made from sheep's milk. Its surface often bears a decorative pattern from the wooden mould.

entries.heading: Golot (Kolot)
entries.what: One of the most important traditional cheeses of the East Black Sea region.

entries.heading: Goma cheese (Masisi cheese, Masisi gouda, Kivu cheese)
