entries.what: A cheese made in the Masisi highlands of eastern DRC, about 25 miles west of Goma, named after Goma. Described as the most widely produced cheese in the area and the only local dairy product sold across the country.

entries.heading: Gomolya (gömölye)
entries.what: a loaf or ball of sweet cheese, about 2–3 kg, made by shepherds on the Great Plain (Alföld); the form with a deep vowel is the Alföld variant, gömölye the other spelling.

entries.heading: Gonnosfanadiga Cirsium
entries.what: One of 16 lesser-known Sardinian cheeses, made by the organic farm Azienda Agricola Biologica Floris.

entries.heading: Gortepap (karnemelkse gortepap)
entries.what: A Dutch porridge of barley groats and buttermilk, served with sugar or syrup (stroop). Classed as a dairy product and dessert.

entries.heading: Gorwydd Caerphilly
entries.what: A Caerphilly made at Gorwydd Farm by Todd and Maugan Trethowan at Tregaron, Ceredigion.

entries.heading: Gotti (brauðostur)
entries.what: A bread cheese that Mjólkursamsalan put into production; it was named through a naming contest, and a song, "Gotti borðar ost", was written for it.

entries.heading: Gouda français
entries.what: A small, round, flattened cheese, 5–6 cm high, about 30–40% fat, of Flemish origin, made in Nord-Pas-de-Calais.

entries.heading: Gournay
entries.what: named in the French Normandy cuisine article as a Normandy cheese, from the Gournay-en-Bray area. Related to the 1828 enriched cheese of Étienne Pommel at Gournay-en-Bray (fr.wikipedia Petit-suisse).

entries.heading: Government cheese
entries.what: A processed cheese distributed through US government food programmes.

entries.heading: Goya
entries.what: a hard cheese from Goya, Corrientes, created in the late 18th century by Gregoria Morales and named after her nickname.

entries.heading: Gräddost
entries.what: Swedish cheese named in the English list with no description.

entries.heading: Graindorge affiné au calvados
entries.what: a Livarot-style cheese ripened in calvados, from the Graindorge producer. Named in the French Normandy cuisine article.

entries.heading: Gran cacio di Morolo (PAT)
entries.what: A large aged cheese from Morolo.

entries.heading: Gran Castelli
entries.what: listed in the Hungary section of the English list of cheeses as a hard, ripened cheese.

entries.heading: Gran Moravia
entries.what: Italian-style aged hard cheese, 30% fat, made in Moravia and ripened in Italy.

entries.heading: Grand Morin (Grand Morin)
entries.what: a cheese listed for the Brie area of Île-de-France; named after the Grand Morin river.

entries.heading: Grand tomachon
entries.what: Bourbonnais tomme from the Allier department.

entries.heading: Granone Lodigiano (PAT)
entries.what: the forerunner of the grana cheeses, valued in the sixteenth century, from the Lodi area; difficult to find; raspadüra is derived from it.

entries.heading: Graskaas
entries.what: A young cheese from the first milk of cows on spring grass.

entries.heading: Grataron du Beaufortain
entries.what: a goat's-milk cheese from the Beaufortain, Savoie, also called grataron d'Arêches.

entries.heading: Graukäse (Formaggio grigio)
entries.what: A lean cheese of the Tyrol, made from a recovery product of butter production; fat under 2 %.

entries.heading: Graval
entries.what: named in the French Normandy cuisine article as a Normandy cheese. No description opened.

entries.heading: Graviera Agrafa (γραβιέρα Αγράφων; Graviera Agrafon)
entries.what: One of three graviera PDOs in the EU register, alongside Kritis and Naxou.

entries.heading: Graviera Kritis (Γραβιέρα Κρήτης; PDO)
entries.what: a yellow hard table cheese from Crete, sold as one of three Graviera PDOs (with Agrafa and Naxos).

entries.heading: Graviera Naxou (Γραβιέρα Νάξου; PDO)
entries.what: the island's best-known cheese; a hard, yellow, firm-textured cheese with a butter-like aroma that strengthens with age.

entries.heading: Graviera Tinou (γραβιέρα Τήνου; Tinos)
entries.what: a hard graviera from Tinos.

entries.heading: Greba (milk-and-butter cookie)
entries.what: A northern Nigerian cookie made with milk and butter, which the source compares to shortbread.

entries.heading: Greek sheep's-milk yogurt (strangistó giaoúrti protó proéleusis; ewe's milk yogurt)
entries.what: traditional Greek yogurt made from ewe's milk. A 2024 study developed a probiotic version with Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus added to starter cultures S. thermophilus and L. bulgaricus; the paper describes the traditional product as the base

entries.heading: Greenlandic coffee cream (whipped cream topping)
entries.what: Whipped cream is a standard topping for Greenlandic coffee, an after-dinner drink of hot coffee, whisky, Kahlúa, Grand Marnier and whipped cream, served in glasses and set alight.

entries.heading: Greuil (Breuil)
entries.what: A cheese of Béarn and the Pays basque.

entries.heading: Grevé
entries.what: Swedish Emmental-like cheese with mild, nutty, sweet taste.

entries.heading: Greyti (a dish with milk)
entries.what: The fo.wikipedia "Mjólk" page says milk is used in greyti, and says nothing about what the dish is. MBM's news on Faroese milk lists greyti among the dishes milk goes into, alongside pancake batter and coffee.

entries.heading: Griș cu lapte (semolina milk pudding)
entries.what: A semolina pudding cooked in milk.

entries.heading: Gris du Périgord
entries.what: A commercial grey-rinded cheese, rind coloured with vegetable charcoal, about 27 % fat.

entries.heading: Grobnički sir
entries.what: a cheese from the Grobnik area (Croatia)

entries.heading: Gros lorrain
entries.what: Lorraine cheese named on the list page.

entries.heading: Groto (drinkable yoghurt)
entries.what: A drinkable yoghurt, described in French Wikipedia's Ivorian cuisine page as "yaourt à boire fait sur du bois dans une boite" (made on wood, in a box).

entries.heading: Grottino
entries.what: semi-hard cheese from the Bündnerland (Graubünden); the article does not place it in Ticino.

entries.heading: Gruyère cream (Crème de Gruyère; Greyerzer Doppelrahm)
entries.what: A double cream from the canton of Fribourg, named after the Gruyères region. Fat content around 50%, above the 45% minimum for Swiss double cream.

entries.heading: Guavaberry coquito (coquito de guayaba; other names: coquito, Christmas coquito)
entries.what: a spiced, rum-based Christmas drink made with milk and coconut, flavoured with guavaberry. The guavaberry page names it as a guavaberry variant of coquito.

entries.heading: Guayanés cheese (queso guayanés)
entries.what: A soft, salty, white cheese from the Guayana region of Venezuela.

entries.heading: Gubbeen
entries.what: semi-soft cow's-milk cheese with a pink-and-white rind; creamy, with mushroom and nutty notes that deepen with age.

entries.heading: Guda (გუდა) — also Tushuri (Tusheti) guda (თუშური გუდა) and გუდის ყველი
entries.what: A Tusheti shepherds' cheese whose preparation takes about 20 days.

entries.heading: Gudbrandsdalsost (also brunost or geitost in Norway; gjetost in US)
entries.what: the most popular brunost in Norway, roughly half of brunost sales (no.wiki).

entries.heading: Guernsey butter (beurre de Guernesey; English "Guernsey butter")
entries.what: Butter made from whole milk, not just cream, historically the island's standard butter. Known for its deep yellow colour, which is attributed to beta-carotene in the milk.

entries.heading: Guernsey cream (crème de Guernesey; cream skin called "wrinkles")
entries.what: Cream from Guernsey milk, which is rich in fat. Sold commercially as Guernsey Cream. Historically the cream on older milkings formed a wrinkled skin, sometimes cracked and blue with mould, which farmers churned in with the milk.

entries.heading: Guernsey milk (fresh whole, low-fat, lactose-free)
entries.what: Milk from Guernsey cows, noted for high fat and protein and golden beta-carotene colour (about 5% fat, 3.7% protein per the breed page). The Guernsey Dairy sells Guernsey milk, a lactose-free low-fat milk, and organic Guernsey milk from its

entries.heading: Gujiya (gujhia)
entries.what: fried pastry filled with sweetened khoa, sugar, coconut and dried fruit.

entries.heading: Gulisua (fried milk-sugar balls)
entries.what: Small balls of milk and sugar, fried.

entries.heading: Güllaç
entries.what: a Ramadan dessert of thin starch wafers layered with walnuts and soaked in milk and rose water, with pomegranate.

entries.heading: Gurt / kurt / qurt (Ru карагурт, karagurt)
entries.what: a round, dried or hardened cheese, salty and hard. The name also appears as karagurt in Russian-language writing.

entries.heading: Karagurt (қарагурт; dried curd)
entries.what: A dairy product listed among Turkmen dairy products in the Russian article.

entries.heading: Guspini Brebiblù
entries.what: One of 16 lesser-known Sardinian cheeses, made by Argiolas Formaggi.

entries.heading: Gvina bulgarit (גבינה בולגרית, "Bulgarian cheese"; Brinza / Bulgarit)
entries.what: A brined, pressed white cheese from the Balkans, brought to Israel by Bulgarian Jews, and common in bourekas and sambusak.

entries.heading: Gypsy tart
entries.what: pastry tart filled with evaporated milk, muscovado or brown sugar.

entries.heading: Habos túrós (curd cream dessert)
entries.what: Layer of vanilla curd-cheese cream under egg-white foam.

entries.heading: Häftings
entries.what: Gotland sheep's-milk hard cheese ("Häftings" and "Häftings Klint").

entries.heading: Haldfør mjólk (UHT long-life milk)
entries.what: Long-life milk used on ships and where fresh milk is not available. Keeps 8 months unopened at up to 25 °C; 2–3 days once opened and chilled. Per 100 g: 3.0 g fat, 3.3 g protein.

entries.heading: Half-and-half
entries.what: A mix of milk and cream, used mainly in coffee; in the US it must contain 10.5–18% milkfat.

entries.heading: Halitzia (Χαλίτσια; spelled as in the source)
entries.what: A feta-like cheese with a slightly sour flavour, eaten in salads.

entries.heading: Halo-halo
entries.what: A shaved-ice dessert in which evaporated milk is the main milk ingredient, poured over the mixture on serving; common toppings include ube ice cream and leche flan. Its ancestor, monggo con hielo, was served with milk and sugar over crushed

entries.heading: Hälsingeostkaka
entries.what: Hälsingland version of ostkaka, sliced and heated with cream in an oven or frying pan.

entries.heading: Halumi (حلومي; halloumi-like)
entries.what: A modern Egyptian cheese that shares its origin word (ḥalūm, medieval Egyptian Arabic) with Cypriot halloumi, but is a different cheese.

entries.heading: Handkäse (Hessischer Handkäse, Handkäs; Bauernhandkäse, Korbkäse, Stangenkäse, Spitzkäse)
entries.what: A small, soft sour-milk cheese, traditionally hand-shaped into small round cakes, usually eaten marinated in onion, vinegar and oil ("mit Musik").

entries.heading: Hapankerma (soured cream), with kermaviili, smetana and ranskankerma
entries.what: Soured cream made by lactic fermentation of cream. In Finland it comes in three main kinds: kermaviili (see its own entry), smetana (sour cream using a Russian culture; Finnish versions about 40% fat) and ranskankerma (crème fraîche; about

entries.heading: Hapiruto (Nepali yak cheese product)
entries.what: A yak cheese product named alongside chhurpi and chuto.

entries.heading: Hard cheese, industrial (сыр)
entries.what: Factory hard cheese; the fastest-growing cheese line in the 2026 output figures.

entries.heading: Hard white cheese / morolique (queso blanco duro artesanal; also called morolique)
entries.what: A semi-dry, firm but soft-textured white cheese with low moisture. It does not melt when heated and is less salty and less crumbly than feta, to which it is similar in appearance.

entries.heading: Harzer Käse (Harzer Roller; Harzer; Harzer Käse)
entries.what: A small, strong-smelling sour-milk cheese with a yellow-to-red smear, a Standardsorte under German cheese rules. Only the low-fat version (under 10% fat in dry matter) exists.

entries.heading: Hasi (goat cheese, named origin)
entries.what: one of the named traditional goat-cheese origins sampled for hygiene; the paper reports its E. coli counts as partly beyond a measurable upper limit.

entries.heading: Hatted kit (Scotland)
entries.what: Scottish milk pudding.

entries.heading: Hauskyjza (hauskyjza; also ser smażony, ser zgliwiały; Polish)
entries.what: A traditional Polish fried cheese dish; name comes from German "Hauskäse" (home cheese).

entries.heading: Haytaliya (هيطلية)
entries.what: A milk pudding named in the Syrian cuisine article.

entries.heading: Hazo (spiced fermented buttermilk)
entries.what: spiced fermented buttermilk, reddish and thicker than buttermilk. Most common in the north, especially Tigray. Served to guests, respected family members and at socio-cultural festivals.

name: Heat-treated milk: pasteurised, UHT and sterilised
names: นมพาสเจอร์ไรซ์
นมสเตอรีไลซ์

entries.heading: Heat-treated milk: pasteurised, UHT and sterilised (นมพาสเจอร์ไรซ์, นมยูเอชที, นมสเตอรีไลซ์)
entries.what: retail milk types listed as processed milk products on the Thai milk article. Sterilised milk has no article of its own.

name: Hegarty's Cheddar, Hegarty's Smoked Cheddar, Templegall

entries.heading: Hegarty's Cheddar, Hegarty's Smoked Cheddar, Templegall
Heidal cheese (heidalsost, heidal)
entries.what: a dark brown Norwegian brunost named after the parish of Heidal, in the northern Gudbrand valley. It is a type of Gudbrandsdalsost.

entries.heading: Heidi (Mirasaka, semi-soft washed-rind blue goat)
entries.what: A semi-soft, washed-rind blue goat cheese from Mirasaka Fromage.

entries.heading: Helado de paila (Nariño)
entries.what: Traditional ice cream of Nariño, usually milk-based; made in a paila (copper pan).

entries.heading: Helado de Tocumbo (ice cream associated with Tocumbo)
entries.what: Ice cream "mostly associated with the town of Tocumbo", listed with fruit jellies as sugar-based desserts.

entries.heading: Helado frescolita con leche
entries.what: A milk ice cream named after the Frescolita soft drink, popular in the barrios (working-class neighbourhoods).

entries.heading: Herbillette
entries.what: Named in the list of French cheeses with origin Vendée, Pays de la Loire.

entries.heading: Hereford Hop
entries.what: An English cheese from Herefordshire, with Dymock given as the town.

entries.heading: Hermelín (Sedlčany hermelín)
entries.what: Czech white-mould cheese, made mainly in Sedlčany, Central Bohemia, sold under many brands. Named after the ermine fur look.

entries.heading: Herregårdssmør (manor-farm butter)
entries.what: manor-farm butter, in demand in towns from the late Middle Ages.

entries.heading: Herreño (Queso herreño; El Hierro)
entries.what: A soft cheese from El Hierro, sold fresh or matured, with an important place in the Canary smoked-soft-cheese market.

entries.heading: Herrgårdsost (Herrgård)
entries.what: Mild, sweet, nutty Swedish cheese with small round holes. Emmental-style; the modern type was refined in the 1800s.

entries.heading: Herzegovina sack cheese (cheese in sack; Nevesinje sack cheese; sir u mijehu)
entries.what: A semi-hard cheese matured in an animal-skin sack, usually made in the Herzegovina region, and linked to the Nevesinje area.

entries.heading: Heumilch (cow milk, hay-fed; Heumilch brand)
entries.what: milk from cows fed without silage, under a certified Austrian brand run by ARGE Heumilch Österreich; the EU recognises it as a "Garantiert traditionelle Spezialität"

entries.heading: Hininy (date and full-fat milk sweet)
entries.what: A dessert from the dish paper: dates, flour, full-fat milk, butter and sugar.

entries.heading: Historic cattle-herd cheese (unnamed; Falklands cattle era)
entries.what: A source on the Falklands' cattle history says some herd cows were kept for milk production, and that the milk was made into cheese and butter. The cheese has no name in the source.

entries.heading: Hjerter i flødesovs (hearts in cream sauce)
entries.what: Danish dish using cream as the sauce (heart-shaped items in cream sauce).

entries.heading: Hlyahanka (ґляґанка), Poltava kashkaval
entries.what: Poltava (Poltavshchyna) sheep cheese, listed as the Ukrainian alternative name of kashkaval.

entries.heading: Hochpustertaler (Formaggio Alta Pusteria)
entries.what: A ripened cheese, white with a dense eye pattern and a hard rind; cylindrical, about 40 cm across, 10 cm high, around 15 kg.

entries.heading: Hokey pokey (honeycomb ice cream)
entries.what: Vanilla ice cream with small lumps of honeycomb toffee. In NZ "hokey pokey" is the local name for honeycomb toffee.

name: Hollandia Evaporated Milk and Mai shai tea

entries.heading: Hollandia Evaporated Milk and Mai shai tea (milk tea)
entries.what: Evaporated milk added to tea by tea sellers (Mai shai) in Jos and northern towns; the brand's marketing claims customers ask for it.

entries.heading: Hollandia yoghurt (drinkable yoghurt; Chi Limited)
entries.what: Plain sweetened and strawberry drinking yoghurt, presented as Nigeria's leading drinking yoghurt, popular in northern cities.

name: Holy Goat fresh curd, La Luna and Nectar

entries.heading: Holy Goat fresh curd, La Luna and Nectar (Sutton Grange, Victoria)
entries.what: Goat cheeses from Carla Meurs and Anne-Marie Monda's organic farm and purpose-built dairy at Sutton Grange, central Victoria. Three are named: a fresh curd, La Luna (a large ring-shaped cheese with a geotrichum "geo" rind), and Nectar (a ne

entries.heading: Homemade (locally produced) butter
entries.what: Butter made locally and sold at markets in Mbarara, south-western Uganda.

entries.heading: Homolje cheese (homoljski sir)
entries.what: a white brined cheese from the Homolje valley and mountains, east of Morava

entries.heading: Homolky (dried curd)
entries.what: named Czech dried curd product on the Tvaroh page.

entries.heading: Homolky (dried curd)
entries.what: Dried tvaroh.

entries.heading: Hooidammer
entries.what: A Dutch organic cheese brand produced in Heerenveen (Friesland). The brand started in 1980 on the cheese farm of Jan and Wennie Craens. Fat 50%, cylindrical shape.

entries.heading: Hooikaas
entries.what: A winter-period cheese from hay-fed cows. Naturally pale, so coloured with annatto.

entries.heading: Hoop cheese
entries.what: A pressed farm cheese shaped in a wooden hoop.

entries.heading: Horácká polévka (Horácko cream soup)
entries.what: Soup of potatoes and cream typical of the Horácko region.

entries.heading: Horezu
entries.what: A sheep's cheese from the town of Horezu (Vâlcea county), named after the town.

name: Household white brined cheese and fresh cheese

entries.heading: Household white brined cheese and fresh cheese (local names not given in the sources read)
entries.what: Traditional artisanal cheeses made in households of North Macedonia, sampled in a review of Western Balkan autochthonous dairy alongside Serbia, Croatia, Slovenia, Bosnia and Herzegovina and Montenegro.

entries.heading: Hóvirág sajt
entries.what: a processed block cheese made by most county dairies in the socialist era, wrapped in foil and cut at the counter.

entries.heading: Hramatka (граматка; hramatka)
entries.what: A beer soup with egg yolks, curd and sour cream. In the 19th century it replaced coffee and tea for the middle class.

entries.heading: Huevitos de leche (milk-candy balls)
entries.what: Small balls of milk candy, a traditional Panamanian dessert sweet.

entries.heading: Human breast milk and colostrum (Bulgarian mothers, research samples)
entries.what: breast milk and colostrum of Bulgarian mothers, sampled for their bacteria; not a donor-milk or retail product

entries.heading: Humboldt Fog
entries.what: A goat cheese named after the fog that rolls into Humboldt Bay.

entries.heading: Hushållsost
entries.what: Mild but somewhat sour Swedish cheese with small granular holes ("household cheese").

entries.heading: Hutsul cow brynza (Гуцульська бринза, коров'яча)
entries.what: second Ukrainian registered food indication of this kind, granted 2020 per the source.

entries.heading: Hutsul sheep brynza (Гуцульська бринза, овеча)
entries.what: Carpathian (Hutsul) sheep brynza, the first Ukrainian food geographical indication of its kind, registered 2019 per the source.

entries.heading: Huweirneh (حويرنة)
entries.what: a salad of hedge mustard dressed with yoghurt

entries.heading: Hvíta (soft fresh curd; hvíta)
entries.what: A soft, mild fresh product eaten at breakfast or as a snack, and used in home-made dressings. Per 100 g: 83 kcal, 7.5 g protein, 4.0 g fat. Sold in 150 g pots; one variant with raspberry, blueberry or redcurrant.

entries.heading: Ibakhbakhane (Ibakhebakhane)
entries.what: An Aurès cheese whose particularity is crushed green barley (z'rabi) added to the milk.

entries.heading: Ice cream and frozen desserts (imported)
entries.what: Ice cream and edible ices imported into Vanuatu, tracked in import statistics and tariff analysis.

entries.heading: Ice cream and plombir (мороженое, пломбир)
entries.what: Russian ice cream incl. plombir (creamy), milk and cream types; Eskimo (эскимо) on stick, Soviet-era.

name: Ice cream and stick ice cream

entries.heading: Ice cream and stick ice cream (Dairibord; Lyons Maid)
entries.what: Dairibord ice creams, sold as "Ice Creams", "Stick Ice Creams & Cones", and under the Lyons Maid brand. Dairibord's Wikipedia page says it owns Lyons Zimbabwe, which makes ice creams.

name: Ice cream from powdered milk and coconut

entries.heading: Ice cream from powdered milk and coconut (Pago Pago, reported by a visitor)
entries.what: A frozen dessert sold in Pago Pago that a visitor reported was made from powdered milk and coconut, sold by the 10-litre bucket.

entries.heading: Ice cream sandwich (street-cart ice cream)
entries.what: ice cream served on bread or between wafers.

name: Ice cream soda and ice cream float

entries.heading: Ice cream soda and ice cream float (root beer float, Boston cooler)
entries.what: Ice cream added to a soft drink or flavoured soda water; a US soda-fountain drink.

entries.heading: Ice cream sundae
entries.what: Ice cream with syrup, fruit or nuts served in a dish; a late-19th-century US dessert.

name: Ice cream, as recorded in children's diets

entries.heading: Ice cream, as recorded in children's diets
entries.what: Ice cream in the diet records of children in the same USAP study sample that includes American Samoa.

entries.heading: Ice cream, industrial (мороженое; aiskrim)
entries.what: Factory ice cream; Emil began in 1993 making only ice cream and makes over 100 flavours.

entries.heading: Ice kacang (shaved ice dessert with milk toppings)
entries.what: shaved ice with red beans, sweet corn, attap chee, grass jelly and syrups, topped with milk.

entries.heading: Ice milk (US ice milk, under 10% milk fat)
entries.what: A frozen dessert made from dairy milk with less milk fat than ice cream.

entries.heading: Iced coffee with milk (Farmers Union Iced Coffee)
entries.what: Packaged iced coffee made from coffee, milk and sweetener. In South Australia, Farmers Union Iced Coffee has outsold Coca-Cola and is one of the state's biggest brands.

entries.heading: Iced milk tea (凍奶茶; chilled milk tea, 冰鎮奶茶)
entries.what: Hong Kong-style milk tea served cold. Also sold bottled and canned in convenience stores.

entries.heading: Icelandic-made blue cheese (industrial)
entries.what: Blue cheese made by Icelandic dairy cooperatives.

entries.heading: Icelandic-made Camembert-style cheese (industrial)
entries.what: Camembert-style cheese made by Icelandic dairy cooperatives.

entries.heading: Icelandic-made Gouda-style cheese (industrial)
entries.what: Gouda-style cheese produced by Icelandic dairy cooperatives.

entries.heading: Ighounane
entries.what: A cheese from the Djurdjura heights in Kabylie, made from colostrum.

entries.heading: Ikivuguto (Kivuguto; Kinyarwanda, also ikivuguto)
entries.what: a traditional Rwandan fermented milk, described as a thick fermented milk consumed in many households and listed among non-alcoholic drinks. Scientific sources describe it as a traditional, spontaneously fermented product that is also a sou

entries.heading: Il grande vecchio di Montefollonico (PAT)
entries.what: large sheep pecorino from Montefollonico.

entries.heading: Île d'Yeu
entries.what: Named in the list of French cheeses with origin Vendée, Pays de la Loire.

entries.heading: Îles flottantes (floating islands)
entries.what: Soft meringue poached and floated on a crème anglaise sauce.

entries.heading: Illa mabisi and illa butter
entries.what: illa mabisi is a churned version of backslopping. The butter is the product: butter granules formed by churning, used in cooking and as a skin lotion. Illa practice is mainly in Southern and Central provinces, among the Illa and Tonga peopl

entries.heading: Imdeghest (Medghissa)
entries.what: A processed cheese from the Chaouia region, made from dried Klila cooked in milk; eaten as a snack.

entries.heading: Imeruli (იმერული ყველი) — also Chkinti (ჭყინტი) and "Imeretian cheese"
entries.what: A traditional white, salted cheese from Imereti; the main cheese in Imeruli khachapuri and one of two cheeses in Adjarian khachapuri. With sulguni it makes up up to 80% of Georgian cheese production (per the Wikipedia page on Chkinti).

entries.heading: Imokilly Regato
entries.what: hard, dry-firm cheese with a piquant, Italian-style flavour and nutty, creamy taste; light golden-creamy colour.

entries.heading: Imported cheese (trade category; not a local cheese)
entries.what: Cheese named as one of the imported items in PNG's food trade. The source's footnotes list "butter, cheese, and sweetened milk" as examples of items that are not ultra-processed.

entries.heading: Imported cheese and curd (industrial, from Australia and Fiji)
entries.what: Cheese and curd bought into Tonga as imports. The trade pages give the value of the imports, not the product types. The Australian figure is US$7.41 thousand in 2025; the Fiji figure is US$461 in 2020.

name: Imported condensed and sweetened milk, milk and cream, yoghurt and buttermilk

entries.heading: Imported condensed and sweetened milk, milk and cream, yoghurt and buttermilk (imported, mainly from Thailand)
entries.what: Dairy products bought in Brunei but not made there. The 2024 import values from Thailand were: concentrated or sweetened milk and cream about US$747K; buttermilk, yoghurt and kefir about US$160K; milk and cream not concentrated about US$52K

entries.heading: Imported dairy (trade category; not a single product)
entries.what: The "Dairy" category of PNG's processed food imports, valued at about US$7.6 million in 2001/05 and about US$13.1 million in 2014/18 (real 2016 USD), about 4% of processed food import value in 2014/18. The same source's footnotes name butte

name: Imported fresh, UHT and dairy products

entries.heading: Imported fresh, UHT and dairy products (general)
entries.what: Dairy products are brought into American Samoa from outside; the same account says meat and dairy are "shipped in" because cattle farming is not practical on the steep terrain.

entries.heading: Imported milk (general; fresh, powdered or tinned, not specified)
entries.what: Milk that is imported in processed form and used as a food staple despite high prices relative to local incomes.

entries.heading: Imported milk and milk products (fresh, UHT, powdered, condensed)
entries.what: the milk eaten in Liberia is not made locally; the national agriculture overview says the country has no dairy industry and all milk is imported. This is the only dairy supply statement found.

entries.heading: Imported milk powder (reconstituted milk; powdered milk)
entries.what: Powdered milk imported into Mauritius, which together with fresh milk makes up the national milk supply. Imports are used because feed for local dairy cows is expensive.

name: Imported milk, cream, yoghurt, cheese and butter

entries.heading: Imported milk, cream, yoghurt, cheese and butter (EU exports to Guinea-Bissau, 2025)
entries.what: EU export values to Guinea-Bissau for 2025: milk and cream not concentrated or sweetened US$1.02M; milk and cream concentrated or sweetened US$908K (the category that would include condensed and evaporated milk, not named on the page); butt

entries.heading: Imsil cheese (임실치즈; Imsil cheese)
entries.what: The cheese produced by the Imsil Cheese Factory in Imsil County, North Jeolla. The source calls it the first domestic Korean cheese, made in Imsil; the factory also makes yogurt.

entries.heading: Inbriago
entries.what: A cow's-milk cheese of the Treviso province made by soaking finished cheeses in grape pomace (vinacce). It is a regional traditional cheese (RTC) of Veneto.

entries.heading: Incanestrato di Castel del Monte (Pecorino canestrato di Castel del Monte)
entries.what: a cheese of the Castel del Monte area, province of L'Aquila.

entries.heading: Industrial butter (Kerrygold)
entries.what: Kerrygold, the national co-operative's main brand, formerly Irish Dairy Board.

entries.heading: Industrial Emmental-type and Gouda-type cheeses (Valio)
entries.what: Supermarket cheeses, with brand names as examples only (for example Mustaleima and Sinileima Emmental, Salaneuvos and Keisarinna Gouda, Alppi Kreivi Bergkäse, Edam 17%, Oltermanni 17% slices).

name: Industrial ghee, butter oil and milk powder

entries.heading: Industrial ghee, butter oil and milk powder (processors)
entries.what: Products of licensed processing plants listed in Wikipedia's list of milk processors in Uganda.

entries.heading: Industrial ice cream (Pilpa, Boudou, Piton des Neiges)
entries.what: ice creams sold under the brands Pilpa, Boudou and Piton des Neiges, listed among the products of CILAM.

entries.heading: Industrial yoghurt and curdled milk (Mali)
entries.what: commercially made yoghurts and curdled milk products sold in Mali, sampled alongside traditional products.

entries.heading: Industrial yoghurt and liquid milk (Chile market)
entries.what: Mass-market liquid milk and yoghurt sold in Chile; the sector article reports yoghurt consumption growing 1.1% and liquid milk 4.1%.

name: Industrial yoghurt from reconstituted milk powder

entries.heading: Industrial yoghurt from reconstituted milk powder (Solam, Yoplait franchise)
entries.what: Industrial yoghurts made in French Guiana from milk powder, produced by Solam, a Yoplait franchisee.

name: Industrial yogurt, doogh and flavoured milk

entries.heading: Industrial yogurt, doogh and flavoured milk (Kalleh Dairy, Amol)
entries.what: Product lines of Kalleh Dairy, an Iranian dairy company in Amol founded in 1991, which says its Amol factory receives over 2,000 tonnes of milk a day. Lines named: fresh yogurt, yogurt with cream, dripped (strained) yogurt, diet yogurt, a b

entries.heading: Industrially processed (heat-treated) milk
entries.what: milk and dairy products sold through the formal channel after industrial heat treatment. A Zambian study sampled such products in Lusaka, Southern and Western provinces and found no S. aureus in them, in contrast to raw milk.

entries.heading: Industrially processed dairy (butter, milk powder, yoghurt)
entries.what: Products made by processing plants across Uganda, sold locally and exported (butter to Kenya).

entries.heading: Infant formula, powdered (imported)
entries.what: powdered infant formula sold in Addis Ababa supermarkets and pharmacies. All products sampled were imported from Asia, Europe or the USA.

entries.heading: Informal human donor milk sharing (Hong Kong)
entries.what: Mothers in Hong Kong share surplus breast milk through private Facebook groups. Hong Kong has no dedicated human milk bank.

entries.heading: Ioulsan (Aoules)
entries.what: A dry cheese from the Hoggar, made by Tuareg herders; resembles skyr, karish and quark, but dried hard.

entries.heading: Ipoh white coffee (Chinese: 怡保白咖啡)
entries.what: A lighter-roasted coffee from Ipoh, usually served with sweetened condensed milk. Hot or iced.

entries.heading: Ircano
entries.what: Listed among Sardinian cheeses.

entries.heading: Irish cream liqueur
entries.what: Cream liqueur made with Irish whiskey, cream and flavourings, 15–20% ABV. Not a traditional Irish product: Baileys was created in London in 1973.

entries.heading: Irkotta (ħaxu; Maltese ricotta)
entries.what: A traditional Maltese ricotta-style cheese, used for savoury and sweet fillings.

entries.heading: Irman Dairy packaged milk (sachet milk, Mogadishu)
entries.what: Locally processed milk sold in 1-litre sachets in Mogadishu, set up as an alternative to imported milk powder and raw milk from local small farmers.

entries.heading: Ísbland (ice-cream base)
entries.what: The base for home-made vanilla ice cream: milk, cream, sugar and vanilla beans; also used for iced coffee, iced cocoa and milkshakes. Per 100 g: 7 g fat, 3 g protein.

entries.heading: Isgelen tarag (ісгэлэн тараг; "isgelen tarag", "cold tarag")
entries.what: A mildly alcoholic fermented milk drink made by Mongolian nomadic families, also important in Buryatia and Inner Mongolia, served to honoured guests. Basis for arkhi distillation.

entries.heading: Iskrem (fløteis, melkeis, fruktis, margarinis)
entries.what: a frozen mix of cream, flavourings and sweeteners. The article sets Norwegian categories: fløteis at least 10 % milk fat; melkeis 4–10 % milk fat; fruktis under 4 % milk fat with at least 10 % fruit or berries; margarinis uses fat other tha

entries.heading: Isle of Man Creamery milk (fresh whole, semi-skimmed and skimmed cow milk)
entries.what: Fluid cow milk sold in whole, semi-skimmed and skimmed forms. The creamery says it is a co-operative of family-owned dairy farms with farm-assured herds supplying "farm fresh, grass-fed" milk.

entries.heading: Isle of Man Double Gloucester
entries.what: A Double Gloucester made by the Isle of Man Creamery, described as buttery, creamy and golden.

entries.heading: Isle of Man Flavoured Cheddars (cracked peppercorn, garlic and chive, jalapeño)
entries.what: Three flavoured mature cheddars from the Isle of Man Creamery: cracked black peppercorn (1%), garlic (0.1%) and chives (0.1%), and jalapeño chilli (0.5%).

entries.heading: Isle of Man Mature Cheddar (Manx cheddar; with flavoured variants)
entries.what: The Isle of Man Creamery's core cheese. The mature cheddar is the base for its blended and smoked varieties. Sold in UK supermarkets, and per Wikipedia also in some Canadian supermarkets.

name: Isle of Man Mild Coloured Cheddar

entries.heading: Isle of Man Mild Coloured Cheddar
entries.what: A mild, naturally coloured cheddar from the Isle of Man Creamery.

name: Isle of Man Mild White Cheddar

entries.heading: Isle of Man Mild White Cheddar
entries.what: A mild, mellow white cheddar from the Isle of Man Creamery.

name: Isle of Man Oak-Smoked Mature Cheddar

entries.heading: Isle of Man Oak-Smoked Mature Cheddar (Manx smoked cheddar)
entries.what: Mature cheddar cold-smoked over oak chips for a subtle taste. Wikipedia names smoked varieties among Manx cheeses sold in UK supermarkets.

entries.heading: Isle of Man Red Leicester
entries.what: A Red Leicester made by the Isle of Man Creamery, described as an old favourite with deep colour and smooth taste.

entries.heading: Isle of Man Vintage Cheddar
entries.what: A long-matured cheddar with a subtly sweet, nutty flavour.

entries.heading: Isle of Mull Cheddar (Isle of Mull cheddar; cow's milk Cheddar)
entries.what: A Scottish Cheddar from the Isle of Mull, described as a very sharp white cheddar with some blue veining at the edges and a slightly nutty taste.

entries.heading: Íslenskar mysuafurðir (whey-based sweet drinks)
entries.what: Sweet drinks made from whey, marketed by the dairy cooperatives. A joint venture of Mjólkursamsalan and Kaupfélag Skagfirðinga.

entries.heading: Israeli feta (gvinat Rosh Hanikra, "Rosh Hanikra cheese")
entries.what: An Israeli brined cheese sometimes sold abroad as "Israeli feta."

entries.heading: Istanbuli / Istanbolly (اسطنبولي)
entries.what: A white cheese similar to feta.

entries.heading: Istarska skuta
entries.what: skuta from Istria

entries.heading: Italian-style ice cream (Wales)
entries.what: ice cream tradition brought to Wales by Italian immigrants who came with the coal and steel industries in the late 19th century.

entries.heading: Italico (Bel Paese; PAT)
entries.what: the Italico name is recognised for a cheese from the Lodi and Pavia areas; the Bel Paese brand was created in Milan in 1906 by Egidio Galbani.

entries.heading: Ititu (concentrated sour milk; "milk curd")
entries.what: A traditional concentrated fermented milk made by pastoralists, mainly Borana (southern Ethiopia) and Kereyu (eastern Oromia). The sources sometimes call it "milk curd" and class it among the fermented milk products.

entries.heading: Ititu (itittuu; concentrated fermented milk / cottage yoghurt)
entries.what: concentrated sour fermented milk, typically made by the Borana in southern Ethiopia and the Kereyu area of Oromia; Afar and Oromia also named. Shelf life 2–3 months at room temperature. Called a cottage yoghurt in the Jimma paper.

entries.heading: Jadel
entries.what: Czech braided cheese stored in brine; prized because it does not melt on heating.

entries.heading: Jalca (Mantaro de Huancayo, "Quesos de Autor")
entries.what: An Andean cheese from Mantaro de Huancayo with red quinoa mixed into the paste.

entries.heading: Jamriyah (milk, ghee and honey dish)
entries.what: A dish from the dish paper with whole wheat flour, sugar, milk, sesame, dates, ghee and honey.

entries.heading: Jāņu siers (Jāņu siers; ķimeņu siers "caraway cheese")
entries.what: the traditional Midsummer (Jāņi) cheese of Latvia, flavoured with caraway seed. It is a symbol of Latvian identity.

entries.heading: Japanibhog (জাপানিভোগ)
entries.what: sweetmeat named in the 2025 Bogura and Dhaka shop survey; priced BDT 700/kg in Bogura.

entries.heading: Japonesa (japonesa; Spanish: japonesa)
entries.what: A sweet fried doughnut with a creamy, custard-like filling, popular in Gibraltar.

entries.heading: Jarlsberg (Jarlsberg cheese)
entries.what: Norway's best-known export cheese, developed in Norway in 1956 by Ole Martin Ystgaard at the Dairy Institute of the Agricultural University of Norway, based partly on 1850s recipes and Swiss 1830s recipes.

entries.heading: Jarma (жарма)
entries.what: A drink made from ground cereals mixed with ayran. It is made fizzy by mixing, not by fermenting.

entries.heading: Jben el Djarra
entries.what: A cheese from the steppe regions, heavily salted and packed in a sealed clay jar for slow fermentation.

entries.heading: Jben el Gfas
entries.what: A moulded cheese from Bou Saâda and Djelfa.

entries.heading: Jben el Qaleb
entries.what: A fresh cheese from the Atlas blidéen and Médéa.

entries.heading: Jben M'fased (Jben el Hamiz)
entries.what: A cheese made from milk that has matured or been deliberately soured, mixed with garlic, chilli and spices.

entries.heading: Jersey butter
entries.what: Butter from Jersey milk, described as central to island cooking.

entries.heading: Jersey cow milk (fresh milk, pure-breed Jersey)
entries.what: Milk from the Jersey breed, known for high butterfat. The island dairies hold a monopoly on local milk supply.

entries.heading: Jersey cream
entries.what: Cream from Jersey milk, described as central to island cooking.

entries.heading: Jersey frozen ice cream
entries.what: Frozen ice cream made by Jersey Dairy from pure-breed Jersey milk.

entries.heading: Jersey kefir
entries.what: Kefir sold by Jersey Dairy from pure-breed Jersey milk.

entries.heading: Jersey milk (ジャージー牛乳, Kurokawa Onsen, Kumamoto)
entries.what: Non-homogenised Jersey milk from Yama no Ibuki, a farm at Kurokawa Onsen, Aso (Minamioguni, Kumamoto), with butterfat over 5% on average. The Jersey brand launched in 2009.

name: Jersey soft ice cream and thickshake

entries.heading: Jersey soft ice cream and thickshake
entries.what: Soft-serve ice cream and thickshake sold by Jersey Dairy.

entries.heading: Jersey yoghurt
entries.what: Yoghurt sold by Jersey Dairy from pure-breed Jersey milk.

entries.heading: Jiaoke (fermented butter, Xilin Gol; transliteration only in the source)
entries.what: A fermented dairy product from Inner Mongolia's Xilin Gol, described as white with a fragrant flavour and similar to sour cream. Fourteen samples were taken in a Northeast Asia microbiome study.

entries.heading: Jibneh mshallaleh (جبنة مشللة / جبنة مصلوقة; also tresse, braided cheese, mshallaleh)
entries.what: A Syrian string cheese, described as originating in Syria, eaten plain or in pastries, and a substitute for Oaxaca cheese.

entries.heading: Jihočeská niva (South Bohemian Niva)
entries.what: PGI blue cheese from South Bohemia, cylindrical, about 2.8 kg, 180–200 mm diameter.

entries.heading: Jihočeská zlatá niva (South Bohemian Golden Niva)
entries.what: PGI sibling of Jihočeská niva, same plant and process.

entries.heading: Jogurella (yoghurt and related, Berglandmilch)
entries.what: a Berglandmilch brand in the yoghurt range

entries.heading: Jogurt za piće (yoghurt drink served with burek)
entries.what: Unsweetened, unsalted yoghurt drink called "jogurt" in the Balkans, usually drunk with burek.

name: Jogurti s voćem i grčki jogurt

entries.heading: Jogurti s voćem i grčki jogurt (Vindija yoghurts)
entries.what: Vindija's yoghurt range, including fruit yoghurt and Greek-style yoghurt, with the "Protein" and "Fortia" lines.

entries.heading: Jogurtové mléko / zákys (drinkable yoghurt)
entries.what: A thinner yoghurt with broken-up curd, usually fruit-flavoured.

entries.heading: Johnny Cake (johnny cake; Bonaire)
entries.what: A flat, round pastry fried in oil, made from flour, milk and butter, eaten on Bonaire as a Kuminda Krioyo snack.

entries.heading: Jólagrautur (Yule rice pudding)
entries.what: Rice pudding with raisins, cinnamon and sugar, traditionally served at Christmas.

entries.heading: Jonchée d'Oléron
entries.what: A cheese from the Île d'Oléron, Saintonge (Charente-Maritime).

entries.heading: Joogijogurt (drinkable yoghurt)
entries.what: thinner yoghurt with jam, no fruit pieces

entries.heading: Joyya (ultra-filtered milk)
entries.what: a milk brand Saputo launched in Canada; the Saputo article cites the launch under the title "Saputo launches ultra-filtered milk brand Joyya in Canada".

entries.heading: Juhayna Greek yoghurt (Juhayna brand; Arabic name not in opened sources)
entries.what: Juhayna's Greek yoghurt range, including The Original, Peach, Pineapple, Mixed Berries, French Vanilla Beans, Oats and Flaxseeds, Acai, The Balanced, The Guilt Free and The Indulging. The category text calls it an authentic Greek yoghurt wi

entries.heading: Juhayna stirred yoghurt (Juhayna brand; Arabic name not in opened sources)
entries.what: Juhayna's stirred yoghurt in 105 g cups, in three versions: plain, light and sweetened. Juhayna describes it as a smooth, creamy yoghurt with a less sour taste.

entries.heading: Juhtúró (brindza)
entries.what: a sheep cheese made mainly in Central and Eastern Europe; the Hungarian Wikipedia article calls it juhtúró, and the same cheese is called brindza.

entries.heading: Junín (Mantaro de Huancayo, "Quesos de Autor")
entries.what: An Andean cheese from Mantaro de Huancayo made with red wine in the paste.

entries.heading: Jura
entries.what: A Swiss cheese of the Franches-Montagnes district of the canton of Jura, in the Gruyère family.

entries.heading: Jus de fruit (mango milk drink)
entries.what: A traditional beverage of mango, milk, sugar and cardamom.

entries.heading: Jus papaye (papaya milkshake)
entries.what: A papaya milkshake: papaya juice blended into a milkshake and flavoured with vanilla.

entries.heading: Jyukushi-gaki (熟柿, Mirasaka washed-rind goat)
entries.what: An autumn goat cheese from Mirasaka Fromage, washed-rind, shaped like a persimmon.

entries.heading: Kaas 'Van Weenink' (kaas van Weenink; Dutch, cow's milk)
entries.what: The main cheese of Kaasboerderij Weenink, an artisanal farm cheese made on the Eimersweg in Lievelde, in the Achterhoek (Gelderland).

name: Kaas by Michi and Rudisa & Nuprocess

entries.heading: Kaas by Michi and Rudisa & Nuprocess (industrial cheese; type not named)
entries.what: Cheese made by two commercial dairies, Michi and Rudisa & Nuprocess, from the early 2000s, per the Dutch article on livestock farming in Suriname.

entries.heading: Kachagolla / kanchagolla (কাচাগোল্লা)
entries.what: a dessert made from dairy ingredients and sugar; from Natore District.

entries.heading: Kachkéis (Kachkéis; Cancoillotte in French; Kochkäse in German, "cooking cheese")
entries.what: A runny, spreadable cheese that is a staple of everyday Luxembourgish meals. The Luxembourg version is closely linked to the French cheese Cancoillotte, which comes from Franche-Comté.

entries.heading: Kačkavalj (general, Serbia)
entries.what: the general Serbian name for a yellow hard cheese; the regional variants follow below

entries.heading: Kaçkavall (kaçkavall; kashkaval type)
entries.what: described as the second most popular cheese in Albania after djathë i bardhë; treated as traditional and often served as a side dish, sometimes raw or fried.

entries.heading: Kadaka juust (Kadaka cheese)
entries.what: smoked semi-hard cheese from the island of Saaremaa.

entries.heading: Kadhi (कढ़ी; karhi)
entries.what: Yoghurt and gram flour gravy; origin Rajasthan, where it was made because vegetables were scarce.

entries.heading: Kærnemælksost (buttermilk cheese)
entries.what: a Danish cheese made from buttermilk, listed on Danish Wikipedia.

entries.heading: Kæsa (mild, firm cheese; kæsa)
entries.what: A mild firm cheese made by MBM at its Hoyvík dairy and sold in Faroese shops. Per 100 g: 325 kcal, 24 g protein, 25 g fat. Used on bread and on tapas boards; MBM recipes include pasta and pizza-waffle dishes with Kæsa.

entries.heading: Kaffeost (kahvijuusto, finska leipäjuusto)
entries.what: A cheese eaten with coffee, traditional in northern Finland, Tornedalen, Norrbotten, Västerbotten and Lappland. Also called meänkieli kahvijuusto, finska leipäjuusto, juustoleipä, finlandssvenska brödost and bondost. Served on its own or in

entries.heading: Kagg (5-kilo Kagg, granular-eyed)
entries.what: A 5-kilo granular-eyed cheese made from 1958 to 1963 at Hejde dairy on Gotland; the Koggost article notes it is not the same as Koggost.

entries.heading: Kaïkou
entries.what: A cheese of the Pays basque.

entries.heading: Kaimaghi (ყაიმაღი; Adjaran კაიმაღი)
entries.what: thick, creamy product, about 60% milk fat, similar to clotted cream; eaten at breakfast or as dessert in the Caucasus and beyond. In Adjara it is the local version.

entries.heading: Kaimaki ice cream (white cream ice cream; mastic)
entries.what: a chewy ice cream flavoured with mastic (kaimaki).

entries.heading: Leipäjuusto (juustoleipä; kahvijuusto in Tornionlaakso and Länsipohja; hiilikko; Kainuun juustoleipä)
entries.what: A squeaky bread cheese traditionally from Pohjanmaa (Southern Ostrobothnia), Lappi and Kainuu, eaten with coffee in diamond-shaped pieces, often with cloudberry jam (lakkahillo).

entries.heading: Kainuun juustoleipä (Kainuulainen juustoleipä; Kainuu bread cheese)
entries.what: A protected-name variant of leipäjuusto from Kainuu and the former Vaala municipality (now in Northern Ostrobothnia). Mild, squeaky texture; dark-spotted surface on both sides.

entries.heading: Kakao (cocoa milk drink)
entries.what: MBM's cocoa drink in four versions: regular (1.5% fat), light (0.5%), luxury (4%), and a sports cocoa (0.8% fat, 3.4 g protein). Per 100 g of the regular one: 1.5 g fat, 3.6 g protein, 5.5 g added sugar.

entries.heading: Kalaba
entries.what: a yoghurt from Nevşehir made from a 2:1 mix with cream separated.

entries.heading: Kalari (Dogra cheese, Jammu)
entries.what: Indigenous cheese of the Dogra people of the Jammu region, developed to keep milk in solid form through hot summers.

entries.heading: Kalimpong cheese
entries.what: Cheese from Kalimpong, West Bengal, started by Jesuit priest Father Andre Butty.

entries.heading: Kalmyk milk tea (калмыцкий чай, джомба)
entries.what: Milk tea brought by the Kalmyks from Dzungaria in the 17th century; spread among North Caucasian groups, Volga Russians, and peoples of Astrakhan and Dagestan. Chechens call it "galmakh chai".

entries.heading: Kalojam (কালোজাম)
entries.what: a dark fried chhana sweet listed among Bangladeshi chhana sweets.

entries.heading: Kalti (კალტი)
entries.what: a Tusheti shepherds' product with a strong smell, a soft consistency and a spicy taste; eaten traditionally with alud (a local beer); about half of production is now sold at markets as dry kalti or Tushuri kalti.

entries.heading: Kalvdans (calf dance, colostrum pudding)
entries.what: A traditional Scandinavian dessert made from colostrum, the first milk a cow gives after calving. It sets to a jiggly, pudding-like texture, hence its name.

entries.heading: Kalvedans (råmelkspudding, spannost, pottost, kjelost, råmjølkspudding)
entries.what: a traditional Norwegian dessert of råmelk (colostrum) and ordinary milk. The high protein of colostrum makes it set firm without gelatin or egg.

entries.heading: Kama (roasted flour mixed with milk or buttermilk)
entries.what: a quick filling meal of roasted grain flour, mostly barley, rye, oat and pea

entries.heading: Kamadet
entries.what: named in the review as a Czech market cheese.

entries.heading: Kanach panir (Kanach panir; mould-ripened, Shirak)
entries.what: A cheese with a greenish appearance and crumbly texture, commonly eaten in Shirak Province, typically served fresh and not used in cooked dishes.

entries.heading: Kandıra manda yoğurdu (Kandıra water buffalo yoghurt)
entries.what: a buffalo-milk yoghurt from Kandıra, Kocaeli.

entries.heading: Kaņepju sviests (hemp butter)
entries.what: Roasted, ground hemp seeds mixed with butter or hemp oil.

entries.heading: Kanlıca yoğurdu (Kanlıca yoghurt)
entries.what: a thick yoghurt named after Kanlıca on the Bosphorus.

entries.heading: Kannoli (kannoli tal-Malta; Maltese cannoli)
entries.what: The Maltese version of the cannoli, a tube-shaped fried pastry shell filled with sweetened ricotta. Wikipedia lists it as a Maltese variation of the cannoli.

entries.heading: Kapiti speciality cheese (Kāpiti)
entries.what: A Fonterra brand in NZ that the Fonterra article lists for speciality cheese, ice cream and yoghurt.

entries.heading: Kappeler Milchsuppe (Kappel milk soup)
entries.what: A soup of milk and bread that Zug and Zürich soldiers shared at Kappel am Albis in June 1529, during the First Kappel War. Its pot became a symbol of negotiated peace and national identity.

entries.heading: Karamelrand and fløderand
entries.what: caramel custard ring (karamelrand) and its vanilla variant fløderand.

entries.heading: Karaván
entries.what: a smoked Hungarian cheese, listed in both the English and Hungarian lists.

entries.heading: Kare-ye mahalli (local butter, کره محلی — script not given)
entries.what: Butter sold in Iran; "local butter" in dairy shops and in most of Iran means yogurt-based butter, which is whiter and sour, unlike cream butter, which is yellow. Also mostly eaten at breakfast and sold in packaged blocks; electric churns ha

entries.heading: Karish (Karish, Kareish; also "defatted cheese"; Arabic name not in opened sources)
entries.what: One of Egypt's most popular local fresh cheeses, somewhat salty, valued for its high protein and low fat.

entries.heading: Karishi (قريشة; also Areesheh; "Lebanese ricotta")
entries.what: A fresh, soft, moist, slightly sweet, crumbly whey cheese made by reheating the whey left after curd or halloumi production. Served at breakfast with bread, tomato or olive oil; used in sweets and stuffed pastries.

entries.heading: Karnemelkse bloempap (karnemelkse pap; bloempap; zoepenbrij in the north)
entries.what: An old Dutch porridge of buttermilk and flour, eaten warm with stroop (syrup) or brown or white sugar. In the north of the Netherlands it is called zoepenbrij.

entries.heading: Kars gravyer
entries.what: A Turkish cheese similar to Emmental, though the name suggests Gruyère.

entries.heading: Kartoffelkäse (Erdäpfelkäse, potato spread)
entries.what: spread named after cheese for its mild, milky taste, per the article; found in Lower Bavaria, Inner Austria and Western Austria

entries.heading: Kartuli (ქართული ყველი)
entries.what: A generic Georgian cheese made from a milk blend.

entries.heading: Karyki Tinou (Καρίκι Τήνου)
entries.what: Tinos cheese; no details.

entries.heading: Kaşar (kashar; kaşar peyniri; Turkish cheddar; Kars and Thrace)
entries.what: "Turkey's other ubiquitous cheese," often called Turkish cheddar. Closer to mild cheddar than other Turkish cheeses.

entries.heading: Kashk / qurut / keşk (کەشک, كشك)
entries.what: A dried, salted sour dairy product made from strained yoghurt or drained buttermilk, ground into powder or dissolved in water. In Iraq it is listed among the kashk-type products of the region, with the Kurdish form keşk.

entries.heading: Kashkawan / Kashkaval
entries.what: A yellow semi-soft cheese believed originally Turkish.

entries.heading: Kashmiri butter (wrapped in chinar leaves)
entries.what: Organic Kashmiri butter wrapped in chinar leaves. Once common, now sold by only a few sellers.

entries.heading: Kaskavali Pindou (Κασκαβάλι Πίνδου; Π.Γ.Ε.)
entries.what: Pindos cheese with PGI status.

entries.heading: Kastelholm (Kastelholm; Swedish name; ÅCA dairy product)
entries.what: A cheese sold by the Åland dairy cooperative ÅCA, described on the tourism site as especially tasty. It is sold in supermarkets across the islands.

entries.heading: Kat'nashor (կաթնաշոռ; curd)
entries.what: A dairy product made by souring milk. Made mainly from low-fat or skimmed milk, mixed with buttermilk (tan). Armenian Wikipedia's infobox classifies it as a cheese type.

entries.heading: Katak (катък; krokmach, kroukmach, kurtmach, katmach; salty sour dairy product)
entries.what: a traditional Bulgarian product, most common in southern Bulgaria; name of Turkish origin meaning "addition".

entries.heading: Katak (катък) — also qatiq, katyk, katuk, krotmach, krukmach, kurtmach, katmach
entries.what: a salty, sour, traditional sheep-milk product, described in sources as a curd or yoghurt-like product. The name is Turkish-derived per bg.wikipedia. Studied as a source of lactic acid bacteria

entries.heading: Kathoura Ikarias (Καθούρα Ικαρίας)
entries.what: Cheese from Ikaria; no details in the source.

entries.heading: Katnapur (կաթնապուր; milk soup)
entries.what: A milk soup. Armenian Wikipedia cites "arishta" milk soup (katnapur with arishta pasta) as a festive dish for the Hambardzum (Ascension) holiday.

entries.heading: Katun (goat cheese, named in Guinean cuisine)
entries.what: Named as "a variety of goat cheese" in the English Wikipedia article on Guinean cuisine.

entries.heading: Katyk / kefir-type sour drink
entries.what: drinkable sour milk used as the base for chakka and diluted into cholob (see below).

entries.heading: Kaya toast butter (butter with kaya)
entries.what: butter spread on toast with kaya (coconut and egg jam). Kaya itself is not dairy; the butter is the dairy part.

entries.heading: Kaymak / kajmak (кайымак)
entries.what: Thick, creamy milk-fat product, about 60% fat, similar to clotted cream. The Kaymak wiki lists Kyrgyzstan among its countries and says the word comes from Turkic "kanak" (skin on milk).

entries.heading: Kazandibi
entries.what: a Turkish dessert whose base is caramelised or burnt; served upside down with the caramelised side up; developed in the Ottoman palace kitchens.

entries.heading: Kefalaki Tinou / Androu (Κεφαλάκι, στρογγυλό, βολάκι)
entries.what: Tinos and Andros cheese; no details.

entries.heading: Kefalonian white-brine cheese (Greek name not given in source; feta-type)
entries.what: traditional artisanal white-brine cheese of Kefalonia, described in the paper as having a history back to Homeric times and as a local trademark.

entries.heading: Kefalos Vuka vuka cheese (Kefalos Vuka; commercial, Zimbabwe)
entries.what: a commercial Zimbabwean cheese named in a 2017 study of lactobacilli from locally sold dairy and beverage products. The study isolated lactic bacteria from it and tested them against E. coli.

entries.heading: Kefalotyri of Epirus (Κεφαλοτύρι, traditional sheep-milk type from Arta and Filippiada)
entries.what: a hard salty cheese made in Epirus. A research programme named "Traditional Kefalotyri of Epirus" was funded for the local producer.

entries.heading: Kefír / acidofilné mlieko (kefir; acidophilus milk)
entries.what: Kefir and acidophilus milk are listed as Slovak-associated soured milk products.

entries.heading: Kéfir casero (domestic kefir from Costa Rican grains)
entries.what: Kefir made at home with domestic kefir grains from Costa Rica. The paper notes that commercial kefir is rising in availability and cost.

entries.heading: Kefir cheese (גבינת קפיר)
entries.what: A cheese made from kefir grains rather than rennet or added acid, listed among Israeli cheeses.

entries.heading: Kéfir de lait (milk kefir)
entries.what: A lightly fizzy fermented drink made with kefir grains (bacteria and yeasts).

entries.heading: Kefir grains (Greek, Athens and Crete)
entries.what: the grains used by two artisanal kefir producers, one in Athens and one in Crete. Lactobacillus kefiranofaciens made up about 95–96% of the bacteria in both.

entries.heading: Kefir, Emil (кефир)
entries.what: Kefir among the products of the Emil dairy in Ust-Kamenogorsk, East Kazakhstan.

entries.heading: Keju parut (Malay: "keju parut", grated cheese; generic, type not named)
entries.what: A generic Malay term for grated cheese. It is an ingredient of the sambal served with nasi katok, a Bruneian dish of steamed rice with fried chicken and sambal.

entries.heading: Keltic Gold
entries.what: A Cornish semi-hard cheese.

entries.heading: Kem (ice cream), kem que and Kem Tràng Tiền
entries.what: Stick ice cream (kem que, cà rem or cà lem, from French crème); Kem Tràng Tiền is a Hanoi shop-brand founded in 1958 that sells several kinds of ice cream.

entries.heading: Kemariya (Takemmarite)
entries.what: A traditional cheese of M'zab, eaten as a festive dessert with honey, peanuts and mint tea.

entries.heading: Kermaviili (cream viili)
entries.what: A Finnish sour cream product used in cooking, baking and cold sauces. Served with dill or chives as a cold sauce for fish, or as a dip base. Made from cream, not milk.

entries.heading: Kerry Blue (Knockatee Cheese, Co. Kerry)
entries.what: Traditional blue cheese in the Stilton style from Knockatee Cheese, Co. Kerry.

entries.heading: Keş (kashk, keşk, keş peyniri)
entries.what: a dried, salty yoghurt product known as keş peyniri, kurut or katık keşi; keşk in southeast Kurdish areas; classed as cheese in Bolu.

entries.heading: Kesäkeitto (summer vegetable soup)
entries.what: A traditional Finnish vegetable soup made with butter and milk.

entries.heading: Kesam
entries.what: a Norwegian lean soured fresh product that can be classed as kvarg; TINE launched TINE Kesam in 2003. Variants: TINE Kesam Mager (1% fat), TINE Kesam Vanilje Mager (0.6% fat).

entries.heading: Kesam (kvarg, fresh curd cheese-like product)
entries.what: a fresh, soured skimmed milk curd, usually called kvarg (German quark). In Norway TINE launched TINE Kesam in 2003 (plain, 1 % fat low-fat version, and vanilla at 0.6 %). Q-Meieriene launched Q-Snjo (vanilla kvarg with jam to stir in) in 20

entries.heading: Keshk / kishk (كشك; keshk)
entries.what: Wheat or cracked wheat fermented with yoghurt, milk or buttermilk, then dried and powdered. In Egypt eaten as a savoury pudding made from yoghurt and flour or as a stock/paste base (per Egyptian cuisine page, "keshk" pudding seasoned with f

entries.heading: Keşkül
entries.what: an almond-based milk pudding sold in Istanbul muhallebici shops, with a name from Ottoman Turkish "keşkül-i fukara" (beggar's bowl).

entries.heading: Kesong puti (kesong puti; quesong puti, kesilyo, kasilyo, quesillo in Cavite, queseo or kiseyo in northern Cebu)
entries.what: A soft, unaged Filipino white cheese, traditionally from unskimmed carabao milk. Mildly salty and tart. Sold wrapped in banana leaves. Used as a side dish, breakfast item and bibingka topping.

entries.heading: Kettugol (cream from milk fat)
entries.what: Cream skimmed from milk ("crème de lait"); the English article says kettugol is derived from milk fat and is used in light cooking and in hair weaving (non-food use).

entries.heading: Kettugol / lebol (milk fat)
entries.what: Milk-fat products used in light cooking and in hair weaving, per the Wikipedia Fulbe article; not called butter or ghee in the text.

entries.heading: Kəsmik (kəsmik, curd; Azerbaijani; likely the cottage-cheese equivalent)
entries.what: A soft curd produced from qatıq, similar in process to süzmə.

entries.heading: Kəsmik (curd)
entries.what: coagulated dairy product described as healthy; made into over 55 products (cakes, creams); recommended as infant food from 6–7 months.

entries.heading: Khacho (ხაჭო; curd / cottage-type curd)
entries.what: dairy product obtained by lactic acid fermentation; sold in semi-fat, fat-free and full-fat forms; used in khachapuri (kotori) and vareniki and khinkali fillings.

entries.heading: Khachoerbo (ხაჭოერბო)
entries.what: Dried cottage cheese shaped into a ball, listed for the mountain regions Mtianeti, Khevi, Khevsureti, Pshavi and Tusheti.

entries.heading: Khailmag (khailmag; caramelised clotted cream / butter)
entries.what: A caramelised clotted-cream product, eaten as a dessert; also described as a butter.

entries.heading: Khaysi / Kaysi (historical; medieval)
entries.what: A medieval Damietta cheese, possibly an ancestor of Dumyati.

entries.heading: Kheer / patar kheer (ক্ষীর; patar kheer)
entries.what: a thick sweetened dessert eaten fresh; Shahnaz et al. 2004 says patar kheer is sold commercially in one region of Bangladesh (region not named).

entries.heading: Kheer / payasam / payesh / doodh pak (खीर, पायसम, পায়েস)
entries.what: Milk pudding made with rice or other grains (or vermicelli, sago, tapioca, barley, pumpkin), with sugar or jaggery and cardamom, saffron, nuts.

entries.heading: Kheer kharkoon (Sindhi milk and dates dish)
entries.what: A Sindhi milk dish prepared with dates.

entries.heading: Kheersha (ক্ষীরশা)
entries.what: sweetmeat named in the 2025 Bogura survey; priced BDT 700/kg; name suggests kheer (sweetened, reduced milk).

entries.heading: Khiram (хярам)
entries.what: A summer drink made by boiling water with about 30% milk, used to quench thirst.

entries.heading: Khirni (Sindhi rice pudding)
entries.what: A hot, sweet pudding of milk and crushed rice, served in Sindh.

entries.heading: Khiroubaneyr (Musa Dagh)
entries.what: A cheese from milk coagulated with yogurt water.

entries.heading: Khiroubaneyr
entries.what: A Musa Dagh preparation made by adding yoghurt water to milk.

entries.heading: Kholodnyk / cold borscht (холодник; холодний борщ)
entries.what: Chilled borscht blended with kefir, yoghurt or soured milk and served with hard-boiled egg.

entries.heading: Khurenge (хурэнгэ, Buryat fermented milk) and darasun (дарасун, Buryat milk spirit)
entries.what: Buryat sour fermented milk drink, distilled into a strong spirit (darasun) by a traditional multi-stage still; the only documented Russian case of distilling fermented milk in this paper, which places it among Mongolic peoples and their nei

entries.heading: Khuruud (хурууд; khuruud)
entries.what: A very hard dried cheese, eaten after soaking in tea or water. Stores indefinitely; historically a food for soldiers on campaign.

entries.heading: Khuruud (khuruud; hard pressed curd)
entries.what: A rock-hard, long-keeping dried curd made from aarts, rehydrated in hot water or added to tea. A second, uncultured form is pressed into moulds as a hospitality plate item.

entries.heading: Khuwa (खुवा; thickened milk)
entries.what: Milk reduced by heating to a thick mass, used as base for peda and barfi.

entries.heading: Kibbeh labaniyyeh (كبّه لبنيّه)
entries.what: meat and bulgur kibbeh boiled in jameed (dried yoghurt) broth

entries.heading: Kibe / qibe (traditional butter; kibe in Amharic)
entries.what: traditional unsalted butter churned from fermented sour milk or cream. Sold on the market as one of the main dairy products. Also used as hair oil and to dress wounds.

entries.heading: Kievitskaas (De Kievit, Grijpskerk; kievitskaas)
entries.what: A well-known product of De Kievit, a dairy at Grijpskerk, Groningen province, operating 1888–1969. The article calls it "kievitskaas" and says the factory was mainly a cheese plant by 1968.

entries.heading: Kiki (پنیر خیکی, "skin cheese"; also پنیر خاکه and پنیر پوستی per the article)
entries.what: A traditional Iranian cheese, historically made in most cities and villages of Iran and still made in some villages, especially among nomadic tribes. The article names Babol (Mazandaran) and tribal groups in North Khorasan.

entries.heading: Kilcreen
entries.what: A cheese from Dart Mountain Cheese, County Londonderry.

entries.heading: Kilis Yörük yoğurdu
entries.what: a Yörük-made yoghurt from Kilis, started with ayran.

name: Killeen Goat Gouda and Killeen Cow Gouda

entries.heading: Killeen Goat Gouda and Killeen Cow Gouda
entries.what: 5 kg wheels, aged two months to a year.

entries.heading: Kinche (porridge boiled in milk or water)
entries.what: porridge boiled in milk or water, then combined with spiced clarified butter, oil and fried onions.

entries.heading: Kindirmo (thick sour cream-like milk)
entries.what: A thick, creamy soured milk in northern Nigeria, eaten plain or with millet dishes. Sometimes described as the thick layer or as yoghurt-like.

entries.heading: Kindirmou
entries.what: A traditional fermented milk of Cameroon, named in the 2026 Pendidam paper alongside artisanal yoghurt and pendidam as products made by women in the Far North; the microbial diversity review lists it as a Cameroon milk product. Second pass:

entries.heading: King Kong (King Kong de Lambayeque)
entries.what: A large layered Lambayeque sweet of biscuits joined by manjar blanco, pineapple jam and peanut jam. A patent was registered in 1943 by the San Roque family firm; it is recognised as a regional heritage item.

entries.heading: Kirnumaito products (buttermilk powder and milk protein concentrate)
entries.what: The milk from continuous butter churns (kirnumaito) is used in Finland to make buttermilk powder and milk protein concentrate.

entries.heading: Kisela pavlaka and pavlaka (кисела павлака; sour cream; sweet cream)
entries.what: sour cream used in stews, pies, salads, and as a condiment with savory meats and cold cuts; in larger markets labelled kisela pavlaka with 15–30% fat, historically closer to clotted cream.

entries.heading: Kiselo mlyako (кисело мляко) — Bulgarian yoghurt
entries.what: the national yoghurt, made with the two bacteria Lactobacillus delbrueckii subsp. bulgaricus and Streptococcus thermophilus, which work together and do not ferment milk alone. Bulgarian standard BDS requires Bulgarian-isolated cultures for

entries.heading: Kita no Oichizu (北のおいちず, Naganuma)
entries.what: A cheese from the Naganuma Ice Cream Dairy Workshop, Hokkaido, with a hint of soy sauce.

entries.heading: Kithul treacle buffalo curd (kithul peni)
entries.what: Meekiri eaten with kithul (Caryota urens) palm treacle poured over it; the treacle sweetness balances the curd's sourness. Coconut syrup is sometimes used instead.

entries.heading: Kittost (washed-rind type)
entries.what: Swedish term for washed-rind cheeses that are dipped in a yeast and bacteria culture in acidified skimmed milk during ripening, forming a "kitt" rind.

entries.heading: Kivevé (sweet cornmeal and milk paste)
entries.what: A semi-sweet paste of andaí squash and cornmeal, with milk and cheese.

entries.heading: Kış yoğurdu (winter / salted yoghurt)
entries.what: a salted yoghurt eaten through the winter; the salted type is cooked and topped with olive oil or butter.

entries.heading: Kjúkur
entries.what: Listed among Icelandic cheese types on the Icelandic cheese overview page.

entries.heading: Klemensker
entries.what: a cheese name linked to Klemensker village on Bornholm, where Bornholms Andelsmejeri, the island's only dairy, makes cheese.

entries.heading: Klobučník
entries.what: named in the review as a Czech market cheese.

entries.heading: Knight Žumbera (Žumbera)
entries.what: named Czech cheese from West Bohemia, produced for decades.

entries.heading: Knockdrinna goat and sheep range (Fresh Goats Log, Goat's Brined Cheese, Gold, Meadow Sheep's Cheese, Snow)
Kobi (კობი)
entries.what: A mixed cow and sheep milk cheese, mostly eaten in eastern Georgia.

entries.heading: Kochkäse
entries.what: A viscous, spreadable sour-milk preparation served on bread, often "mit Musik" with onion marinade. Known as Cancoillotte in France, Kachkéis in Luxembourg, Brennkäse in the Odenwald, and Glundner Käse in Kärnten.

entries.heading: Koffie verkeerd
entries.what: Coffee with a large amount of ordinary milk. The name ("wrong coffee") distinguishes it from coffee with a splash of milk. In Belgium, lait russe.

entries.heading: Koffieverrijker (coffee creamer; Friesche Vlag coffee milk)
entries.what: Coffee creamers sold under Dutch brands; the Friesche Vlag name survives mainly on creamers after 2012. Other names on the page: Nutroma, Goudband, Halvamel, Completa.

entries.heading: Koggost (Gotland hard cheese)
entries.what: A hard cheese made in Klintehamn on Gotland during the 1980s, per the sv article (past tense).

entries.heading: Kohupiim (kohupiim; Lõuna-Eesti: vaarapiim)
entries.what: a soft white curd, eaten salted or sweetened and used in many dishes. Central to Estonian desserts and cold table.

entries.heading: Kohupiim (curd; vaarapiim in South Estonian dialects)
entries.what: soft curd used in desserts and eaten salted or sweetened; high in calcium and phosphorus

entries.heading: Kohupiimakreem (curd cream dessert)
entries.what: creamy curd dessert named on the Estonian cuisine page

entries.heading: Koji Cheese KURA (Japanese name not in sources)
entries.what: A soft cheese matured with koji mould and sake lees, developed by a seven-institution consortium led by Nippon Veterinary and Life Science University; sold since summer 2021.

entries.heading: Koko Samoa (koko Samoa; cocoa drink)
entries.what: A traditional Samoan cocoa drink made from cocoa beans ground into a paste and sweetened; milk is sometimes added.

entries.heading: Koldskål (kærnemælkskoldskål; "cold bowl")
entries.what: sweet chilled dairy drink or dessert from Denmark, eaten cold, mostly in summer; traditionally served with tvebakker or kammerjunkere biscuits, sometimes with strawberries or banana. Also eaten as a main meal in NW Jutland.

entries.heading: Koliba
entries.what: named in the review as a Czech market cheese.

entries.heading: Komboïri (milk soup)
entries.what: A soup made with milk, listed as a Peul dish.

entries.heading: Komos (κόμος; Naxos)
entries.what: a Naxos cheese suited to frying (saganaki).

entries.heading: Kondensmilch (evaporated / condensed milk)
entries.what: milk concentrated to about 23 % dry matter; sold unsweetened or sweetened, in four fat grades

entries.heading: Kondensmilch / Dosenmilch (evaporated and sweetened condensed milk)
entries.what: milk with part of its water removed, shelf-stable in cans, bottles, cartons or tubes. German law sets fat tiers: unsweetened full-fat at least 7.5%, coffee cream at least 15%, partly skimmed 1.0 to under 7.5%, skim up to 1%; sweetened full-

entries.heading: Kopanisti (Κοπανιστή; Π.Ο.Π. Cyclades)
entries.what: Salty, spicy cheese from the Cyclades (Mykonos, Tinos, Andros, Syros, Naxos); a meze, often served as mostra with bread, tomato and olive oil, or with ouzo.

entries.heading: Kopanisti Ikarias (Κοπανιστή Ικαρίας)
entries.what: Ikaria version of kopanisti; no details in the source.

entries.heading: Kopanisti Mykonou (κοπανιστή Μυκόνου; PDO)
entries.what: a salty, peppery cheese made across the Cyclades (PDO shared by all Cyclades islands per travel.gr), most famous from Mykonos; spreadable.

entries.heading: Kopi peng (iced coffee with condensed milk)
entries.what: iced local coffee made with condensed milk.

entries.heading: Kopi-C (coffee with evaporated milk)
entries.what: local coffee sweetened with sugar and evaporated milk.

entries.heading: Korall (Коралл)
entries.what: Soviet-era soft processed cheese flavoured with shrimp; about 10% fish paste; around 60% fat, at most 2% salt.

entries.heading: Korbáčik / korbáčiky (korbáčiky, korbáčik; Slovak; "cheese strings")
entries.what: a Slovak cheese pulled into long threads and plaited; sold today as a snack for children (Liptov brand steamed version named in search results).

entries.heading: Korfou (Κορφού Κέρκυρας; Corfu yellow cheese)
entries.what: a yellow cheese of Corfu.

entries.heading: Korfou Kerkyras (Κορφού Κέρκυρας)
entries.what: Corfu cheese; no details.

entries.heading: Koryciński (ser koryciński, koryciński; Podlaskie specialty)
entries.what: A rennet cheese from Gmina Korycin in the Podlaskie Voivodeship. Sold as "Swojski" with spiced, herbed or garlic variants.

entries.heading: Kos (yoghurt)
entries.what: thick yoghurt, the basis of several Albanian dishes and drinks; eaten at breakfast with bread

entries.heading: Koskenlaskija (processed cheese, Valio)
entries.what: A Finnish processed cheese sold as a block, spread and slices; flavoured versions include cold-smoked reindeer, green pepper, paprika and herb-garlic.

entries.heading: Kosora (Blue Cheese II Kosora; Japanese name not in sources)
entries.what: A blue cheese made at Niseko Cheese Factory (Niseko-cho, Hokkaido) on European cheesemaking principles.

entries.heading: Kostroma cheese (Костромской сыр)
entries.what: One of the most widely produced cheeses in Russia; mild, slightly sour; first made in the second half of the 19th century at dairies founded by Vladimir Blandov, Kostroma (first dairy 1878; about 120 factories by 1912).

entries.heading: Kozji sir Zadravec (Međimurje goat cheese)
entries.what: a goat cheese made at home or on a farm in Međimurje, named Zadravec in the image file name

entries.heading: Kraft Fresh Mozzarella (Morinaga / Kraft Japan, mozzarella fresh)
entries.what: A fresh mozzarella sold in Japan under the Kraft brand by Morinaga Milk Industry.

entries.heading: Kraft Kireteru Cheese (processed slice; Japanese name not in sources)
entries.what: A pre-sliced processed cheese from Morinaga's Kraft line in Japan, released in 1990.

entries.heading: Kraft Philadelphia Cream Cheese (Morinaga, Japan market)
entries.what: Philadelphia-style cream cheese sold in Japan under the Kraft brand by Morinaga Milk Industry.

entries.heading: Kraški ovčji sir (Karst sheep cheese)
entries.what: Hard sheep-milk cheese from the Karst (Kras) region, with a PDO.

entries.heading: Krčki sir
entries.what: a cheese from the island of Krk

entries.heading: Krem / kremë e thartë (cream and sour cream)
entries.what: fresh cream used in desserts; sour cream served with grilled meats

entries.heading: Krem karamele (custard) and pastry cream
entries.what: custard dessert of milk, cream, egg yolk, sugar and vanilla, flavoured with citrus zest or cinnamon; a pastry cream is used as a filling in zupa and other desserts

entries.heading: Krema (Greek custard)
entries.what: a custard sweet flavoured with vanilla and chocolate, made with yogurt.

entries.heading: Kremas / Crémasse / krèmas (Haitian Creole, Crémasse in French)
entries.what: A sweet, creamy, rum-based drink served cold, mostly at Christmas and at social events. It is also sold in markets.

entries.heading: Kremost (Norwegian cream cheese)
entries.what: a fresh cheese used for spreads, baking (ostekake), flavouring and thickening; available in several flavours, fat levels, and organic versions.

entries.heading: Kriol trifle (milk-based coconut dessert)
entries.what: a Kriol dessert similar to coconut cake, made with milk, flour, sugar, eggs, lemon essence, margarine, baking powder and half-green grated coconut

entries.heading: Krivi Vir kačkavalj (krivovirski kačkavalj)
entries.what: a caciocavallo-type cheese named after Krivi Vir in the Zaječar region

entries.heading: Kruidenkaas, Weenink herb cheeses (Dutch: kruidenkaas; cow's milk)
entries.what: The farm's "befaamde kruidenkazen" (famous herb cheeses), made at the same Lievelde farm, from the same cow's milk.

entries.heading: Krupicová kaše (semolina porridge)
entries.what: Semolina porridge served with butter, honey or cocoa.

entries.heading: Kruudmoes (kruutmoes; groenmoes; melkmoes)
entries.what: An old hearty porridge for agricultural workers in Gelderland and Overijssel, with buttermilk, barley groats, bacon, smoked sausage, raisins and lots of fresh herbs (chervil, parsley, celery, fennel, dill, spearmint, sorrel).

entries.heading: Ksinishta ruhan (Yaghnobi fermented goat milk)
entries.what: traditional fermented goat milk made by the Yaghnob people in the Upper Zarafshan valley of Tajikistan; the Yaghnobi livelihood relies on goats and cows.

entries.heading: Küflü peynir (Kuflu, mould-ripened cheese of Konya and Karaman)
entries.what: a traditional mould-ripened cheese of Turkey's Central Anatolia, mainly from Konya and Karaman provinces.

entries.heading: Kulturmelk (TINE trademark for soured milk)
entries.what: TINE's trademark for soured milk. Full-fat version 3.8 % fat; skimmed version 0.4 % fat. Also sold flavoured as TINE Cultura and TINE Biola. TINE says it suits baking as an ingredient.

entries.heading: Kumështi (kumësht, whey drink; also "Kumështa")
entries.what: a drink made from the whey left over when cheese or gjizë is made; per the Albanian article, many dairy producers in Kosovo, North Macedonia and Albania sell it to consumers as a diet-product drink

entries.heading: Kumis / airag / 马奶酒 (mare's milk wine)
entries.what: Fermented mare's milk, slightly alcoholic, historically consumed in northern China by Han, Khitan and Jurchen peoples and widely in Mongol-ruled territory. Chinese name 马奶酒 (also 奶酒).

entries.heading: Kumis ice cream
entries.what: Ice cream flavoured with kumis, reported as sold in Astana.

entries.heading: Kumõss (fermented mare's milk)
entries.what: mare's milk fermented by lactic acid bacteria and yeast

entries.heading: Künefe peyniri
entries.what: Used to make künefe (knafeh), the hot dessert with kadayıf and melted cheese.

entries.heading: Kunik
entries.what: A blend of goat's milk and cow's cream.

entries.heading: Kupres cheese (Kupreški sir)
entries.what: A cheese from Kupres in western Bosnia, recognised by the producers' association; the bs Wikipedia Sir page links to an article about award-winning Kupres cheeses.

entries.heading: Kurut / Kurt (курут, курт, коро́т, ак гурт)
entries.what: Central Asian dried curd, also used in Bashkiria and among Khakas and Shor (Russian regions).

entries.heading: Kurut and keş
entries.what: Dried bricks from yogurt (kurut) and from çökelek (keş). Keş is a fermented, strained sour yogurt that can be eaten as cheese or used in soups.

entries.heading: Kvargli
entries.what: a Hungarian curd cheese with a yellow coating and a strong smell; the Hungarian article links it to Olmützer Quargel (Olomouc, Czech Republic).

entries.heading: Kwaito (Kwaito cheese; no article on en.wikipedia)
