entries.what: A South African gouda-style cheese made from cow's milk, with a creamy texture and mild flavour. Sold plain or smoked, and sometimes flavoured with peppercorns or other peppers.

entries.heading: Kwerionik
entries.what: Traditional cultured milk made by pastoral Bahima in western Uganda, consumed within about 7 days.

entries.heading: Kyalagyosh
entries.what: A matsun soup with sour cream, named on the English Armenian cuisine page alongside spas and mantapour.

entries.heading: Kymyz / kumys / kumis (кымыз, qymyz)
entries.what: Fermented mare's milk, central to Kyrgyz and Kazakh steppe drink culture. Atlas describes it as tangy, lightly fizzy and probiotic.

entries.heading: Kyselica (sour cream soup)
entries.what: Wallachian soup with sour cream, bacon, potatoes, eggs and sausage.

entries.heading: La Chonta cheese (queso chonta)
entries.what: a cheese in an Ecuadorian food composition study of traditional foods, where it had the highest calcium content among the foods listed.

entries.heading: La Clua de Meià (Clua)
entries.what: Goat cheese made at La Clua, a hamlet in Artesa de Segre (Noguera), where young settlers revived an abandoned village in the 1970s and turned to artisanal goat cheese.

entries.heading: La Fournaise
entries.what: A hard-paste cheese named after the volcano; producer's range.

entries.heading: La Peral (Queso de La Peral)
entries.what: blue cheese from Asturias, somewhat like Roquefort, made in a small dairy in San Jorge de La Peral, municipality of Illas.

entries.heading: La Serena (made in Chiapas)
entries.what: A Spanish sheep cheese reproduced in Chiapas using Merino sheep's milk.

entries.heading: La Vache qui rit
entries.what: An industrial processed cheese brand (formerly "crème de gruyère") from Fromageries Bel, made from a blend of cheeses.

entries.heading: Laban / yoghurt (لبن)
entries.what: yoghurt is the base of Palestinian cooking: dried into jameed, strained into labneh, and used as a sauce for mansaf-type dishes.

entries.heading: Laban rayeb (لبن رايب; laban rayeb)
entries.what: A liquid, unpasteurised fermented milk. Smells like buttermilk, slightly acidic.

entries.heading: Laben Beldi (Moroccan fermented milk)
entries.what: A traditional Moroccan fermented milk drink listed by Luxlait.

entries.heading: Labneh Anbaris (لبنة قنبريس; labneh anbaris)
entries.what: A pungent, aged form of labneh made in sealed earthenware anbaris jars over several months; shaped into balls or preserved in oil.

entries.heading: Labneh Ambaris (لبنة قنبريس; labneh anbaris, labneh mka'zaleh)
entries.what: A traditional Lebanese fermented goat-milk product derived from labneh. Much more pungent and acidic than fresh labneh; made for winter storage.

entries.heading: Labneh balls (Labneh mka'zaleh / mda'baleh / mdahbaleh)
entries.what: Labneh is strictly a strained yogurt rather than a cheese, but Palestine's way of preserving it in balls is listed here as a local product.

entries.heading: Labneh makbouseh (لبنة مكبوسة; labneh mka'zaleh, mda'baleh, mdahbaleh; labneh balls in oil)
entries.what: Labneh strained longer, salted, shaped into small balls and kept in olive oil; the oil preserves it for months at room temperature.

entries.heading: Labneh, Turkish low fat (Awafi brand)
entries.what: A low-fat labneh sold under the Awafi brand in Qatar, labelled "Turkish Labneh Low Fat".

name: Lacthosa fluid milk, cream butter, cheese, yoghurt and ice cream

entries.heading: Lacthosa fluid milk, cream butter, cheese, yoghurt and ice cream (Lácteos de Honduras S.A.)
entries.what: the largest dairy producer in Honduras, founded 1992 by Schucry Kafie in San Pedro Sula. Its range is more than 250 products sold across Central America, including milk, malta, cream, cheeses, juices, ice cream, yoghurt and purified water.

entries.heading: Lacto (lacto; mukaka wakakora in Shona)
entries.what: Curdled or sour milk, named "lacto" and called mukaka wakakora (sour milk) in Shona, served with sadza.

entries.heading: Lactoperoxidase-treated raw milk (Mali)
entries.what: raw milk treated with a lactoperoxidase system to keep it from spoiling at ambient temperature on the way to collection centres.

entries.heading: Ladotyri (λαδοτύρι; Naxos)
entries.what: a Naxos cheese matured in olive oil for three months before eating.

entries.heading: Lahpet yay cho (Burmese milk tea; laphet yei cho / lahpet yei gyo; other names: Burmese milk tea, lahpet yeijo)
entries.what: black tea served sweet and milky, the signature drink of Myanmar tea shops; Indian immigrants introduced it, and tea houses spread during British rule.

entries.heading: Lait battu / bouri (churned buttermilk), with cassonade dessert and toetjespap
entries.what: Buttermilk from churned cream (lait battu). The Walloon word in Liège is bouri. Drunk raw in Belgium, sometimes flavoured with grenadine. Also cooked with cassonade (brown sugar) into a creamy sweet dessert popular in Belgium and northern F

name: Lait concentré sucré et non sucré

entries.heading: Lait concentré sucré et non sucré (condensed and evaporated milk)
entries.what: Milk concentrated by evaporation; sweetened version and unsweetened version both listed as French dairy categories.

entries.heading: Lait d'ânesse (donkey's milk, cosmetics)
entries.what: Donkey's milk used as the base of cosmetics, most often soap, sold mostly direct from farms.

entries.heading: Lait de brousse (bush milk)
entries.what: Raw milk from village or herder sources, sold through N'Djamena milk bars.

entries.heading: Lait de chamelle (dromedary camel milk, spontaneously fermented; Tunisian)
entries.what: Dromedary camel milk, drunk fresh and also processed into a fermented product in arid and semi-arid areas, southern Tunisia included.

entries.heading: Lait de chèvre (goat's milk)
entries.what: Milk of the domestic goat, used less than cow's milk in human food; in France mainly turned into goat cheese and yoghurt.

entries.heading: Lait de jument (mare's milk)
entries.what: Mare's milk sold in France as a premium fresh milk, cosmetics and freeze-dried sachets.

entries.heading: Lait en poudre (dried milk)
entries.what: Milk dried to powder, used as an ingredient and for reconstitution.

entries.heading: Lait fermenté (fermented milk, 1.5% fat)
entries.what: A fresh, lightly acidic fermented milk at 1.5% fat, sold by Luxlait.

name: Lait pasteurisé, stérilisé, UHT, standardisé, écrémé

entries.heading: Lait pasteurisé, stérilisé, UHT, standardisé, écrémé (drinking milk)
entries.what: The standard French retail milks: fresh pasteurised, UHT long-life, sterilised, standardised for fat, whole, half-skimmed and skimmed.

entries.heading: Lait reconstitué en poudre (reconstituted milk powder, Vitalait)
entries.what: Milk powder reconstituted in Togo and sold by Vitalait.

entries.heading: Lait ribot (lait baratté, Breton fermented milk)
entries.what: A Breton drink made from whole fresh milk that is fermented and then beaten to make it liquid, so the fat is kept. Traditionally drunk on Fridays.

entries.heading: Lait UHT Candia and Lovelac (CILAM)
entries.what: long-life milks sold under the brands Candia and Lovelac, listed among the products of the Compagnie laitière des Mascareignes (CILAM).

entries.heading: Lakto (lakto)
entries.what: Named as a Latvian fermented milk product in the table.

entries.heading: Laktosufrí mjólk (lactose-free milk)
entries.what: Milk for people who cannot tolerate lactose, sold by MBM; also a lactose-free cocoa at 0.8% fat.

entries.heading: Laktosufrítt soltið jogurt (lactose-free skimmed yoghurt)
entries.what: A skimmed yoghurt with the same creamy taste as ordinary yoghurt, lactose-free.

entries.heading: Laktosufríur rómi (lactose-free cream)
entries.what: Lactose-free cream sold in 250 ml and 1-litre packs, for home and business use; MBM began it because of demand.

entries.heading: Lalmohon (লালমোহন)
entries.what: a chhana-based sweet listed among Bangladeshi sweets.

entries.heading: Lampaanmaito (sheep milk)
entries.what: Thick, fatty sheep's milk, mostly made into yoghurt or cheese. World production in 2013 was about 10 million tonnes, 1.4% of all milk. Asia produces 48%, Europe 30%. Largest European producers: Greece, Spain, Italy and France.

entries.heading: Långfil and filmjölk (långfil, "long viili"; filmjölk)
entries.what: Långfil is a viili-type product found in western Finland and Sweden, which varies in consistency and fermentation. Filmjölk ("viili milk") is found in western Finland and Sweden and also in Norway (called kulturmelk or surmelk there), and i

entries.heading: Lappi (Lappi cheese)
entries.what: Very similar to Emmental, with smaller holes and a firmer texture; less flavourful because it is pasteurised; recipe developed in Lapland, Finland.

entries.heading: Lapte de pasăre (bird's milk; bulgări de zăpadă)
entries.what: A Romanian dessert: a fine vanilla custard with small spoonfuls of cooked egg-white foam floating on top; also called "bulgări de zăpadă" (snowballs).

entries.heading: Laskiaispulla cream filling (kermavaahto)
entries.what: The Shrovetide bun (laskiaispulla) is filled with whipped cream and either almond paste or jam. Bakeries began adding whipped cream only in the 1900s; almond paste is preferred on the Vaasa coast ("mantelin vyöhyke"). An older form was eate

entries.heading: Lassi-paneer (Punjabi cheese made from lassi)
entries.what: A cheese extracted from lassi after the lassi is prepared. It is eaten with water, salt and chili, or cooked with potatoes and spices into a curry resembling scrambled eggs.

entries.heading: Latchiiri (dakkere) — fermented-milk yoghurt with couscous
entries.what: A common meal of fermented-milk yoghurt eaten with corn couscous.

entries.heading: Latchiri
entries.what: A Fula dish of millet, corn or couscous, often served with yoghurt or milk.

entries.heading: Latte (hafuḥ)
entries.what: Espresso with milk, offered in Israeli cafés alongside instant, iced and espresso-style coffee.

entries.heading: Latte brûlé (latte brulè)
entries.what: Romagnol spoon dessert, served cold, with caramel and egg yolk.

entries.heading: Latte di pecora (sheep milk)
entries.what: sheep milk used for traditional Apulian cheeses (Canestrato pugliese, Pecorino Foggiano, Scamorza di pecora).

entries.heading: Latte fermentato probiotico (probiotic fermented milk)
entries.what: fermented milk with L. acidophilus, L. casei, L. lactis and Bifidobacterium bifidum; close to yoghurt, leads to kefir.

entries.heading: Latte fieno (haymilk; Italian name)
entries.what: milk from cows fed hay without silage, with the Italian name latte fieno.

entries.heading: Latte macchiato
entries.what: espresso poured into steamed milk, with the Italian name meaning stained milk.

entries.heading: Latteria di Cividale
entries.what: Dairy cheese named after Cividale del Friuli.

entries.heading: Latteria di Fontanafredda
entries.what: Dairy cheese named after Fontanafredda.

entries.heading: Latvian washed-rind cheese (unnamed; "Latvian cheese")
entries.what: a strong-smelling cheese listed by the English Wikipedia list of cheeses as Latvian. No name is given.

entries.heading: Lavaş peyniri
entries.what: A distinctive cheese from Karacadağ near Diyarbakır.

entries.heading: Layali Lubnan (ليالي لبنان; Beirut nights, qashtalia)
entries.what: A common Lebanese homemade dessert with a semolina milk pudding base and a qishta layer, topped with pistachios and qatir.

entries.heading: Lazine yoghurt and cream (Lazine; jogurt i pavlaka)
entries.what: yoghurt and cream from the Montenegrin producer Lazine, described as a "domaći proizvođač" (domestic producer) and bought by a shopper in Montenegro.

entries.heading: Lben / Leben (fermented milk drink; also rayeb)
entries.what: Sour fermented milk drunk daily across Algeria; also the base for klila.

entries.heading: Le Barbeillon
entries.what: named as a Loir-et-Cher cheese.

entries.heading: Le Bon du Jura
entries.what: A cheese listed under Jura, with no description on the list page.

entries.heading: Le Cap Noir
entries.what: A "character" cheese with a dark, black rind.

entries.heading: Le Curé Nantais (Curé nantais; Fromage du curé)
entries.what: Strong, smoky soft cheese with an orange rind, from Pornic. Made from raw cow's milk from six farms in the Pays de Retz.

entries.heading: Le Gouverneur
entries.what: A traditional light camembert-style cheese, the lightest in the producer's range.

entries.heading: Le Gré des Champs (Montérégie, Quebec)
entries.what: An organic raw-milk firm-paste cheese with a nutty flavour from the Montérégie region.

entries.heading: Le Gruyère Premier Cru (Gruyère Premier Cru)
entries.what: A premium Gruyère made and matured exclusively in the canton of Fribourg.

entries.heading: Le Maréchal
entries.what: Swiss hard cheese from Granges-près-Marnand, Vaud, made by the Rapin family, meant as an alternative to Gruyère.

entries.heading: Le Moulis
entries.what: A cheese range from the Couserans in Ariège, sold under a commercial brand within the Tomme des Pyrénées IGP.

entries.heading: Le Pavé du Plessis
entries.what: named in the French Normandy cuisine article as a Normandy cheese; a pavé-type cheese. No description opened.

entries.heading: Le Reussillon
entries.what: A semi-hard creamy cheese listed under Jura.

entries.heading: Le Rêve du Jura
entries.what: A semi-hard organic-milk cheese listed under Jura.

entries.heading: Le Riopelle de l'Isle (Isle-aux-Grues, Chaudière-Appalaches, Quebec)
entries.what: A triple-cream cheese named after painter Jean-Paul Riopelle; its label reproduces one of his paintings.

entries.heading: Le Tendrebon
entries.what: A soft cream cheese listed under Jura.

entries.heading: Le'Vital yoghurt (Emil)
entries.what: Low-calorie yoghurts made by the Emil dairy.

entries.heading: Lebanese Double-Cream (pressed-brined karishi; locally "double cream", not a cream)
entries.what: Karishi curds salted and pressed to expel residual whey, giving a firmer, denser cheese. Not a cream; no added fat.

entries.heading: Leben / laban (Levantine sour milk)
entries.what: A soured milk drink eaten cold with meals.

entries.heading: Leben / lben (Tunisian buttermilk)
entries.what: The aqueous fraction left after the fat is removed from rayeb. Tunisian lben is described as a dairy food largely consumed in Tunisia, valued for its probiotic bacteria.

entries.heading: Lebol (butter from pendidam making)
entries.what: The butter skimmed off the fermented milk during pendidam production in the Far North. Second pass: Edima et al. 2014 record a separate lebol (traditional butter) at a production site in Ngaoundéré (Bini Dang), in Adamawa.

entries.heading: Lećevački sir
entries.what: a cheese named for Lećevica (Dalmatia)

entries.heading: Leche con lúcuma (milk and lúcuma drink)
entries.what: Fresh milk blended with lúcuma fruit and ice.

entries.heading: Leche con plátano (milk and banana drink)
entries.what: Fresh milk blended with banana and ice.

entries.heading: Leche crema (milk dessert)
entries.what: A dessert of milk, named among Paraguayan desserts.

entries.heading: Leche de larga vida / UHT (aseptic long-life milk)
entries.what: Long-life milk sold in Tetra Brik cartons, which need no refrigeration until opened.

entries.heading: Leche dormida (milk drink made from cuajada)
entries.what: A milk drink made with cuajada, sugar, lemon and cinnamon.

entries.heading: Leche evaporada y condensada (evaporated and condensed milk)
entries.what: Canned milks used as core ingredients in many Puerto Rican desserts and drinks (coquito, tres leches, ponche de malta).

entries.heading: Leche flan
entries.what: The Philippine version of crème caramel, denser and sweeter than the Spanish original, made with condensed milk and only egg yolks. A staple at celebratory feasts; also used in flan cake, puto flan and halo-halo.

entries.heading: Leche fresca / raw cow milk (drinking milk)
entries.what: Cow milk drunk as a beverage and used in licuados; a 2018 survey tested raw cow milk sold in El Salvador for aflatoxin M1.

entries.heading: Leche fresca pasteurizada / entera (fresh pasteurised whole milk)
entries.what: Whole and skimmed milk sold cooled and pasteurised, from collection centres; the main form of fresh milk in Peru alongside evaporated and UHT.

entries.heading: Leche frita (leche frita; "fried milk"; Catalan "llet de Pasqua", Basque "pella")
entries.what: A set custard of milk and flour, cut into pieces, fried, and glazed with sugar and cinnamon.

entries.heading: Leche merengada (leche merengada; no other names found)
entries.what: A Spanish drink of milk and egg white, sweetened and spiced, served partly frozen.

entries.heading: Leche poleada (corn-starch milk and egg drink)
entries.what: A dessert-style drink of milk, eggs and corn starch, sometimes served as a warm drink.

entries.heading: Leche Primeros Pasos (milk-based drink for children aged 12 to 36 months)
entries.what: Vanilla-flavoured milk preparation sold by Conaprole for children aged 12 to 36 months.

entries.heading: Leche saborizada y chocolatada (Colet and other flavoured milks)
entries.what: Flavoured milks sold by Conaprole under the Colet name: Colet Clásico (chocolate, 250 ml and 1 L), Colet Dulce de Leche (whole, 250 ml and 1 L), Colet Choco Bombón, Colet Light (skimmed chocolate), Colet 0% lactosa and Colet Caffé Latte. Al

entries.heading: Lecheburra (leche burra)
entries.what: a dessert named in both Nicaraguan cuisine lists. No description in any opened source.

entries.heading: Leconet sec et frais
entries.what: A cheese of the Corrèze, Limousin.

entries.heading: Ledikeni (লেডিকেনি)
entries.what: a light, fried, reddish-brown ball of chhena and flour, soaked in sugar syrup; devised in the mid-19th century.

entries.heading: Leite (fresh and UHT cow milk)
entries.what: Cow milk; main producing states: Minas Gerais (about 41% of national production, 2012 data), Paraná (19%), Goiás (fastest growth in number of producers). São Paulo fell from 29% (2001) to 10% (2012). Rio Grande do Sul, Bahia and Ceará also

entries.heading: Leite de onça
entries.what: Drink from Cachoeira do Arari, Pará (Marajó region), linked to the Festividades do Glorioso São Sebastião and to Carnival. Cachaça and condensed milk, with cocoa powder or chocolate syrup and spices (cinnamon, cloves) in the common recipe.

entries.heading: Leite evaporado
entries.what: Milk with part of the water removed by evaporation, no added sugar (unlike condensed milk).

entries.heading: Leite reconstituído UHT (reconstituted UHT milk)
entries.what: the main local milk product, made in Angola from imported powder and sold as fluid UHT milk (leite fluido UHT), with demand rising in cities.

entries.heading: Leite-creme
entries.what: A Portuguese milk dessert, a custard made from milk, flour, sugar and egg yolks.

entries.heading: Lengcha (লেংচা)
entries.what: sweetmeat named in the 2025 Bogura survey; priced BDT 700/kg.

entries.heading: Lepasuitsujuust (alder-smoked cheese)
entries.what: a small smoked cheese wheel bought in Tartu; the smoke flavour is light and it is described as mild, as most Estonian cheeses are.

entries.heading: Les Hayons
entries.what: named in the French Normandy cuisine article as a Normandy cheese. No description opened.

entries.heading: Lèt (liquid milk; cow and goat)
entries.what: Plain liquid milk. The Haitian Creole article on "Lèt (likid)" says cow or goat milk is the kind used to feed grown-ups ("lèt vach oswa lèt kabrit se san sa itilize pou nouri gran moun").

entries.heading: Lévéjac
entries.what: A farm cheese range from the GAEC Le Lévéjac, Saint-Georges-de-Lévéjac, Lozère (Tomme de Lévéjac).

entries.heading: Leveles, centrifugális and krémtúró
entries.what: three Hungarian curd types named on the Hungarian list: leveles (drained), centrifugális (centrifuged), and krémtúró (cream curd).

entries.heading: Lfrik (fermented camel milk)
entries.what: Traditional fermented camel milk of Morocco, a pastoral product.

entries.heading: Liban (smoked Liban, "Liban Erbil"; Arabic and Kurdish script not given in source)
entries.what: The everyday yoghurt of Iraq, eaten with bread as a main breakfast dish. Smoked Liban from Erbil is the best-known variety and is prized for its flavour.

entries.heading: Libba (Libba', Laba)
entries.what: a Yemeni cheese whose name comes from the Arabic word for colostrum. Mostly eaten in countryside communities in Yemen and Somalia; not sold as a product and not served in restaurants.

entries.heading: Liburnski sir
entries.what: a cheese of the Liburnia region (Kvarner)

entries.heading: Licor de oro (milk-whey liqueur, Chiloé)
entries.what: A typical Chilote liqueur from Chiloé, made of aguardiente and whey, coloured yellow with saffron and lemon peel.

entries.heading: Liederkranz
entries.what: A semi-soft, pale-interiored cheese with a pale yellow-orange crust.

entries.heading: Lietuviškas varškės sūris (Lithuanian curd cheese; varškės sūris)
entries.what: A traditional Lithuanian fresh curd cheese, from naturally soured milk, pressed into a triangular prism with rounded corners. Registered as a PGI in 2013, the third Lithuanian protected product in the EU. It was printed on a 2005 Lithuanian

entries.heading: Lighvan (Liqvan; Persian پنیر لیقوان; Tabrizi and superior grades)
entries.what: A sour, salty curd cheese from Liqvan, a village on the northern slope of Mount Sahand near Tabriz, East Azerbaijan, north-west Iran. Eaten at breakfast or dinner with fresh bread.

entries.heading: Liliputas
entries.what: A Lithuanian semi-hard cheese made since 1958 at the Belvederis dairy (Belvederio sūrinė) near Seredžius, Jurbarkas district. Registered as an EU PGI in March 2015, the seventh Lithuanian food to get the status.

entries.heading: Limonada suíça (com leite condensado)
entries.what: A lemonade-based drink with condensed milk; listed in the milk drinks section of "Brazilian cuisine".

entries.heading: Liptauer triestino
entries.what: Spreadable cheese mixture named after Liptauer, made in the province of Trieste.

entries.heading: Liptovski sir (Liptauer-style spread)
entries.what: Spreadable skuta mix with sour cream, paprika, caraway and black pepper, ripened in a cool place.

entries.heading: Liqenasi (goat cheese, named origin, pasteurised milk)
entries.what: a named traditional goat-cheese origin sampled after manufacture for hygiene.

name: Liquid UHT milk and milk drinks

entries.heading: Liquid UHT milk and milk drinks (Mengniu, Yili)
entries.what: Mainstream industrial liquid milk, UHT milk and milk drinks sold in China by the two largest dairy companies. Mengniu's segment includes yoghurt and milk beverages; Yili sells sterilised and fresh milk under the Yili brand; organic milk und

entries.heading: Livno cheese (Livanjski sir; Livanjski sir; Traditional Livno Cheese)
entries.what: A dry, yellow hard cheese from the Livno area (Livanjsko polje) in western Bosnia, with Kupres, Glamoč and Tomislavgrad also named as places it is made. Made in the 19th century on family farms.

entries.heading: Llanboidy
entries.what: A named Welsh cheese, listed with Caerphilly, Y Fenni, Red Devil and Black Bomber as produced in Wales.

entries.heading: Llaollao frozen yoghurt (Llaollao)
entries.what: A frozen yoghurt sold through a Spanish chain, based in Denia (Alicante).

entries.heading: Llenguat
entries.what: A strong, spicy, pasty cheese from the Pallars, originally a way to use leftover or accidentally fermented curing cheeses, usually from serrat.

entries.heading: Local cow's and sheep's milk (fresh milk, modern)
entries.what: A Nuuk restaurant reports using organic cow's and sheep's milk from Greenland to make its first Greenlandic cheese.

entries.heading: Local Edam-type cheese (no local name given)
entries.what: A local Belarusian version of Edam, very popular for decades in the Russian Empire.

entries.heading: Local yoghurt (yaourt; made by a factory in Tahiti, name not given)
entries.what: Yoghurt made by a local yogurt factory in Tahiti, which takes most of the small quantity of fresh milk produced on the island.

entries.heading: Locally processed cheese (unnamed; Mbarara City, Uganda)
entries.what: a locally processed cheese sold in Mbarara City, south-western Uganda, alongside yogurt, homemade butter and eshabwe (a butter sauce). It is one of the "commonly consumed" fermented milk products of the region.

entries.heading: Lody mleczne (milk-based ice cream)
entries.what: Frozen dessert made from a dairy-based mass (lody mleczne), as opposed to water-based lody wodne. Plant drinks (soy, rice, oat) can also be used.

entries.heading: London fog
entries.what: a hot tea drink of Earl Grey tea, steamed milk and vanilla syrup or honey or maple syrup; some versions add cream on top with cinnamon, nutmeg or lavender.

entries.heading: Long-life full-fat milk (Al Khamayil; Arabic حليب طويل الأمد)
entries.what: Full-fat long-life milk launched in May 2025 by Oman Flour Mills Company SAOG under the Al Khamayil brand, aimed at households, cafes and food service. It stays fresh for months without refrigeration.

name: Long-life liquid cream: crème liquide UHT

entries.heading: Long-life liquid cream: crème liquide UHT
entries.what: UHT liquid cream, sold by Luxlait for cooking, with good heat stability.

entries.heading: Long-life UHT milk (Parmalat Botswana)
entries.what: Long-life UHT milk made by Parmalat Botswana.

entries.heading: Loppered milk (soured milk for churning)
entries.what: Milk left to sour and thicken (loppered) before it is churned. Its acidity is credited with helping the butter form and giving quality.

entries.heading: Lori (Լոռի)
entries.what: A light yellow, firm cheese with small holes, said to melt well and to have a cheddar-like texture. Named after the Lori region.

entries.heading: Lorik (لۆریک)
entries.what: A cheese made by reheating the whey left over from cheese production; eaten fresh in spring and summer. A preserved form was mixed with wild mountain herbs and stored for winter.

entries.heading: Los Tambores
entries.what: a raw sheep cheese from Samper de Calanda (Teruel), with a natural rind and a strong flavour.

entries.heading: Lõss (skimmed milk)
entries.what: milk with almost all its fat removed as cream; under the EU definition, pasteurised, sterilised or UHT milk with fat at most 0.5%

entries.heading: Lossaba
entries.what: A cheese of the Pays basque.

entries.heading: Loupák (loupák, sweet roll)
entries.what: A crescent-shaped roll of sweetened dough containing milk.

entries.heading: Lučina
entries.what: spreadable cream cheese made since 1981, now in many named variants.

entries.heading: Lusignan
entries.what: A cheese of Poitou and Charentes, named after Lusignan (Vienne).

entries.heading: Luzerner Rahmkäse
entries.what: cheese from Canton Lucerne made from pasteurised milk with cream.

entries.heading: Maarqaa (Oromo wheat and milk porridge)
entries.what: porridge-like dish from wheat, milk, chili and spices.

entries.heading: Maasdam (Maasdammer)
entries.what: A Dutch Emmental-style cheese with larger holes and a sweet, nutty taste. Made to compete with Swiss Emmentaler by being cheaper and quicker.

entries.heading: Maasora (local name; Arabic-script spelling not sourced; other names: none found)
entries.what: a locally made soft cheese sold in retail dairy markets in Tripoli, Sabha, Tobruk and Regdalin, and sampled in two Libyan studies.

entries.heading: Maast / mast / labanyat (Persian ماست)
entries.what: the basic fermented milk; the starter curd for doogh and many sauces.

entries.heading: Mabisi (mabisi; Zambian and regional names: "sour milk")
entries.what: a spontaneously fermented raw cow milk eaten as a drink or with maize porridge, thick or thin, sour.

entries.heading: Mabisi (Zambian fermented milk; "sour milk")
entries.what: traditional spontaneously fermented raw milk, the main Zambian traditional dairy product. Drunk on its own as a drink or as a thick yoghurt-like mix, or eaten with rice, sweet potato, pumpkin or leftover nsima. Often used in place of relish

entries.heading: Mabisi whey and instant mabisi
entries.what: the whey drained from mabisi. Used in cooking porridge, given to children as a drink, and fed to dogs and pigs. Also used to make "instant mabisi".

entries.heading: Mabisi with nsima or porridge
entries.what: mabisi mixed with leftover nsima (maize meal porridge; sometimes millet, sorghum or cassava) and eaten as a main meal when no relish is available. Also eaten with rice, sweet potatoes and pumpkin.

entries.heading: Macanese egg tart (Macau-style pastel de nata; 葡撻)
entries.what: a Portuguese-derived custard tart with a caramelised, browned top, distinct from the Hong Kong style. Served fresh from the oven with cinnamon and icing sugar.

entries.heading: Maccagno (Toma Maccagno, Macagn; PDO)
entries.what: PDO cheese from the Biellese and Valsesia areas of Piemonte.

entries.heading: Macedonian white brined goat's-milk cheese (local name not given in the sources read)
entries.what: A traditional artisanal brined white cheese made from goat's milk in North Macedonia; the 2026 study looked at seasonal variation (spring vs. autumn) in microbiota, chemistry and texture across 60 days of ripening.

entries.heading: Machecoulais
entries.what: Named in the list of French cheeses with origin Loire-Atlantique, Pays de la Loire (Machecoul is in the Pays de Retz).

entries.heading: Madártej (floating island; Hungarian name)
entries.what: Egg-white meringue floating on a vanilla custard sauce.

entries.heading: Madhuparka (मधुपर्क)
entries.what: Ancient offering of honey mixed with curd or ghee, given to honoured guests in Vedic practice.

entries.heading: Madidé djir (byan, madidé)
entries.what: A millet porridge made with milk and sugar; general term for this bouillie is madidé.

entries.heading: Madidé foule (byan woudou)
entries.what: A bouillie of peanut paste, white millet, lait caillé and wheat flour.

entries.heading: Madlouka (مدلوقة)
entries.what: A semolina-and-milk sweet with starch and sugar, topped with fried almonds and cashews.

entries.heading: Madraji golla (মাদরাজি গোল্লা)
entries.what: sweetmeat named in the 2025 Dhaka survey, the most expensive product found there at BDT 680/kg.

entries.heading: Maduro ahumado (Valle Central)
entries.what: A smoked, ripened cheese from the Valle Central, cured for several weeks with a bacterial culture and smoked over coffee wood, giving an intense flavour.

entries.heading: Mafrooda processed cheese (Obour Land; Arabic name not in opened sources)
entries.what: Obour Land's Mafrooda processed cheese in 50 g packs, in creamy and roumy (Rumi) flavours; a cheddar flavour is named on the same listing.

entries.heading: Mafrouka kashta (مفروكة قشطة)
entries.what: A semolina dessert made with qishta cream and ground pistachio, one of the Lebanese sweets in the national food-composition table.

entries.heading: Magija (chocolate-coated varškės sūreliai; Žemaitijos pienas)
entries.what: a line of curd cheese snacks (varškės sūreliai) from the Lithuanian dairy Žemaitijos pienas, mostly with a chocolate or glaze coating; flavours include vanilla, caramel, poppy seed, condensed milk and milk-chocolate fillings.

entries.heading: Mahalepi (μαχαλλεπί; Cypriot milk pudding)
entries.what: A blancmange-style set dessert flavoured with rose, usually served cold and cut into pieces.

entries.heading: Mahali cheese (Mahali; Persian پنیر محلی)
entries.what: A local mild cheese from Mazandaran province, north Iran, kept in salt brine.

entries.heading: Mainland (cheese and butter)
entries.what: A Fonterra brand for cheese and butter in NZ, including brie-style Creamy, Double Cream and Blue varieties.

entries.heading: Mainzer Käse (Mainzer Handkäs)
entries.what: A sour-milk cheese invented in 1813 by a farmer named Kaul in Groß-Gerau (Hesse) and sold at the Mainz weekly market. In Mainz it is usually called "Handkäs" and often served marinated ("Handkäs mit Musik").

entries.heading: Maiorchino (maiorchino di Novara di Sicilia)
entries.what: a Sicilian sheep's-milk cheese from the northern slopes of the Peloritani mountains, province of Messina; wheels of 10–12 kg, about 12 cm high and 35 cm across. The version of Novara di Sicilia has its own separate PAT recognition.

entries.heading: Maish krej (Kashmir)
entries.what: "A traditionally ripened Himalayan cheese" from Kashmiri cuisine, also called "milk chapati" in the text.

entries.heading: Maishanu (mai shanu; butter and cooking butter oil)
entries.what: Fresh or soured-milk butter sold in Hausa villages and used as a cooking fat; butter oil is a major fat in the diet of semi-nomadic Fulani.

entries.heading: Maitokiisseli (milk kissel)
entries.what: A creamy pudding made from milk and starch, flavoured with sugar and vanilla or cocoa. Finnish name maitokiisseli; uses corn starch. Fruit kissel (kiisseli) itself has no milk but is served with sweetened quark, cream or ice cream.

entries.heading: Maizes zupa (rye bread soup)
entries.what: Rye bread soup with whipped cream, dried fruit and cranberries.

entries.heading: Majdoula (Baladna brand)
entries.what: A cheese named "Majdoula Cheese" in the Baladna-brand cheese range in Qatar. The name is a local (Arab) name.

entries.heading: Majdoule (madjoul; also Armenian string cheese)
entries.what: A string cheese described as culturally Syrian and mainly made in Northern Syria, though it originates from Armenia.

entries.heading: Makamo
entries.what: A fermented milk made by pastoral groups in Uganda, used as the raw material for the butter-like product Mashita.

entries.heading: Make-at-home yoghurt (EasiYo)
entries.what: A powder that is mixed with water and fermented at home to make yoghurt.

entries.heading: Makkhan / white butter (मक्खन)
entries.what: Locally called makkhan; India's white butter, not yellow because buffaloes convert carotene to vitamin A.

entries.heading: Mákos guba (poppy-seed bread in milk)
entries.what: Kifli or bread slices layered with poppy-seed sauce made from milk, butter, sugar and nuts.

entries.heading: Malabi (מלבי; muhallabia / muhalabiyya in Arabic; other names)
entries.what: A creamy starch-set milk pudding, from the same family as muhallebi. In Israel it is sold from street carts and served with a thick sweet syrup and toppings such as pistachio or coconut.

entries.heading: Malai (fresh cream / clotted cream)
entries.what: Fresh cream used for richness in desserts and tea.

entries.heading: Malai / cream (মালাই; sar)
entries.what: the fat-rich part of milk, 18–80% milk fat (Banglapedia); used to make butter, ghee and ice cream; used in Mughal desserts and in the cream sauce of rasomalai.

entries.heading: Malai / milk skin (मलाई; sar, kene, aadai, paada, saay, chhali, sor)
entries.what: Film that forms on heated milk, rich in fat and protein; spread on bread as a butter substitute and used in sweets and cream dishes.

entries.heading: Malaikari (মালাইকারি)
entries.what: a chhana-based sweet attributed to Comilla in Banglapedia.

entries.heading: Malaka (Μαλάκα)
entries.what: the curd mass that forms in the first stage of Cretan graviera production; not sold as a finished cheese.

entries.heading: Malaxia (μαλαξιά; Andros)
entries.what: named as an Andros cheese; no details found.

entries.heading: Malaxia Androu (Μαλαξιά Άνδρου)
entries.what: Andros cheese; no details.

entries.heading: Malga o Ugovizza
entries.what: Mountain-hut cheese named after Ugovizza (Tarvisio area).

entries.heading: Malteada (malted milkshake)
entries.what: A malted milkshake-style drink made without ice cream.

entries.heading: Malted milk (麦芽乳, bakugaunyū)
entries.what: A powder of barley malt, wheat flour and powdered milk, sold as a drink (unsaccharified type) or as a bread-making enzyme ingredient (saccharified type). Listed among Japanese milk beverages.

entries.heading: Malted milk and malted shake
entries.what: A powder of malted barley, wheat flour and evaporated whole milk powder, used in drinks and baking; the malted milkshake followed.

entries.heading: Malted peanut milk drink (with non-fat milk powder)
entries.what: A peanut-based beverage developed through a Malawian consumer-driven approach. It is made with peanut paste, malted barley or sorghum, and non-fat dry milk powder, plus sugar, salt, xanthan gum and water.

entries.heading: Mamak ravak (Mamak Ravak yoghurt)
entries.what: a full-fat cow-cream yoghurt from Mamak, Ankara.

entries.heading: Mamirolle
entries.what: A semi-hard washed-rind cheese developed in 1935 by the dairy school at Mamirolle, Doubs.

entries.heading: Manaba fresh white cheese (queso manaba)
entries.what: an Ecuadorian artisanal fresh white cheese, which the source says does not fully meet regulations, with Salmonella risk noted.

entries.heading: Manda (মণ্ডা)
entries.what: chhana-based sweet named in Banglapedia's list.

entries.heading: Mandas Spadula
entries.what: One of 16 lesser-known Sardinian cheeses, made by Caseificio Pinna.

entries.heading: Mango float (crema de mangga)
entries.what: A Filipino no-bake icebox cake of stacked graham crackers, sweetened condensed milk, whipped cream and ripe carabao mangoes. A milkshake version uses milk. Regional versions use ube or durian.

entries.heading: Manicamp
entries.what: A small Maroilles-style cheese named after the commune of Manicamp; cited in accounts going back to the French Revolution; it disappeared in the 1950s and was rediscovered in 1999. Produced now by the Ferme de la Pâturelle at Quierzy (Aisne

entries.heading: Mannapuuro (semolina porridge)
entries.what: A Nordic porridge of semolina (mannasuurimo), salt and milk or water (juice is also named). Runny versions are called mannavellinen.

entries.heading: Manouli (μανούλι; Karpathos)
entries.what: a fresh cheese from Karpathos.

entries.heading: Manouli Karpathou
entries.what: a fresh, velvety cheese from Karpathos.

entries.heading: Manoura (μανούρα; Naxos, Sifnos, Andros)
entries.what: on Naxos, the drained curd before it becomes arseniko; the Sifnos "manoura" is named in a Wikipedia list without detail.

entries.heading: Manoura Sifnou (Μανούρα Σίφνου, γυλωμένη)
entries.what: Sifnos cheese; no details.

entries.heading: Manshanu (cream used as culture)
entries.what: A cream stored in a wooden calabash, used to start the next batch of nono (back-slopping). Named in the paper as "Manshanu".

entries.heading: Manteiga da terra (manteiga de garrafa; manteiga de gado, manteiga do sertão, manteiga nordestina)
entries.what: A butter that stays liquid at room temperature, sold in glass bottles. A typical product of the Brazilian Northeast, largely artisanal and sold informally (fairs, small shops, rural properties). Used in regional dishes such as carne de sol.

entries.heading: Mantequilla de campo (artisanal country butter)
entries.what: Artisanal country-style butter, sold as "mantequilla artesanal de campo" (Futaleufú brand, Los Lagos region); made from cow's cream and salt.

entries.heading: Manufactured yoghurt (Adamawa market)
entries.what: Yoghurt sold on the Adamawa (Ngaoundéré) market as a manufactured product, one of two yoghurt types named by Edima et al. 2014 alongside the semi-manufactured kossam yoghurt.

entries.heading: Mao (Sindhi milk sweet)
entries.what: A sweet dish made from milk and sugar, listed in the Sindhi cuisine article.

entries.heading: Maquée
entries.what: A fresh Walloon cheese, eaten salted or sweet; listed on French Wikipedia as a "fromage blanc".

entries.heading: Mar del Plata (Holanda; Cáscara Colorada)
entries.what: a semi-fatty cheese from the coastal city of Mar del Plata, also called Holanda or Cáscara Colorada.

entries.heading: Marasee (milk and butter dessert)
entries.what: A dessert from the traditional dish paper with whole wheat flour, sugar, powdered milk, oil, honey and butter.

entries.heading: Mare's milk, Chilean Corralero horse (leche de yegua)
entries.what: Milk from Chilean Corralero mares on three breeding farms in southern Chile. A 2024 study sampled 45 milks and analysed composition, fatty acids and IgG. The authors say it is richer in lactose and lower in fat and protein than cow and huma

entries.heading: Maredsous
entries.what: A loaf-shaped semi-hard cheese named after the Maredsous Abbey (Anhée, Namur province), with a firm orange rind and pungent aroma; sliceable, 45% fat per the English page.

entries.heading: Maribo (Maribo cheese)
entries.what: a Danish semi-hard cheese named after the town of Maribo on Lolland; compared to Dutch Gouda.

entries.heading: Maromme
entries.what: named in the French Normandy cuisine article as a Normandy cheese, from the Maromme area (Seine-Maritime). No description opened; the dedicated French page was not found.

entries.heading: Marqueta
entries.what: A white cheese of Veracruz, often coated in chili paste.

entries.heading: Marshmallow ice cream (restaurant dessert)
entries.what: Marshmallow ice cream served with a chocolate mousse cake at a Bermuda restaurant (Fresco's).

entries.heading: Maršov cheese (Maršovský sýr)
entries.what: named Czech cheese from Nové Město na Moravě, produced for decades.

entries.heading: Marzolino / Marzolina (PAT)
entries.what: A sheep cheese made in spring (marzo).

entries.heading: Marzolino di Lucardo (Pecorino di Lucardo)
entries.what: sheep marzolino from Lucardo.

entries.heading: Masala chai / milk tea (मसाला चाय)
entries.what: Black tea brewed in milk and water with sugar and spices; most tea in India is sweetened milk tea.

entries.heading: Masala tea (chai; Hindi/Fiji Hindi "chai")
entries.what: spiced black tea brewed with milk, drunk daily in many households.

entries.heading: Mashanza (mashanza; local name in Congolese languages not given by source)
entries.what: named in a review as one of the indigenous African cheeses, "of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (formerly Zaire)". The review gives no further description.

entries.heading: Mashita
entries.what: A milk-fat product produced by the Bahima in Uganda, churned from makamo.

entries.heading: Masse (masse; Mozambique fermented milk)
entries.what: a traditional fermented milk named as a Mozambican example alongside zabady (Egypt), rob, biruni, garris (Sudan), madila (Botswana) and omashikwa (Namibia) in a review of indigenous African fermented milks.

entries.heading: Massini (masini, flamet)
entries.what: Dessert of pionono (rolled sponge) layers filled with whipped cream, topped with burnt egg yolk. Popular in Uruguay; also known as flamet in Catalonia.

entries.heading: Mast (ماست) — yogurt, incl. cow, buffalo, sheep and goat traditional yogurts
entries.what: The Persian word for yogurt; the base of doogh, ash-e doogh, and mast-o khiar. Traditional yogurts differ by region in milk, back-slopping or spontaneous fermentation, whey removal and grains.

entries.heading: Mast chekide (ماست چکیده; spelled mâst chekide in source)
entries.what: A kefir-like sour yogurt from northern Iran with a sharp taste, usually mixed with delal (a pesto-like herb purée).

entries.heading: Mast-o khiar (ماست و خیار; yogurt and cucumber dip)
entries.what: Yogurt blended with cucumber, garlic and mint, served as an appetiser.

entries.heading: Mastelo (Μαστέλο Χίου)
entries.what: Cheese from Chios.

entries.heading: Mate cocido con leche
entries.what: yerba mate boiled and served like tea with milk and sugar to taste.

entries.heading: Mate con leche (mate de leche)
entries.what: Yerba mate infusion prepared with milk, listed among drinks in Uruguayan gastronomy.

entries.heading: Mate dulce (sweet milk mate)
entries.what: A hot mate made with milk, sugar and dried orange peel, served in a gourd.

entries.heading: Matenitsa (мътеница) — buttermilk drink
entries.what: a Bulgarian buttermilk-type drink; the Bulgarian disambiguation page calls it a drink made from yoghurt, similar to ayran; also used as the liquid for popara

entries.heading: Matété (cream dessert)
entries.what: A dessert named "Matété (crème)" in French Guianese cuisine.

entries.heading: Matha / mattha (মাঠা)
entries.what: buttermilk drink, named alongside ghol; Solop village in Sirajganj District.

entries.heading: Matho (chilled buttermilk, Sindhi)
entries.what: Chilled buttermilk served in Sindh, as an accompaniment to mitho lolo.

entries.heading: Matsvnis supi (მაწვნის სუპი; matsoni soup)
entries.what: a soup made mainly of matsoni.

entries.heading: Mattas farm cheese (Mattas gårdsmejeri ost; Mattas Gårdsmejeri, Sund)
entries.what: A cheese made by the small Mattas farm dairy in Sund, northern Åland, alongside its ice cream and yoghurt. The dairy names its products after its first cows.

entries.heading: Mattentaart (curd tart, Geraardsbergen)
entries.what: A pastry from the Geraardsbergen area whose filling is "matten" (curdled milk); EU protected designation of origin since 2007.

entries.heading: Maytag Blue
entries.what: A blue cheese with green veins, hand-shaped and cave-aged.

entries.heading: Mazarin
entries.what: A light camembert-style cheese, sold alone and in a pair with Notre Dame de la Paix.

entries.heading: Maziwa mgando / Maziwa mtindi (soured milk and yoghurt)
entries.what: soured milk and yoghurt, listed for Tanzania.

entries.heading: Mbaipy (cornmeal dish with milk and cheese)
entries.what: A cornmeal dish cooked with milk. Variants include mbaipy cuajada (with curd) and mbaipy choclo.

entries.heading: Mbaipy dulce (mbaipy-he-é, sweet milk dessert)
entries.what: A sweet cornmeal dessert made with milk.

entries.heading: Mbouraké coating (dish component)
entries.what: a coating for pain perdu made of breadcrumbs, peanut butter and milk.

entries.heading: Mechouna (Chnina)
entries.what: A soft fresh cheese, eaten fresh or dried, served in small portions; the spiced version is called Chnina.

entries.heading: Medaffarah (مدعفرة, Syrian name as spelled in the source)
entries.what: A Syrian traditional cheese, one of four studied in a 2013 Syrian university chemical analysis alongside Akawi, Shankalish and Sorkeh.

entries.heading: Meekiri (මී කිරි, mee kiri; buffalo curd)
entries.what: A traditional fermented buffalo-milk gel from Sri Lanka, sold along highways in shallow earthen pots and eaten for breakfast or dessert; most often served with kithul treacle. Served at weddings, alms-giving and at home, especially in the s

entries.heading: Meeny Hill Blue (Meeny Hill)
entries.what: A blue cheese from Dart Mountain Cheese, Park, County Londonderry.

entries.heading: Meeny Hill Goat
entries.what: A cheese from Dart Mountain Cheese, County Londonderry.

entries.heading: Meia de leite
entries.what: A similar drink to the galão with coffee and milk mixed 1:1, served in a large cup.

entries.heading: Meikaas
entries.what: A fresh white Dutch cheese, typically a few days to a week old, the first cheese of the year when cows go to pasture.

entries.heading: Melcochas de natilla (natilla taffy)
entries.what: Sticky taffy-like candy made from natilla and sugar. Traditional in San Ramón.

entries.heading: Melkkos
entries.what: A traditional Afrikaans farm food, like a melktert without the crust; served warm on cold evenings or as a light morning meal or supper.

entries.heading: Melktert (milk tart)
entries.what: South African dessert with a sweet pastry base and milk custard filling.

entries.heading: Melkunie (Melkunie Holland; Campina Melkunie)
entries.what: A Dutch dairy brand with origins in 1872. Its consumer milk and desserts (MONA) were among the largest in the Netherlands in the 1980s. Merged into Campina in 1990; the Melkunie name was dropped in 2001, sold to Arla Foods in 2009 with the

entries.heading: Mélusine
entries.what: A cheese of Poitou and Charentes.

entries.heading: Meriari (μεριάρι; Karpathos)
entries.what: a piquant Karpathos cheese.

entries.heading: Meriari Karpathou
entries.what: a complex, piquant cheese from Karpathos.

entries.heading: Merlyn Cream Liqueur
entries.what: dairy-based cream liqueur.

entries.heading: Mesost (cow whey cheese; messmör)
entries.what: Swedish whey product made by boiling down whey from cheesemaking until it caramelises. Sold as messmör (spread) or mesost (firmer).

entries.heading: Messmör (whey spread)
entries.what: A soft, sweet, brown spread sold in tubes across the Nordic countries; a whey-based product closely related to Norwegian prim and distinct from brunost.

entries.heading: Metata Ayib (spiced Ethiopian cottage cheese; "Meteta Ayib")
entries.what: A spiced variant of ayib, made in the northwest of Ethiopia and a well-liked beverage there. It has a longer shelf life than ordinary ayib, according to one source.

entries.heading: Mhalbi (rice milk dessert)
entries.what: A traditional rice cream made with milk, from Constantine.

entries.heading: Mhalbiya (mhalbia; milk dessert)
entries.what: A milk dessert, described in the article as a kind of rice pudding with sugar and rose water.

entries.heading: Mihaliç peyniri (kelle peyniri)
entries.what: A hard sheep's cheese that can be grated, from Karacabey, Bursa. Named after the Byzantine and Ottoman town of Mihaliç.

entries.heading: Mil Lel Parmesan (Saputo brand)
entries.what: Parmesan cheese sold under the Mil Lel brand of Saputo Dairy Australia.

entries.heading: Milawa Goat Camembert (Milawa Cheese Co, Victoria)
entries.what: A goat camembert from Milawa Cheese Co, a family business founded in the 1980s by David and Anne Brown and made at the historic Milawa Butter Factory.

entries.heading: Milchmischgetränk (milk mixed drinks, fruit milk, cocoa drink)
entries.what: a dairy-based drink with at least 70 % dairy ingredients and at most 30 % other foods

entries.heading: Milchpulver (milk powder: whole, skim and whey)
entries.what: whole milk powder has about 26% fat, 25% protein and 38% lactose; skim milk powder about 36% protein, 52% lactose and about 4% residual water; whey powder (sweet or sour, from cheese making) about 11% protein and 70% lactose.

entries.heading: Milchrahmstrudel (Millirahmstrudel, milk-cream strudel)
entries.what: a classic Viennese pastry from the Austro-Hungarian period, with a custard-like topping (Überguss)

name: Milk and cream, concentrated or sweetened

entries.heading: Milk and cream, concentrated or sweetened (imported)
entries.what: Milk and cream that is concentrated or sweetened, imported into Bermuda, valued at US$1.54 million from the United States in 2025.

name: Milk and cream, not concentrated or sweetened

entries.heading: Milk and cream, not concentrated or sweetened (imported)
entries.what: Milk and cream, not concentrated or sweetened, imported into Bermuda, valued at US$1.96 million from the United States in 2025.

entries.heading: Milk and dairy-based drinks (packaged, supermarket)
entries.what: A category of packaged milk and dairy-based drinks sold in two major supermarket chains in Dakar (2021 survey).

name: Milk and millet meal with yoghurt and sweet tea

entries.heading: Milk and millet meal with yoghurt and sweet tea (Wodaabe diet)
entries.what: Wodaabe staple of milk, ground millet, yoghurt and sweet tea.

entries.heading: Milk as brick (UHT) or powdered milk (consumed; industrial)
entries.what: The questionnaire asks about "all types of milk (brick, powder, milk consumed with cereals, etc.)", so both shelf-stable brick milk and powdered milk are in use.

entries.heading: Milk at breakfast (fresh, tinned or powdered; not specified)
entries.what: milk drunk at home breakfasts with bread, cereal, tea and coffee.

entries.heading: Milk beverages (乳飲料, nyū inryō)
entries.what: Dairy drinks with at least 3% milk solids, including fortified, coffee, fruit and lactose-reduced types. Named products like coffee milk and fruit milk fall under this heading.

entries.heading: Milk coffee and chocolate milk (mleko sa kafom; čokoladno mleko)
entries.what: milk served with breakfast alongside tea or coffee; milk coffee and chocolate milk are listed as breakfast drink options in Serbian cuisine.

entries.heading: Milk drinks (flavoured and other milk drinks)
entries.what: Milk-based drinks sold by the island dairy. The product list names "milk drinks" without detail.

entries.heading: Milk eaten with lahoh (historical)
entries.what: milk drunk or eaten with lahoh, recorded as a historical custom.

entries.heading: Milk from dual-purpose crossbred cattle (raw milk to collection centres)
entries.what: milk from dual-purpose cattle farms that is delivered to milk collection centres. A 2012 study measured milk yield over two years on 34 farms.

entries.heading: Milk from imported powder (reconstituted milk, melkpoeder)
entries.what: Milk made from imported milk powder. Two of the four commercial milk processors work only with imported powder; Melkcentrale Paramaribo uses it alongside local milk.

entries.heading: Milk gravy (cream gravy)
entries.what: A milk-based gravy served with buttered biscuits at 19th-century farmhouse meals.

entries.heading: Milk heat treatment (UHT / sterilised milk)
entries.what: Milk heat-treated for shelf life; the Croatian article describes UHT as the common method.

entries.heading: Milk hoppers
entries.what: A named spicy hopper variant.

entries.heading: Milk kanten (牛乳寒天, gyūnyū kanten)
entries.what: A set agar jelly made with milk, eaten chilled and cut into cubes; common school-lunch and home dessert.

entries.heading: Milk powder and brands (imported and repacked; Milk Vita)
entries.what: most powder milk is imported and repacked by local businesses under brand names: Red Cow, Anchor, Budget, Danish, Dano, Diploma, Energy, Fresh, Milk Vita, Nido, Star Ship, Quality (Shahnaz et al. 2004). Dano was the market leader (about 15%

entries.heading: Milk powder and fermented milk (Mezam division, Bamenda)
entries.what: Milk powder and fermented milk sold in Mezam division (the Bamenda area), sampled with raw milk in a Bacillus cereus study. Bacillus cereus was found in 8.22% of raw-milk samples and 13.33% of milk-powder samples, and not in the fermented m

entries.heading: Milk powder and tinned milk (leite em pó / leite enlatado; Tetum "susu" not confirmed)
entries.what: Packaged milk bought in shops, mainly as powder or tinned, and recorded in household diet surveys as the only milk most households consume.

entries.heading: Milk powder in sachets (Cowbell, Loya, Miksi, Peak)
entries.what: Powdered milk sold in small sachets, the everyday milk for many Nigerians since the 1990s; Cowbell (Promasidor, introduced sachets in 1993) and Loya and Miksi; Peak powdered sachets also.

entries.heading: Milk protein concentrate
entries.what: Milk protein powder used as an ingredient.

entries.heading: Milk served with paratha roti (Surinamese roti, "paratha roti")
entries.what: Plain milk drunk alongside the Surinamese paratha roti, according to the Dutch article on roti. It is a serving habit, not a manufactured product.

entries.heading: Milk Shake (vanilla milkshake mix)
entries.what: A vanilla-flavoured mix to make a home milkshake, with frozen fruit or chocolate suggested; per 100 g: 3.5 g fat, 4.1 g protein.

entries.heading: Milk skin (奶衣)
entries.what: A brown skin that forms on the surface of richly milked tea, linked with a milk tea of good body.

entries.heading: Milk tablets / solid milk (奶片)
entries.what: Solid milk product sold in China, Hong Kong and Macau; produced by a Mengniu–Arla joint venture formed in 2006.

entries.heading: Milk toast
entries.what: Toasted bread in warm milk with sugar and butter; in New England a milk-based white sauce over toast.

entries.heading: Milk with blood (Maasai traditional diet, historical)
entries.what: milk was the staple of the Maasai diet; in the dry season, fresh blood was mixed into the milk.

entries.heading: Milk with maize porridge (Turkana)
entries.what: the Turkana morning meal, maize porridge eaten with milk; lunch and dinner use plain porridge with stew.

name: Milk with millet, yoghurt and sweet tea

entries.heading: Milk with millet, yoghurt and sweet tea (Wodaabe diet)
entries.what: the Wodaabe diet, with milk, ground millet, yoghurt and sweet tea.

entries.heading: Milk with rice (Sutlyash, сутлиаш)
entries.what: a rice milk pudding listed among Bulgarian sweets

entries.heading: Milk with tea or coffee
entries.what: tea or coffee drunk with milk at breakfast.

entries.heading: Milk-based cold soups (okroshka on kefir or sour milk, svyokolnik)
entries.what: Okroshka, the Russian cold soup, often now on kefir or natural sour milk; svyokolnik, a cold beet soup made with yoghurt, buttermilk or soured milk.

entries.heading: Milk-based frozen and bar-style items (奶砖)
entries.what: Named in a photo caption on the Chinese ice cream page as "奶砖", an ice-cream brick in a plastic box.

entries.heading: Milk, blood and butter mixture (historic practice)
entries.what: Cattle were bled and the blood mixed with milk and butter, which was not uncommon in Gaelic Ireland.

entries.heading: Milk, commercial packaged (whole, 2%, low-fat; "milk" food type in the CHL intake data)
entries.what: whole, 2% and low-fat milk, the milk classes recorded in dietary recalls of young children

name: Milk, cow's milk as recorded in children's diets

entries.heading: Milk, cow's milk as recorded in children's diets (whole, 2%, low-fat, flavoured)
entries.what: Milk in the diet records of children aged 2–8 in the Children's Healthy Living study, whose sample includes American Samoa; milk was among the largest contributors of calcium and riboflavin in the sample.

entries.heading: Milk, diluted (englas) and milk drunk fresh
entries.what: Milk drunk fresh with meals, added to tea today; a diluted form, englas, was milk mixed with water.

entries.heading: Milk, fresh or heat-treated (gála)
entries.what: hot milk served at the traditional Greek breakfast with coffee and tea.

entries.heading: Milk, pasteurised (bottled, supermarket)
entries.what: Ordinary pasteurised cow's milk sold in Bermuda's shops; the only dairy product the sources name for a local dairy.

entries.heading: Milk: fresh, UHT, lactose-free, organic (Mëllech; Lait frais, Lait UHT, Lait 0% lactose, Lait bio)
entries.what: Luxlait sells fresh milk (longer shelf life), UHT long-life milk, 0% lactose milk, and organic milk, with a "Lait 0 KM" line.

entries.heading: Milkana (brand; Sierra Leone retail dairy brand)
entries.what: named as the most-scanned dairy brand in Sierra Leone in a retail shopper-panel study

entries.heading: Milkos cream (Milkos, Bijelo Polje; pavlaka)
entries.what: cream from Milkos, a dairy in Bijelo Polje (northern Montenegro), sold in Montenegrin shops.

name: Milkshakes and dairy beverages in milk bars

entries.heading: Milkshakes and dairy beverages in milk bars
entries.what: Milkshakes and dairy drinks served in NZ milk bars, which the source says have largely been replaced by dairies and cafés.

entries.heading: Milkshakes made from péi milk
entries.what: milkshakes made with Réunion milk, sold at the Miel Vert fair.

entries.heading: Milky
entries.what: An Israeli dairy pudding sold in chocolate, vanilla and mocha flavours, topped with whipped cream. It is a product name, so it is listed as an example of a kind.

entries.heading: Milleens
entries.what: washed-rind farmhouse cheese sold in large rounds and small rounds called "dotes".

entries.heading: Milner
entries.what: A Dutch cheese brand. A Goudse kaas made from half-fat milk rather than whole milk, so it has less fat than a 48+ Gouda.

entries.heading: Milo tea with milk powder (galactagogue drink)
entries.what: A "tea" made from Milo (a malted chocolate drink) and milk powder, listed as a liquid food for breastfeeding mothers in Ghana.

entries.heading: Milseán (millsén)
entries.what: A sweet drink made by heating milk or soft sweet curd with butter.

entries.heading: Minas (Queijo Minas; Minas artesanal; Minas padrão / frescal / meia cura / curado)
entries.what: "Queijo minas" is a family name for cheeses from Minas Gerais. The best-known artisanal form is a semi-hard cylinder used in pão de queijo; the fresh form is soft and white and is eaten with goiabada as "Romeu e Julieta".

entries.heading: Minyak samin (ghee / clarified butter)
entries.what: Clarified butter, called minyak samin in Indonesian.

entries.heading: Mirasaka Mozzarella (Mirasaka stretched-curd)
entries.what: A stretched-curd mozzarella from Mirasaka Fromage, Hiroshima.

entries.heading: Mirasaka Ricotta (リコッタ, whey ricotta)
entries.what: A fresh ricotta from Mirasaka Fromage, made from pure leftover whey with no added milk or coagulant.

entries.heading: Miročki sir (Miročka cheese)
entries.what: a white cheese from Miroč mountain, Đerdap area, eastern Serbia

entries.heading: Miromando
entries.what: strong cheese of the Ardèche (Boutières and Monts du Vivarais).

entries.heading: Míša (frozen curd treat)
entries.what: A frozen curd treat produced since 1961.

entries.heading: Mish (مش; meš)
entries.what: A traditional Egyptian cheese made by fermenting salty cheese for months or years, usually at home.

entries.heading: Mishavin (mishavin; Kelmend, northern Albanian Alps)
entries.what: a traditional soft cheese from the Kelmend region of Malësi e Madhe municipality in the northern Albanian Alps.

name: Miso-Pickled Mozzarella
names: 味噌漬けモッツァレラ

entries.heading: Miso-Pickled Mozzarella (味噌漬けモッツァレラ, Tamuraya)
entries.what: A Hokkaido mozzarella marinated in miso, sold by Tamuraya.

entries.heading: Misto capra (goat mix)
entries.what: A Trentino goat cheese, named "misto capra". PAT.

entries.heading: Mizotte
entries.what: Cow's-milk cheese named after mizotte, a salt-marsh grass (Puccinellia maritima) of the flooded Vendée marshes.

entries.heading: Mladi sir (young cheese)
entries.what: A young, fresh cheese made widely in Bosnia.

entries.heading: Mlečni zdrob (milk semolina porridge; mlečni gres / gris)
entries.what: Semolina porridge cooked in milk; alternative names mlečni gres, gres, gris.

entries.heading: Močnik
entries.what: Thick dish of cereal flour (zdrob) cooked in water or milk; varieties by flour: buckwheat, white, maize, oat.

entries.heading: Modern industrial yoghurt
entries.what: packaged yoghurt made with defined fermentation, heat treatment and enzymes, mostly for the domestic market. Traditional yoghurt-type products (ergo, ititu) remain separate.

entries.heading: Moelleux du Revard
entries.what: disc 22 cm across, 8 cm thick, about 1.5 kg; from Mont Revard heights near Aix-les-Bains.

entries.heading: Moesin di Fregona (Moesin)
entries.what: A cheese from Fregona in the Treviso province (Cansiglio area), made by a single producer, the Agricansiglio co-operative.

entries.heading: Mohant (mohant cheese)
entries.what: Bohinj cheese with a whitish-yellow paste, distinctive pungent smell and taste; sometimes bitter after long ripening.

entries.heading: Mokrin cheese (mokrinski sir)
entries.what: a white brined cheese named after Mokrin

entries.heading: Molbo (Molbo cheese; formerly "Danish Edam")
entries.what: a mild, light, slightly tangy and salty Danish cheese from the Mols region, very similar to Edam.

entries.heading: Molke-Getränke and Sig (whey drinks and sweet whey)
entries.what: whey used in soft drinks and as a sweet. Lattella is a whey soft drink labelled Molkenerzeugnis; Rivella is a whey-based drink mixed with fruit concentrate, spices and sugar. Sig is a sweet made by boiling sweet whey until it caramelises sl

entries.heading: Molkenkur (historical whey cure)
entries.what: Whey drunk as a health cure. Around 1890 Switzerland had about thirty Molkenkurorte (whey-cure resorts); by about 1900 whey was considered of little use.

entries.heading: Molozyvo (молозиво; colostrum dessert)
entries.what: Medieval Rus' treat made from colostrum (first milk), despite a church ban.

entries.heading: Momiji (楓, Niseko Momiji)
entries.what: A Niseko Cheese Factory cheese that won at the Artisan Cheese Award.

entries.heading: Monda (মণ্ডা)
entries.what: a sweet yoghurt patty from Muktagachhar, said to be first made in 1824.

entries.heading: Mondseer (Mondseer Schachtelkäse)
entries.what: Austrian Schnittkäse from Mondsee in Upper Austria, sold in boxes since about 1900. First recorded 1830.

entries.heading: Mongolian butter (Xilin Gol, China)
entries.what: Traditional butter from Xilin Gol (Inner Mongolia), nearly pure fat, produced by family-scale producers.

entries.heading: Mongolian dried milk curd (奶豆腐, khuruud / "milk tofu")
entries.what: Mongolian dairy food; dried curd sold sweet (加糖) or sour, a snack that keeps well. Chinese name 奶豆腐 ("milk tofu").

entries.heading: Mongolian salt milk tea (蒙古奶茶, 咸奶茶)
entries.what: Brick tea, milk and butter boiled together and salted; "rather salty" by design. Mongolian milk tea; the region is not stated beyond Mongolian areas of China.

entries.heading: Moni with milk
entries.what: boiled millet flour balls that may be mixed with sugar and milk.

entries.heading: Mons goat cheese (Tešanj)
entries.what: A goat cheese from Tešanj, in north-central Bosnia.

entries.heading: Mont Bébour (Petit Mont Bébour)
entries.what: A soft-paste cheese named after the Bébour forest, made in La Réunion; a smaller 240 g Petit Mont Bébour is also sold.

entries.heading: Mont Vully
entries.what: semi-hard cheese from Cressier in Canton Fribourg, named after the hill across Lake Murten.

entries.heading: Montafoner Sauerkäse (Sura Kees)
entries.what: Lean sour-milk cheese from the Montafon valley, Vorarlberg, known since the 12th century. Related to Tiroler Graukäse.

entries.heading: Montagna
entries.what: A mountain cheese of the Province of Trento. PAT.

entries.heading: Montatimu
entries.what: Corsican cheese listed on the French cheese list.

entries.heading: Montbriac
entries.what: commercial brand from the Compagnie Fromagère de la Vallée de l'Ance, Beauzac (Haute-Loire).

entries.heading: Montcarré
entries.what: named in the French Normandy cuisine article as a Normandy cheese. No description opened.

entries.heading: Monte Baldo (and Monte Baldo primo fiore)
entries.what: A Trentino cheese named after Monte Baldo, the mountain above Lake Garda. "Primo fiore" is a first-flush version. PAT.

entries.heading: Monte Re (Ricotta pecorina Monte Re; Pecorino Monte Re)
entries.what: Friulian cheese named after Monte Re.

entries.heading: Montébore
entries.what: traditional cheese from the Terre del Giarolo mountain community, especially Fabbrica Curone, Piemonte (Alessandria province).

entries.heading: Monterey Jack (Jack; Pepper Jack, Colby-Jack, Cheddar-Jack, Dry Jack are variants)
entries.what: The classic California white cheese, mild and melting.

entries.heading: Monteson
entries.what: A Trentino cheese, named on the register list. PAT.

entries.heading: Montforte blue (Wisconsin)
entries.what: A Wisconsin blue cheese from Montfort.

entries.heading: Montgomery pie
entries.what: A dessert with a molasses and lemon filling under a buttermilk cake topping.

entries.heading: Montoire
entries.what: a Loir-et-Cher cheese.

entries.heading: Moosbacher
entries.what: Austrian cheese named in the English list.

entries.heading: Moose milk (lait d'orignal)

entries.heading: Morbier
entries.what: A semi-hard cow's-milk cheese from the Jura mountains with a thin black line running through the middle.

entries.heading: Morcella
entries.what: A Minnesota cheese, creamy with an earthy flavour, sprinkled with morel mushrooms (Minnesota's state mushroom).

entries.heading: Mori no Cheese Chōjuku (森のチーズ 長熟, Nasu no Mori)
entries.what: An aged pressed cheese from Cheese Workshop Nasu no Mori (Toda, Nasushiobara, Tochigi).

entries.heading: Morir soñando (Morir soñando)
entries.what: A cold drink of orange juice, sugar, evaporated milk and crushed ice. It has spread to other Caribbean and Latin American countries.

entries.heading: Morlacco del Grappa (Morlacco; Morlacco di Grappa; Burlacco)
entries.what: A traditional Veneto cheese from the Grappa massif, made from the milk of the Burlina cow (a native breed at risk). It is a Slow Food presidium and a regional traditional cheese.

entries.heading: Morolique (unripened hard white cheese, artisanal)
entries.what: a semi-dry, firm, soft-textured unripened cheese that does not melt with heat. It resembles homemade feta in appearance but is less salty and not crumbly.

entries.heading: Mortrett (Murtret)
entries.what: traditional product made from leftover pieces of lightly aged cheese; historically used to season food in place of salt.

entries.heading: Moru (Tamil-origin buttermilk-style drink)
entries.what: A thinner drink, similar to lassi, seasoned with salt, asafoetida, curry leaves and mustard seeds.

entries.heading: Moshalal (Baladna brand)
entries.what: A cheese named "Moshalal Cheese" in the Baladna-brand cheese range in Qatar.

entries.heading: Mossfield (Mature, Garlic & Basil, Tomato & Herb, Young Plain, Cumin Seed)
entries.what: organic Gouda-style cheese; Mature aged over 8 months; flavoured varieties.

entries.heading: Motal (Մոթալ)
entries.what: A mountain cheese flavoured with wild herbs and aged for months in an animal-skin bag or in pots.

entries.heading: Motal pendiri (motal pendiri; Azerbaijani; Qazax motal, Qarabağ motal)
entries.what: A crumbly, salty cheese, stronger than feta, eaten broken into pieces with fresh herbs. The cheese is named after the motal, a container made from a small-horned animal's skin. Motal use is also described for butter and şor.

entries.heading: Motal şoru
entries.what: dairy product said to be prepared only in leather vessels (motal).

entries.heading: Mothais sur feuille (La Mothe-Saint-Héray)
entries.what: A goat cheese named after La Mothe-Saint-Héray (Deux-Sèvres), wrapped and ripened on a chestnut or plane leaf which draws moisture in.

entries.heading: Mothe-Bougon (Bougon)
entries.what: A cheese of Mothe-Bougon, Deux-Sèvres.

entries.heading: Mothe-Saint-Héray
entries.what: A cheese of La Mothe-Saint-Héray, Deux-Sèvres; related to Mothais sur feuille.

entries.heading: Mottin charentais
entries.what: A soft double-cream cheese made by Savencia in Saint-Saviol, Charente; formerly called crottin charentais.

entries.heading: Mouradian (Le Mouradian)
entries.what: A soft, fragrant cheese sold in the Dely Ibrahim shop in Algiers.

entries.heading: Mozzarella and yoghurt (Milka Krem, Philippine Carabao Center)

entries.heading: Mozzarella dei Monti Sibillini (STG)
entries.what: A fresh stretched-curd cheese from the Monti Sibillini area, registered as a Traditional Speciality Guaranteed (STG) product under EC Regulation 509/2006.

entries.heading: Mozzarella di Brugnato (La Spezia)
entries.what: a mozzarella from Brugnato, province of La Spezia.

entries.heading: Mozzarella di Gioia del Colle (DOP)
entries.what: A soft, fresh, stretched-curd cheese from the Altopiano della Murgia, EU PDO since 2019.

entries.heading: Mozzarella di vacca (Molise)
entries.what: A cow's-milk mozzarella listed for Molise in the national table of traditional products.

entries.heading: Mozzarella pecorina (Abruzzo)
entries.what: a sheep's-milk mozzarella typical of Sardinia, Abruzzo and Lazio.

entries.heading: Mozzarella silana (Mozzarella silana)
entries.what: A mozzarella from the Sila, listed for Calabria.

entries.heading: Mozzarella-style cheese (monks' factories)
entries.what: A fresh Italian-style cheese listed among the products of the Belgian monks' cheese factories in Masisi.

entries.heading: Mr Whippy (soft-serve)
entries.what: the UK soft-serve brand sold from ice cream vans.

entries.heading: Mtsi Limnou (Μτσι Λήμνου)
entries.what: Lemnos cheese; no details.

entries.heading: Mudaffara (muddaffara; majdula; Sudanese braided cheese)
