entries.heading: Muenster (American Muenster)
entries.what: An American cheese that may imitate Alsatian Munster; milder than French Munster.

entries.heading: Muhalbiya (rice pudding with whole milk; GCC sweet)
entries.what: A rice pudding made with whole milk, sugar, rice flour and vanilla, one of the traditional GCC sweets.

entries.heading: Muhallebi / mahalabiya (balouza, mahalayeh)
entries.what: A milk pudding thickened with rice flour, cornstarch or semolina, flavoured with rose or jasmine water.

entries.heading: Mujalaleh (المجلّلة)
entries.what: a dish of dough combined with clarified butter (ghee)

entries.heading: Mülifoafal (Farferlsuppe, Burgenland milk soup with flour dumplings)
entries.what: Burgenland soup, also called Farferlsuppe; once common in poorer households; Franz Maier-Bruck regarded it as a kind of national dish of the Burgenlanders (the "Hienzen"); it nearly disappeared from Burgenland tables after the Second World

entries.heading: Multekrem (cloudberry cream)
entries.what: a traditional Norwegian dessert of cloudberries mixed with whipped cream and sugar, served raw or warm; a Christmas dinner dessert; served with krumkake or kransekake, or filled in krumkaker.

entries.heading: Mumuíla cattle milk economy (fresh milk for diet and sale)
entries.what: cattle milk is the basis of the diet of the transhumant agro-pastoralists of southwest Angola (Huíla and Namibe), including the Mumuíla. The study says the economic use of cattle is mostly milk production, which also brings cash income. It

entries.heading: Munavoi (egg butter)
entries.what: A spread of butter, salt and boiled egg, sometimes lightened with cottage cheese. Spread on karjalanpiirakka (Karelian pies); Estonia also has it, served on rye bread at Easter.

entries.heading: Munguzá (mungunzá)
entries.what: Sweet dish of whole white corn cooked in a broth of milk (or coconut milk), with sugar, cinnamon and cloves. Originated in the Northeast; called canjica in much of the country and mingau de milho in Maranhão and Piauí.

entries.heading: Muntanacciu
entries.what: A cheese made in mountain pastures in Corsica, named as a related cheese on the Venaco page.

entries.heading: Muravera Costa Rei Iaia
entries.what: One of 16 lesser-known Sardinian cheeses, made by Caseificio Iesum.

entries.heading: Murazzano (Murazzano DOP)
entries.what: small PDO cheese, 10–15 cm across, 300–400 g, from the Alta Langa.

entries.heading: Murcia al vino (Murcian wine cheese)
entries.what: Wine-washed goat's cheese from Murcia.

entries.heading: Murciano-Granadina goat cheese (queso Murciano-Granadina)
entries.what: a traditional matured goat cheese made in Andalusia, named after the Murciano-Granadina breed.

entries.heading: Murciano-Granadina semi-hard goat cheese (queso de cabra semicurado, Andalusia)
entries.what: Traditional semi-hard pressed goat's cheese from Andalusia, with pale colour and yogurt, butter and cake aromas.

entries.heading: Murianengo (Moncenisio)
entries.what: a Gorgonzola-like cow's-milk cheese from Piedmont.

entries.heading: Murol du Grand Bérioux (Murolait; Grand Murols)
entries.what: about 450 g, 12 cm across, with a 3 cm central hole; the plug becomes the murolait (about 50 g, red paraffin).

entries.heading: Mursik (Kalenjin fermented milk; other names: rotik for the blood variant, possibly maziwa lala per Wikipedia — see Unsure)
entries.what: a sour, spontaneously fermented milk of the Kalenjin of the Rift Valley, with a smoky, bluish-tinted flavour from the lining of the gourd. Used at marriages, athletic celebrations, and given to breastfeeding mothers.

entries.heading: Murtabak cheese (murtabak keju; mozzarella-filled murtabak)
entries.what: A variant of murtabak, the stuffed fried flatbread, sold in Malaysia and Singapore. Mozzarella is added as an extra filling beside the usual spiced meat.

entries.heading: Murtaler Steirerkäse (Steirerkäse, Murtal variety)
entries.what: Styrian sour-milk cheese from the Murtal, a regional variety of Steirerkäse.

entries.heading: Murtarat
entries.what: traditional cheese mainly from the province of Biella, Piemonte.

entries.heading: Musei Smeraldo Erborinato
entries.what: One of 16 lesser-known Sardinian cheeses, made by Latteria Sociale Santadi, with a blue-veined style.

entries.heading: Musulupu dell'Aspromonte (Musulupu)
entries.what: A local cheese from the Aspromonte, listed for Calabria.

entries.heading: Muvrinu
entries.what: Corsican cheese listed on the French cheese list.

entries.heading: Mycella
entries.what: a creamy, traditional Danish blue cheese, described as a Danish version of Gorgonzola.

entries.heading: Mymoo smooth yoghurt
entries.what: A smooth yoghurt listed in Namibia Dairies' yoghurt range.

entries.heading: Myseost (whey cheese)
entries.what: the Danish term for whey cheese (boiled-down whey).

entries.heading: Mysingur (velliostur, rauðseyddur drafli)
entries.what: A named Icelandic whey-based cheese-type item listed on the Icelandic cheese overview page with the alternative names velliostur and rauðseyddur drafli.

entries.heading: Mysuostur (brown whey cheese; mysuostur, mysost)
entries.what: A caramel-coloured whey cheese made by boiling whey until most of the water evaporates.

entries.heading: Nacho cheese
entries.what: A cheese sauce for chips.

entries.heading: Nadughi (ნადუღი)
entries.what: a smooth, milky-white, soft curd with a cream tint and a taste typical of albumin. Eaten salted, or with mint. Described as a long-established national dairy product.

entries.heading: Nai lao / Beijing yoghurt (北京酸奶, 奶酪 nǎilào)
entries.what: A traditional fermented milk drink popular across China, mainly associated with Beijing. The name nǎilào (奶酪) is also the Chinese word for cheese in some regions, which is a source of confusion.

entries.heading: Nai zha / Thi (奶渣, naizha)
entries.what: A very firm, sour, slightly sweet yak cheese from northern Yunnan near the Tibetan Autonomous Region.

entries.heading: Naidoufu (奶豆腐, nǎidòufu; "milk tofu")
entries.what: A Mongolian milk-curd block sold as snacks, sweet or unsweetened, sometimes flavoured with dried jujube.

entries.heading: Naigeda (naigeda; Kazak artisanal cheese)
entries.what: Traditional Kazak artisanal cheese from Xinjiang.

name: Nakasatsunai Camembert
names: ナカサツナイ カマンベール

entries.heading: Nakasatsunai Camembert (ナカサツナイ カマンベール, Tokachino Fromage)
entries.what: A petit camembert from Tokachino Fromage, a Hokkaido maker.

entries.heading: Nalžovy (Nalžovský sýr)
entries.what: south Bohemian cheese similar to Camembert, produced since the late 19th century; in the Šumava mountains.

entries.heading: Nammilk (fresh and long-life milk)
entries.what: A Namibia Dairies brand under which fresh and long-life milk is sold.

entries.heading: Nanaimo bar
entries.what: a Canadian no-bake dessert named after Nanaimo, British Columbia, with a wafer, nut and coconut crumb base, a custard icing and a chocolate ganache topping.

entries.heading: Nanoški sir (Nanos cheese; nanoški sir)
entries.what: Yellow, piquant hard cheese named after the Nanos plateau, produced since the 16th century.

entries.heading: Nanteau (Nanteau)
entries.what: a cheese listed for the Gâtinais area of Seine-et-Marne.

entries.heading: Napolact (industrial brand; FrieslandCampina)
entries.what: A brand of the Dutch company FrieslandCampina, used only in Romania; it ran three factories in 2015 (Baciu, Țaga and Târgu Mureș).

entries.heading: Narchvi (ნარჩვი)
entries.what: a Svan cheese from Upper Svaneti, eaten dry or warmed and poured over dishes, and used as a filling for khachapuri and other pastries.

entries.heading: Naré (Fulani butter from churned fermented milk, and its melted oil)
entries.what: A butter made by Fulani vendors, churned from fermented milk. Melting it gives an oil used in cooking and as a body ointment.

entries.heading: Năsal
entries.what: A pungent cheese matured in a cave near the village of Năsal, historically linked to the Schilling family.

name: Nasu no Brown Cheese
names: 那須のブラウンチーズ

entries.heading: Nasu no Brown Cheese (那須のブラウンチーズ, whey cheese)
entries.what: A brown whey cheese from Nasu no Mori, made from whey left over from cheesemaking.

entries.heading: Natas do Céu
entries.what: A layered dessert of crushed biscuits, whipped cream and an egg-based sweet on top.

entries.heading: Natilla piurana (natilla; toffee from Piura)

entries.heading: Natillas (natillas)
entries.what: A thin, pourable custard, richer than flan, with cinnamon and no caramel. Often topped with a María biscuit.

entries.heading: Natural Goats Log (Fivemiletown Natural Goat's Log)
entries.what: A fresh goat's cheese log made by Fivemiletown Creamery.

entries.heading: Nazareth
entries.what: A hard Belgian cheese with a dark brown rind and a mild, subtle flavour, named after the village of Nazareth in East Flanders. Fat content 45%. Used in some quick-service restaurants as "kaas croketten".

entries.heading: Nevegal (Nevegal cheese; Formaggio Nevegal)
entries.what: A cow's-milk cheese of the Belluno province, named after the Nevegal alpine pasture where it was first made in shared dairies. Now widely sold across Veneto.

entries.heading: New Zealand cheddar (factory and artisan)
entries.what: Cheddar made in New Zealand, mostly in factories and some by artisan makers by hand. Factory cheddar is usually sold young in New Zealand.

entries.heading: Ngapyaw baung (banana pudding)
entries.what: a Mon-style banana pudding.

entries.heading: Ngonguenha (milk-based savoury dish)
entries.what: a savoury dish of toasted manioc (cassava) flour, sugar and milk, per the Wikipedia Angolan cuisine article.

entries.heading: Nguri (牛乳, niúrǔ; giam-ngu-ring, xiánniúnǎi "salty milk")
entries.what: A ball-shaped buffalo cheese from southern China, very salty, eaten with congee.

entries.heading: Nidel (Nidle, Nidelrahm; Rahm/cream grades)
entries.what: Nidel is the Swiss-German word for Rahm (cream). In canton Bern "Nydle/Niidle" means cream in general, while in Obwalden it means whipped cream. Swiss fat grades: Halbrahm (about 15%), Vollrahm (about 35%), Doppelrahm (at least 45%). Cream

entries.heading: Nidwaldner Alpkäse (Nidwaldner Alpkäse; Alpkäse, German)
entries.what: An alp cheese from Nidwalden, mostly semi-hard, about 6 to 8 kg, in mild, spicy or "rezent" (sharp) flavours. The article notes that Nidwalden's Alpkäse varies more than in other mountain cantons.

entries.heading: Niolo (niulinchi; niulincu)
entries.what: A cheese named for the Niolo valley; the fr page says Niolo is the exclusive region for making niulinchi cheeses, with herders' know-how spreading to Filosorma and Balagne.

entries.heading: Njeguški sir (Његушки сир; Njeguški sir)
entries.what: Full-fat cheese from Montenegro with Cetinje given as its place of origin; the page says it was named the second-best cheese in the world in 2022.

entries.heading: Nøkkelost (nøkkelost; "key cheese"; kuminost; "Kuminost Spiced Cheese" in US)
entries.what: a semi-hard Norwegian yellow cheese flavoured with cumin and cloves.

entries.heading: Nom priao and yoghurt (นมเปรี้ยว, โยเกิร์ต)
entries.what: nom priao is the general Thai name for both drinkable and thick fermented milk. Yoghurt (โยเกิร์ต) is the thick, spoonable type.

entries.heading: Nom yen (นมเย็น, also Nom Chompoo)
entries.what: a pink iced milk drink. The name means "cold milk", and Chompoo refers to its pink colour.

entries.heading: Non-food uses of butter (hair oil, wound dressing, ritual)
entries.what: butter used as a hair oil, to treat wounds, and in ritual use at celebrations and to host guests.

entries.heading: Nônô kumu (Malian traditional fermented milk category)
entries.what: a traditional fermented milk category named in a 2025 study of Malian products; the abstract does not describe it further.

entries.heading: Noord-Hollandse kaas (Noord-Hollandse Gouda)
entries.what: A regional Gouda-type cheese from North Holland, smoother, sweeter and fruitier than Gouda. Carries an EU PDO.

entries.heading: Norse-era cow and small-stock milk (fresh milk)
entries.what: Milk from cattle, later from sheep and goats, drunk and processed by Norse settlers.

entries.heading: Norvegia
entries.what: a common Norwegian yellow cheese, produced since the 1890s; made by Tine.

entries.heading: Norzola
entries.what: a Norwegian blue cheese, milder and smoother than Gorgonzola, with fat at 60% of dry matter; developed after Norway voted against joining the EC in 1972.

entries.heading: Nostrano (Nostrano de casèl, Nostrano di malga, Nostrano di Primiero)
entries.what: A family of farm cheeses from Trentino under several local names (de casèl, di malga, di Primiero). PAT.

entries.heading: Nostrano Valtrompia (Nostrano Valtrompia DOP)
entries.what: a DOP cheese from the Val Trompia, Province of Brescia; the Bagòss article calls it the DOP-protected cousin of Bagòss.

entries.heading: Notre Dame de la Paix
entries.what: A well-ripened, creamy camembert-style cheese with a strong flavour.

entries.heading: Notre-Dame de Carentan
entries.what: named in the French Normandy cuisine article as a Normandy cheese, from the Carentan area (Manche). No description opened.

entries.heading: Notre-Dame de Grâce
entries.what: named in the French Normandy cuisine article as a Normandy cheese. No description opened.

entries.heading: Nunu (nunu; "fura de nunu" when served with millet balls)
entries.what: A West African fermented milk product, yoghurt-like, made in Ghana and Nigeria; in the Ghana sample it was consumed as a dairy beverage.

entries.heading: Nurri Dolce Alba
entries.what: One of 16 lesser-known Sardinian cheeses, made by Caseificio Mattana.

entries.heading: Nuss-nuss (nuṣṣ-nuṣṣ, "half-half")
entries.what: A coffee mixed with milk, described as a Moroccan variant of café crème ("half-half").

entries.heading: Nýmjólk (whole cow's milk)
entries.what: Whole milk. Milk drinking into adulthood is very common in Iceland.

entries.heading: O'Reilly's goat cheese (O'Reilly's natural; O'Reilly's chive; O'Reilly's mustard seed)
entries.what: Goat's cheese from Fivemiletown Creamery sold natural, hand-rolled in chives, or coated in mustard seed.

name: Oak flavoured milk and coffee milk

entries.heading: Oak flavoured milk and coffee milk
entries.what: A pasteurised flavoured milk and coffee milk brand, now owned by Lactalis (France). It began in New South Wales in 1967 as a dairy-co-operative label (Raymond Terrace and Hunter Valley), and launched in Queensland, South Australia and Victo

entries.heading: Oakwood (Oakwood smoked cheddar)
entries.what: A mature cheddar smoked naturally with wood chips from sustainably foraged local oak logs.

entries.heading: Oázis
entries.what: a smoked Hungarian cheese listed in the English list.

entries.heading: Obwaldner Alpkäse (Obwaldner Alpkäse; Alpchäs)
entries.what: a hard raw-milk alpine cheese of about 12 kg, from the canton of Obwalden. Ripening ranges from about three months (mild) to two years.

entries.heading: Óðals Búri
entries.what: A cheese in the Óðals range of the Icelandic dairy cooperative Mjólkursamsalan, now sold in 8-slice packs (previously sold in pieces).

entries.heading: Oïkos yoghurt (partly made from Réunion milk)
entries.what: a Danone yoghurt line that the Miel Vert coverage says is partly made from Réunion milk.

entries.heading: Oka (Oka, Quebec; other names: Oka cheese)
entries.what: A semi-soft washed-rind cheese from Oka in the Laurentides region of Quebec, with a copper-orange rind washed by hand.

entries.heading: Olanchano cheese (queso olanchano; from the Olancho region)
entries.what: a cheese named for Olancho, served with carneada alongside chismol, roasted plantains, chorizo, tortillas and beans.

entries.heading: Olandiškas sūris (Edam-type cheese, made in Lithuania before WWI)
entries.what: An Edam-type cheese made in Lithuania before WWI, about 14.2 % of output in that period.

entries.heading: Old English (Kraft)
entries.what: A processed cheese spread brand.

name: Old-style milk bars
names: ไอติมโบราณ
ไอศกรีมโบราณ

entries.heading: Old-style milk bars (ไอติมโบราณ, ไอศกรีมโบราณ)
entries.what: rectangular milk bars, eaten as bars or cut into a bowl. The Thai article says they developed from tube ice cream under King Rama VII.

name: Oliang / Lao iced coffee with condensed milk

entries.heading: Oliang / Lao iced coffee with condensed milk (kafe lao, kafae yen; oliang)
entries.what: strong Lao coffee served over ice, either black (oliang) or with sweetened condensed milk at the bottom of the glass, followed by a green tea chaser.

entries.heading: Olivet (Olivet cendré / Olivet bleu)
entries.what: a historical Loiret farmhouse cheese dusted with vine-shoot charcoal ash, sold in several styles.

entries.heading: Olivet cendré (Cendré d'Olivet)
entries.what: A French cheese from Olivet on the Loire, Centre-Val de Loire.

entries.heading: Øllebrød (beer bread porridge)
entries.what: a thick porridge of sourdough rye bread and beer, often hvidtøl; medieval origin, eaten at breakfast in winter.

entries.heading: Olmützer Quargel
entries.what: A small sour-milk cheese sold as sticks or short rolls, with a pungent smell similar to Harzer cheese.

entries.heading: Olomoucké tvarůžky (Olomoucké syrečky; tvargle; tvarůžková)
entries.what: PGI cheese from Loštice and the Haná region around Olomouc, Moravia. Strong smell and pungent flavour; sold in small disks, rings or sticks.

entries.heading: Ølost (Telemark ølost; milk and beer drink)
entries.what: a traditional Norwegian warm drink of milk and beer, served hot with sugar and sometimes small pieces of cheese; in the recipe source it is eaten at breakfast or as an evening snack, especially at Christmas.

entries.heading: Olshoro (milk-flavoured fermented maize and bean food)
entries.what: a fermented food of the Arusha region, mainly for children; milk is not the base, the fermented food is.

entries.heading: Oltermanni (Valio)
entries.what: A Finnish mild cheese brand-type, often eaten on rye bread or with karelian pasties; a 17% fat version from 1997, a 9% low-fat version from 2008, and a 33% version (Täyteläinen).

entries.heading: Om Ali (أم علي; Umm Ali)
entries.what: Egypt's national dessert, eaten at iftar during Ramadan.

entries.heading: Om sữa (milk clay-pot dish, northern Vietnam)
entries.what: A northern cooking technique in which a dish is cooked in a clay pot with milk.

entries.heading: Omani halwa (ghee-based sweet)
entries.what: A halwa served with dates and kahwa (coffee). Ghee is one of its ingredients.

entries.heading: Omavele (Nhaneca-Humbe; sour milk; also "leite azedo" in Huíla)
entries.what: a traditional acidified milk of the Nhaneca-Humbe (Nyaneka-Humbe) agro-pastoral people of southwest Angola. The thesis describes it as low in pH, nutritionally valuable and reasonably safe. Wikipedia lists a Huíla "sour milk with maize porr

entries.heading: Oob (fresh Taizz cheese)
entries.what: the fresh form of the Taizz farmstead cheese, called "Oob" in the UNDP assessment.

entries.heading: Örgü peyniri (braided cheese)
entries.what: A specialty of Diyarbakır, made as strips of elastic cheese wound into a braid.

entries.heading: Original (Gotland sheep cheese)
entries.what: A Gotland sheep's-milk cheese that resembles feta; sold plain or flavoured with basil or pink pepper.

entries.heading: Orri (Casa Raubert mature cheese)
entries.what: One of the three mature cheeses from Casa Raubert, Escàs, named with Conlloc and Pletiu.

entries.heading: Ortler (Ortles)
entries.what: A semi-hard cheese from the upper Val Venosta, named after Mount Ortles. Wheels about 2 kg; brown rind, straw paste with small regular eyes.

entries.heading: Oscos (Queso de Oscos)
entries.what: cheese of the Los Oscos and Alto Navia area in western Asturias, made since medieval times per documents from the Benedictine monastery of Villanueva de Oscos; revived by Industrias Lácteas Monteverde using traditional methods after it had

entries.heading: Oscypek (oscypek; Polish, also "oscypek")
entries.what: A smoked sheep's-milk cheese of the Tatra Mountains, traditionally made by Goral herders and now also sold as street food in the south with cranberry jam.

entries.heading: Ossetian cheese (Ирон цыхт / сулугун; Iron Ossetic)
entries.what: Traditional cheese of the Ossetian people in the North Caucasus; the English article lists Russia as country of origin and does not mention Georgia.

entries.heading: Ossolano (Ossolano DOP)
entries.what: PDO cheese made only in the Val d'Ossola (Verbano-Cusio-Ossola, Piemonte); DOP recognised 2017. The related Ossolano d'Alpe is made from alpine pasture milk at 1,400 m and above.

entries.heading: Ostfriesentee mit Sahne (East Frisian tea with cream and Kluntje)
entries.what: strong black tea blend from East Frisia, served with cream and rock sugar (Kluntje).

entries.heading: Ostkaka (cheesecake)
entries.what: Traditional Swedish dessert, documented from 1538 and possibly older, made from rennet-curdled milk.

entries.heading: Ostkaka (Swedish cheesecake; curd dish and dessert)
entries.what: Swedish dish and dessert made from curdled milk and wheat flour, traditionally baked; Småland and Hälsingland varieties. Served with jam, whipped cream, or cloudberries.

name: Other cheeses named on the Azerbaijani "popular cheese types" list

entries.heading: Other cheeses named on the Azerbaijani "popular cheese types" list (industrial and imported)
entries.what: Bakşyteyn, Bri, Brınza, Quda, Qorqonsola, Dor blyu, Kamamber, Limburqer, Maazdam, Motsarella, Parmezan, Rokfor, Rus, Tilziter, Feta, Filadelfiya, Çedder, İsveç pendiri, Edamer, Emmental, Liqvan.

entries.heading: Otlu peynir (Van herbed cheese)
entries.what: Herbed cheese made mainly in East Anatolia; semi-hard, from raw sheep's milk.

entries.heading: Ottawa (Polička)
entries.what: named Czech cheese from Polička, produced for decades.

entries.heading: Oudi ouan oulli (Tuareg white cheese)
entries.what: A Tuareg cheese similar to fromage blanc, served in small portions.

entries.heading: Ovaltine (malt drink made with milk)
entries.what: A branded malt drink made with milk, consumed by adolescents in the study.

entries.heading: Óvári
entries.what: a Hungarian semi-hard cheese of the pusztasajt (Great Plain pasture cheese) type.

entries.heading: Ovidur
entries.what: a cheese named on the Croatia list

entries.heading: Oxford Blue
entries.what: An English "French-style" blue cheese.

entries.heading: P'it Saint-Faron (P'it saint-faron)
entries.what: a cheese listed for the pays briard.

entries.heading: P'tit Basque
entries.what: A small cheese of the Pays basque (sheep-cheese brand style).

entries.heading: P'tit Havrais
entries.what: named in the French Normandy cuisine article as a Normandy cheese, from the Le Havre area. No description opened.

entries.heading: Packaged cheese (supermarket, Dakar; unnamed)
entries.what: Cheese sold in two major supermarket chains in Dakar. The 2021 survey counted 110 cheese products in its cheese category, all classed as ultra-processed.

entries.heading: Packaged commercial cheese (Parmalat and other brands)
entries.what: cheese brands sold to consumers in Zambia. A consumer panel scanned 163 cheese products from 20 brands, with Parmalat the most scanned brand.

entries.heading: Packaged fluid milk (distributed brands)
entries.what: Packaged milk sold in shops under brand names. Brands named on a distributor's list are Bonny Milk and Moo Milk, given here only as examples of the kind.

name: Packaged full-cream, half-cream and skimmed milk

entries.heading: Packaged full-cream, half-cream and skimmed milk (Juhayna, Obour Land; Arabic name not in opened sources)
entries.what: Packaged milk from two Egyptian dairies. Juhayna sells full cream, half cream, skimmed, lactose-free, 0% and zero-fat variants (full cream in 200 ml, 0.5, 1 and 1.5 L; half cream in 1 L only). Obour Land sells full cream (200 ml and 1 L) an

entries.heading: Packaged laban and yoghurt (Almarai, Mazoon; Arabic لبن / زبادي)
entries.what: Supermarket laban and yoghurt sold in Oman under the Almarai and Mazoon brands, in sizes from 150 g to 2 kg and 180 ml to 2 L. Products include full-fat fresh laban, plain full-fat yoghurt, Almarai Zabadi, Greek-style plain yoghurt, and fla

entries.heading: Packaged milk, whole and reduced-fat 2% (English; no local name in the source)
entries.what: The most-recorded dairy item for young children in three FSM states. 2% milk was top dairy item in Pohnpei (65 children), Yap (77) and Kosrae (44); whole milk was second in Pohnpei (58), Yap (32) and Kosrae (29). Average milk intake (the fo

entries.heading: Packaged pasteurised and UHT milk (toned, standardised, full cream) (पैकेज्ड दूध)
entries.what: Packaged milk sold by fat grade: full cream 6%, standardised 4.5%, toned 3.0%, double toned 1.5%, skimmed 0.5%. Usually pasteurised, often mixing cow and buffalo.

entries.heading: Padduni
entries.what: a small goat's-milk ball cheese (about 300 g), named from the Sicilian word for "ball"; the fresh counterpart of Sicilian goat cheese.

entries.heading: Padraccio (also Paddaccio; goat's milk; PAT)
entries.what: A goat's milk cheese from the Pollino area of Basilicata, eaten fresh.

entries.heading: Paglierina
entries.what: semi-aged cheese from Piemonte, mainly the provinces of Torino and Cuneo; Rifreddo and Barge versions well known.

entries.heading: Pain patat (pen patat)
entries.what: A soft, sweet bread flavoured with cinnamon and made with sweet potato, served cold from the fridge or at room temperature.

name: Pain perdu soaked in condensed milk

entries.heading: Pain perdu soaked in condensed milk (dish)
entries.what: a French-toast-style dish that the chef calls a Gabonese classic and a favourite of children.

entries.heading: Palet de chèvre (Palet de chèvre)
entries.what: a small goat cheese from near Rambouillet.

entries.heading: Palet du Plateau (Taravao, Tahiti)
entries.what: one of the three cheeses named by the Taravao producer.

entries.heading: Palmero (Queso palmero; Queso de La Palma; Queso Palmero DOP)
entries.what: A cylindrical, flattened goat cheese from La Palma, usually smoked, with a firm, elastic paste and a clean, goaty, slightly acidic flavour.

entries.heading: Palmito (queso palmito; Zarcero palmito)
entries.what: A fresh, light, salty, stringy cheese, shaped into a rolled knot or sphere that shows its layers. Developed in Zarcero, Alajuela province, in the late 19th century by Italian immigrants. The Spanish article likens it to mozzarella.

entries.heading: Palouza (milk dessert)
entries.what: A light, eggless Algerian cream dessert served chilled, from Algiers.

entries.heading: Pálpusztai
entries.what: a Hungarian soft cheese known for a strong, pungent smell.

entries.heading: Pamonha (pamonha de sal; pamonha de doce; garapa de pamonha)
entries.what: A traditional Brazilian food from indigenous cooking, common in the Southeast, Northeast, Goiás, Mato Grosso, Paraná, Rondônia and Tocantins. Salty version common in the Centre-West (often filled with meat, cheese or sausage; doce version o

entries.heading: Pan bati (Papiamento; "smashed bread")
entries.what: A flat bread or pancake made with sorghum flour, wheat flour and milk; served plain or with sugar or other fillings.

entries.heading: Panchamrita (पंचामृत)
entries.what: Five-ingredient offering: milk, curd, ghee, honey, sugar; used in Hindu and Jain worship and abhishek.

entries.heading: Pandir (matured cheese; "pandir tikki" filling)
entries.what: An aged cheese used as the filling of a Chitrali tikki bread ("pandir tikki"). The word "pandir" appears in the dish name, which suggests a local cheese name, but the sources do not say so explicitly.

entries.heading: Panela (queso de canasta, queso panela)
entries.what: A white fresh cheese found in most of Mexico, sold as a loaf or cone; mild, slightly sweet and sour.

entries.heading: Paniņas (paniņas)
entries.what: Named as a Latvian fermented milk product in the first pass; the Latvian Wikipedia article describes it as the liquid left when cream is churned into butter. It is used in dairy production to adjust fat content and to make fresh and ferment

entries.heading: Pannes cendré
entries.what: a Loiret ash-ripened cheese.

entries.heading: Pannónia
entries.what: a Hungarian version of Swiss Emmental.

entries.heading: Pañoleta
entries.what: a name used for a format or shape of small fresh goat cheese in Aragón, and also listed as a separate cheese in the English list.

entries.heading: Panquehue (queso Panquehue)
entries.what: A Chilean cheese from the Andean Aconcagua region, similar in taste to Tilsit, often mixed with chives or red pepper flakes. One of Chile's most popular cheeses; in 2005 it was the first Chilean cheese imported into the United States under

entries.heading: Pantua (পান্তুয়া; pantooa)
entries.what: Deep-fried chhena balls from Bengal, eaten across eastern India and Bangladesh.

entries.heading: Pantysgawn
entries.what: A soft goat cheese from Blaenavon, Wales, made by the Craske family from Pant-Ys-Gawn Farm, and now sold by Abergavenny Fine Foods Ltd (since 1987). Sold as small rounds or 2-pound logs.

entries.heading: Papaya milk (木瓜牛乳; 木瓜牛奶)
entries.what: A milk drink of more than half milk, blended with concentrated papaya juice (or papaya powder in some versions). Creamy, lightly sweet, pale orange.

entries.heading: Papitas de leche
entries.what: A traditional Venezuelan sweet, described on the cuisine page as "traditional sweet treats or milk truffles".

entries.heading: Paponi (ბურეღი / ფაფონი; Lazeti)
entries.what: sweet baked pastry filled with milk pudding, from Lazeti; linked to galaktoboureko.

entries.heading: Paraguay cheese (queso Paraguay, queso paraguayo; Guaraní kesú Paraguái; queso paraguay duro when aged)
entries.what: the national cheese of Paraguay, described as an important part of the culture and a source of protein and calcium in the diet. Fresh it is soft, creamy and slightly acidic; aged it turns yellowish, dry and full of holes. Used widely in sal

entries.heading: Parapal (raw-milk blue cheese, Es Pinaró de ses Monges)
entries.what: Blue cheese made by Es Pinaró de ses Monges, Mallorca, described as raw-milk.

entries.heading: Parcharotyr (Παρχαροτύρι; parcharotyri)
entries.what: A Pontic Greek cheese, flavoured with herbs, smoked and slowly matured. The name is said to mean "high mountains". Made today in Kilkis (Central Macedonia).

entries.heading: Parenica (parenica; Slovak)
entries.what: a Slovak steamed cheese shaped in strips and woven into snail-like spirals; typical rolls about 100 g.

entries.heading: Parenyica
entries.what: a pressed cheese named on the Hungarian list without description.

entries.heading: Parmalat Botswana cheese (variety not named)
entries.what: Cheese listed among the products of Parmalat Botswana, alongside UHT milk and cream.

entries.heading: Parmesan
entries.what: an Italian-style hard cheese listed as made in Kenya.

entries.heading: Parmesan-type hard cheese (Võru Juust)
entries.what: a Parmesan-type hard cheese made by Võru Juust, alongside its block cheese.

entries.heading: Parmesano (Peruvian parmesan)
entries.what: Parmesan-style cheese made in Peru, named among Puno and national contest cheeses; the Andino matured-cheese article says parmesan needs at least 12 months.

entries.heading: Parrano
entries.what: A trademarked Gouda-style semi-firm cheese.

entries.heading: Parthenay
entries.what: A cheese of the Parthenay area, Deux-Sèvres (Poitou).

entries.heading: Pasha (pasha; paasha)
entries.what: A Russian-origin Easter dessert, tied to the Eastern Slavic and Orthodox tradition, and also to the Orthodox Karelian Easter tradition in Finland. Made with rahka, cream, sugar, egg and butter, flavoured with vanilla and almond crumb. Raisi

entries.heading: Paška skuta (skuta)
entries.what: a skuta (whey cheese) from Pag

entries.heading: Paskha (паска / пасха; Easter cheese dessert)
entries.what: Easter dessert of tvorog, eggs, sugar, raisins and nuts pressed into a pyramid.

entries.heading: Paški sir (Paški sir; Pag cheese)
entries.what: a sheep's milk cheese from the island of Pag in northern Dalmatia; sheep graze aromatic salt-tolerant plants shaped by the bora wind, which the sources credit for the flavour.

entries.heading: Passendale
entries.what: A Belgian semi-hard cheese, loaf-shaped, with a hard brown rind with white spots, golden interior with small holes, firm, moist and creamy, mild and slightly sweet. Often used in France as a stand-in for Tilsit.

entries.heading: Pastel de nata (custard)
entries.what: The custard of the Portuguese custard tart, made with milk, eggs, sugar, lemon and cinnamon, baked in puff-pastry cases. Lisbon, Belém is the origin named on the page.

entries.heading: Pasteurised and UHT cow milk (شیر پاستوریزه، شیر UHT)
entries.what: Pasteurised milk (from 7 commercial brands) and UHT milk (from 12 commercial brands) sold in Markazi Province.

entries.heading: Pasteurised and UHT liquid milk
entries.what: Processed liquid milk sold by a small number of processing companies; consumers prefer pasteurisation and UHT over unprocessed milk (choice experiment, LKR 150 baseline price).

entries.heading: Pasteurised camel milk (Kenya, urban)
entries.what: camel milk pasteurised and sold to urban markets in Kenya; the review describes peri-urban dairies operating and Kenya as more commercially developed for camel milk than its neighbours.

entries.heading: Pasteurised donor human milk (Canadian milk banks)
entries.what: donor milk from Canadian human milk banks, supplied to babies in hospitals and to families in some trials. The Rogers Hixon Ontario Human Milk Bank (Mount Sinai, Toronto) pools milk from donors and pasteurises it; NorthernStar Mothers Milk

entries.heading: Pasteurised drinking milk
entries.what: Packaged drinking milk, Israel's main industrial milk product. The Tnuva article says the company's sales account for about 70% of the Israeli dairy market, and its historic specialty was drinking milk.

entries.heading: Pasteurised fresh milk (cow and goat, certified herds)
entries.what: Heat-treated fresh milk from certified herds, the standard milk supply after the raw-milk ban.

entries.heading: Pasteurised fresh milk and heat-treated (reconstituted) milk
entries.what: Pasteurised fresh milk sold by La Laiterie du Berger under the Dolima brand, and reconstituted milk from powder that is pasteurised in bottles or sterilised in bricks.

name: Pasteurised, UHT, skim, fortified and powdered milk; cream; butter

entries.heading: Pasteurised, UHT, skim, fortified and powdered milk; cream; butter (processing plants)
entries.what: products made at Tanzanian processing plants and sold through shops and supermarkets.

entries.heading: Pastilla à la crème
entries.what: A pastilla made with cream, mentioned among desserts flavoured with orange blossom and rose water.

entries.heading: Pastilla au lait
entries.what: A pastilla, a sweet pastry, prepared with milk; listed among well-known Moroccan pastries.

entries.heading: Pastillas de leche (pastillas; milk pills)
entries.what: A soft, hard or toasted milk candy made from milk, refined sugar and calamansi juice. Originated in San Miguel, Bulacan; later spread to Cagayan and Masbate. Flavoured variants include peanut, pili, ube, mango, macapuno and durian; filled v

entries.heading: Pastizzi tal-irkotta and qassatat (ricotta-filled pastries)
entries.what: Flaky pastry filled with irkotta (Maltese ricotta), a traditional savoury snack. Pastizzi and qassatat are sold in bakeries and shops. Included here because the milk filling is a main ingredient, not only a garnish; the cheese itself is not

entries.heading: Pastore Misto
entries.what: One of 16 lesser-known Sardinian cheeses, made by Caseificio Monte Accas (Siliqua).

entries.heading: Pastorella del Cerreto di Sorano
entries.what: pastoral cheese from Cerreto di Sorano, made from mixed cow and sheep milk.

entries.heading: Pastoret yoghurt (iogurt Pastoret; yogur Pastoret)
entries.what: Yoghurts from a dairy in La Segarra, Lleida (Catalonia), sold in natural cow's milk and goat's milk versions.

entries.heading: Pastöriserad bröstmjölk (donated human milk)
entries.what: Breast milk donated to a milk bank; the Swedish article says mothers who do not make enough milk of their own may buy it pasteurised.

entries.heading: Pategrás
entries.what: the most popular Argentine semi-hard cheese; the Spanish article also treats Mar del Plata as a related name.

entries.heading: Pathein halawa (Burmese sticky sweetmeat)
entries.what: a sticky sweetmeat from Pathein made with glutinous rice, butter and coconut milk.

entries.heading: Pâtichon de Châtillon
entries.what: a Centre-Val de Loire cheese.

entries.heading: Pavé corrézien (Pommerol brand, Duroux family dairy)
entries.what: A block-shaped Corrèze cheese about 30 cm long, looking like Cantal but whiter and milkier; sold under the Pommerol name, after the Limousin village where the company began in 1936.

entries.heading: Pavé d'Affinois (Fromage d'Affinois)
entries.what: brand of a 2 kg hexagonal wheel, cut into six portions; registered trademark.

entries.heading: Pavé de Roubaix (fromage)
entries.what: A rectangular loaf-shaped cheese traditionally made in Roubaix since the early 20th century, in two versions: demi-vieux and extra-vieux.

entries.heading: Pavé du Gois
entries.what: Named in the list of French cheeses with origin Loire-Atlantique, Pays de la Loire.

entries.heading: Payesh / khir / firni (পায়েস; milk rice pudding)
entries.what: a milk rice pudding; Kolkata versions vary by grain and add-ins (dates, figs, berries).

entries.heading: Payoyo (queso payoyo)
entries.what: Mixed-milk cheese from the Grazalema area of Cádiz (Sierra de Cádiz), Andalusia.

entries.heading: Paznauner Almkäse
entries.what: Alpine cheese from the Paznaun valley in Tyrol.

entries.heading: Peak evaporated milk (FrieslandCampina WAMCO)
entries.what: Nigeria's leading evaporated milk, sold in sachets and small cans; Peak also has powdered and fattening (unskimmed) variants. Market leader in the category.

entries.heading: Peanut ice cream roll (花生捲冰淇淋)
entries.what: A thin, wheat-based wrapper rolled around ice cream scoops, shaved peanut brittle and fresh cilantro, folded like a burrito (the "ice cream burrito" name in Western media). Also made with pineapple or taro fillings.

entries.heading: Pecorino a crosta fiorita (Pecorino buccia di rospo)
entries.what: sheep pecorino with a flowering (bloomy) rind; "buccia di rospo" is its local name.

entries.heading: Pecorino a latte crudo abbucciato
entries.what: raw-milk sheep pecorino, "abbucciato" variety (meaning not confirmed by any source).

name: Pecorino a latte crudo della montagna pistoiese

entries.heading: Pecorino a latte crudo della montagna pistoiese (Pecorino di Pistoia)
entries.what: raw-milk sheep pecorino from the mountains of the Pistoia province.

name: Pecorino a latte crudo della Provincia di Siena

entries.heading: Pecorino a latte crudo della Provincia di Siena (Pecorino senese)
entries.what: raw-milk sheep pecorino from the province of Siena.

entries.heading: Pecorino ai bronzi (PAT)
entries.what: Sheep pecorino from the Bronzi area.

entries.heading: Pecorino alle erbe aromatiche (Pecorino fresco verde)
entries.what: fresh sheep pecorino flavoured with herbs ("verde").

entries.heading: Pecorino bagnolese
entries.what: a hard sheep cheese from the Laceno plateau in Irpinia, made from the Bagnolese breed; grated when very mature.

entries.heading: Pecorino crotonese (Pecorino Crotonese; DOP)
entries.what: Sheep's milk cheese from the province of Crotone, Calabria, used as an appetiser, grated over first courses and in cooking.

entries.heading: Pecorino d'Abruzzo
entries.what: the regional sheep's-milk pecorino of Abruzzo, named on the Abruzzo cuisine page and linked to local variants (Atri, Farindola, marcetto).

entries.heading: Pecorino d'Abruzzo / Pecorino di Farindola
entries.what: a pecorino from Abruzzo; Farindola version.

entries.heading: Pecorino dei Monti della Laga (PAT)
entries.what: Sheep pecorino from the Monti della Laga.

entries.heading: Pecorino dei Sibillini
entries.what: A named sheep cheese from the Monti Sibillini area, listed in the regional product list alongside the Slow Food presidia. Presumably the same family as the Marche pecorino above, but the sources I opened give only the name.

entries.heading: Pecorino del Casentino
entries.what: sheep pecorino from the Casentino.

entries.heading: Pecorino del Matese
entries.what: A pecorino of the Matese massif (Molise/Campania border area) listed in the national table of traditional products.

entries.heading: Pecorino del Monte Poro (Pecorino del Monte Poro; DOP)
entries.what: DOP sheep's cheese from the province of Vibo Valentia, Calabria, from semi-free-range flocks on Monte Poro.

name: Pecorino del Parco di Migliarino-San Rossore

entries.heading: Pecorino del Parco di Migliarino-San Rossore
entries.what: sheep pecorino named for the Migliarino-San Rossore park.

entries.heading: Pecorino del Pollino (Pecorino del Pollino)
entries.what: Sheep's milk cheese from the Calabrian highlands of the Pollino area.

name: Pecorino della Garfagnana e delle Colline Lucchesi

entries.heading: Pecorino della Garfagnana e delle Colline Lucchesi (Pecorino baccellone)
entries.what: pecorino from Garfagnana and the Lucca hills; baccellone is the local name.

entries.heading: Pecorino della Locride (Pecorino della Locride)
entries.what: Sheep's milk pecorino from the Locride area of Calabria.

entries.heading: Pecorino della Lunigiana
entries.what: sheep pecorino from Lunigiana.

entries.heading: Pecorino della Sabina (semplice e alle erbe) (PAT)
entries.what: Sheep pecorino from Sabina.

entries.heading: Pecorino della vallata "Stilaro Allaro" (Pecorino dello Stilaro-Allaro)
entries.what: Sheep's milk pecorino from the Stilaro–Allaro valley, listed for Calabria.

entries.heading: Pecorino delle Balze Volterrane (DOP)
entries.what: DOP sheep pecorino listed for Tuscany.

entries.heading: Pecorino delle cantine di Roccalbegna
entries.what: sheep pecorino aged in the cellars (cantine) of Roccalbegna.

entries.heading: Pecorino delle colline senesi
entries.what: sheep pecorino from the Siena hills.

entries.heading: Pecorino di Atri (pecorino di Atri; pecorino marcetto as a rare variant)
entries.what: a traditional sheep's cheese from the Atri area, on the border of the Teramo and Pescara provinces. Production today is almost entirely home-based.

entries.heading: Pecorino di Capracotta
entries.what: A pecorino from Capracotta (IS) listed in the national table of traditional products.

entries.heading: Pecorino di Farindola (pecorino di Farindola; Caseus Vestinus in ancient sources)
entries.what: a sheep's-milk cheese from the town of Farindola on the eastern side of the Gran Sasso massif, also made in small amounts in nearby towns in the Pescara and Teramo provinces.

entries.heading: Pecorino di Ferentino (PAT)
entries.what: Sheep pecorino from Ferentino (Frosinone).

entries.heading: Pecorino di Fossa del Greppo (Il Fossa del Greppo, pecorino di fossa)
entries.what: sheep pecorino from the Greppo pits, listed as a traditional product (PAT) in Tuscany.

entries.heading: Pecorino di Garfagnina
entries.what: a Tuscan pecorino from the Garfagnana valley.

entries.heading: Pecorino di malga (Liguria)
entries.what: a sheep's-milk cheese from Ligurian mountain pastures, listed in the regional table.

entries.heading: Pecorino di Moliterno / Pecorino lucano
entries.what: pecorino from Basilicata.

entries.heading: Pecorino di Norcia del pastore (Pecorino di Norcia del pastore)
entries.what: A cylindrical cheese, 8–14 cm high and 15–24 cm across, with a yellow rind that darkens with age and a white to straw-yellow paste. Piquant, mellowing with age.

entries.heading: Pecorino di Picinisco (Pecorino di Picinisco DOP)
entries.what: A DOP sheep cheese from the Valle di Comino, Frosinone province, Lazio.

name: Pecorino di Pienza stagionato in barriques

entries.heading: Pecorino di Pienza stagionato in barriques (PAT)
entries.what: small hard sheep cheese from the Siena area, aged in oak barriques (wine barrels).

entries.heading: Pecorino di Romagna
entries.what: pecorino from Emilia-Romagna.

entries.heading: Pecorino foggiano
entries.what: a pecorino from the Province of Foggia, Apulia.

entries.heading: Pecorino fresco di malga
entries.what: A sheep's-milk cheese from the alpine pastures of the Asiago plateau (Vicenza province). It is a PAT product of Veneto.

entries.heading: Pecorino in botte (cask-aged pecorino)
entries.what: A pecorino aged in a wooden cask, listed as a traditional product.

entries.heading: Pecorino in grotta del viterbese (PAT)
entries.what: Sheep pecorino aged in caves in the Viterbo area.

entries.heading: Pecorino leccese / Pecorino brindisino
entries.what: pecorini from the provinces of Lecce and Brindisi, Apulia.

entries.heading: Pecorino misto (Pecorino misto)
entries.what: A pecorino made from mixed sheep and goat milk, listed for Calabria.

entries.heading: Pecorino primo sale (Pecorino primo sale)
entries.what: Young, lightly salted sheep's milk pecorino listed for Calabria.

entries.heading: Pecorino rosso (picurinu russu)
entries.what: a Sicilian sheep's-milk cheese with a red rind from tomato sauce and olive oil.

name: Pecorino stagionato in foglie di noce

entries.heading: Pecorino stagionato in foglie di noce (PAT)
entries.what: sheep cheese from Montefollonico, aged with walnut leaves.

entries.heading: Pecorino veneto / Pecorino dei Berici
entries.what: pecorini from Veneto.

entries.heading: Peda / pedha (पेड़ा)
entries.what: Sweet made from khoa, sugar and flavourings, usually cardamom.

entries.heading: Peguial
entries.what: named in the Cantabrian cheese history of Rodrigo de Reinosa as a product distinct from requesón.

entries.heading: Péi crème fraîche (Cilam)
entries.what: crème fraîche made from Réunion milk; Cilam supplied it to the Miel Vert fair.

entries.heading: Péi milk (lait péi; local fresh cow milk)
entries.what: fresh milk produced on Réunion's Hauts farms and sold locally under the name "péi" (local).

entries.heading: Péi-milk ice cream (L'Île en Glace)
entries.what: ice cream made with milk from Hauts breeders. Vanilla flavour in 2022; in 2023 a version with honey from Coopémiel de Bourbon.

entries.heading: Pendidam (pendidam; nyalloundé and wourwandé are its curd and whipped-curd stages; Fulfulde/Far North local usage, names as the source gives them)
entries.what: A traditional skimmed fermented milk of the Far North Region of Cameroon (Maroua, Mora, Kaélé, Mokolo). Commonly sold in periodic markets; the price in the 2026 study was about US$0.40–1.00, higher in towns than in rural areas.

entries.heading: Pendir / peinir (Turkmen peýnir; Ru "сыр")
entries.what: a Turkmen cheese name given as peinir / pendir in tourism writing. Advantour says it is made from goat and sheep milk.

entries.heading: Penteleu (brânză Penteleu; cașcavalul Penteleu)
entries.what: A Romanian cheese originating in the Buzău Mountains (Munții Buzăului), also sold as a brand.

entries.heading: Pepper Jack
entries.what: A version of Monterey Jack flavoured with chili peppers.

entries.heading: Peppermint crisp tart
entries.what: A fridge tart made with fresh cream and Peppermint Crisp chocolate.

entries.heading: Perchorotyri Pontiako (Περχαροτύρι ποντιακό)
entries.what: Pontic cheese; no details.

entries.heading: Perfect Italiano (cheese)
entries.what: A cheese brand listed under New Zealand and Australia in the Fonterra article.

entries.heading: Persillé des Aravis
entries.what: crumbly blue goat cheese of the Aravis valley, Haute-Savoie.

entries.heading: Pétafine
entries.what: strong cheese from the Dauphiné (Drôme and Isère); recipe said to come from the Voiron area (Chartreuse).

entries.heading: Petit Billy
entries.what: an industrial brand of goat cheeses from the Triballat Noyal plant (Groupe Olga). The page calls it one of the few goat cheeses made in Brittany.

entries.heading: Petit Caciocavallo (NEEDS)
entries.what: A small gourd-shaped caciocavallo from Cheese Workshop NEEDS, Hokkaido.

entries.heading: Petit chèvre fermier d'Île-de-France (Petit chèvre fermier d'Île-de-France)
entries.what: a small farm goat cheese of Île-de-France.

entries.heading: Petroto (Πετρωτό)
entries.what: Named in the Greek Macedonian cuisine article as a cheese of Chalkidiki (Πετρωτό Χαλκιδικής).

entries.heading: Petroto Tinou (Πετρωτό, Πετρωτή, Πέτρωμα Τήνου)
entries.what: Tinos cheese; no details.

entries.heading: Phaluda / hpaluda (Myanmar falooda)
entries.what: rose syrup with milk, basil seeds, vermicelli or noodle, jelly and egg custard, served with ice cream.

entries.heading: Piacentinu Ennese (piacentino ennese)
entries.what: a DOP sheep's-milk cheese made with saffron and whole black peppercorns; cylindrical, 3.5–4.5 kg, about 20–21 cm across.

entries.heading: Picón de Cantabria (Quesucos de Liébana; Torta de Potes; Queso de Áliva; Queso de Brez)
entries.what: Cantabrian cheeses from Liébana and nearby valleys (Quesucos, Torta de Potes, Áliva, Brez).

entries.heading: Pied-de-Vent (Magdalen Islands, Quebec)
entries.what: A soft raw cow's-milk cheese from the Magdalen Islands; the name is a French-Canadian phrase for sunlight breaking through clouds.

entries.heading: Piena kokteiļi (milk shakes)
entries.what: Milk-based drinks.

entries.heading: Piimä (piimä; asidofiluspiimä, rasvaton piimä, vähälaktoosinen piimä)
entries.what: A sour milk drink, thicker than milk. Finnish Wikipedia names two regional cultures: a western "long piimä" culture and an eastern "kokkelipiimä" culture. Variants named in the same article: fat-free piimä, asidofilus piimä and lactose-redu

entries.heading: Pikauba (Saguenay–Lac-Saint-Jean, Quebec; Pikauba (cheese))
entries.what: A handmade cow's-milk cheese from the Saguenay–Lac-Saint-Jean region, named after the Pikauba River.

entries.heading: Pilkul (ピルクル)
entries.what: A lactic acid bacteria drink made by Nissin York (日清ヨーク), containing Lactobacillus paracasei NY1301, a FOSHU (Foods for Specified Health Uses) product.

entries.heading: Piltinis / sampilinis (Lenten preserved soured milk)
entries.what: a traditional way of keeping sour milk through the winter, made during Lent.

entries.heading: Pimento cheese (Palmetto Cheese brand as an example)
entries.what: A snack spread for crackers or sandwiches.

entries.heading: Pinconning cheese
entries.what: An aged Colby, sharpness from medium mild to super sharp (10+ years); also sold as curds.

entries.heading: Pirotski kačkavalj
entries.what: a kačkavalj from the Pirot area; the wheel is crumbly when mature, with a slight piquancy

entries.heading: Pischedda
entries.what: Listed among Sardinian cheeses.

entries.heading: Pishirilgan sut (baked milk; cooked milk)
entries.what: Milk that is heated for a long time, giving a yellowish colour and longer keeping than raw milk. Used to make red qatiq and in confectionery.

entries.heading: Pithiviers au foin (Bondaroy au foin)
entries.what: a disc about 12 cm across and 2.5 cm thick, aged on hay for 3–5 weeks, which gives a slightly fruity flavour.

entries.heading: Piton des Neiges (Le Piton des Neiges; Le Coeur des hauts Piton des Neiges)
entries.what: A hard-paste cheese named after the island's highest peak. The producer sells a 240 g "Le Coeur des hauts Piton des Neiges", described as a 100% Péi pressed-paste cheese with cream and ripening cultures.

entries.heading: Piton des Neiges farm yoghurt (natural, cane-sugar and vanilla)
entries.what: a yoghurt range made from Réunion milk, with a natural farm yoghurt, a natural farm yoghurt sweetened with cane sugar, and a vanilla farm yoghurt flavoured with Bourbon vanilla.

entries.heading: Piton des Neiges mixed-fruit yoghurts (Green mix, Red mix)
entries.what: twelve-pot packs of fruit-flavoured yoghurts, described as "sublimated by the delight of fresh milk".

entries.heading: Piton Maïdo (fromage local; the producer's name, Fromages de La Réunion, uses this name)
entries.what: Hard-paste cheese made in La Réunion, named after the Maïdo summit; sold by the producer as one of its best-selling hard cheeses.

entries.heading: Pivní sýr (beer cheese)
entries.what: German-origin soft cheese, introduced to Czech in 1924, now common in Czech cuisine; eaten with beer, not made with beer.

entries.heading: Piye wresha / pai halwa (festival milk dessert)
entries.what: a festival dessert.

entries.heading: Plain milk (牛乳, gyūnyū) and LL/UHT milk
entries.what: Raw milk only, unadjusted, with fat at least 3.0% and non-fat solids at least 8.0%. Most Japanese market milk is UHT (ultra-high temperature) for long shelf life; LL (long-life) milk is aseptically packed and keeps about 3 months unopened.

entries.heading: Planalto de Bolona cheese (local name not confirmed; Portuguese "queijo" assumed, not sourced)
entries.what: a traditional cheese from the Planalto de Bolona, on the Cape Verde Islands, produced in what the authors call uncommon environmental conditions. The study sampled milk, curd and cheese across the making period and looked at its microbes: l

entries.heading: Plant-clotted milk (curd)
entries.what: fresh goat or sheep milk clotted with plant material. The wild-plant paper describes two traditional clotting plants.

entries.heading: Plantanillas
entries.what: Carabao-milk pastillas wrapped in egg-yolk crepes.

entries.heading: Plasmon (milk powder with albumin; infant food brand)
entries.what: milk powder with albumin for infants, sold by the Italian Plasmon company, founded in Milan in 1902 as the Italian Plasmon Syndicate by Cesare Scotti; the brand also makes biscuits and other foods.

entries.heading: Pletiu (Casa Raubert mature cheese)
entries.what: One of the three mature cheeses from Casa Raubert, named with Orri and Conlloc.

entries.heading: Pljevaljski sir (Пљеваљски сир; Pljevlja cheese)
entries.what: Soft, brined white cheese from northern Montenegro, Pljevlja municipality; protected production area with a national intangible-heritage listing.

entries.heading: Plombir (пломбір; Soviet-era milk ice cream)
entries.what: The main Ukrainian milk-based ice cream type, traditional plombir ("cream ice cream in cups") and plombir with fruit or chocolate. Kyiv production linked to Bernard Semadeni (sold until 1925).

entries.heading: Podliveni (podliveni sir)
entries.what: a traditional Serbian soft fresh cheese, made by hand in rural households, sometimes flavoured with peppers and parsley

entries.heading: Pogradeci (goat cheese, named origin)
entries.what: one of the named traditional goat-cheese origins sampled for hygiene.

entries.heading: Poivre d'âne (Pèbre d'aï; poivre d'ane)
entries.what: a soft cheese from the Mont Ventoux area, named after the savory (Satureja montana) that coats it.

entries.heading: Pollo en crema
entries.what: chicken in a cream-based sauce, listed among Guatemalan main dishes.

entries.heading: Polooštiepok (polooštiepok; Slovak)
entries.what: one of three Slovak retail cheeses (with eidam and parenica) analysed for chemical elements in a 2026 Foods paper; samples came from two producers.

entries.heading: Poltrdi sir brez konzervansov (poltrdi siri Zelene doline)
entries.what: Semi-hard cheese made without preservatives.

entries.heading: Pomazánkové máslo (spreadable butter)
entries.what: A Czech butter-like spread developed in the 1970s; stays spreadable from the fridge with lower energy.

entries.heading: Pommern (Pommern; ÅCA dairy product)
entries.what: An ÅCA cheese described as award-winning.

entries.heading: Ponche (punch; grogue with condensed milk)
entries.what: A variation of grogue (sugarcane spirit) sweetened with condensed milk or sugarcane molasses, per the cuisine article.

name: Ponche a la romana and pineapple ice cream

entries.heading: Ponche a la romana and pineapple ice cream (ice-cream drinks)
entries.what: Ponche a la romana is champagne with pineapple ice cream, typically served on New Year's Eve. Terremoto (vino pipeño with pineapple ice cream) is also served with ice cream.

entries.heading: Ponche de crème (rum and milk punch)
entries.what: a rum-based creamy punch, served at rum shops and at Christmas; the TT version of ponche crema, which originated in Venezuela.

entries.heading: Ponche de huevo (Dominican breakfast eggnog)
entries.what: A warm breakfast drink of evaporated milk, egg yolk, coffee and nutmeg, eaten on cool mornings and at holidays.

entries.heading: Ponche de malta (malta drink with condensed milk)
entries.what: A malt drink in which condensed milk is one of the ingredients; the Puerto Rican cuisine article mentions it.

entries.heading: Ponche Kuba (cream liqueur, alcoholic milk-style drink)
entries.what: A thick, creamy, tan-coloured cream liqueur named in the Antiguan cuisine article as a drink.

entries.heading: Pongal (sweet, sakkarai pongal)
entries.what: Boiled rice cooked with milk and jaggery; served as an offering after the pot boils over.

entries.heading: Poronmaito (reindeer milk)
entries.what: Milk from reindeer. Pasteurised Finnish reindeer milk is a permitted raw milk for pohjalainen leipäjuusto and Kainuun juustoleipä (see the cheese file).

entries.heading: Port wine cheese
entries.what: A cheese spread heavily dosed with port wine.

entries.heading: Porta salud
entries.what: An aged strong-flavoured Mexican cheese.

entries.heading: Poshekhonsky cheese (Пошехонский сыр)
entries.what: Russian hard cheese named after the Poshekhonye cheese-making plant (Poshekhonsky District, Yaroslavl Oblast); developed by P. A. Avdienko and R. E. Gerlakh, technology approved at VNIIMS Uglich; production from the 1960s.

entries.heading: Posset
entries.what: English milk curdled with wine or ale, a medieval and early-modern hot remedy; later a cold, set cream and lemon dessert similar to syllabub.

entries.heading: Postre de colegial (Amazon school-day dessert)
entries.what: An Amazon dessert listed in La República's Amazon dessert selection; it includes one cup of milk.

entries.heading: Pouding chômeur ("poor man's pudding")
entries.what: a Quebec dessert of cake batter over a hot syrup of maple, brown or white sugar; the cake rises through the syrup and forms a layer.

entries.heading: Pouligny-Saint-Pierre (Pouligny-Saint-Pierre)
entries.what: a truncated square pyramid of about 250 g (a 150 g size also exists), sold with white-rind or blue-rind styles.

entries.heading: Powdered milk for school feeding (World Food Programme)
entries.what: powdered milk supplied to schools in the most food-insecure regions of Honduras by the World Food Programme, in a small programme alongside the national school meals.

name: Powdered milk reconstituted into liquid milk

entries.heading: Powdered milk reconstituted into liquid milk (melkepulver, industrial liquefaction; Norwegian "melkepulver")
entries.what: Fresh-style milk made by mixing imported milk powder with water in an industrial plant, because local herds are not kept. Svalbard has no sustained dairy supply of its own.

entries.heading: Power Shake (protein milk drink)
entries.what: A milk-based protein drink, 20 g protein per 250 ml pack, mild strawberry taste. Made in partnership with the Faroese Island Games 2027. Per 100 g: 8.0 g protein, 0.5 g fat.

entries.heading: Prästost (Präst)
entries.what: Old Swedish hard cheese, first recorded as a tithe paid to the priest (präst), from the 16th century.

entries.heading: Pratolina
entries.what: named goat cheese from Tuscany.

entries.heading: Prekmurska gibanica (Prekmurje gibanica; layered pastry)
entries.what: Layered pastry from Prekmurje; one of four fillings is curd (skuta or quark), alongside poppy seed, walnut and apple.

entries.heading: Prentza (Πρέντζα Κεφαλονιάς)
entries.what: a creamy cheese associated with Kefalonia.

entries.heading: Prentza Kefalonias (Πρέντζα Κεφαλονιάς)
entries.what: Cephalonia cheese; no details.

entries.heading: Přepuštěné máslo (clarified butter / ghí)
entries.what: Clarified butter of nearly pure milk fat; the Czech name covers ghí.

entries.heading: Prescinsêua (Prescinseua, Quagliata ligure; Genoa, Savona, La Spezia)
entries.what: a traditional soft cheese of Liguria, used in pansoti, torta pasqualina, barbagiuai and the Recco focaccia. (The Recco consortium discourages its use in focaccia, and stracchino is now often used instead.)

entries.heading: Pressato a mano (PAT)
entries.what: A sheep cheese pressed by hand.

entries.heading: Prga (prga; Prgica)
entries.what: a cheese from Podravina (northern Croatia)

entries.heading: Pría (Queso de Pría; Ahumado de Pría)
entries.what: cheese made in the village of Pría, Llanes council; the smoked version, "Ahumado de Pría", is the more famous of the two styles.

entries.heading: Prim (pålegg; "prim")
entries.what: a softer, spreadable brunost-type product. Most prim is made by TINE Meierier on Jæren.

entries.heading: Primina and Schärdinger Sommerbutter (butter brands)
entries.what: Primina was a premium butter brand of the dairy Schärdinger, introduced in the early 1970s; Schärdinger Sommerbutter was made at the Taufkirchen an der Pram plant, which the article calls the second-largest butter plant in Austria

entries.heading: Primo sale di latte ovino (PAT)
entries.what: A young sheep cheese.

entries.heading: Primosale (and tuma, the fresh pecorino curd)
entries.what: a stage of pecorino ripening, and a typical Sicilian pecorino; unsalted fresh curd is tuma; salted right away it becomes primosale after about a month.

entries.heading: Prljo (Прљо; also torotan, tucanik, chukani sir)
entries.what: Lean hard cheese from the Piva River area of Montenegro, also made in other Dinaric mountain areas; traditional product of Montenegrin cuisine.

entries.heading: Processed cheese, Arla (Manama plant)
entries.what: processed cheese made at Arla Foods' plant in Manama, Bahrain, sold under the Puck, Arla, Dano and Kraft brands and private labels.

entries.heading: Processed dairy products (imported, general)
entries.what: The trade paper names "processed dairy products" and "high fat processed dairy products" among imports to Vanuatu since trade liberalisation.

entries.heading: Processed milk (加工乳, kakō nyū)
entries.what: Milk made from raw milk with added dairy products (skim powder, cream or butter), sold cheaper. Labelled 加工乳 and often shown simply as "ミルク". Includes low-fat and rich "特濃牛乳" types.

entries.heading: Processed white block cheese (Happy Cow-type; "processed white American cheese" in recipes)
entries.what: A mild, soft processed block cheese used as the base of the everyday Belizean cheese dip, and in the country's shops as one of the staple cheeses. The Belizean recipe names the brand Happy Cow, which the author describes as imported from Au

entries.heading: Protéines de lactosérum (WPC, WPI)
entries.what: Dried whey protein concentrates (30–90% protein, WPC) and isolates (about 90%, WPI), used in sports and senior foods and industry.

entries.heading: Provel
entries.what: A gooey, buttery processed cheese for St. Louis-style pizza.

name: Provola affumicata di bufala / Provola di bufala

entries.heading: Provola affumicata di bufala / Provola di bufala
entries.what: buffalo-milk provole from Campania and Lazio.

entries.heading: Provola dei Monti Sicani
entries.what: a traditional provola from the Monti Sicani mountain area (Palermo and Agrigento provinces).

entries.heading: Provola dei Nebrodi
entries.what: a DOP provola from the Nebrodi mountains (Messina metropolitan area), shaped like a caciocavallo; formerly a PAT product.

entries.heading: Provola delle Madonie
entries.what: a pear-shaped provola from the Madonie mountains of northern Sicily; locally also called caciocavallo.

entries.heading: Provola di bufala (semplice e affumicata) (PAT)
entries.what: A buffalo provola.

entries.heading: Provola di vacca (semplice e affumicata) (PAT)
entries.what: A cow's-milk provola.

name: Provola e caciotta a pasta filata

entries.heading: Provola e caciotta a pasta filata (Trentino)
entries.what: Provola and caciotta made by stretching the curd, Province of Trento. PAT.

entries.heading: Provola siciliana
entries.what: one of Sicily's oldest cheeses, similar to caciocavallo but smaller, with a shorter salting and ripening period.

entries.heading: Provola silana
entries.what: a Calabrian stretched-curd cheese.

entries.heading: Provoleta
entries.what: an Argentine variant of provolone, a small disc that is grilled and served at the start of an asado.

name: Provolone invecchiato di bufala di Formello

entries.heading: Provolone invecchiato di bufala di Formello (PAT)
entries.what: An aged buffalo provolone from Formello (Roma).

entries.heading: Provolone Sardo
entries.what: A cow's-milk provolone-style cheese listed among Sardinian cheeses.

entries.heading: Provolone sardo / Provolone siciliano
entries.what: provolone-type cheeses from Sardinia and Sicily.

entries.heading: Provolone vaccino (PAT)
entries.what: A cow's-milk provolone.

entries.heading: Ptashyne moloko (пташине молоко; "bird's milk")
entries.what: Post-Soviet confection, a chocolate-covered soft marshmallow-like sweet. In Ukraine it is called ptashyne moloko (culinary article in Ukrainian Wikipedia).

entries.heading: Ptasie mleczko (milk-foam confection)
entries.what: A chocolate-coated confection filled with a mild, milk-flavoured foam, originally vanilla.

entries.heading: Pudding (dairy dessert)
entries.what: A usually sweet dessert made with milk or thickened with a starch product (such as maizena), with eggs, custard, custard powder or gelatine as optional setting agents. Usually made in a pudding mould.

entries.heading: Pudim de leite / pudim flan
entries.what: Custard of milk, eggs and sugar with caramel, served inverted.

entries.heading: Pudim de leite condensado
entries.what: Brazilian milk pudding made with condensed milk, called pudim de leite; a home dessert.

entries.heading: Pudín de pan (pudín de pan)
entries.what: Cuban bread pudding, usually served with guava marmalade.

entries.heading: Pudink (layered custard)
entries.what: Multi-flavoured layered custard served in glasses or moulds.

entries.heading: Pule (Pule / magareći sir / sir pule)
entries.what: a rare, very expensive Serbian cheese made from mostly donkey milk. The page calls it the most expensive cheese in the world (about US$1,300/kg).

entries.heading: Puleva (Puleva)
entries.what: A dairy brand whose range the article describes as very diversified, with milk, milkshakes, cheeses and infant cereals (papillas) as examples.

entries.heading: Pultost (pultost; "soft sour-milk cheese")
entries.what: a traditional Norwegian sour-milk cheese flavoured with caraway seeds.

name: Pur Brebis de l'Abbaye de Belloc

entries.heading: Pur Brebis de l'Abbaye de Belloc
entries.what: A sheep cheese from the Abbaye de Belloc, Pyrénées-Atlantiques.

entries.heading: Purchased dairy products (general)
entries.what: Dairy eaten in Timor-Leste is largely bought rather than made at home, because the local ruminants are not customarily milked.

entries.heading: Pustertaler Bergkäse (Formaggio di montagna della Val Pusteria)
entries.what: A sweet, aromatic cheese with a hint of walnut; suited to red wine and winter dishes such as polenta.

entries.heading: Puzzone di Moena (Spretz tzaorì; Puzzone di Moena)
entries.what: A DOP cheese with a reddish-brown, oily rind and a robust, slightly spicy flavour with a mild bitter aftertaste; strong, pungent smell. About 10 kg, cylindrical, about 35 cm across.

entries.heading: Pyongyang pizza restaurant imported cheese (unnamed)
entries.what: Imported cheese, flown in from Italy, used in pizza in a Pyongyang restaurant (Pizza Restaurant, Kwangbok Street, also called Italian Restaurant), reported around 2009. Not a North Korean product.

entries.heading: Pyramide
entries.what: a Centre-Val de Loire pyramid cheese.

entries.heading: Pyramide cendrée
entries.what: An ash-coated pyramid cheese of Poitou and Charentes.

entries.heading: Qapchi (habas con leche)
entries.what: A dish from Ayacucho, Apurímac and Cusco of broad beans and potatoes mixed with milk, seasoned with huacatay, onion and ají.

entries.heading: Qara qumiz (қара құмыз; "black koumiss")
entries.what: The clear liquid that separates from airag after it is churned and left to settle; historically favoured by rulers.

entries.heading: Qara-qurut (black whey dried)
entries.what: A dark, dried product made by boiling the liquid drained from doogh or kashk, then drying the curd that forms.

entries.heading: Qatayef (قطايف)
entries.what: a sweet, stuffed dumpling eaten during Ramadan, filled with cream (qishta) and pistachios

entries.heading: Qatiq (qatiq; Latin "qatiq", Cyrillic not shown in source)
entries.what: A thick fermented milk, more solid than ayran, from the Turkic countries and Bulgaria. Its base for several other products (suzma, ayron, sariyog, chalop).

entries.heading: Qatyq (қатық)
entries.what: Thickened, soured milk, drunk or used as a base for curds.

entries.heading: Qatyq / qatiq (қатық)
entries.what: A more solid yoghurt than ayran, from Turkic countries and Bulgaria; in Kazakh cuisine it is strained, thickened sour milk (also called buttermilk in the beverage section).

entries.heading: Qaymaq (cream / clotted cream)
entries.what: milk fat layer used as food and as butter fat; colloquially "üz". Industrial cream exists in ~20% and ~35% fat.

entries.heading: Qimaq (Muslim-influenced preserved cream, from Yinshan zhengyao)
entries.what: Dairy preserved by lactic-acid fermentation, recorded in the Yinshan zhengyao (a Chinese text, 1456 Ming manuscript) under Muslim influences in Mongolian cuisine.

entries.heading: Qishta / eshta (قشطة / إشطة; kishta, kashta, ashta)
entries.what: Thick cream set on the surface of heated milk, eaten as a dessert and used in other dishes; sometimes flavoured with orange blossom water. Highly perishable (a few days even refrigerated).

entries.heading: Qoryqtyq (қорықтық)
entries.what: Thickened milk made on the steppe as herdsmen's food.

entries.heading: Quarkkäulchen (quark fritters; Quarkkeulchen)
entries.what: flat fried patties of quark dough, from Saxony (called Quarkkließle in the Vogtland).

entries.heading: Qudam (Kashmir, Gujjar tribes)
entries.what: Cheese of the Gujjar tribes of Kashmir, named in the List of cheeses India section.

entries.heading: Queijada de requeijão de Beja
entries.what: A small pastry tart with a filling of requeijão, a traditional Easter sweet from Beja, with a crisp, lightly salted shell and a creamy, sweet filling.

entries.heading: Queijo Alpino (Alpino de Corumbá de Goiás)
entries.what: Swiss-style cheese made in Corumbá de Goiás, Goiás.

entries.heading: Queijo amarelo da Beira Baixa
entries.what: A yellow PDO cheese from the Beira Baixa region.

entries.heading: Queijo Araxá (Minas Araxá)
entries.what: a cylindrical cheese from the Araxá Plateau (9 municipalities), produced since the 18th century; less salty and milder than Canastra.

name: Queijo Azul de Ovelha; Curado de Ovelha; Extra Curado de Ovelha

entries.heading: Queijo Azul de Ovelha; Curado de Ovelha; Extra Curado de Ovelha (sheep)
entries.what: traditional southern Brazilian sheep cheeses named in the review.

entries.heading: Queijo Azul do Bosque
entries.what: a cylinder of about 200 g made in Joanópolis, São Paulo.

entries.heading: Queijo Boursin de Cabra (Rochedinho, MS)
entries.what: French-origin herb cheese made in Rochedinho, Mato Grosso do Sul; balls of about 200 g.

entries.heading: Queijo Braz Mato-grossense
entries.what: a cheese from Cuiabá, Mato Grosso.

entries.heading: Queijo Cabra da Serra; Aroeira (goat, Northeast)
entries.what: named in the review among goat cheeses from the Northeast that have won awards.

entries.heading: Queijo Campo das Vertentes (Minas Campo das Vertentes)
entries.what: a Minas artesanal cheese made since the 18th century by Portuguese immigrants in the Campo das Vertentes area (14 municipalities).

entries.heading: Queijo Castelões
entries.what: A cheese listed in the Portugal section.

entries.heading: Queijo Coalho (queijo de coalho; "curd cheese")
entries.what: the most typical artisanal cheese of Brazil's Northeast, produced on hinterland farms since the colonial period, now also industrial and sold in almost all states.

entries.heading: Queijo Cobocó
entries.what: named as the only surviving example of the original cylindrical "plate" shape of Queijo Prato.

entries.heading: Queijo Colonial (Queijo de Colônia / Colonial; Witmarsum colony)
entries.what: a cheese made by hand on farms of German and Italian settler families ("colonos") in southern Brazil, named after the colonial farming system rather than the Portuguese colonial period.

entries.heading: Queijo Coração em Brasa (Joanópolis, SP)
entries.what: ripened 20–30 days under vegetable charcoal; filled with a layer of smoked chipotle, habanero and cayenne pepper.

entries.heading: Queijo curado de ovelha
entries.what: A cured sheep cheese listed in the Portugal section.

entries.heading: Queijo D'Alagoa Faixa Dourada (Alagoa, MG)
entries.what: a cylinder of about 1 kg; aromatic, pungent, persistent, slightly salty, soft consistency.

entries.heading: Queijo da Canastra (Canastra Minas artesanal)
entries.what: a cylindrical cheese from the Serra da Canastra in Minas Gerais, of Portuguese-immigrant descent; medium-strong, slightly spicy, dense and creamy.

entries.heading: Queijo da Serra da Estrela (Serra da Estrela)
entries.what: A strongly flavoured PDO sheep cheese from the Serra da Estrela mountains, made mainly from November to March.

entries.heading: Queijo de Azeitão
entries.what: A Portuguese sheep cheese named after the town of Azeitão; a well-known PDO.

entries.heading: Queijo de cabra
entries.what: A goat cheese listed in the Portugal section without a protected name.

entries.heading: Queijo de cabra transmontano
entries.what: A PDO goat cheese from Trás-os-Montes.

entries.heading: Queijo de Castelo Branco
entries.what: A whitish PDO cheese from the Castelo Branco region.

entries.heading: Queijo de Évora
entries.what: A PDO sheep cheese from Évora, yellowish, slightly acidic and mildly spicy.

entries.heading: Queijo de Idanha
entries.what: A cheese listed in the Portugal section, named after Idanha.

entries.heading: Queijo de Nisa
entries.what: A PDO sheep cheese from Nisa, Portalegre district, with a strong aroma and slightly acid taste.

entries.heading: Queijo de Santarém
entries.what: A cheese listed in the Portugal section, named after Santarém.

entries.heading: Queijo de Tomar
entries.what: A cheese listed in the Portugal section, named after Tomar.

entries.heading: Queijo do Maio (goat-milk cheese of Maio; Portuguese "queijo de leite de cabra"; "queijo do Maio")
entries.what: A goat cheese from Ribeira Dom João, on the east of the island of Maio, about 13 km from the capital Porto Inglês. Made by a cooperative, the Queijaria Dom João, whose producers say it is an old local craft that almost every household has p

entries.heading: Queijo do Marajó
entries.what: a cheese from Marajó Island in Pará, made for over 200 years; eaten plain or in dishes.

entries.heading: Queijo do Pico
entries.what: A PDO cheese from the island of Pico in the Azores, also called Queijo de São João do Pico; a fatty cheese with a yellow rind, a strong salty taste and an intense aroma.

entries.heading: Queijo do Reino (Queijo Reino)
entries.what: considered the first industrially matured cheese in Brazil; name from luxury European goods imported after 1808.

entries.heading: Queijo do Serro (Serro Minas)
entries.what: a cylindrical cheese from the Serro region of Minas Gerais, about 0.7–1.25 kg; white, fine, homogeneous paste; softer and more acidic when eaten fresh.

entries.heading: Queijo dos Envendos
entries.what: A cheese listed in the Portugal section, named after Envendos.

entries.heading: Queijo Duprado
entries.what: A cheese listed in the Portugal section.

entries.heading: Queijo Embriago d'Alagoa (Alagoa, MG)
entries.what: 40-day ripened cheese with Brevibacterium linens and white mould rind; creamy texture; washed with jaboticaba liqueur.

entries.heading: Queijo fatiado importado (sliced cheese, imported)
entries.what: sliced cheese, listed in the report as one of the most consumed dairy products in Angola. Cheese is also among the leading imports by quantity, after milk powder and fluid milk.

entries.heading: Queijo fresco
entries.what: A generic fresh cheese listed in the Portugal section.

entries.heading: Queijo Manteiga (Queijo-manteiga; Requeijão do Norte / do Sertão)
entries.what: a Northeastern semi-fat cheese typical of the sertão and Seridó region of Rio Grande do Norte and Paraíba; also called Requeijão do Norte.

entries.heading: Queijo mestiço de Tolosa
entries.what: A PGI mixed-milk cheese from the parish of Tolosa in Nisa; the name "mestiço" refers to the mixed milks.

entries.heading: Queijo Mussarela (Muçarela, Brazilian)
entries.what: the most widely eaten cheese in Brazil; Brazilian production differs from Italian technique.

entries.heading: Queijo picante (piri-piri spicy cheese; "queijo picante")
entries.what: a spicy cheese flavoured with piri-piri (chili), tested in a 2014 Portuguese-language master's study on Angolan dairy products.

entries.heading: Queijo picante da Beira Baixa (Queijo Cabreiro)
entries.what: A spicy PDO cheese from the Beira Baixa region, also called Queijo Cabreiro.

entries.heading: Queijo Prato (Queijo lanche)
entries.what: a mild, yellow cheese common in sandwiches and snacks, made across Brazil.

entries.heading: Queijo Rabaçal
entries.what: A PDO cheese listed in the Portugal section.

entries.heading: Queijo Saloio
entries.what: A cheese listed in the Portugal section and in the English list as a brand.

entries.heading: Queijo São Jorge
entries.what: A PDO cheese from the island of São Jorge in the Azores, made only from raw whole cow's milk; the protected area is the whole island.

entries.heading: Queijo Serpa
entries.what: A PDO sheep cheese from Serpa in Alentejo; on the Ark of Taste.

entries.heading: Queijo Serra do Salitre
entries.what: a creamy, mild cheese from the Serra do Salitre mountain area, formerly counted in the Cerrado.

entries.heading: Queijo Serrano (Serrano artesanal)
entries.what: a traditional cheese of the southern highlands (Campos de Lages, Santa Catarina; Campos de Cima da Serra, Rio Grande do Sul), dating from 1831 (review).

entries.heading: Queijo Terrincho (Queijo de Freixo)
entries.what: A PDO sheep cheese with a soft, slightly greasy white paste and an orange rind; also called Queijo de Freixo.

name: Queijo Tulha, Cuesta Azul, Pirâmide do Bosque, Giramundo, Simental, Tropeiro

entries.heading: Queijo Tulha, Cuesta Azul, Pirâmide do Bosque, Giramundo, Simental, Tropeiro (Southeast artisanal and industrial names)
entries.what: named in the review as typical Southeast products that also appear in industrial production; no details given.

entries.heading: Queijo Zola Mato-grossense
entries.what: a creamy, slightly spicy blue cheese from Cuiabá, Mato Grosso; aroma of mushroom and rural.

entries.heading: Quesada pasiega (quesada pasiega)
entries.what: A lightly sweet, pudding-like cake from the Valles Pasiegos, made from curdled milk, butter and sugar; served warm or cold.

entries.heading: Quesaílla (merendera)
entries.what: a cheese from the Extremadura cheese zones, also called "merendera"; named in the spain.info article, which notes a resemblance to the Portuguese quesaílla.

entries.heading: Queseo (queseo; northern Cebu)
