entries.what: A local white cheese of northern Cebu, celebrated at the Queseo Festival in Compostela, which the Carabao article mentions.

entries.heading: Quesillo, Canarian (quesillo canario)
entries.what: A flan-type dessert, firmer than traditional flan.

entries.heading: Quesito valenciano
entries.what: A preparation from Carabobo state, made from white cheese, red and green sweet peppers, onion, butter and milk; formerly used as a filling for another local dish.

entries.heading: Queso 7 cueros ("seven layers")
entries.what: A Colombian cheese built of layers called "cueros" (hides).

entries.heading: Queso ahumado (queso ahumado de Mérida)
entries.what: The "famous smoked cheese" of Mérida state, named in the Mérida section of the Gastronomía article.

entries.heading: Queso Alhama de Granada
entries.what: a cheese named after Alhama de Granada (Granada)

entries.heading: Queso andino (andino)
entries.what: A matured Andean cheese from Ayacucho and Cusco with a soft, buttery paste, pale yellowish colour and a thin, firm rind; the Andino category is a national contest category.

entries.heading: Queso añejo
entries.what: The aged version of queso fresco, sometimes coated in chili (enchilado).

entries.heading: Queso Arribes de Salamanca (Salamanca)
entries.what: a sheep cheese from the province of Salamanca, with acidic, salty and piquant taste and a long finish.

entries.heading: Queso blanco Panamá (queso blanco Panamá; queso prensado; queso molido)
entries.what: The national queso blanco defined in the Panamanian technical standard: the product obtained by separating the whey after coagulation of pasteurised national fluid milk, ready to eat soon after manufacture. The standard names two variants a

entries.heading: Queso blanquet (queso de cabra de Alicante; blanquito)
entries.what: A small white disc of goat cheese from the Montañas de Alicante, mildly sweet and lightly salted.

name: Queso blanquet; Queso de la Nucia; Queso de cazoleta; Queso de servilleta

entries.heading: Queso blanquet; Queso de la Nucia; Queso de cazoleta; Queso de servilleta
entries.what: Valencian Community cheeses; cazoleta and servilleta are named for their moulds or cloths.

entries.heading: Queso camerano (queso de los Cameros; queso de cabra de los Cameros; "queso fresco de montaña")
entries.what: A protected goat's-milk cheese from the Sierra de los Cameros in La Rioja, sold fresh or ripened. The fresh variety has a soft paste; the ripened varieties are pressed and firmer.

entries.heading: Queso Campesino (queso campesino; quesito)
entries.what: A Colombian farm-style fresh cheese (listed as "Quesito" in one name).

entries.heading: Queso cápita (layered-curd cheese)
entries.what: made by layering curds, and stretches into threads when heated, per the Spanish Wikipedia gastronomy article.

name: Queso castellano; Queso de Burgos; Queso de Villalón; Queso curado de oveja churra de Villadiego

entries.heading: Queso castellano; Queso de Burgos; Queso de Villalón; Queso curado de oveja churra de Villadiego
entries.what: Castilian cheeses. Queso de Burgos is a fresh cheese; Villadiego is a cured sheep's cheese of the Churra breed.

entries.heading: Queso Cebreiro (queso Cebreiro; Cebreiro cheese)
entries.what: A Galician cheese from the mountains of Lugo province, eaten fresh or cured.

name: Queso Cebreiro; Queso de Lanzarote etc.

entries.heading: Queso Cebreiro; Queso de Lanzarote etc. (Galicia)
entries.what: Cebreiro is a Galician PDO cheese from the Cebreiro area.

entries.heading: Queso Chistabín
entries.what: Aragonese cheese listed by name.

entries.heading: Queso chonero (queso manaba chonero)
entries.what: traditional fresh cheese from the Chone canton in Manabí province, Ecuador. Salty, soft, compact; melts and stretches easily; used in savory and sweet dishes.

entries.heading: Queso chota con finas hierbas (Chota, Cajamarca)
entries.what: A Chota cheese with fine herbs, from Lácteos Conga (Cajamarca), third place in the 2024 Innovation category.

entries.heading: Queso Chubut (Chubutense)
entries.what: a semi-hard cow's-milk cheese from the Welsh colony of the lower Chubut Valley, made today in Gaiman by the Cooperativa Lechera de Gaiman (Colega); the "Chubut" brand is described as the first registered cheese brand in Argentina.

entries.heading: Queso Colonia (Queso Colonia; Colonia)
entries.what: The best-known Uruguayan cheese, named after the Colonia department. It was introduced in 1868 by Juan Teófilo Karlen, a Swiss settler, at Nueva Helvecia, and descends from Emmental but is softer and milder.

entries.heading: Queso con orégano (San Juan de la Maguana)
entries.what: A cheese named in the Dominican food article as a local product of San Juan de la Maguana, a province in the southwest.

entries.heading: Queso corazón (heart cheese)
entries.what: A cream cheese of Chiapas traditionally moulded into a heart shape.

entries.heading: Queso costeño (queso costeño; queso blanco/fresco; queso de capa variant)
entries.what: A fresh white salted cheese from Colombia's Caribbean coast, eaten mainly at breakfast, in mote de queso, and grated into arepas, bollos, buñuelos.

entries.heading: Queso crema / doble crema (queso crema de Chiapas, queso crema de cuadro)
entries.what: A cream-style cheese with cream added, used in desserts and eaten fresh; the Chiapas version is protected.

entries.heading: Queso Crema de Chiapas
entries.what: A ripened cream cheese of Chiapas, sold plain or seasoned.

entries.heading: Queso crema tipo Filadelfia (cream cheese style)
entries.what: a cream cheese style sold on retail shelves, listed at $3.75 in the 2026 elsalvador.com article. The article says only that some products are not imported.

entries.heading: Queso cremado
entries.what: a fresh soft cheese with a slightly sour taste, per the Spanish Wikipedia gastronomy article.

entries.heading: Queso crineja (queso crineja; crineja)
entries.what: A cheese listed in Venezuela as braided ("trenzado"); the Gastronomía article names it among the fresh cheeses of the south-llanero region.

entries.heading: Queso cuñumbuquino con cecina (San Martín)
entries.what: A San Martín cheese made with cecina, the cured pork of the region, which won first place in the Innovation category at the 2024 national contest (brand De la Vaca a la Boca, Tarapoto area).

entries.heading: Queso Danbo
entries.what: a matured cheese defined in the Food Code (article 632 tris), with an industrial-use name.

entries.heading: Queso de Acehúche (Spanish)
entries.what: an artisanal raw goat's-milk cheese, very fatty, with a strong smell and slightly spicy flavour.

entries.heading: Queso de Andalucía de cabra
entries.what: a goat cheese labelled as Andalusian (regional name only)

entries.heading: Queso de año (queso de año; queso de concha negra per the es.wikipedia Queso de mano article; llanero alias in List of cheeses)
entries.what: A traditional Venezuelan cheese, typical of the Llanos and also made in Zulia. Very hard, salty and intense in flavour; it is matured, but for a shorter time than Parmesan, so it stays white.

entries.heading: Queso de Aracena
entries.what: a cheese from Aracena, in the Sierra de Aracena, Huelva

name: Queso de Babia y de Laciana

entries.heading: Queso de Babia y de Laciana (Babia y Laciana; León)
entries.what: a traditional goat cheese of the Babia and Laciana valleys in León.

entries.heading: Queso de barra
entries.what: A panela-like cheese of the Yucatán area.

entries.heading: Queso de Burgos (Burgos)
entries.what: fresh white cheese from the province of Burgos, named after the city's weekly market where farmers sold sheep's-milk cheeses; about 35,000 tonnes a year.

name: Queso de cabra de La Vera

entries.heading: Queso de cabra de La Vera (goat cheese of La Vera; Spanish)
entries.what: a goat's-milk cheese from the La Vera valley, coated in smoked paprika (pimentón de La Vera).

entries.heading: Queso de cabra payoyo (queso payoyo; cabra payoya)
entries.what: a cheese of the Sierra de Grazalema, sold under a registered trademark of a producer in Villaluenga del Rosario.

entries.heading: Queso de Cádiz
entries.what: a goat cheese labelled after the province of Cádiz

entries.heading: Queso de Campo Real (queso de Campo Real; "Gran Campo Real" as a trade name)
entries.what: Cylindrical farm cheese, about 3 kg, 22 cm across, 12 cm high, with a hard natural rind marked with a pleita (woven esparto) pattern on the sides and a flor on the flat faces. The paste is firm and compact, with small and some larger eyes,

entries.heading: Queso de capa (Mompós)
entries.what: The costeño variant from Santa Cruz de Mompox.

entries.heading: Queso de capas (layered fresh cheese, Guatemala)
entries.what: a fresh cheese named for how it is moulded: the curd goes into the mould in layers, each layer drained before the next is added. The thesis calls it widespread in the country.

entries.heading: Queso de cassoleta (cazuelita; saladito valenciano; queso de Puzol; queso de Burriana)
entries.what: A small round salted cheese with a volcano-shaped top from the mould.

entries.heading: Queso de Crema (double-cream cheese)
entries.what: a soft, fine, unctuous cheese made from whole milk and cream, defined in the Food Code (article 620).

entries.heading: Queso de El Burgo
entries.what: Aragonese cheese from El Burgo.

entries.heading: Queso de flor (Flor de Guía) / Queso palmero
entries.what: Canary Islands cheeses, Flor de Guía from Gran Canaria and Palmero from La Palma.

entries.heading: Queso de Grazalema
entries.what: a cheese of Grazalema, Cádiz

entries.heading: Queso de La Adrada (Ávila)
entries.what: a goat cheese listed on the Spanish Wikipedia cheese list for Castilla y León; La Adrada is a town in the Tiétar valley area of Ávila province.

entries.heading: Queso de La Bureba (Bureba; Burgos)
entries.what: a sheep cheese named after La Bureba, a comarca of Burgos province; listed on the Spanish Wikipedia cheese list.

entries.heading: Queso de La Calahorra
entries.what: a sheep cheese from La Calahorra, Granada

name: Queso de la Gomera; Queso de Lanzarote; Queso herreño

entries.heading: Queso de la Gomera; Queso de Lanzarote; Queso herreño
entries.what: Canary Islands cheeses from La Gomera, Lanzarote and El Hierro.

name: Queso de la Montaña de León

entries.heading: Queso de la Montaña de León (Montaña de León; León)
entries.what: a cow's-milk cheese named for the Montaña (mountain) area of León province; listed on the Spanish Wikipedia cheese list.

entries.heading: Queso de La Nucía
entries.what: A soft white truncated-cone cheese from La Nucía (Alicante), weighing about 1–2 kg.

entries.heading: Queso de La Peral
entries.what: Asturian cheese from La Peral.

entries.heading: Queso de La Serena (Spanish)
entries.what: a Merino sheep's-milk cheese from the La Serena area, spread on bread.

entries.heading: Queso de Málaga
entries.what: a goat cheese labelled after the province of Málaga

entries.heading: Queso de mano (queso de mano, "handmade cheese"; hand-made cheese)
entries.what: A flat, round, soft and elastic cheese with easily separable layers, resembling mozzarella. It is the usual filling for arepas and cachapas and is also eaten with sweet breads (golfeados, catalinas).

entries.heading: Queso de Murcia al vino (Queso de Murcia al vino DOP; other names: queso murciano al vino)
entries.what: A semi-cured goat's-milk cheese whose rind is washed with red wine. The paste is compact, ivory-white and creamy and elastic; the flavour is medium, acidic, mildly salty, with fresh dairy notes of cream, butter and goat. Often served as a t

entries.heading: Queso de Oropesa
entries.what: A cheese listed in the Castile–La Mancha section of the English list of cheeses. Oropesa is a town in Toledo province.

name: Queso de Oropesa; Queso del Tiétar; Queso de la Vera; Queso de Gata-Hurdes; Queso de la Siberia extremeña; Queso de Acehúche; Quesaílla

entries.heading: Queso de Oropesa; Queso del Tiétar; Queso de la Vera; Queso de Gata-Hurdes; Queso de la Siberia extremeña; Queso de Acehúche; Quesaílla
entries.what: Cheeses from Castile-La Mancha (Oropesa) and several Extremaduran districts.

entries.heading: Queso de Poro de Balancán
entries.what: A cheese of Balancán, Tabasco, with a protected collective trademark (2012).

entries.heading: Queso de rosca (Castilla y León)
entries.what: a sheep's-milk cheese from Castilla y León, part of the region's gastronomy; the cheeses were pierced with a stick or rope and hung in strings from the ceiling, out of reach of animals.

entries.heading: Queso de Sacramenia (Sacramenia; Segovia)
entries.what: a cheese named after Sacramenia, a village in the province of Segovia, listed under Segovia in the Gastronomía de Castilla y León article.

entries.heading: Queso de servilleta (formatge de tovalló; formatge de mocador)
entries.what: A square-to-round cheese whose curd is drained in a knotted cloth napkin, leaving a small nipple-like point on top. Mildly salty, firm, few holes, usually at most about 2 kg.

entries.heading: Queso de Sierra Morena
entries.what: a goat cheese labelled after the Sierra Morena range

entries.heading: Queso de Tafí (Tafí del Valle cheese)
entries.what: Argentina's oldest cheese, a regional artisanal cheese from Tafí del Valle, Tucumán, held to be the first Argentine dairy product with an Indicación Geográfica (IG) seal.

entries.heading: Queso de Teruel
entries.what: a cheese name for sheep and goat cheeses made by several dairies in the province of Teruel.

name: Queso de Tetilla variants and Serrat, Llenguat, Tou dels Til·lers, Tupí

entries.heading: Queso de Tetilla variants and Serrat, Llenguat, Tou dels Til·lers, Tupí (Catalonia, Pyrenees)
entries.what: Pyrenean and Pre-Pyrenean Catalan cheeses; Tupí is linked to a Wikipedia article.

entries.heading: Queso de Trasmoz
entries.what: a cured cheese made by a cooperative in Trasmoz (Zaragoza).

entries.heading: Queso de Urbiés
entries.what: Asturian cheese from Urbiés.

entries.heading: Queso de Villalón (Villalón de Campos; Valladolid)
entries.what: fresh cheese made in Villalón de Campos (Valladolid) and, by extension, Tierra de Campos; cylindrical, slightly sweet and slightly bitter; now an appetiser cheese, also used in salads and desserts, with quince paste or jam.

entries.heading: Queso de Zacapa (Spanish; "sweet cheese" from the Zacapa region, used in Zacapa bread)
entries.what: A regional cheese from the Zacapa area, used in a moist sweet bread called pan con queso dulce, which the Spanish article links to the Quesadilla de Zacapa.

entries.heading: Queso del Benasqués (El Benasqués)
entries.what: a cured cow's-milk cheese from Sahún in the Benasque valley, made by Quesos El Benasqués.

entries.heading: Queso del Cerrato (Cerrato; Palencia)
entries.what: a cheese of the Cerrato area in Palencia province, named in the intro of the Gastronomía de Castilla y León article and listed under Palencia.

entries.heading: Queso del Tiétar (Tiétar valley; Ávila, also cross-border with Cáceres)
entries.what: a goat cheese listed on the Spanish Wikipedia cheese list under Castilla y León; the Tiétar valley runs between Ávila and Cáceres (Extremadura).

entries.heading: Queso doble crema (Cundiboyacense highlands)
entries.what: A double-cream cheese from the Cundiboyacense highlands (named as from Chiquinquirá and Ubaté); the arepa ocañera recipe can also use it.

entries.heading: Queso duro blando
entries.what: a hard-style cheese with a mild, smooth, pleasantly salty taste. The English Wikipedia Quesadilla salvadoreña article calls it a strong, salty cheese linked to queso blanco, and says it may be swapped for Parmesan.

entries.heading: Queso duro viejo (aged hard cheese)
entries.what: an older, stronger hard cheese, aged about eight days, per the Spanish Wikipedia gastronomy article. Retail price listed at $5.50 in the 2026 elsalvador.com article.

entries.heading: Queso Echo y Ansó
entries.what: Aragonese cheese from the Echo and Ansó valleys, Huesca.

name: Queso Emmental y Cheddar en fetas

entries.heading: Queso Emmental y Cheddar en fetas (Conaprole)
entries.what: "Emmental en fetas" and "Cheddar en fetas" (en fetas = sliced), sold by Conaprole.

entries.heading: Queso en aceite (cheese in oil)
entries.what: A method of keeping partly matured cheese submerged in a fatty medium, usually olive oil. Served cubed as a tapa with red wine.

entries.heading: Queso envuelto en hoja (leaf-wrapped cheese, Santander)
entries.what: A cheese wrapped in leaf from the Bucaramanga metropolitan area in Santander.

entries.heading: Queso Fontina (Conaprole)
entries.what: Fontina-type cheese sold by Conaprole.

entries.heading: Queso fresco de Guatemala (fresh white cheese, several local versions)
entries.what: the common fresh cheese of Guatemala. The thesis says it is made artisanally even in modern industrial plants, and that the method is basically the same everywhere; the salt level and coatings vary by area. In Zacapa, where it is about 30 °

entries.heading: Queso fresco hondureño (queso fresco; Honduran fresh cheese)
entries.what: a fresh, slightly salty, crumbly cheese that is a staple of Honduran cooking; used on baleadas and catrachas, and also listed with pupusas, quesadillas and empanadas.

entries.heading: Queso Gruyerito (Conaprole)
entries.what: Conaprole sells a Gruyerito "horma" (block) of 8 kg, sold by weight, and a plain "Queso Gruyerito" with no description.

entries.heading: Queso helado arequipeño (queso helado)
entries.what: An Arequipa frozen dessert of milk, condensed milk, coconut and cinnamon. Its name is taken from its pieces of condensed milk, which look like cheese. Called an emblem of Arequipa's cooking and a dessert from picanterías and street stalls.

entries.heading: Queso ibérico
entries.what: A cheese described as similar to Manchego and made in the same region from a blend of milks.

entries.heading: Queso jalapeño
entries.what: A soft cheese with bits of jalapeño, served cold or melted in quesadillas.

entries.heading: Queso llanero (queso llanero; queso blanco duro llanero)
entries.what: The llanos (plains) white cheese, grated over dishes such as pabellón and pasta, and used as an arepa and empanada filling.

entries.heading: Queso Magro (lean cheese)
entries.what: Listed as dairy output, with no details in the source.

entries.heading: Queso majado con chile (chile-mashed cheese)
entries.what: a salty, dry, porous cheese mixed with hot chile, per the Spanish Wikipedia gastronomy article. Retail listing as queso seco con chile in the 2026 elsalvador.com article at $3.75.

entries.heading: Queso mantecoso (queso mantecoso de Cajamarca; "buttery cheese")
entries.what: A Cajamarca cheese with a slightly acid flavour and creamy, buttery texture; in 2024 a Cajamarca mantecoso (Lácteos D'Celendín) scored 95/100 and was named best cheese in Peru.

entries.heading: Queso menonita (Chihuahua cheese)
entries.what: Mexican cheese from Chihuahua, first made by Mennonite communities of northern Mexico; now made widely.

entries.heading: Queso Minas Frescal
entries.what: a fresh cheese, meant to be eaten soon after it is made, defined in the Food Code.

entries.heading: Queso molido (queso prensado)
entries.what: A pressed cheese from Zacazonapan, State of Mexico, sometimes covered in red chili paste.

entries.heading: Queso Molido y Añejo (Tepalcatepec)
entries.what: An aged, ground-curd cheese named for Tepalcatepec.

entries.heading: Queso morado (Ayacucho)
entries.what: A cheese from the Mi Vaquita brand in Ayacucho named "queso morado" in the 2024 contest Innovation category (second place); the same brand's Ternura Negra (purple corn) won the 2025 national prize.

entries.heading: Queso mozzarella rayado (shredded mozzarella)
entries.what: shredded mozzarella listed at $4.60 in the 2026 elsalvador.com article.

entries.heading: Queso nata de Cantabria (queso de Cantabria until 2007)
entries.what: a fatty, pressed cheese made across Cantabria; creamy, bone-coloured paste usually without holes; pieces 400 to 2,800 g; soft bone-coloured rind.

entries.heading: Queso Nube (Val de Cinca)
entries.what: a soft mould-ripened sheep cheese from Fonz (Huesca), named "Nube" (cloud).

entries.heading: Queso Paipa
entries.what: A regional cheese from the Sogamoso Valley, Boyacá, made in Paipa and Sotaquirá at about 2,525 m; reinvention of the older Reinoso cheese.

entries.heading: Queso paisa (queso paisa; paisa)
entries.what: A cheese the Gastronomía article calls "Paisa", a commercial brand name used generically for fresh pasteurised cheese.

entries.heading: Queso palmita (queso palmita; Palmita-type cheese)
entries.what: A soft, salty, fresh white farm cheese from Venezuela, sold in large wheels packed in pressed wooden crates.

entries.heading: Queso Pañoleta
entries.what: Aragonese cheese listed by name.

entries.heading: Queso paria (paria)
entries.what: A traditional Andean cheese from the Puno highlands, pale yellow and semi-hard, with a mildly salty flavour; one of the two main regional Andean cheeses named in national standards.

entries.heading: Queso Parmiggiano (Conaprole)
entries.what: Conaprole's "Queso Parmiggiano", the Italian spelling of Parmigiano.

entries.heading: Queso Parrillero y Provolone (Conaprole)
entries.what: "Queso Parrillero" and "Paquete parrillero provolone", both sold by Conaprole. The name "parrillero" suggests a grilling cheese, but the source does not say so.

entries.heading: Queso pata de mulo (Tierra de Campos; Palencia, León, Valladolid, Zamora)
entries.what: a cured sheep cheese with a compact, crumbly paste, no eyes, bone-white (ivory in the most aged pieces), yellow-ochre rind; saltier and oilier than other cured sheep cheeses. Named for its cylindrical shape ("mule's hoof"). Originally matur

entries.heading: Queso Patamulo (Aragon)
entries.what: Aragonese cheese listed by name.

entries.heading: Queso Pera
entries.what: A Colombian pressed cheese shaped like a pear.

entries.heading: Queso poroso (porous cheese)
entries.what: a salty, strong, dry, porous cheese crumbled as a topping on dishes, per the Spanish Wikipedia gastronomy article.

entries.heading: Queso Port Salut (Conaprole)
entries.what: Port Salut-style cheese sold by Conaprole.

entries.heading: Queso Prato
entries.what: a matured cheese defined in the Food Code (article 633 tris), with an industrial-use name.

entries.heading: Queso rallado y en hebras (Conaprole)
entries.what: Grated cheese sold by Conaprole in 40 g, 80 g and 200 g packs, and "Queso en hebras", a grated Parmigiano-style cheese in strands.

entries.heading: Queso ranchero (incl. Queso Ranchero de Cabra, Perote)
entries.what: A ranch-made white cheese of northern Mexico, similar to Monterey Jack. Some sold in street markets.

entries.heading: Queso rayado (grated cheese)
entries.what: a grating cheese listed at $3.50 in the 2026 elsalvador.com article.

entries.heading: Queso Real del Castillo
entries.what: A semi-hard cheese of Baja California.

entries.heading: Queso Reggianito y Sbrinz (Conaprole)
entries.what: "Queso Reggianito" and "Queso Sbrinz", both sold by Conaprole.

entries.heading: Queso sabor Cheddar (Conaprole)
entries.what: "Queso sabor Cheddar" and "Queso sabor Cheddar doypack" (a pouch), sold by Conaprole.

entries.heading: Queso Sándwich (sandwich cheese; queso de sándwich)
entries.what: A cheese made for the sandwich de miga, the Uruguayan sandwich.

entries.heading: Queso seco (Spanish; "dry cheese"; used in chuchitos)
entries.what: A dry, salty white cheese that is crumbled over chuchitos, small corn-masa steamed tamales wrapped in corn husk and served with tomato sauce and meat.

entries.heading: Queso seco con chile (see queso majado con chile above)
Queso seco hondureño (queso seco; "smoked dry cheese" in one source; queijo seco in the list)
entries.what: a dry, crumbly, salty cheese, used as an optional topping for sopa de frijoles with sour cream, avocado and lemon, and crumbled over beans.

entries.heading: Queso Semiduro (Conaprole)
entries.what: A cheese sold by Conaprole under the generic name "Queso Semiduro".

entries.heading: Queso Tandil
entries.what: a matured cheese defined in the Argentine Food Code; the Code also allows an industrial-use name ("Queso Tandil de uso industrial"). The name comes from Tandil, a city in Buenos Aires province.

entries.heading: Queso telita (queso telita)
entries.what: A mild farmer's cheese from Venezuela, packaged in liquid.

entries.heading: Queso Termal (Termal)
entries.what: A Uruguayan cheese made using salty waters from the Almirón Hot Springs.

entries.heading: Queso Tilsit
entries.what: a matured cheese defined in the Food Code (article 633 bis), with an industrial-use name.

entries.heading: Queso tipo suizo (Swiss-style cheese, Peru)
entries.what: Swiss-style cheese made by Peruvian dairies including the Chugur quesería in Cajamarca (sold at about S/ 29.50 per kilo in 2025).

entries.heading: Queso Tronchón (Valencian Community)
entries.what: A second Tronchón listed for the Valencian Community, separate from the Aragonese one.

entries.heading: Queso Tybo
entries.what: a matured cheese defined in the Food Code (article 633), with an industrial-use name and a Tybo Sandwich variant.

entries.heading: Queso Untable (spreadable cheese)
entries.what: Listed as dairy output in Uruguay, with no details.

entries.heading: Queso Yamandú (Yamandú; Zapicán's parent cheese)
entries.what: A Uruguayan cheese from the 1950s, developed by the dairy school of the Universidad del Trabajo in Nueva Helvecia. It is credited to Luis Bertotto and Rubén Schneider. Some experts call it the only cheese of wholly Uruguayan origin. It was

entries.heading: Queso Zacatecas
entries.what: An aged cheese named after Zacatecas, served grated, not sliced.

entries.heading: Queso Zapicán (Zapicán)
entries.what: A smaller, rectangular version of Yamandú, made from leftover curd.

entries.heading: Quesucos de Liébana (Quesucos lebaniegos)
entries.what: a small cheese from the Liébana valley, with a protected name; the smoked version is a Cantabrian speciality.

entries.heading: Qula (曲拉, qū lā; Tibetan yak cheese, also chura family)
entries.what: Hard, high-protein Tibetan dairy cheese; the most distinctive of the Chinese cheese types in the catalogue (about 60% protein).

entries.heading: Qumësht i pasterizuar dhe UHT (heat-treated milk, pasteurised and UHT)
entries.what: pasteurised and UHT milk sold in Tirana shops alongside raw milk

entries.heading: Qumësht pluhuri për foshnje (infant powdered milk, sold in Albania)
entries.what: powdered infant milk consumed in Albania; the study bought fourteen types for radioactivity testing

entries.heading: Qurt / Kurt (құрт, қүрүт; ақ құрт, қара құрт)
entries.what: Hard dried balls or shapes of curd, eaten dry or dissolved in water for soups and sauces. Kazakh Wikipedia lists shapes külshe, zharma, sykpa and shüirmek; white and black qurt.

entries.heading: Qurut / kurut (курут)
entries.what: Dried, salted, fermented curd shaped into balls, strips or chunks and dried until hard. Eaten as a snack or seasoning and dissolved into dishes. The Kyrgyz wiki calls it a sheep's-milk product. The Kyrgyz diet paper lists "dried suzmo (kuru

entries.heading: Qurut / quroot (Pashto قروت/توروې; Persian کشک kašk; also "kurt" in the Meiji text)
entries.what: a sun-dried sour yogurt or buttermilk curd, dissolved in water to make sauces. Afghan Wikipedia calls it a hard, very sour cottage-type product.

entries.heading: Qurutob (Tajik national dish built on qurut)
entries.what: national dish of Tajikistan; flatbread (fatir) covered with liquid made by dissolving qurut in water, topped with onions, vegetables, herbs, sometimes meat or chili.

entries.heading: Rabri
entries.what: Sweet, dense, off-white or pale-yellow condensed milk dessert.

entries.heading: Rabri / rabdi (रबड़ी)
entries.what: Sweetened, reduced milk dessert served chilled; layers of cream form on the surface (lachha).

entries.heading: Raclette (French industrial)
entries.what: French raclette-type cheese; the French list tags it as made in Bretagne, Franche-Comté and Rhône-Alpes.

entries.heading: Raclette de Savoie (raclette, generic: Valais origin)
entries.what: Raclette de Savoie, IGP 27 January 2017; Savoie and Haute-Savoie plus some communes in Ain and Isère.

entries.heading: Raclette du Valais (Walliser Raclette, Raclette valaisanne)
entries.what: The Valais raclette cheese, protected by AOP. Its paste is ivory-coloured and smooth with few small holes; it comes in flat round or flat rectangular loaves.

entries.heading: Raclette Nature (Fromage pour raclette; La Petite Raclette)
entries.what: A mild cheese made for creamy raclette.

entries.heading: Raejuusto (grynost)
entries.what: A soft granular fresh cheese, low in fat and high in protein, eaten alone or with cucumber, olive oil and black pepper, or used as a soup garnish.

entries.heading: Rahka (maitorahka; kvarkki; uunipiimä)
entries.what: A firm fermented milk product, also called kvarkki or uunipiimä. Used for desserts with fruit or berries and whipped cream, for rahkapiirakka (curd pie) and for pasha.

entries.heading: Raïb / Raïbi (fermented drinks, pomegranate, pistachio, mango)
entries.what: Raïb is a North African fermented milk drink, and Raïbi is a flavoured version in pomegranate, pistachio or mango, both listed by Luxlait.

entries.heading: Raïeb torkey
entries.what: A traditional white cheese eaten with a spoon like yoghurt, said to be inherited from the Ottoman period.

entries.heading: Raita (राइता)
entries.what: A dahi-based dish named in the Nepali dahi article among dahi-based drinks.

entries.heading: Raketost (Mjuk Raketost)
entries.what: A Swedish soft cheese packed in a waxed cardboard tube, pushed up out of the tube and sliced with a string attached to the tube. Launched in 1947 and most popular in the 1960s; the last original cheese was made in 1979. Kavli, the brand own

entries.heading: Raku (酪, らく)
entries.what: A product placed after milk and before 生酥 in the Mahāparinirvāṇa Sūtra sequence (milk → raku → fresh so → cooked so → daigo).

entries.heading: Ran Ran Farm chèvre (Japanese name not in sources)
entries.what: A fresh goat cheese from Ran Ran Farm, sold in major Tokyo department stores.

entries.heading: Ras (Arabic name not in opened sources)
entries.what: Cited in Egyptian studies as one of three main traditional cheeses (Karish, Domiati, Ras). In the UAE the name Ras replaces Rumi.

entries.heading: Ras malai
entries.what: Chhena dumplings soaked in sweetened, flavoured milk; popular in India, Bangladesh and Pakistan.

entries.heading: Rasbari (rasgulla form)
entries.what: Chhena balls soaked in sugar syrup, known in Nepal as rasbari (or rasbhari). Rasgulla originated in eastern India; popular in Nepal under this name.

entries.heading: Rasco (Rasco)
entries.what: A cheese listed for Calabria.

entries.heading: Rasmalai (রসমালাই)
entries.what: Paneer discs in thickened, sweet milk; popular in India, Pakistan and Bangladesh, mainly in summer.

entries.heading: Rasomalai / rosomalai (রসমালাই)
entries.what: chhana balls soaked in sweetened, cardamom-flavoured thickened milk (malai). In Bangladesh it is often made with buffalo milk.

entries.heading: Raukfår
entries.what: Blue-mould sheep cheese from Gotland.

entries.heading: Raviggiolo del Mugello
entries.what: fresh soft cheese from the Tosco-Romagnolo Apennines; the Mugello version is the cow-milk one.

entries.heading: Raviggiolo di pecora pistoiese
entries.what: sheep-milk raviggiolo from the Pistoia area.

entries.heading: Raviggiolo di pecora senese
entries.what: sheep-milk raviggiolo from the Siena area.

entries.heading: Raw / unpasteurised milk (cow, yak and zom, mithun, buffalo)
entries.what: Most milk in Bhutan is produced on smallholder farms. The main use is turning it into butter and datshi cheese in almost all milk-producing households; some is sold raw.

entries.heading: Raw buffalo milk (susu bubalu; Tetum term not confirmed)
entries.what: Raw buffalo milk is drunk by a small share of cattle-farming households in the survey area, a practice the study names as a possible route of brucellosis transmission to people.

entries.heading: Raw fermented milk (local name not given in sources read)
entries.what: fermented raw milk sold in Libyan markets, sampled separately from yoghurt.

entries.heading: Raw goat's milk
entries.what: raw goat's milk sold in Libya and sampled in the 2016 study.

entries.heading: Raw mare's milk (شیر مادیان)
entries.what: Raw mare's milk, sold and consumed in Yazd; described as widely used for Iranian infants.

entries.heading: Raw milk and fermented milk (Maasai and Samburu everyday use)
entries.what: the everyday milk of Maasai and Samburu herders. Fresh raw milk is drunk unprocessed; fermented milk is considered better by Samburu ("ripened" milk).

name: Raw milk from cow, goat and sheep

entries.heading: Raw milk from cow, goat and sheep
entries.what: Milk from cows, goats and sheep used as the raw material for Israeli handmade dairy products.

entries.heading: Raw she-camel's milk (no local name given in sources read)
entries.what: raw she-camel milk sold in Libyan markets.

entries.heading: Raw sheep's milk
entries.what: sheep's milk, which the 2016 study says Libyans buy and drink alongside cow's and goat's milk.

entries.heading: Raxap and doghap (Uyghur drinkable yoghurts)
entries.what: Raxap is a drinkable yoghurt; doghap is a chilled version of a similar yoghurt drink. Eaten in Uyghur communities of Xinjiang alongside kumis and ayran.

entries.heading: Rdzis korkoti (რძის კორკოტი)
entries.what: wheat grains boiled in milk, from Samtskhe-Javakheti.

entries.heading: Rebarba
entries.what: A strong cheese traditionally made from the mould and scrapings of ripening Roquefort, or from old tomme and buttermilk and whey.

entries.heading: Reblec (Reblec)
entries.what: A cow's-milk cheese of Valle d'Aosta recognised as a traditional agri-food product (PAT).

entries.heading: Reblec de crama (Reblec de crama; Reblec di crema)
entries.what: A cow's-milk cheese of Valle d'Aosta, a PAT entry listed separately from Reblec.

entries.heading: Reconstituted imported milk powder (used for local products)
entries.what: Imported milk powder, repackaged locally, reconstituted and used to make local dairy products such as yoghurt and gappal.

name: Reconstituted milk from imported milk powder

entries.heading: Reconstituted milk from imported milk powder (นมผง, recombined milk)
entries.what: liquid milk made by reconstituting imported milk powder with water. The 1996 paper says about half of Thai liquid milk was recombined, and that milk powder was imported.

entries.heading: Reconstituted milk from imported powder
entries.what: Milk made by mixing imported powder with water, used as a substitute for fresh milk in the period studied.

entries.heading: Recuit
entries.what: A fresh cheese whose curd separates from liquid whey; associated with the Empordà.

entries.heading: Recuit de drap
entries.what: A soft, glossy, creamy, sweet and milky fresh cheese, often served as a dessert with honey or sugar; must be kept at 2–4 °C.

entries.heading: Red Devil
entries.what: A named Welsh cheese, listed with Caerphilly, Y Fenni, Llanboidy and Black Bomber as produced in Wales.

entries.heading: Red Hawk
entries.what: A soft, mildly salty triple-crème with a red-orange rind.

entries.heading: Red Holland
entries.what: a Dutch-style cheese listed as made in Kenya.

entries.heading: Red jajek (matsnaprtosh in Artsakh; yoghurt sauce)
entries.what: A yoghurt sauce with matsun, sour cream and beetroot. Called matsnaprtosh in Artsakh (Nagorno-Karabakh).

entries.heading: Red-dyed wagashi (wagashi colored with dye sorghum)
entries.what: wagashi coloured red for sale in Benin, where women selling wagashi need a ready-to-use dye; the colour comes from a sorghum plant, not a synthetic dye.

entries.heading: Redykołka (redykołka; Polish)
entries.what: A traditional Polish smoked cheese sometimes called the "younger sister" of oscypek. It is made from leftover bundz and is often shaped into animals, hearts or wreaths. It was historically given in pairs as a gift.

entries.heading: Reggianito (Reggianito Argentino)
entries.what: a hard, granular grating cheese developed by Italian immigrants as a Parmesan-style cheese, shaped as smaller wheels.

entries.heading: Reindeer butter (Tsaatan)
entries.what: Butter made by the Tsaatan (Dukha) reindeer herders.

entries.heading: Reindeer cream cheese (unnamed variety)
entries.what: A rich reindeer cream cheese described as yellow outside, white inside, turning golden when cut, and prone to going rancid; the Sámi ate it with coffee in place of cream.

entries.heading: Reindeer milk yoghurt (Tsaatan)
entries.what: Yoghurt made by the Tsaatan (Dukha) reindeer herders of Khövsgöl, part of the core of their diet.

entries.heading: Remoudou (r'moûdou)
entries.what: A small Walloon cheese from the Land of Herve, sold in pieces of 200–500 g. Its name comes from the Walloon verb "rimoûd" (to re-milk).

entries.heading: Renaico
entries.what: Listed under Chile in the English Wikipedia "List of cheeses", with no description. The English Wikipedia page "Renaico" is about a town in the Araucanía Region and does not mention cheese, so the cheese's origin there is unconfirmed.

entries.heading: Rennet casein (Dairygold)
entries.what: Rennet casein, named by the company as one of its main products.

entries.heading: Repollitos con dulce de leche
entries.what: a Guatemalan dessert named with dulce de leche as the filling or topping.

entries.heading: Requeijão de ovelha (sheep's requeijão)
entries.what: A requeijão made from sheep's milk.

entries.heading: Requeixo (requesón / requeixo; whey cheese)
entries.what: A traditional Galician whey cheese made by draining the curd from curdled milk ("leite callado").

entries.heading: Resbaladera (resbaladera; rice and barley drink with milk)
entries.what: A drink of rice and barley with milk and sugar, named in the Panamanian lexicon column.

entries.heading: Reypenaer
entries.what: An aged Goudse kaas, matured in Woerden by the Van den Wijngaard family in a historic cheese warehouse at Utrechtsestraatweg 19, a national monument. The family started trading cheese in 1934.

entries.heading: Rica aged cheeses (queso curado)
entries.what: Aged cheese introduced in the Dominican market by Pasteurizadora Rica in 1986, together with butter.

entries.heading: Rica butter (mantequilla)
entries.what: Butter introduced by Pasteurizadora Rica in 1986, together with aged cheeses.

entries.heading: Rica evaporated milk (lactose-free evaporated milk)
entries.what: Evaporated milk from Grupo Rica, introduced in 2008; a lactose-free version was created in 2011 for people with lactose intolerance.

name: Rica powdered whole milk and Milkkids

entries.heading: Rica powdered whole milk and Milkkids (powdered dairy food for children)
entries.what: Powdered whole milk introduced by Grupo Rica in 2008; Milkkids, a powdered dairy food for children's growth, launched in 2016.

entries.heading: Rica UHT long-life milk (Listamilk; La Vaquita; lactose-free 0% fat)
entries.what: Long-life milk from Grupo Rica (Pasteurizadora Rica). UHT was proposed in 1991 and is linked to the Listamilk line; La Vaquita milk was launched in 1997; lactose-free 0% fat milk in 2012.

entries.heading: Rica yoghurt (Rica Yogurt; natural, vanilla, strawberry)
entries.what: A yoghurt sold by Grupo Rica, launched in 2019 in natural, vanilla and strawberry flavours.

entries.heading: Ricotta affumicata (sheep whey)
entries.what: A smoked sheep-whey ricotta listed for Calabria. It may be the same product as Ricotta affumicata crotonese.

entries.heading: Ricotta affumicata crotonese (Ricotta Affumicata Crotonese)
entries.what: A smoked ricotta from the Upper Crotonese area and the town of Mammola.

entries.heading: Ricotta affumicata dell'Alpago
entries.what: A smoked ricotta of the Alpago area (Belluno) named in the Veneto cuisine article.

entries.heading: Ricotta affumicata di malga (Scuete fumade)
entries.what: Smoked mountain-hut ricotta from Carnia; used in cjarsons.

entries.heading: Ricotta calda con siero (PAT)
entries.what: A ricotta made from heated whey.

name: Ricotta di bufala affumicata, infornata, salata

entries.heading: Ricotta di bufala affumicata, infornata, salata (PAT)
entries.what: Buffalo ricotta in smoked, oven-baked and salted forms.

entries.heading: Ricotta di capra (Ricotta caprina friulana)
entries.what: Ricotta made from goat whey in Friuli Venezia Giulia.

entries.heading: Ricotta di capra affumicata (Ricotta di capra affumicata)
entries.what: Smoked goat-whey ricotta listed for Calabria.

entries.heading: Ricotta di fuscella di Sant'Anastasia
entries.what: a fresh, soft, white cheese shaped as a truncated pyramid in conical perforated baskets (fuscelle), under 2 kg.

name: Ricotta di pecora e di capra dei Monti Lepini

entries.heading: Ricotta di pecora e di capra dei Monti Lepini (PAT)
entries.what: A ricotta from sheep and goat whey in the Monti Lepini.

entries.heading: Ricotta di pecora grossetana
entries.what: ricotta from sheep whey, Grosseto.

entries.heading: Ricotta di pecora massese
entries.what: ricotta from sheep whey, Massa area.

entries.heading: Ricotta di pecora pistoiese
entries.what: ricotta from sheep whey, Pistoia area.

entries.heading: Ricotta fioreta delle vallate vicentine (fioreta)
entries.what: A semi-liquid whey ricotta of Recoaro Terme and the Valle dell'Agno (Vicenza), a PAT product. It is eaten fresh and is the basis of gnocchi con la fioreta, celebrated in Recoaro.

entries.heading: Ricotta Iblea
entries.what: a traditional ricotta from the Ragusa area, made from Modicana cow's-milk whey; about 8% fat.

entries.heading: Ricotta infornata
entries.what: a traditional baked ricotta from Sicily.

entries.heading: Ricotta ligure (Recottu; Val Stura, Val d'Aveto, Valle Scrivia, Val Graveglia)
entries.what: a Ligurian ricotta made from whey, produced in several valleys (Stura, Aveto, Scrivia, Graveglia).

entries.heading: Ricotta marzotica
entries.what: A round, tapered Apulian whey cheese made in the provinces of Lecce and Taranto from whey left over from cheesemaking. Its name means "March-style" because production runs from mid-February to May.

entries.heading: Ricotta ovina di Arischia
entries.what: a sheep's-milk ricotta from Arischia (province of L'Aquila).

entries.heading: Ricotta Romana (Ricotta romana DOP)
entries.what: A DOP ricotta from sheep's-milk whey, made in Lazio. Slightly sweet; used mostly as a filling.

entries.heading: Ricotta Schotte
entries.what: Whey cheese made in Friuli Venezia Giulia.

entries.heading: Ricotta scorza nera di Scanno
entries.what: a ricotta from Scanno (province of L'Aquila) with a dark rind.

entries.heading: Ricotta secca (PAT)
entries.what: A dried ricotta.

entries.heading: Ricotta viterbese (PAT)
entries.what: A sheep-whey ricotta from Viterbo.

entries.heading: Ricotta-type fresh cheese (sold in Libya as "ricotta")
entries.what: a ricotta-style soft cheese sampled in Libyan retail dairy in two studies; the 2022 study calls it a fresh, locally made soft cheese.

entries.heading: Ricotta, artisanal (unnamed in source; Tunisia)
entries.what: Artisanal ricotta sold unpackaged at retail points in northern Tunisia.

entries.heading: Ricottone salato (Riccotone Salato)
entries.what: A salted ricotta with a truncated-cone shape and an intense, slightly spicy flavour, from the Crotone to Locri area.

entries.heading: Ridderost (Ridder)
entries.what: a Norwegian specialty with a smeared surface; produced at Tresfjord since 1969 (TINE).

entries.heading: Riebel / Ribel (maize-wheat porridge cooked in milk)
entries.what: A traditional dish of toasted cornmeal and wheat semolina, cooked, then fried until it forms crumbly lumps. Eaten with coffee or milk, or sweetened, or with apple sauce. Known as Ribel in Liechtenstein; the Rheintaler maize is a protected o

entries.heading: Rietfontein (300 ml drink)
entries.what: A Namibia Dairies brand with a 300 ml product marketed as "Pure refreshment" and many flavours.

entries.heading: Rigouta (رقوطة; Arabic script not given in the sources read; also called gouta)
entries.what: A traditional fresh cheese from Béja in northern Tunisia, close to Italian ricotta, with a shelf life of 2–3 days.

entries.heading: Riisipuuro (rice porridge)
entries.what: A Nordic dish; part of Finnish Christmas food (joulupuuro, with an almond hidden in it). Also used as the filling for karjalanpiirakka.

entries.heading: Rijstebrij (rijstepap; dikke rijst)
entries.what: An old sweet dish of rice cooked in sweetened milk. Optional vanilla, saffron or cinnamon; often sprinkled with candy sugar; raw egg yolks or butter for a richer version; raisins optional.

entries.heading: Rijstevlaai (rice-and-cream pie)
entries.what: A Dutch pie filled with a rich rice-and-cream filling.

entries.heading: Rijstevlaai / rijsttaart (rice tart)
entries.what: A yeasted tart with a rice-pudding style filling, topped with whipped cream and chocolate. Also called rijsttaart. The Dutch page places it especially in the Euregio Maas-Rijn region. The Verviers rice tart (tarte au riz / dorèye de Vervier

entries.heading: Ripened cheeses of Uganda (varieties not named)
entries.what: Ripened Ugandan cheese varieties, studied as a reservoir of lactic acid bacteria and yeasts for possible starter cultures.

entries.heading: Risalamande (rice pudding with almonds)
entries.what: Danish Christmas dessert (served at julefrokost too): rice pudding mixed with whipped cream, sugar, vanilla and chopped almonds, served cold with cherry sauce (kirsebærsovs). Dates to about 1900, modelled on riz à l'impératrice.

entries.heading: Risengrød (rice porridge)
entries.what: rice porridge served with butter; Danish Christmas food.

entries.heading: Risgrynsgröt (rice porridge)
entries.what: Swedish rice porridge (round grain rice) traditionally eaten at Christmas but year-round; served with sugar, cinnamon, milk, butter, jam or sauce. Almond (mandel) tradition.

entries.heading: Rivella (whey-based soft drink; Mivella variant)
entries.what: A Swiss soft drink introduced in 1952 by Rivella AG, made from milk whey (milk serum) with lactose, lactic acid and minerals. Among Switzerland's most popular drinks. Flavoured lines include Rivella Red (1952), Blue (1959) and Green Tea (19

entries.heading: Rob (الروب; soured milk)
entries.what: a soured milk named in the dairy list of the Arabic Wikipedia Sudanese cuisine article.

entries.heading: Robiola d'Alba
entries.what: soft cheese from the Alba area (Langhe) of Cuneo, also parts of Torino, Asti and Alessandria, and Savona valleys; sometimes flavoured with pepper, truffle, chives or rocket.

entries.heading: Robiola della Val Bormida (Liguria, upper Val Bormida, Savona)
entries.what: a small cylindrical cheese (about 200–400 g) with a soft interior and little or no white rind, made in the upper Val Bormida (province of Savona). It is mentioned in a medieval treatise by Pantaleone da Confienza, a physician to the House o

entries.heading: Robiola di Roccaverano (Robiola di Roccaverano DOP)
entries.what: small cylindrical fresh goat cheese, 250–350 g, from the eastern Langhe.

entries.heading: Robiola Lombardia
entries.what: a Robiola of the Lombardy version: small rolls with a thin milky-white to pink bloomy rind and a cream-coloured, smooth, tangy interior; about 52% fat.

entries.heading: Rochebaron
entries.what: brand of the Compagnie Fromagère de la Vallée de l'Ance; about 600 g, vegetable-charcoal coating.

entries.heading: Rocher nantais
entries.what: Named in the list of French cheeses with origin Loire-Atlantique, Pays de la Loire.

entries.heading: Rødgrød med fløde (red berry porridge with cream)
entries.what: Danish (and N. German) berry pudding, served with cream, milk, vanilla sauce, whipped cream or ice cream; the name's "fløde" means cream.

entries.heading: Rødkit
entries.what: a Danish cheese named on Danish Wikipedia.

entries.heading: Roghan-e heyvani / Kermanshahi oil (روغن حیوانی; roghane heiwâni; Kermanshahi oil)
entries.what: A traditional fermented butter-like product from Kermanshah province, prized for nutrition; it contains lactic acid bacteria with probiotic potential.

entries.heading: Roka Blue
entries.what: A processed blue cheese.

entries.heading: Rolled cheese (Vojvodina rolled pasta filata; local name not given in the source)
entries.what: a traditional cheese of Vojvodina in northern Serbia, made from stretched curd and formed into the characteristic rolls

entries.heading: Rollot
entries.what: A soft washed-rind cheese, about 300 g, round (8–9 cm across, 3–4 cm thick) or heart-shaped; soft and melting, slightly salty and tangy, fruity and spicy with age.

entries.heading: Romano (American Romano)
entries.what: A US and Canadian term for a class of hard, salty cheese suited mainly to grating; the American imitation of pecorino romano.

entries.heading: Rómi at píska UHT (long-life whipping cream)
entries.what: Long-life whipping cream that does not need cold storage before opening; MBM says its properties match fresh cream.

entries.heading: Rómi til matgerð (cooking cream, 18%)
entries.what: Cream for soups and sauces; keeps 4–5 days chilled once opened, 6 months unopened. Carries a "matrómi" name on the page.

entries.heading: Rómi til písking (whipping cream, 38%)
entries.what: Cream sold for whipping; keeps 2–3 days chilled once opened. Used in cakes and desserts, per MBM's recipes.

entries.heading: Rømmegrøt (sour cream porridge)
entries.what: a Norwegian porridge in which sour cream is the base ingredient, together with whole milk, wheat flour, butter and salt. Traditionally a delicacy for special occasions and holidays; it marked haymaking (slåttegrøt) and St John's Eve (Jonsok

entries.heading: Ron ponche (Christmas eggnog-style drink)
entries.what: A traditional Christmas drink, equated with eggnog on the Panama pages.

entries.heading: Roob (homemade curdled milk, bread starter)
entries.what: homemade curdled milk, roob, used to speed fermentation of the flatbread batter.

entries.heading: Rookkaas (smoked processed cheese)
entries.what: A melted cheese with a smoky flavour, sausage-shaped and sold sliced in packs.

entries.heading: Roomano
entries.what: An aged hard cheese with less butterfat than other Gouda-style cheeses.

entries.heading: Rosace de Reims
entries.what: Cheese tagged to Champagne-Ardenne on the list page.

entries.heading: Rosogolla / rasgulla (রসগোল্লা)
entries.what: spongy chhana balls cooked in sugar syrup, a major Bangladeshi sweet.

entries.heading: Roti golok (Kelantan)
entries.what: A soft sweet bread from Kelantan made with generous amounts of butter and sweetened condensed milk, sometimes with cheese or chocolate.

entries.heading: Rotondo
entries.what: Corsican cheese listed on the French cheese list.

entries.heading: Rouaba (roab, rouba; Arabic/Chadian name shown as Raïb for the source milk)
entries.what: A sour buttermilk. In Chad it is the traditional cultured milk; per one source it is mixed with wheat porridge.

entries.heading: Roue de Ris
entries.what: sheep cheese brand made by L'Artisanale de Ris (about 1,000 t milk a year) in Ris, Puy-de-Dôme.

entries.heading: Roumy
entries.what: A hard yellow cheese derived from Greek kefalotyri, used grated like Parmesan.

entries.heading: Rozz be-laban (رز بلبن; rozz belaban)
entries.what: Egyptian rice pudding, "rice with milk".

entries.heading: Rozz bel-leben (rice in fermented milk)
entries.what: short-grain rice cooked in water and fermented milk, such as buttermilk or kefir, then topped with butter or olive oil and lemon juice. A savoury dish, unlike the sweet rice pudding elsewhere in the Arab world. A variant uses imgata or rish

entries.heading: Rozz bi haleeb (ريز بالحليب; riz bil halib)
entries.what: A creamy rice pudding made with milk and cream, sweetened and thickened.

entries.heading: Rozz me'ammar (رز معمر)
entries.what: Cooked rice baked with milk, butter or cream, and stock, usually served at festive meals.

entries.heading: Rubing (乳饼, rǔbǐng; Bai name yond bap / youdbap; Sani/Yi name also given)
entries.what: A firm fresh cheese from central and southern Yunnan, like paneer or halloumi, usually cooked savoury.

entries.heading: Rucăr (cașcaval)
entries.what: A Romanian cașcaval variety named in the Romanian cașcaval list; no description given.

entries.heading: Rucavas baltais sviests (Rucava white butter)
entries.what: Traditional butter from Rucava, leaner than ordinary butter, about 40% fat on average.

entries.heading: Ruffec
entries.what: A cheese of Poitou and Charentes, named after Ruffec (Charente).

entries.heading: Rūgpienis (rūgpienis, raugintas pienas; soured milk)
entries.what: milk thickened by lactic acid streptococci into a firm, sour, white-to-cream product. Eaten in Lithuania since old times; the most traditional sour milk, eaten with porridge, boiled or fried potatoes and bread.

entries.heading: Rūgušpiens (rūgušpiens; soured milk)
entries.what: Soured milk, a common Latvian drink, usually served alongside hot meals; also used to make skābputra and biezpiens.

entries.heading: Rulo de cabra (goat log)
entries.what: a goat's-milk log-shaped cheese named in the spain.info article.

entries.heading: Rum-raisin ice cream
entries.what: an ice cream flavoured with rum-soaked raisins, listed among Grenadian sweets.

entries.heading: Rumay mantequilla con sal (salted butter, Osorno)
entries.what: Salted butter "elaborada en Osorno" (Rumay brand), with the page's description "todo el sabor y magia del Sur de Chile".

entries.heading: Rumi (رومي; جبنة رومى; gebna Rumi; roumi / roomi; Ras in UAE and other sources)
entries.what: Egypt's main hard cheese. The name means "Roman", but it is Egyptian.

entries.heading: Rushan (乳扇, ruzhan; Bai name not given; also 邓川乳扇, 乳线, 饵线)
entries.what: Thin dried sheets of stretched curd from the Dali area (Lake Erhai, Yunnan), eaten fried or grilled, often as a sweet street snack.

entries.heading: Russian cheese (Российский сыр; "Syr Rossiysky" brand)
entries.what: Standard Russian semi-hard cheese developed in the 1960s at VNIIMS in Uglich (Yaroslavl Oblast). Many factories in Russia and other post-Soviet states make it.

name: Russian processed and soft cheeses named in the Russian article "Сыр"

entries.heading: Russian processed and soft cheeses named in the Russian article "Сыр" (names and short notes only, from the table in the source; milk not stated in the source)
Ruz bi-allaban (رز باللبن; rice with milk)
entries.what: a dish named in the Arabic Wikipedia Sudanese cuisine article.

entries.heading: Rygeost (smoked cheese)
entries.what: a Danish smoked cheese (rygeost), listed as a Danish cheese type on Danish Wikipedia.

entries.heading: Sabajón (alcoholic egg-milk drink)
entries.what: An alcoholic drink from eggs and milk with fruit juices and liqueur, listed in Colombian alcoholic beverages.

entries.heading: Saga
entries.what: a soft, creamy Danish cheese mixing blue and Brie traits, with a very mild blue veining.

entries.heading: Sago pudding
entries.what: Dessert of sago, sugar, milk and eggs, popular across communities and at Tamil weddings and festivals.

entries.heading: Saint Helena ice cream (unique St Helena ice-cream)
entries.what: a local ice cream, named only as "unique St Helena ice-cream"

entries.heading: Saint-Albray
entries.what: A cheese of the Pyrénées-Atlantiques.

entries.heading: Saint-Aubin
entries.what: Named in the list of French cheeses with origin Maine-et-Loire.

entries.heading: Saint-félicien (Saint-félicien, Dauphiné)
entries.what: small cylinder 150–220 g, from the Dauphiné; close to Saint-marcellin.

entries.heading: Saint-Florentin
entries.what: A soft washed-rind cow's-milk cheese from the village of Chailley, near Saint-Florentin, Yonne.

entries.heading: Saint-foin (Saint-foin)
entries.what: a cheese listed near Rambouillet, Yvelines.

entries.heading: Saint-Gelais
entries.what: A cheese of Poitou and Charentes.

entries.heading: Saint-Laurent (fromage)
entries.what: a soft cow's-milk cheese of the Champsaur.

entries.heading: Saint-Maure (made in Mexico)
entries.what: A French-style cheese also made in Mexico.

entries.heading: Saint-Tahitien (Saint-Tahitien; made in Taravao, Tahiti)
entries.what: one of the three local cheeses of French Polynesia, named after the archipelago, made in Tahiti.

entries.heading: Sakagura (Japanese name not in sources; washed in local sake)
entries.what: A Kyodo Gakusha Shintoku Farm cheese washed in local sake.

entries.heading: Sakeru Cheese (さけるチーズ, Sakeru)
entries.what: A pull-apart string cheese by Megmilk Snow Brand, first sold in 1980 as "string cheese" and renamed in 1995.

entries.heading: Sakhana (wheat, date and milk dish; soup)
entries.what: A thick soup made from wheat, dates, molasses and milk, eaten during Ramadan.

entries.heading: Sakman (sikman, Ru сикман)
entries.what: a salty, delicate, mild white cheese described as similar to feta.

entries.heading: Sikman (сикман)
entries.what: Named in the Russian Turkmen-cuisine article among dairy products. No description found.

entries.heading: Sakouliasti (σακουλιαστή; Nisyros)
entries.what: a Nisyros fresh cheese.

entries.heading: Sakouliasti Nisyrou
entries.what: a white, velvety, gently sour cheese from Nisyros.

entries.heading: Sakura (Japanese name not in sources; Sakura cheese)
entries.what: A soft cheese made at Kyodo Gakusha Shintoku Farm in Tokachi, Hokkaido, aimed as a Japanese-style cheese rather than an imitation of a European one.

entries.heading: Sakuramochi (Japanese name not in sources; Mirasaka spring goat)
entries.what: A spring goat cheese from Mirasaka Fromage, wrapped in cherry leaf.

entries.heading: Salatost
entries.what: named on TINE's product page as a milk-based product, with no further detail.

entries.heading: Salcë shakulli (salcë shakulli; "hide-sack sauce")
entries.what: a dense, tangy, concentrated dairy product made by shepherds during summer grazing to preserve yoghurt.

entries.heading: Salcë shakulli (strained yoghurt matured in skin sack)
entries.what: thick, creamy, salty concentrate of strained yoghurt, stored for winter

entries.heading: Saleeq (rice cooked with milk)
entries.what: Rice cooked in broth with milk added; served with chicken or meat.

entries.heading: Salignon / Salagnun
entries.what: usually smoked; lower Aosta Valley and Piedmont.

entries.heading: Salsa huancaína (huancaína sauce; papa a la huancaína)
entries.what: A creamy yellow sauce of ají amarillo (or ají verde) mixed with milk and cheese, poured over sliced boiled potatoes.

entries.heading: Salted spreadable butter (Isle of Man Creamery)
entries.what: A 250 g tub of salted butter sold as "Isle of Man Creamery Spreadable", described as "Delicious Isle of Man Creamery Salted Butter - now spreadable!".

entries.heading: Salted whey butter (Isle of Man Creamery)
entries.what: A 250 g salted butter sold by the Isle of Man Creamery; the page describes it as having "a sharp flavour and deep colour".

entries.heading: Šaltibarščiai (cold beet soup with kefir)
entries.what: a cold beet soup of the Eastern European region (Lithuania, Poland, Latvia, Ukraine, Russia, Belarus), with a milk base.

entries.heading: Salva
entries.what: a PDO cheese from Lombardy.

entries.heading: Salva Cremasco (Salva Cremasco DOP)
entries.what: a DOP soft, fat, washed-rind cheese from the Crema area.

entries.heading: Samogitian hard cheese (Žemaitiškas kietasis sūris)
entries.what: A hard cheese whose production in Samogitia dates to about the 16th century. Outside Samogitia it was known as "Lithuanian cheese". It is probably the origin of Džiugas.

entries.heading: Samsø (Samsø cheese)
entries.what: a Danish cheese named after the island of Samsø; mild and nutty when young, pungent and sweet-sour when older.

entries.heading: Samuli
entries.what: A heat-clarified milk-fat product made from Mashita in Uganda, with a fatty texture used in cooking and a longer shelf life than fresh butter products.

entries.heading: Sana
entries.what: A fermented milk drink, similar to kefir, buttermilk and soured milk, slightly sweet, at least 3.6% fat, which bakers also use in breads and pastries.

entries.heading: Sandefjordsmør (butter and cream sauce)
entries.what: a butter and cream sauce served with fish dishes, such as salmon, garnished with fresh dill and peppercorn. Reputedly first made in Sandefjord (Vestfold) in 1959.

entries.heading: Sandes de queijo (sandes de queijo; Portuguese, "cheese sandwich")
entries.what: a toasted cheese sandwich on Portuguese-style pão bread, sold at stalls and described as cheaper than prego rolls.

entries.heading: Sandesh (সন্দেশ)
entries.what: a milk-based sweet from the Bengal region, listed in Bangladeshi sweet lists.

entries.heading: Sandesh / shondesh (সন্দেশ)
entries.what: Bengal's signature sweet; lightly cooked chhena with sugar, moulded.

entries.heading: Sandex (সন্দেশ spelling variant)
entries.what: chhana-based sweet named in Banglapedia's list.

entries.heading: Sanglé (with sweetened lait caillé)
entries.what: a thick millet porridge served with sweetened lait caillé.

entries.heading: Şanlıurfa sadeyağı (Urfa yağı)
entries.what: a sheep-milk clarified butter from Şanlıurfa, registered as a geographical indication.

entries.heading: Santa Bárbara (Alcañiz)
entries.what: a cheese from Alcañiz (Teruel), named in the regional guide.

entries.heading: Santadi Cabriolu
entries.what: One of 16 lesser-known Sardinian cheeses, made by Central Formaggi.

entries.heading: Santo Stefano d'Aveto (San Stè, San Sté; Val d'Aveto, Rezzoaglio)
entries.what: a cheese of the Val d'Aveto (Santo Stefano d'Aveto, Rezzoaglio area) whose whey is used to make Sarasso.

entries.heading: Saputo consumer brands (Devondale, Sungold, Great Ocean Road, Liddells)
entries.what: National supermarket brands of Saputo Dairy Australia. Devondale lists milk, butters and spreads, cheese, milk powders and cream; Sungold and Great Ocean Road list fluid milk (Great Ocean Road also flavoured milk); Liddells lists lactose-fr

entries.heading: Sar / seruts (սար, սերուցք; kaymak-type cream)
entries.what: A thick cream skimmed off heated milk, eaten with honey, bread or fruit, and used in desserts such as gata, kadaif and baklava. Mainly called sar or seruts in Armenian; the Armenian name in the kaymak article is ser.

entries.heading: Šar cheese (šarski sir / sharr)
entries.what: a hard highland cheese from the Šar Mountains, flavoured by local herbs, especially dill

entries.heading: Sar-e-shir (سرشیر; also kaymak, nemshak)
entries.what: A thick, rich cream (about 60% fat) skimmed from heated milk, close to clotted cream, served at breakfast and as a dessert.

entries.heading: Sarasso (Sarazzu; upper Val d'Aveto, Genoa)
entries.what: a ricotta-style cheese from the Val d'Aveto made from the salted, aged whey left after making San Stè (Santo Stefano d'Aveto).

entries.heading: Sarasson (sarassou)
entries.what: fresh preparation from central-eastern France; the older base of cervelle de canut.

entries.heading: Sardara Su Rei
entries.what: One of 16 lesser-known Sardinian cheeses, made by Azienda Agricola Coile Scalas.

entries.heading: Sardo (Sardo argentino)
entries.what: an Argentine grating cheese modelled on Pecorino Romano, which is sheep's milk.

entries.heading: Sárgasajt (pogácsasajt)
entries.what: a mixed-coagulation (acid and rennet) curd cheese, also called pogácsasajt.

entries.heading: Sárgatúró
entries.what: a sweet, yellow cheese from Szabolcs County, made with quark and eggs, and eaten at Easter.

entries.heading: Sárgatúró (sárgatúró; csurgatott túró, édestúró, tojástúró)
entries.what: Sweet yellow curd made from milk and eggs, eaten at Easter.

entries.heading: Sariyog (sariyogʻ; also maska yogʻ) — butter
entries.what: Butter from qatiq, by churning qatiq.

entries.heading: Sarımsaqlı qatıq (garlic yoghurt)
entries.what: qatıq flavoured with garlic, served as an accompaniment; also used in the dish axsaq oğlaq and eaten with qayğanaq.

entries.heading: Sarpuria (সরপুরিয়া; sarpuria)
entries.what: Bengali sweet from Krishnanagar, Nadia district, West Bengal; also popular in rural Bangladesh.

entries.heading: Sarshir (сарширр)
entries.what: named in the breakfast list alongside kaymak; no description.

entries.heading: Sartinesu (Sartinese; casgiu sartinesu; fromage sartenais)
entries.what: Farmhouse cheese of southern Corsica; cylindrical, 15–20 cm across, 8–10 cm high, 1.5–2.5 kg, about 45–50% fat, named after Sartène.

entries.heading: Sasayuki (Japanese name not in sources; bamboo-leaf camembert)
entries.what: A camembert-style cheese from Kyodo Gakusha Shintoku Farm, wrapped in bamboo leaf from the farm.

entries.heading: Satoyama No Cheese (里山のチーズ)
entries.what: A mild, semi-soft cheese made near Tokyo by Noriyuki and Akiko Ikagawa, their first cheese.

entries.heading: Savaron
entries.what: Auvergne cheese, a "nom de fantaisie" that emerged in 1945 as an imitation of Saint-nectaire made outside its AOC zone.

entries.heading: Savó and zsendice (whey and whey curd)
entries.what: Whey is the by-product of túró making. Zsendice is a soft, sour-cream-like curd that forms when whey is heated; orda is made from it (orda is a cheese per Hungarian Wikipedia, so excluded).

entries.heading: Savory (ice cream brand, Chile)
entries.what: A Chilean ice cream brand. The Soprole article says that in 1959 Soprole created the Savory ice cream brand with AFIA, and that it was sold to Nestlé in 1965.

entries.heading: Saw hlaing mont (Rakhine-style baked sweet)
entries.what: a Rakhine-style baked sweet of millet, raisins, coconut and butter.

entries.heading: Sázava
entries.what: named Czech cheese, produced for decades, possible PGI candidate.

entries.heading: Scamorza appassita – Cacetto di Supino (PAT)
entries.what: A dried scamorza (cacetto) from Supino.

entries.heading: Scamorza molisana (listed in the Molise row of the regional table)
entries.what: A Molise variant of scamorza listed in the national regional table of traditional products.

entries.heading: Scamorza molisana / Scamorza di bufala
entries.what: scamorza variants from Molise and Campania.

entries.heading: Scamorza vaccina (semplice e ripiena) (PAT)
entries.what: A cow's-milk scamorza.

entries.heading: Schafmilch (sheep milk)
entries.what: milk from ewes; on average about 6.8% fat, 6.0% protein and 5.0% lactose, with more unsaturated fat, minerals and some vitamins than cow milk.

entries.heading: Schärdinger Jaus'nkäs (snack cheese)
entries.what: a Schärdinger cheese brand named in the company history

entries.heading: Schärdinger Landfrischkäse (fresh cheese)
entries.what: a Schärdinger fresh cheese brand; Berglandmilch also lists a Landfrischkäse

entries.heading: Scharfe Maxx (Scharfe Maxx)
entries.what: a hard Swiss cheese from the canton of Thurgau, with a sharp flavour that resembles Appenzeller but is creamier.

entries.heading: Schichtkäse (Sahneschichtkäse)
entries.what: A gelatinous, firm, layered fresh cheese with a pure lactic-acid flavour, distinct from the pasty texture of quark. Higher-fat version (at least 40% fat in dry matter) sold as Sahneschichtkäse.

entries.heading: Schlagobers / Schlagsahne (whipping cream)
entries.what: cream suitable for whipping; "Schlagobers" is the Austrian term ("Obers" in eastern Austria, "Rahm" in Austria, southern Germany and Switzerland)

entries.heading: Schmand (also Schmant, Schmetten)
entries.what: thick, spoonable soured cream with at least 20% fat.

entries.heading: Schmierkase (Bengal; "Dutch cheese")
entries.what: Early Bengali cottage cheese, also called "Dutch cheese", named in the Bengal cuisine article.

entries.heading: Schnittkäse group (Bergkäse and cut cheeses from South Tyrol, named on the register)
entries.what: The register names a group of local cut cheeses: Alta Badia, Gran Spicchio / Gran Dolomiti, Dolomitenkönig, Malga Gardena, Monte Maria (Marienberger), Braies (Pragser Stange), Pusteria (Pustertaler), Silandro leggero (Schlanderser leicht),

name: School milk: fresh, UHT and powdered milk

entries.heading: School milk: fresh, UHT and powdered milk (industrial)
entries.what: Milk supplied to the national school feeding programme (PAE), served free each school day.

entries.heading: Schwyzer Alpkäse (Schwyzer; Alpkäse of the Muotatal)
entries.what: A semi-hard Alp cheese weighing 7–9 kg, made on the alpine pasture during the season.

entries.heading: Scotta (siero di scotta; ricotta di scotta)
entries.what: the whey left over from cheese making, reheated to make a second curd; the page calls it a cheese-making residue.

entries.heading: Scottish tablet
entries.what: crystalline Scottish sweet of sugar, condensed milk and butter.

entries.heading: Scuete frante
entries.what: Crumbled whey cheese from Friuli.

entries.heading: Sea moss punch (milk)
entries.what: a cooling, spiced sea-moss drink described as Trinidad's answer to the summer milkshake.

entries.heading: Seabird meat soaked in milk
entries.what: Seabird meat is placed in a bowl of milk overnight to extract oil.

entries.heading: Semi-hard cheese (Sri Lankan market)
entries.what: Five semi-hard cheese samples in the 2024 Sri Lankan market survey.

entries.heading: Semicotto Caprino
entries.what: A semi-cooked goat cheese listed among Sardinian cheeses.

entries.heading: Semicotto Ovino
entries.what: A semi-cooked sheep cheese listed among Sardinian cheeses.

entries.heading: Semiduros (mainly Alajuela)
entries.what: White, fairly solid cheeses with holes, usually grated over pasta and other dishes; mainly from Alajuela.

entries.heading: Semifreddo
entries.what: class of semi-frozen desserts, typically ice-cream cakes, semi-frozen custards and some fruit tarts. Listed as Italian.

entries.heading: Semolina and jaggery pudding
entries.what: Less common dessert of semolina, jaggery and milk, flavoured with cinnamon, nutmeg and vanilla.

entries.heading: Semuda (PAT)
entries.what: a cheese from the Como area used in polenta uncia (a traditional polenta dish).

entries.heading: Sepet peyniri (basket cheese, kelle peyniri)
entries.what: a Turkish cheese of the Aegean region; fresh versions unsalted, dry versions mildly salted; seaside versions around Karaburun, Çeşme and Ayvalık are called kelle cheese.

entries.heading: Ser podpuszczkowy dojrzewający (farm rennet cheese, cow and goat)
entries.what: A traditional Polish rennet cheese made by small farms. Sold in farm shops and farmers' markets.

entries.heading: Séras (Séras; Sérai; whey cheese)
entries.what: A whey cheese of Valle d'Aosta made from the residual whey of Fontina or Toma production, eaten fresh or salted and smoke-aged. Its name comes from the Franco-Provençal sérai, from Latin serum ("whey"); it is mentioned in Pantaleone da Conf

entries.heading: Sericaia (sericá, siricaia)
entries.what: An Alentejo sweet, between a pudding and a cake, made from milk, eggs, sugar, flour, cinnamon, lemon and salt.

entries.heading: Serradura (layered cream and biscuit dessert; Macanese)
entries.what: a Portuguese-origin dessert that became famous in Macau, when Macau was under Portuguese colonial rule.

entries.heading: Serrat (Formatge serrat; serrat d'ovella)
entries.what: A cylindrical Pyrenean cheese with a light rind and a compact, fat-rich, intensely flavoured interior that turns slightly spicy with age. The name means "closed-grained" because the interior has no holes.

entries.heading: Serrenti Su Entu
entries.what: One of 16 lesser-known Sardinian cheeses, made by Caseificio Murtas (Silius).

entries.heading: Serwatka drinks (whey drinks)
entries.what: Whey (serwatka), the liquid left from cheese or casein production, can be made into whey-based milk drinks.

name: Set yoghurt from indigenous cow milk

entries.heading: Set yoghurt from indigenous cow milk (Thamankaduwa White and Lankan cattle)
entries.what: Set yoghurt from the milk of two Sri Lankan indigenous cattle types, compared with Friesian and Jersey milk. The abstract reports higher firmness and cohesiveness in the indigenous-milk yoghurts.

name: Set yoghurt, stabilised with gelatin or Dawul Kurundu leaf

entries.heading: Set yoghurt, stabilised with gelatin or Dawul Kurundu leaf (Sri Lanka, research formulation)
entries.what: Set yoghurt that the study describes as popular among children and adults in Sri Lanka. It tests Dawul Kurundu (Neolitsea involucrata) leaf extract as a plant stabiliser against 0.6% gelatin, the usual stabiliser; 0.8% extract gave the leas

entries.heading: Šėta cheese (Šėtos sūris)
entries.what: A cheese famous in the interwar period, made in a dairy at Šėta (the "sūrinė", cheese house).

entries.heading: Sethemi
entries.what: South African spontaneously fermented milk, traditionally made in gourds and clay pots.

entries.heading: Sextner Almkäse (Formaggio di montagna di Sesto)
entries.what: A mountain cheese from Sesto (Val Pusteria), about 7 kg, cylindrical.

entries.heading: Sfela (Σφέλα; PDO)
entries.what: A protected white brined cheese of the southern Peloponnese, made in Messinia and Laconia.

entries.heading: Sfela Messinias and Lakonias (Σφέλα; Π.Ο.Π.)
entries.what: Cheese from Messinia and Laconia (Peloponnese); PDO.

entries.heading: Sfela touloumotiri (Σφέλα τουλουμοτύρι; non-PDO artisanal variant)
entries.what: A non-PDO artisanal variant of Sfela, studied alongside the PDO industrial cheese.

entries.heading: Sgushchyonka / varenaya sgushchyonka (сгущённое молоко, сгущёнка; варёная сгущёнка)
entries.what: Sweetened condensed milk, colloquially "sgushchyonka" in Russia, industrial since 1932 (Mikoyan initiative). Boiled version, варёная сгущёнка, is brown, used as cream, sauce and baking filling.

entries.heading: Sh'ayriyah (شعيرية; milk vermicelli dessert)
entries.what: Vermicelli cooked in ghee, then soaked in a sweet milk mixture.

entries.heading: Shahi haleeb (شاهي حليب; shai adeni, shai mulaban) (Yemeni milk tea)
entries.what: very sweet Yemeni milk tea, "Shahi haleeb, Shai Adeni, or shai mulaban". Popular in Yemen and parts of the Arabian Peninsula.

entries.heading: Shahi tukra (bread pudding)
entries.what: Fried bread in milk, sugar and spices; Mughal-era dish that is now a festive staple in Pakistan.

entries.heading: Shakreyyeh / laban emmo (شقريّة / لبن عمو)
entries.what: a less ceremonial urban version of mansaf, using fresh (not dried) yoghurt in place of jameed, sometimes with poultry. Common in Palestine.

entries.heading: Shanina / shaneeneh (الشنينة; شنينة)
entries.what: a cold, salty-sour drink made from aged goat-milk yoghurt, the Jordanian cousin of ayran and doogh

entries.heading: Shar tos (шар тос; yellow butter, "yellow oil")
entries.what: Yellow butter oil made by gently melting white butter; a key ingredient of suutei tsai. Yak butter aged three years is considered medicinal.

entries.heading: Sheep and goat milk, raw (leite de ovelha, leite de cabra)
entries.what: Raw sheep and goat milk, mainly for PDO cheeses in Portugal; a small share goes into requeijão whey.

entries.heading: Sheep butter from žinčica (ovčie maslo)
entries.what: Butter made from some of the žinčica (whey) production, per the Slovak article.

entries.heading: Sheep ghee (molten sheep ghee)
entries.what: molten sheep ghee served with asida.

name: Sheep milk and katun summer dairy

entries.heading: Sheep milk and katun summer dairy (katun; katunski sir/kajmak)
entries.what: katuns are summer mountain pastures where livestock are milked, mainly sheep, and where dairy is made. The products are grouped as bijeli mrs ("white food") and include kajmak, butter, sour milk and cheese.

entries.heading: Sheer berinj and sheer khurma (milk puddings)
entries.what: sheer berinj is a rice pudding (per Afghan cuisine article); sheer khurma is named in the same list with no description.

entries.heading: Sheer khurma (vermicelli milk pudding for Eid)
entries.what: Vermicelli pudding made for Eid, named "milk and dates" in Persian.

entries.heading: Sheer yakh (Afghan ice cream; a disappearing dish)
entries.what: Afghan ice cream ("a traditional ice cream from Afghanistan"), listed in the Afghan cuisine article and sold in summer ice-cream shops called shir yakh feroshi.

entries.heading: Sheermal (saffron milk bread)
entries.what: Leavened sweet bread, saffron and cardamom flavoured, of Persian origin; brought to Pakistan after Partition.

entries.heading: Sheldon's cream soda (1852 recipe)
entries.what: A 1852 US recipe for cream soda made with egg and milk, from the Michigan Farmer.

entries.heading: Shellal
entries.what: A white, braided, very salty cheese flavoured with mahlab.

entries.heading: Shimiin arkhi (шимийн архи; "milk vodka", distilled dairy spirit)
entries.what: A distilled spirit made from fermented milk, most often by herding families for their own use; the name means "milk arkhi". Mostly rural and home-made; homemade versions are shared with city relatives.

entries.heading: Shir rogho (Hazara; hot milk tea with butter)
entries.what: hot milk tea with butter added, a drink in Hazara cuisine.

entries.heading: Shira shapik (Chitral milk, bread and butter-oil dish)
entries.what: A Chitrali dish listed in the Chitrali cuisine article's references (a 1998 census source), described as "Made of milk, bread & butteroil."

entries.heading: Shosha (Tibetan cream-skin cheese, also churul)
entries.what: A Tibetan cheese said to resemble Limburger in flavour.

entries.heading: Shredded cheddar and cheddar (Baladna brand, industrial)
entries.what: Industrial cheddar, shredded, and a shredded cheddar-and-mozzarella blend, sold under the Baladna brand in Qatar.

entries.heading: Shredded mozzarella (Baladna brand, industrial)
entries.what: Industrial shredded mozzarella sold in Qatar under the Baladna brand, in light and standard versions.

entries.heading: Shrikhand (श्रीखंड; shikharini)
entries.what: Sweet strained yoghurt, served with puri or in a thali. Gujarat and Maharashtra both claim its origin; the historical name is shikharini (linked to about 500 BC).

entries.heading: Shropshire Blue
entries.what: An orange-coloured English blue cheese, sharper and creamier than Stilton, with a tangy aroma.

entries.heading: Sierra de Albarracín (pure sheep cheeses)
entries.what: a range of pure sheep cheeses from Albarracín (Teruel); named one of the most awarded dairies in Aragón.

entries.heading: Sikarni (सिकर्नी)
entries.what: A dahi-based drink in Nepali cuisine, named alongside raita and lassi.

entries.heading: Silifke yoğurdu (Silifke yoghurt)
entries.what: a goat-milk yoghurt from Silifke, Mersin, with EU protected geographical indication status (per review).

entries.heading: Siliqua L'Aigos
entries.what: One of 16 lesser-known Sardinian cheeses, made by Armentizia Moderna.

entries.heading: Silivri yoğurdu (Silivri yoghurt)
entries.what: a yoghurt named after Silivri, Istanbul.

entries.heading: Simpoukoukira Leonidiou (Σιμπουκουκίρα Λεωνιδίου)
entries.what: Leonidio (Peloponnese) cheese; no details.

entries.heading: Single and double cream
entries.what: Liquid cream sold as single cream and double cream by the Isle of Man Creamery.

entries.heading: Single Gloucester
entries.what: The lower-fat, lighter version of Double Gloucester.

entries.heading: Sinnai Caprotto
entries.what: One of 16 lesser-known Sardinian cheeses, made by Caseificio Vergara.

entries.heading: Sir Laurier d'Arthabaska (Centre-du-Québec)
entries.what: A soft, very fruity cheese named after Sir Wilfrid Laurier, Canada's first French-Canadian prime minister.

entries.heading: Sirevi Vindija (Vindija cheese range)
