entries.what: the cheese range of Vindija (Varaždin), listed as "Sirevi" on the company site and sold as "Sirevi Vindija"

entries.heading: Sitaka (σιτάκα; Kasos)
entries.what: a Kasos cheese with a gently sour finish.

entries.heading: Sitaka Kasou and Karpathou (Σιτάκα Κάσου και Καρπάθου)
entries.what: Kasos and Karpathos cheese; no details.

entries.heading: Sitfubi (fresh milk cooked with cornmeal)
entries.what: a Swazi dish of fresh milk cooked and mixed with cornmeal.

entries.heading: Sjenički kravlji sir (Sjenica cow's cheese)
entries.what: a white brined cheese from the Pešter plateau, produced year-round

entries.heading: Sjenički ovčiji sir (Sjenica sheep's cheese)
entries.what: the seasonal sheep-milk version of the Sjenica white brined cheese; served cold

entries.heading: Skabeputra (скабэпутра; skabeputra)
entries.what: A soup of potatoes, beets, groats and wild pears, poured over with sour milk.

entries.heading: Skim milk powder
entries.what: Milk with the fat removed, dried to powder.

entries.heading: Skimmed cow's milk with lahoh (Taiz)
entries.what: skimmed cow's milk added to lahoh batter in Taiz, per the flatbread review.

entries.heading: Skjørost (skyr; surmjølkost)
entries.what: a traditional Norwegian sour-milk cheese; associated with the Røros area, served with tjukkmjølk, rømme, sometimes a little sugar, with cured meats (spekemat).

entries.heading: Skólajógúrt (school yoghurt)
entries.what: A yoghurt product from Mjólkursamsalan, no longer produced.

entries.heading: Skopelos goat's milk
entries.what: milk from the Skopelos, an indigenous Greek dairy goat breed adapted to dry, hot climates. In Greece it is used mainly for traditional cheeses.

entries.heading: Skotyri Iou (Σκοτύρι Ίου)
entries.what: Ios cheese; no details.

entries.heading: Skuta (true skuta; prava skuta)
entries.what: Fresh whey cheese; a by-product of cheesemaking, eaten fresh or warm.

entries.heading: Skuta (curd)
entries.what: Soft fresh curd made from coagulated milk; described as a dairy product, not a cheese, on the Slovene disambiguation page.

entries.heading: Skutni sir (curd cheese)
entries.what: Mild, grainy curd cheese, sometimes with cream, sold in jars; the sibling of prava skuta.

entries.heading: Sky juice (Bahamian sky juice; sky juice)
entries.what: A Bahamian drink whose dairy base is condensed or evaporated milk, mixed with a coconut base and usually gin (rum may be substituted). Optional nutmeg and cinnamon.

entries.heading: Skyrhræringur (skyr porridge)
entries.what: Porridge mixed with skyr to form a dish.

entries.heading: Slattato
entries.what: A soft, fresh cow's-milk cheese from the Montefeltro, made from October to March. Eaten about a week after production. Traditionally sold wrapped in fig or cabbage leaves.

entries.heading: Sliced cheese, sold at Svalbardbutikken (skivet ost; kind unstated)
entries.what: A sliced cheese on sale in Longyearbyen's general store, listed among its fresh goods. The page names no brand or variety.

entries.heading: Smen / Dhan (fermented butter; Dhan in Algeria)
entries.what: A rancid-flavoured, aged butter made in households. Used to flavour traditional dishes, meat and pastries, and in traditional medicine.

entries.heading: Smetannyk (сметанник; sour-cream cake)
entries.what: Sponge-style cake with a whipped sour-cream and sugar cream, often vanilla; layers may be half cocoa-mixed, giving striped slices. Variants add rum, dried fruit, jam or condensed milk.

name: Smoked and butter cheeses on the register

entries.heading: Smoked and butter cheeses on the register (Raucherkäse, Butterkäse Lagundo)
entries.what: Named on the register as smoked and butter-style cheeses from the Province of Bolzano. PAT.

entries.heading: Smoked braided string cheese (Estonian name uncertain; file name suggests "suitsujuust")
entries.what: a supermarket snack; firmer and chewier than similar cheese abroad.

entries.heading: Smoked Cheddar (King Island Dairy, Tasmania)
entries.what: A King Island Dairy cheddar listed as "Smoked Cheddar".

name: Smoked cheese of Áliva and Pido

entries.heading: Smoked cheese of Áliva and Pido (quesos ahumados de Áliva, quesos de Áliva)
entries.what: smoked cheeses from the Áliva and Pido areas of the Picos de Europa / Cantabria; named as examples of Cantabrian smoked cheeses.

entries.heading: Smørolje (butter oil)
entries.what: a product made from cream or from melted butter, with nearly all water and non-fat solids removed; 99.9 % milk fat (butter is 83 %). Used for frying, rømmegrøt, béarnaise, soups and glazing; smoke point 182 °C, melts at 30–32 °C, sets at 18

entries.heading: Smotana (cream; kyslá smotana = sour cream)
entries.what: Cream and sour cream are staple ingredients in Slovak cooking.

entries.heading: Smurostur (spreadable cheese; bacon, mushroom and ham)
entries.what: Spreadable cheese sold by Mjólkursamsalan in bulk, in flavours with bacon, mushroom or ham spread.

entries.heading: Smyr (buttery spread)
entries.what: A softer spread for bread, sauces and cooking, sold by MBM. Per 100 g: about 64 g fat, of which 46 g saturated.

entries.heading: Snackies (yoghurt range)
entries.what: A product listed under the yoghurt range of Namibia Dairies.

entries.heading: Snezhanka (Снежанка) — dry tarator, milk salad
entries.what: a thick, dry yoghurt salad with no added water; also called dry tarator or milk salad (млечна салата)

entries.heading: Snezhok (снежок)
entries.what: Soviet-era sweet sour-milk drink, mass-produced across the CIS; developed in the USSR in the 1960s as a substitute for Bulgarian yoghurt, which was not popular there.

entries.heading: Snøfrisk
entries.what: fresh, tart, mild goat-flavoured cream cheese in a triangular plastic box; natural and four flavours (dill, red onion and thyme, grilled pepper, chanterelle).

entries.heading: Snow Brand 6P (雪印 6P チーズ, 6P)
entries.what: Snow Brand's best-known processed cheese, mass-produced from 1954, part of the company's long-standing goal of processed cheese suited to Japanese tastes.

name: Snow Brand Camembert
names: 雪印 カマンベール

entries.heading: Snow Brand Camembert (雪印 カマンベール)
entries.what: A Hokkaido camembert from Megmilk Snow Brand, sold since 1962.

entries.heading: Snow Brand Hokkaido 100 Gouda (Gouda Crush; Japanese name not in sources)
entries.what: A longer-aged gouda from Megmilk Snow Brand, made from Hokkaido raw milk and aimed at cooking.

entries.heading: Snow White (雪白)
entries.what: Sprite or 7 Up with vanilla ice cream.

entries.heading: So (蘇, historical dairy product)
entries.what: A dairy product made in Japan from the Asuka period; the court ordered its production in 700. It is considered a kind of cheese by Japanese sources.

entries.heading: So (蘇, そ; also 酥)
entries.what: An ancient Japanese milk product, reportedly made by solidifying layers of milk skin; it was produced by the imperial household office (Tennyakuryo) and given to emperors. It is listed as the stage before daigo in the Mahāparinirvāṇa Sūtra

entries.heading: Soap Fulani
entries.what: Named in the 2019 study as one of the dairy foods in local diets; no description.

entries.heading: Sobia (سوبيا; subia)
entries.what: Egyptian cold rice drink with milk, coconut, sugar and vanilla.

entries.heading: Soda gembira
entries.what: A cold drink of soda water, sweetened condensed milk, syrup and ice, served in hot weather and popular with young people.

entries.heading: Soft cheese (Sri Lankan market)
entries.what: Three soft cheese samples in the 2024 Sri Lankan market survey.

entries.heading: Soft cheese with flavour, 125 g (Obour Land)
entries.what: Obour Land soft cheeses in 125 g packs, each with a flavour: roumy (Rumi), cheddar, pastrami, bramilly and flamank.

entries.heading: Soft chhurpi (नरम छुर्पी)
entries.what: The soft stage of chhurpi: white, mild, often slightly fermented for tang. Eaten as a protein-rich vegetable substitute.

entries.heading: Soft sweet curds
entries.what: Soft sweet curds were a staple of Gaelic Ireland. Pressed curd, táth, is compared to paneer or cottage cheese and is treated as cheese, so it is not covered here.

entries.heading: Sõir
entries.what: traditional Estonian dish from cottage cheese, eggs, cream and caraway, pressed in cloth. Made mainly in Võrumaa, Setomaa and South Tartumaa.

entries.heading: Sõir (milk, cottage cheese and egg mixture)
entries.what: a cooked mixture of milk, cottage cheese and eggs (Estonian cuisine page)

entries.heading: Söla (Tumma, Sola delle Alpi Marittime; Alpi Marittime)
entries.what: a sheep's-milk cheese of the Alpi Marittime, known in Liguria as Sola or Tumma.

entries.heading: Somali milk tea (shaah cadeeys)
entries.what: Breakfast tea served with milk added after brewing.

entries.heading: Sombi (sweet milk-rice soup; coconut rice pudding)
entries.what: A sweet milk-rice soup in Senegal, served as a dish, with a coconut-rice pudding version in the cited recipe.

entries.heading: Sopi (drinking yoghurt)
entries.what: A drinking yoghurt with a fresh, sour taste; flavours strawberry, raspberry/blueberry/blackcurrant, vanilla and tropical. Per 100 g: 0.5 g fat, 2.9 g protein.

entries.heading: Soprole (brand range: yoghurt, liquid milk, desserts, butter, manjar, probiotics)
entries.what: Chilean dairy company. Its Spanish Wikipedia article says: "Bajo la marca Soprole, produce y comercializa yogur, leche líquida, postres, mantequilla, manjar y probióticos."

entries.heading: Şor (şor, salted curd; Azerbaijani)
entries.what: Salted kəsmik, the curd left after buttermilk (ayran) is strained.

entries.heading: Şor (salted kəsmik)
entries.what: salted kəsmik ("salted curd"); kəsmik is made from qatıq or ayran.

entries.heading: Sorbetes (Filipino ice cream; "dirty ice cream")
entries.what: Traditional Filipino ice cream sold by street vendors (sorbeteros) from wooden pushcarts, served in a cone, wafer or pandesal. Early flavours included mantecado (butter), ube, queso helado (cheese), pinipig, melon, mango, jackfruit, avocado

entries.heading: Sorkeh (sorke, surke — soft Syrian cheese; distinct from Shanklish in this study)
entries.what: A soft Syrian cheese analysed in a 2013 Syrian university study as a traditional product alongside Akawi, Medaffarah and Shankalish.

entries.heading: Sot la trape
entries.what: Local Friulian cheese name (rendered "sot la trape" in the EN list).

entries.heading: Soumaintrain
entries.what: A cheese named after the Yonne commune of Soumaintrain.

entries.heading: Sour and sweet cream (кисела павлака; слатка павлака)
entries.what: Cream skimmed from milk. Sweet cream (about 24% fat) is skimmed before souring and used for whipping, ice cream, cooking cream and sauces; sour cream is skimmed later in souring and has 10–20% fat.

entries.heading: Sour butter (масла; masla)
entries.what: Butter used with sour cream to enrich soups and porridges; less common than tvarog in the past. Sour butter from the former Dzisna county was exported to Britain and was the most expensive variety there until World War I.

entries.heading: Sour goat milk (Socotra)
entries.what: sour goat milk, eaten on its own or with rice, per the Socotra goat study.

entries.heading: Sour milk products
entries.what: A sour milk product in the yoghurt and sour milk category. Named only as a category; no product name given.

entries.heading: Soured cream (for butter-making)
entries.what: Cream allowed to sour before churning into butter.

name: Soured or fresh zebu milk in vegetable dishes

entries.heading: Soured or fresh zebu milk in vegetable dishes
entries.what: Fresh or soured zebu milk is often cooked into vegetable side dishes in the arid interior south and west.

entries.heading: Sourki (Musa Dagh)
entries.what: A pyramid-shaped curd cheese of spices and curds, dried and then stored until it goes mouldy.

entries.heading: Spas
entries.what: A traditional Armenian soup built on matsun, served warm in winter and chilled in summer. Matsun is the only core dairy ingredient; butter is added as well.

entries.heading: Spearmint flavoured milk (Western Australia)
entries.what: A green-coloured, spearmint-flavoured milk drink, described as a West Australian treat.

entries.heading: Spinach matsoni (ისპანახი მაწვნით)
entries.what: a Georgian salad of cooked spinach mixed with matsoni yoghurt.

entries.heading: Spisestedet Sarfalik restaurant cheeses (Greenlandic cheese, Nuuk; cheese names not given)
entries.what: The restaurant's first Greenlandic cheeses, "made of organic cow's or sheep's milk". The blue cheese is made with lingonberry and crowberry; the sheep's milk cheese is flavoured with thyme and parsley from Greenland.

entries.heading: Sportsajt
entries.what: a fresh, lactic-acid curd cheese listed without description.

entries.heading: Spray cheese (Easy Cheese)
entries.what: A spray cheese introduced in mid-20th-century novelty packaging.

entries.heading: Spreadable and fresh cheese (Valio Viola type)
entries.what: Industrial fresh cheese spreads sold in Finland.

entries.heading: Squarquaglione dei Monti Lepini (PAT)
entries.what: A sheep cheese from the Monti Lepini.

entries.heading: St. Severin (Schärdinger brand)
entries.what: a Schärdinger cheese brand named in the company history

entries.heading: Staazer
entries.what: Austrian semi-hard cheese named in the English list.

entries.heading: Stagionato di bufala di Formello (PAT)
entries.what: An aged buffalo cheese from Formello.

entries.heading: Staka Kritis (Στάκα Κρήτης)
entries.what: Cretan cheese; no details.

entries.heading: Steamed milk soup (蒸牛奶 tong sui)
entries.what: A traditional tong sui dessert listed with red bean, mung bean, black sesame and sago.

entries.heading: Stelvio (Stilfser)
entries.what: A DOP cheese from South Tyrol, aged at least 60 days, with a characteristic flavour from brushing with a salt solution containing bacteria.

entries.heading: Sterilised full cream milk (Steri Milk; Dairibord; Dairibord Sterilised Full Cream Milk)
entries.what: A packaged full-cream milk sold by Dairibord as "Sterilised Full Cream Milk", listed under the "Steri Milk" category. Dairibord opened a factory making sterilised milk "steri" at Chipinge in 1983.

entries.heading: Sterilised milk (sterilized milk)
entries.what: Sterilised milk was one of the four milk and cheese products sampled in Kuwaiti hospitals for antibiotic residues (50 samples).

entries.heading: Sterilized cream, Arla (Manama plant)
entries.what: sterilized cream made at Arla Foods' plant in Manama, Bahrain.

entries.heading: Stracchino / Crescenza (Stracchino; crescenza)
entries.what: a soft, square, rindless cheese eaten very young, with a creamy texture and mild, slightly tangy flavour. Also called crescenza.

entries.heading: Stracchino Bronzone (PAT)
entries.what: a fresh, soft Lombard stracchino.

entries.heading: Stracchino di capra (PAT)
entries.what: A goat stracchino.

entries.heading: Strachitunt (Strachitunt DOP)
entries.what: a DOP blue cheese from Lombardy; the Lombard cuisine article lists it among the DOP cheeses.

entries.heading: Stracon (Stracón)
entries.what: A cow's-milk cheese from the Veronese area between Monte Baldo and the Lessinia. The name is a Veronese dialect word for "very tired", because the milk of cows on the long walk to pasture was made into cheese on the way.

entries.heading: Strained Greek yogurt (giaourti; strangistó giaoúrti)
entries.what: yogurt thickened by draining off most of its whey, keeping its sour taste. Greek cuisine eats it with honey, often with walnuts, and it is the base of tzatziki.

entries.heading: Strathdon Blue (Strathdon Blue; cow's milk blue)
entries.what: A creamy, semi-soft, full-fat blue cheese from Tain, Ross-shire, influenced by Bleu d'Auvergne, with a tangy flavour.

entries.heading: Strazzatella silana (Strazzatella silana)
entries.what: A Sila cheese listed for Calabria.

entries.heading: String cheese
entries.what: A snack-size stretched cheese, often blended with cheddar.

entries.heading: Stutenmilch (mare milk; with Kumys)
entries.what: milk of a mare in lactation. Lower in fat, protein and casein than cow milk, higher in lactose, and in some ways similar to human milk. Sold fresh, frozen or as freeze-dried powder.

entries.heading: Su Zinnibiri
entries.what: One of 16 lesser-known Sardinian cheeses, made by Caseificio Garau.

entries.heading: Sữa đặc (sweetened and unsweetened condensed/evaporated milk)
entries.what: Sweetened condensed milk (sữa đặc có đường) and unsweetened evaporated milk (sữa bay hơi, sữa đặc không đường). Condensed milk is a key ingredient in Vietnamese coffee and desserts.

entries.heading: Sữa tươi (fresh pasteurised milk)
entries.what: Liquid milk sold as fresh (tươi) milk; most 'fresh' milk on sale is reportedly made from milk powder.

entries.heading: Subenhara (Subenhara-kaas; Dutch, dessert cheese)
entries.what: A dessert cheese named after Zevenaar (Gelderland). Discontinued.

entries.heading: Submarino (remo)
entries.what: hot milk with a chocolate bar melted into it. Began in Argentina in the early 1900s and is traditional in Uruguay too. A winter drink, typically served in a tall glass in a metal holder.

entries.heading: Sucre à la crème (sugar cream)
entries.what: a Quebec confection of cream, sugar and brown sugar; butter, maple syrup, nuts, vanilla or chocolate are sometimes added. Originally made with cream and maple sugar.

entries.heading: Südlü plov (milk pilaf)
entries.what: plov cooked in milk, no meat, with butter, raisins, dates, honey and cream.

entries.heading: Suero costeño (suero atollabuey, suero costeño; "fermented sour cream")
entries.what: A traditional fermented dairy product of Colombia's Caribbean coast. Creamy, white, lumpy, with a sour/salty taste; used mainly as a dressing or sauce, for example with arroz de lisa in Barranquilla and with bollos.

entries.heading: Suero de leche agria (whey from leche agria)
entries.what: The lower layer that separates from leche agria.

entries.heading: Sugar pie (tarte au sucre)
entries.what: a Quebec classic of flour, butter and sugar (beet or brown), sometimes with maple syrup.

name: Suluguni / Sulguni — Georgian; Russian production only

entries.heading: Suluguni / Sulguni — Georgian; Russian production only
entries.what: Georgian cheese from Samegrelo/Svaneti; Georgia registered it as a national product in 2011 and as a geographical indication in 2012.

entries.heading: Summarskál (summer skál, soured milk drink)
entries.what: A light summer drink of soured milk, lemon, sugar and vanilla. Per 100 g: 67 kcal, 2.9 g protein, 1.3 g fat. Keeps 2–3 days chilled once opened.

entries.heading: Sunsation strawberry dairy fruit mix
entries.what: A Namibia Dairies "dairy fruit mix" under the Sunsation brand, with a new strawberry flavour described as "a refreshing dairy fruit mix the whole family will love".

entries.heading: Super Milk (Dairibord)
entries.what: A Dairibord milk product listed as "Super Milk".

entries.heading: Sūreliai (Lithuanian curd snacks)
entries.what: a curd-based snack; common in Lithuania and the Baltics, and in Russia, Belarus, Ukraine and Kazakhstan under the name "curd snack".

entries.heading: Suripico (suripico; sweet from curdled milk)
entries.what: A sweet made from curdled milk with cane honey and spices.

entries.heading: Surti paneer (Surat, Gujarat)
entries.what: A paneer from Surat, Gujarat, drained then ripened in whey.

entries.heading: Sušená syrovátka (dried whey)
entries.what: Dried whey made as a by-product of cheese and tvaroh production.

entries.heading: Suspiro a la limeña (suspiro limeño)
entries.what: A Lima dessert: a creamy milk-based base topped with a port-wine meringue and a dusting of cinnamon. Its name is traced to the poet José Gálvez Barrenechea's description.

entries.heading: Sussa / Suusac (fermented camel milk)
entries.what: fermented camel milk eaten by pastoral communities in the border areas of Somalia, Kenya and Ethiopia, and in arid and semi-arid parts of Eastern Africa.

entries.heading: Susu bubuk (powdered milk), Frisian Flag Full Cream Energo and Kompleta
entries.what: Milk powder sold under the Frisian Flag brand: Full Cream Energo (repackaged as Full Cream Energo in 2025), Kompleta Cokelat and Kompleta Vanilla.

entries.heading: Susu cair perisa (flavoured liquid milk), Frisian Flag Energo and Nutribrain
entries.what: Frisian Flag liquid milk: Full Cream, Coconut Delight, Strawberry, Sweet Delight, Swiss Chocolate, several low-fat flavours, Susu Sereal (cokelat and kopi), Nutribrain (cokelat, plain, stroberi), Energo (cokelat, stroberi) and Energo+ (matc

entries.heading: Susu formula bayi dan balita (infant and toddler milk), Frisian Flag Primamum, Primamil and Primagro
entries.what: Frisian Flag products for mothers and young children: Primamum Cokelat; Primamil 0–6 and 6–12 bulan; Primagro 1+ and 3+ (chocolate, honey and vanilla flavours).

entries.heading: Süt (сүт; boiled milk)
entries.what: Boiled milk, the base for many Kazakh dairy products.

entries.heading: Süt helvası (milk halva)
entries.what: a halva from Bursa made from raw cow milk, sugar, flour and butter, with pine nut and vanilla optionally.

entries.heading: Suusac (suusa; fermented camel milk)
entries.what: Traditional fermented camel milk named suusac, recorded for Somalia alongside Kenya and Ethiopia.

entries.heading: Suutei tsai (сүүтэй цай; salt milk tea, "suutei tsai")
entries.what: The salty milk tea of Mongolia, one of the most common drinks; served to every visitor to a ger and drunk with meals and through the day; some regions add rice or small dumplings to make it a soup.

entries.heading: Suytlash (süýtlaş; süýtli unaş; milk vermicelli pudding)
entries.what: Vermicelli pudding made with milk, served as the second course at wedding feasts. Some variants use rice instead of vermicelli. Turkmen cookbooks file it under soups.

entries.heading: Suzbe (сүзбе)
entries.what: Soft curd from strained sour milk.

entries.heading: Suzma / suzmo (сузьма)
entries.what: Concentrated, drained yoghurt. The Kyrgyz diet paper lists "suzmo (concentrated yogurt)" and "concentrated ayran (suzmo)" among milk products.

entries.heading: Süzmə (strained curd; Azerbaijani)
entries.what: A soft curd made by straining qatıq.

entries.heading: Süzmə (strained qatıq)
entries.what: qatıq strained to remove liquid; thick. Dried süzmə becomes qurut.

entries.heading: Șvaițer
entries.what: A Swiss-style cheese in Romanian (from Schweizer Käse), made industrially; the redirect target is the Emmental article.

entries.heading: Svecia
entries.what: Swedish semi-hard cow's-milk cheese with small irregular holes and a mildly acidic taste.

entries.heading: Šveicariškas sūris (Swiss-type cheese, made in Lithuania before WWI)
entries.what: A Swiss-type cheese made by manor dairies in Lithuania before WWI.

entries.heading: Sveita kúmenostur (kúmen cheese)
entries.what: A cheese flavoured with kúmen, sold by Mjólkursamsalan in a 460 g pack.

entries.heading: Sveppaostur (mushroom cheese, small pack)
entries.what: A mushroom cheese sold by Mjólkursamsalan in a small 20 g pack.

entries.heading: Svrljig kačkavalj (svrljiški kačkavalj)
entries.what: a kačkavalj named after Svrljig, linked by the English list to the Kashkaval article

entries.heading: Svrljig white cheese (svrljiški sir)
entries.what: a white brined cheese named after Svrljig, in the Nišava valley

entries.heading: Svrljiški belmuž (belmuž)
entries.what: a warm, very calorie-rich shepherd's dish of cheese cooked with corn flour; served as a starter or breakfast, with sour milk

entries.heading: Sweet and sour yogurt (branded; seven brands sampled)
entries.what: sweet and sour yogurts from seven brands in Bangladesh, sampled in Rangpur, Bogura, Manikganj, Dhaka, Munshiganj, Chattogram and Cox's Bazar (2021 study); the paper also says the samples came from local confectionery shops, so the channel i

entries.heading: Sweetened and evaporated condensed milk (as used in Singapore)
entries.what: concentrated milk used in tea, coffee, bandung and ice kacang; sweetened condensed milk is the traditional milk for teh tarik.

name: Sweetened condensed milk and evaporated milk

entries.heading: Sweetened condensed milk and evaporated milk (as used in local tea culture)
entries.what: concentrated milk products used in the milk teas, coffee and desserts above; widely used in Hong Kong tea culture.

entries.heading: Sweetened condensed milk coffee
entries.what: Coffee served with sweetened condensed milk instead of black, hot or iced. The usual form in urban areas.

name: Sweetened condensed milk in tea and coffee

entries.heading: Sweetened condensed milk in tea and coffee (tinned condensed milk)
entries.what: Tinned condensed milk added to tea and coffee. The source says the cheapest tea and coffee varieties are served this way.

entries.heading: Sweetened condensed milk on cereal
entries.what: condensed milk poured over breakfast cereal to sweeten it

name: Sweetened condensed milk, in coffee and drinks

entries.heading: Sweetened condensed milk, in coffee and drinks
entries.what: Sweetened condensed milk is sold at street-side kiosks, added to black coffee, mixed into hot water as a drink, and eaten with steamed cassava or sweet potatoes in rural areas.

name: Swiss Emmental-style and French Cantal-style cheeses

entries.heading: Swiss Emmental-style and French Cantal-style cheeses (Nepal)
entries.what: European-style cheeses made by small-scale cheesemakers in Langtang and Ilam, Nepal.

entries.heading: Syllabub
entries.what: sweetened cream or milk curdled with wine or cider, sometimes thick enough to eat with a spoon.

entries.heading: Syrniki (сырнікі; syrniki)
entries.what: Fried pancakes of tvorog, flour, eggs and sugar, usually sweet, eaten for breakfast or dessert, with jam, sour cream or butter. Named as Belarusian cuisine dish.

entries.heading: Syrnyky (сирники; quark fritters)
entries.what: Fried fritters made with quark; often eaten with sour cream or jam.

name: Tabletas de leche y de coco

entries.heading: Tabletas de leche y de coco (milk and coconut tablets)
entries.what: a sweet made as tablets from milk and coconut, listed among Honduran sweets.

entries.heading: Tabor
entries.what: Local cheese named "Tabor", listed for the province of Trieste.

entries.heading: Tadj
entries.what: A semi-soft cheese from the Bouira region, wrapped in a branch of rosemary.

entries.heading: Taignon
entries.what: A mountain cheese of raw whole milk, listed under Jura.

entries.heading: Taiwanese cheese foam (nǎi gài, 奶蓋; powdered-cheese foam)
entries.what: a salty-tangy foam served on cold tea, which began at Taiwanese night markets around 2010.

entries.heading: Taiwanese pearl milk tea (珍珠奶茶)
entries.what: Tea with milk plus cooked black tapioca pearls; toppings include pudding, coconut jelly and grass jelly.

entries.heading: Takammart (Takemmart)
entries.what: A Tuareg cheese from Tamanrasset province; "cheese" in the Tamasheq language.

entries.heading: Takesumi (Japanese name not in sources; bamboo-ash cheese)
entries.what: A cheese from Fromagerie Sen in Otaki, about 90 minutes from Tokyo, dusted in bamboo ash, aged on site, shaped like a soft mochi.

entries.heading: Talagani (Ταλαγάνι)
entries.what: Greek semi-hard cheese; no details.

entries.heading: Talattouri (ταλαττούρι; Cypriot tzatziki)
entries.what: A dip served in the meze.

entries.heading: Talesh cheese (Talesh; Persian پنیر تالشی)
entries.what: A traditional cheese from Talesh County, Iran.

entries.heading: Tallaga (artisanal soft white Damietta cheese; Arabic name not in opened sources)
entries.what: An artisanal form of traditional Egyptian soft white Damietta cheese, with a short shelf life.

entries.heading: Tamgout (Fafi Tamgout)
entries.what: An Algerian semi-hard cheese made from raw cow's milk without additives, styled on Vacherin Fribourgeois and a Gruyere and Gouda blend; slogan "a Swiss idea, an Algerian cheese".

entries.heading: Tarkhana
entries.what: A mixture of yoghurt (matzoon) and flour or bulgur, dried and ground to a powder used to thicken soups. Also called a flour and matzoon soup. Found on the English Armenian cuisine page.

entries.heading: Tarkhineh (soup with grain and yogurt)
entries.what: A soup built on grain and yogurt.

entries.heading: Tartaletas de leche
entries.what: a milk-filled pastry dessert named in Guatemalan dessert lists.

entries.heading: Tarte au citron (butter-based lemon tart)
entries.what: A buttery lemon tart, listed as a Monégasque dessert.

entries.heading: Tarte au maton (Grammont tart)
entries.what: A traditional tart from Grammont (Geraardsbergen in Dutch), with a curdled-milk filling; also made around Lessines and Ath. Protected name since 2007: "tarte au maton de Grammont", limited to Grammont and Lierde.

entries.heading: Tasabea (milk and flour porridge)
entries.what: A traditional dish for events, made with milk and water.

name: Tasmanian Heritage and South Cape specialty cheeses

entries.heading: Tasmanian Heritage and South Cape specialty cheeses (Saputo brands)
entries.what: Specialty cheeses under the Tasmanian Heritage and South Cape brands of Saputo Dairy Australia. No individual cheese is named.

entries.heading: Tastee Cheese (canned processed cheese; Tastee)
entries.what: Canned processed cheese made by Dairy Industries Jamaica Limited (DIJL) in Kingston. It is a Jamaican Easter tradition ("bun and cheese"), per the newswire article.

entries.heading: Tatao (rice boiled in milk)
entries.what: Rice boiled in milk and drizzled with honey, eaten as a dessert.

entries.heading: Táth (historic)
entries.what: historic Irish pressed curd, perhaps like paneer or cottage cheese.

entries.heading: Tätmjölk
entries.what: A traditional soured milk variant in which the container is rubbed with sundew or butterwort leaves, which carry protein-degrading enzymes, to thicken the milk.

entries.heading: Tatouillard
entries.what: A soft bloomy-rind cheese listed under the Jura canton.

entries.heading: Taumil (dried milk, Schärdinger)
entries.what: Taumil brand dried milk products made by Schärdinger at Taufkirchen an der Pram

entries.heading: Taupinière de Charente
entries.what: A cheese of the Charente.

entries.heading: Tavë kosi (baked lamb and rice with yoghurt sauce)
entries.what: a baked lamb-and-rice dish topped with a yoghurt and egg sauce; the name means "pan of yoghurt"

entries.heading: Tavuk göğsü (chicken-breast pudding)
entries.what: a milk pudding with very finely shredded chicken breast, giving a chewy texture; Ottoman records from the 1400s.

entries.heading: Teh halia tarik (ginger pulled tea)
entries.what: a teh tarik variant made with ginger tea instead of black tea.

entries.heading: Teh madras (Sabah and Labuan)
entries.what: A tea drink served in three layers: milk at the bottom, black tea in the middle, and foam on top. It is listed as a variant of teh tarik.

entries.heading: Teja (teja iqueña; chocoteja)
entries.what: A dumpling-shaped sweet from Ica filled with manjar blanco and dried fruit or nuts, with a fondant-like sugar shell; a chocolate version is called chocoteja.

entries.heading: Tejbegríz (milk semolina porridge)
entries.what: Porridge of milk and wheat semolina (búzadara), resembling pudding; served to children at breakfast.

entries.heading: Tejberizs (milk rice)
entries.what: Rice porridge cooked in milk; eaten warm or cold as dessert or breakfast.

entries.heading: Tejes málé (milk corn flatbread)
entries.what: Sweet corn flatbread made with milk or soured milk.

entries.heading: Tejleves (milk soup)
entries.what: Sweet milk-based "soup" in several flavours.

entries.heading: Telemea (telemea de Ibănești; de Sibiu; de Argeș; de Brașov; de Carei; de Harghita; de Huedin; de Nucet; de Oaș; de Vâlcea; de Covurlui)
entries.what: The Romanian brined white cheese, national and EU-protected in several regional forms. It is the Romanian relative of feta and its recipe later spread to Greece, Macedonia, Bulgaria and Poland (per cheese.com).

entries.heading: Telemes (Τελεμές)
entries.what: Greek semi-hard cheese; no details.

entries.heading: Teleorman (cașcaval)
entries.what: A Romanian cașcaval variety named in the Romanian cașcaval list; no description given.

entries.heading: Teli (теле)
entries.what: Named in the Russian Turkmen-cuisine article among dairy products. No description found.

entries.heading: Telli
entries.what: Named with Aho and Golot in the Trabzon study; shows elevated lead and mercury in the study.

entries.heading: Tëmbëloriz / sultjash (rice pudding with milk)
entries.what: rice pudding made with milk, rice and cinnamon, optionally with nuts and raisins; Albanian variants also called sultjash or qumësht me oriz

entries.heading: Templais
entries.what: A cheese of the Aquitaine area.

entries.heading: Tenili (ტენილი ყველი) — also Meskhuri Tenili
entries.what: A traditional string cheese from Meskheti (Samtskhe-Javakheti), described as the most complicated of Georgian cheese techniques; the name means "stuffed cheese".

entries.heading: Tennengauer Almkäse
entries.what: Alpine cheese from the Tennengau in Salzburg state.

entries.heading: Ternespiim (colostrum; first milk after calving)
entries.what: milk a cow gives in the first 24–36 hours after calving; light yellow, buttermilk-like taste; more protein and immunoglobulins than normal milk, about half the lactose, nearly twice the dry matter

entries.heading: Tesselse Groene (Texelse Groene; green Texel sheep cheese)
entries.what: A Dutch sheep cheese made for centuries on Texel and also on Wieringen and Terschelling. Exported to several European countries. Its sharp taste is said to come from grass juice in the sheep's droppings.

entries.heading: Testouri (Testouri; Arabic script not given in the sources read)
entries.what: A fresh soft cheese named after the Testour region in northern Tunisia, one of the two most popular fresh cheeses in Tunisia.

entries.heading: Tête de Maure (Tête de Maure; Haitian name for aged Edam)
entries.what: A Dutch-style aged Edam sold and used in Haiti under the name Tête de Maure. The source calls it "Haitian Dutch cheese" and says it is in nearly every Haitian kitchen.

entries.heading: Tête de Moine AOP
entries.what: A semi-hard raw-milk cheese invented by the canons of the Bellelay Abbey, in the Bernese Jura (district of Moutier, commune of Saicourt). Cylindrical, 10–15 cm in diameter, about 850 g on average (up to 2.5 kg).

entries.heading: Tetero
entries.what: A coffee with a lot of milk and little coffee, close to a latte macchiato; the article notes it is wrongly called "café blanco".

entries.heading: Teurgoule (Norman baked rice pudding)
entries.what: A slow-baked Norman rice pudding with milk, rice, sugar and cinnamon; a regional dessert of Lower Normandy.

entries.heading: Težački sir iz maslinove komine
entries.what: a farm cheese made with olive pomace

entries.heading: Thai milk tea (ชาไทย, cha yen)
entries.what: iced tea sweetened with condensed milk, finished with evaporated or whole milk.

entries.heading: Thandai (ठंडाई; sardai)
entries.what: Summer drink with milk, almond, fennel, poppy, watermelon kernel, rose petal, black pepper, cardamom, saffron and sugar; the centrepiece of Holi.

entries.heading: Thick cream (crème maturée)
entries.what: Thick cream sold by Luxlait for culinary preparation; the name suggests a maturing step.

entries.heading: Thick tonga mabisi
entries.what: a thicker variant of tonga mabisi, found in all provinces except Northern. Ranked fourth in popularity in the national survey.

entries.heading: Thollon
entries.what: a raw-milk cow's-milk cheese from Savoie, cylindrical, 40–50 cm across, 8–12 cm high, 5–12 kg, about 30% fat in dry matter. Traditionally a lean family cheese tied to butter-making, not sold widely.

entries.heading: Ti Bénare
entries.what: A soft-paste cheese with a robust character, sold in 150 g.

entries.heading: Ti Tamarin
entries.what: A fine, mild, creamy cheese, sold in 150 g.

entries.heading: Ti'frais (fresh cheese range; Ti frais des Hauts)
entries.what: A fresh cheese range sold in several flavours: nature, Greek-style (à la grecque), chilli (piment), mixed peppers (aux poivres), ginger (gingembre), and garlic and fine herbs (ail / fines herbes). Sold in two-packs as well.

entries.heading: Tibetan butter sweets and pastries (thue, masan, papza mogu, day-see)
entries.what: Thue cake (yak butter, brown sugar, water); masan (tsampa, dry curd cheese, yak butter, sugar); papza mogu (dough balls with melted butter, sugar, dry curd cheese); day-see (sweet rice cooked in unsalted butter with raisins and nuts, served

entries.heading: Tibok-tibok
entries.what: A Kapampangan rice-and-milk pudding from Pampanga, especially popular in Cagayan. Served in squares or diamonds, topped with latík (coconut curds).

entries.heading: Tilsit (Samanlac, Puno)
entries.what: A Tilsit-style cheese made by the Samanlac cooperative in Puno; placed second in the 2024 Internacional category.

entries.heading: Tilžės sūris (Tilsit-type cheese, made in Lithuania before WWI)
entries.what: A cheese type made in Lithuanian manor dairies before World War I. It made up about 78 % of Lithuanian cheese output in that period.

entries.heading: Tinginys ("lazy" dessert; condensed-milk slice)
entries.what: one of the most popular Lithuanian home desserts. Made without cooking.

entries.heading: Tinned (evaporated) and powdered milk
entries.what: Tinned or powdered milk eaten or drunk in urban Ghana; it appears as a named item in the food-habits consumption table of a 2025 study. The same study cites a 1948 protest in Ghana against high prices of imported food, including evaporated

entries.heading: Tintern
entries.what: A soft Welsh Cheddar blend flavoured with fresh chives and shallots.

entries.heading: Tiri flaounas (flaouna cheese; also "flaouna cheese")
entries.what: The traditional cheese of the Cypriot Easter flaouna, a cheese-filled baked pastry also eaten in parts of Greece (Turkish name pilavuna).

entries.heading: Tirkeeran
entries.what: A cheese from Dart Mountain Cheese, County Londonderry.

entries.heading: Tiroler Almkäse / Tiroler Alpkäse (g.U.)
entries.what: Alpine cheese from North and East Tyrol, protected by g.U.

entries.heading: Tiroler Bergkäse (PDO; Tiroler Bergkäse g.U.)
entries.what: Hard alpine cheese from Tyrol, the PDO version of Bergkäse. Non-PDO Bergkäse from Tyrol also exists and differs in starter, rennet and ripening time.

entries.heading: Tiroler Graukäse (g.U.; Tyrolean grey)
entries.what: Strongly sour and sharp cheese from Tyrol that gets sharper as it ripens. The same family as Montafoner Sauerkäse.

entries.heading: Tizian
entries.what: named in the review as a Czech market cheese.

entries.heading: Toblacher Stangenkäse (Stanga di Dobbiaco)
entries.what: A semi-hard cheese that melts like mozzarella; small flaky texture; sweet flavour.

entries.heading: Tokachi Raclette Moor Wash (Japanese name not in sources)
entries.what: A raclette-style cheese made by the Tokachi Raclette Collective (eight makers in Tokachi who standardised local raclette production), aged in a communal cellar and washed with alkaline moor water from local hot springs.

entries.heading: Tolminc (tolminski sir; Formaggio di Tolmino)
entries.what: Round hard cow-milk cheese from the Upper Soča valley (Zgornje Posočje), named after the town of Tolmin; smooth straw-coloured rind, occasional lentil- or pea-sized eyes, sweet and piquant.

entries.heading: Toma brigasca (Tuma; Terra brigasca)
entries.what: the sheep's-milk toma of the Terra brigasca, named in the Ligurian cuisine article.

entries.heading: Toma del lait brusc (Toma bianca alpina)
entries.what: traditional Piedmontese toma and Slow Food presidium.

entries.heading: Toma di Gressoney (Toma di Gressoney; Toma del Gressoney)
entries.what: A summer alpine pasture (alpeggio) cheese of the Valle del Lys, made only in summer, including above 2,200 m. Round, 5–12 cm side height, 15–30 cm across, 2–5 kg.

entries.heading: Toma di Mendatica (Toma di Mendatica dell'Alta Valle Arroscia; Valle Arroscia, Val Roja, province of Imperia)
entries.what: a semi-hard toma from the upper Arroscia valley around Mendatica, in the upper Roja valley and elsewhere in the province of Imperia.

entries.heading: Toma Shiranuka Semi-Hard (トマ・白糠)
entries.what: A semi-hard cheese from Shiranuka Rakueisha, Hokkaido, sold cut into bite-sized pieces.

entries.heading: Tomas peyniri (serto; karın kaymağı)
entries.what: A Turkish cheese, also called serto or karın kaymağı; made in the Eastern Anatolian tulum tradition. Name comes from the Greek word for leather.

entries.heading: Tombea (Slow Food presidium)
entries.what: an alpine cheese from the Bresciano pastures, made from spring to summer and aged very long.

entries.heading: Tome de Belley
entries.what: a small cylindrical goat cheese made in the Ain department.

entries.heading: Tome de Corse
entries.what: Tomme-type cheese from Corsica, listed on the French cheese list under Tommes.

entries.heading: Tome de Rhuys
entries.what: a raw-milk farm cheese of about 1.9 kg and 50% fat, made on the Presqu'île de Rhuys.

entries.heading: Tometta / Tomino
entries.what: small Piedmontese cheeses, many sub-types (asciutto, fresco, di Andrate).

name: Tomini di Bollengo e del Talucco

entries.heading: Tomini di Bollengo e del Talucco
Tomino canavesano (fresco and asciutto)
entries.what: traditional tomino from the Canavese, province of Torino.

entries.heading: Tomme au foin
entries.what: A keeping cheese of 1.5–2 kg, with a taste of hay and walnut, ripened inside a hay-filled meule which keeps the moisture in and protects the cheese.

entries.heading: Tomme blanche (Savoie)
entries.what: Savoyard tomme made from a faisselle of curd.

entries.heading: Tomme crayeuse (Savoie)
entries.what: Savoyard tomme.

entries.heading: Tomme d'Annot (Annot)
entries.what: a tomme from the arrière-pays niçois, from the high pastures of the middle mountains of the Var valley.

entries.heading: Tomme d'Arles (Tomme d'Arles, Camargue)
entries.what: a Camargue sheep cheese, flavoured with Provençal herbs.

entries.heading: Tomme de Champoléon
entries.what: a tomme listed among the specialties of the commune of Champoléon, Hautes-Alpes.

entries.heading: Tomme de l'Ubaye
entries.what: a small cow's-milk tomme from the Ubaye valley, made by the Coopérative Laitière de la Vallée de l'Ubaye (Barcelonnette).

entries.heading: Tomme de la Chaux d'Abel
entries.what: A soft washed-rind tomme from the Jura bernois / Franches-Montagnes area, per the list page.

entries.heading: Tomme de Provence (other names: tomme à l'ancienne; tomme de chèvre de Haute-Provence)
entries.what: a soft goat cheese made across Provence, similar to Banon but without the chestnut-leaf wrap.

entries.heading: Tomme des Reussilles
entries.what: A soft tomme with a fresh taste, listed under Jura; the name points to the Reussilles village.

name: Tomme di Valgrisenche / Toma di Gressoney

entries.heading: Tomme di Valgrisenche / Toma di Gressoney (Tomme de Gressoney)
Tomme du Champsaur (sub-cheeses: Tomme de Tende, Tomme de la Vésubie, Tomme des Vigneaux, Tomme du Queyras, Tomme de l'Ubaye)
entries.what: a family of tommes from the Champsaur and the Alpes-Maritimes and Hautes-Alpes valleys; fresh tomme and a farm tomme de garde.

entries.heading: Tomme du Limousin
entries.what: A tomme of the Limousin.

entries.heading: Tomme du Vent (Taravao, Tahiti)
entries.what: one of the three cheeses named by the Taravao producer.

entries.heading: Tomme fermière des Hautes-Vosges
entries.what: Farm tomme from the Hautes-Vosges, tagged Alsace on the list page.

entries.heading: Tomme fermière du Limousin
entries.what: A farm tomme of the Limousin, a collective brand, named in the 2024 regional contest.

entries.heading: Tomme forte de Savoie
entries.what: traditional Savoyard preparation from old tommes.

entries.heading: Tomme neuchâteloise (Tomme neuchâteloise)
entries.what: A small Neuchâtel cheese with a soft paste and a flowered (bloomy) rind. The source gives no further detail.

entries.heading: Tommes (Mutschli, Tomme du Valais, Tummeli)
entries.what: A small semi-hard cheese of German-speaking Switzerland, Valais, Fribourg and the Romansh area, on Switzerland's list of culinary heritage since 2009. In Valais it is called Tomme and is distinct from the Tomme Vaudoise and Tomme de Savoie.

entries.heading: Tonga mabisi
entries.what: the most common mabisi type, produced in all provinces and by all main ethnic groups interviewed. Named after the Tonga people, who are most associated with the method. Left to ferment to a stiff, sour product.

entries.heading: Topfenknödel (quark dumplings)
entries.what: dumplings whose dough is made from Topfen

entries.heading: Topfenpalatschinken (quark pancakes)
entries.what: well-known variant of the Palatschinke, filled with Topfen (quark) and raisins; especially Viennese cuisine

entries.heading: Tophi (Kalanga sorghum dish with sour milk and melon)
entries.what: A Kalanga dish made from bogobe with sour milk and a cooking melon (lerotse).

entries.heading: Topleniy moloko (топлёное молоко)
entries.what: Milk cooked slowly for hours until brown and thicker; base for ryazhenka and varenets; Russian, Belarusian and Ukrainian traditional dish.

entries.heading: Torrades de Santa Teresa (sweet milk-soaked French toast)
entries.what: Stale bread soaked in milk flavoured with lemon peel, dipped in beaten egg, fried in butter, lard or oil, and sprinkled with sugar and optional cinnamon. Named as a typical Andorran sweet on the official recipe index.

entries.heading: Torrijas, milk version (torrijas con leche; torreja, picatostes in Asturias)
entries.what: Stale bread soaked in warm milk, sugar and cinnamon, coated in egg and fried, then dusted with sugar and cinnamon.

name: Torta de La Serena / Queso de La Serena

entries.heading: Torta de La Serena / Queso de La Serena
entries.what: Thistle-curdled sheep's-milk cheese from La Serena in Extremadura. Eaten young as Torta (spooned from the top) or aged as a harder Queso.

entries.heading: Torta de leche
entries.what: a dessert named in the Nicaraguan cuisine list. No description in any opened source.

entries.heading: Torta de los Barros (Spanish)
entries.what: a cheese from the Tierra de Barros area of Badajoz province, named in the spain.info article.

entries.heading: Torta Titano (wafer cake with cocoa, coffee and hazelnut cream)
entries.what: square wafers stacked in five layers, filled with cocoa, coffee and hazelnut cream, finished with dark chocolate.

entries.heading: Torta Tre Monti (torta di San Marino; wafer cake with milk, cocoa and hazelnut cream)
entries.what: a round wafer cake about 20 cm across, made of round wafers sandwiched with cocoa-and-hazelnut cream in five layers, edge finished with dark chocolate.

entries.heading: Tosap (тосап)
entries.what: Scum scraped from the sides of a metal pot, used as medicine.

entries.heading: Tou (sheep cheese, Son Jover)
entries.what: Named sheep cheese of Son Jover, Mallorca.

entries.heading: Touaregh (Tamasheq/Tuareg name; French "touaregh")
entries.what: A ripened cheese from Mali, named by a review as one of the two ripened cheeses produced in West Africa by traditional methods (the other being tchoukou from Niger).

entries.heading: Toucy
entries.what: a cheese of the Centre.

entries.heading: Touloumisio (τουλουμίσιο; Naxos)
entries.what: aged cheese and myzithra layered together inside a touloumi (goatskin sewn like a wineskin) to mature.

entries.heading: Touloumotyri (Τουλουμοτύρι; Cyclades, Lesbos, Tzia)
entries.what: Greek cheese; no details in the sources.

entries.heading: Toumin dal Mel (toumin del Mel)
entries.what: small cylindrical toma, about 10 cm across, 150–250 g, from Valle Varaita (Cuneo).

entries.heading: Tounjski sir
entries.what: a cheese from Tounj (Karlovac area)

entries.heading: Tournon-Saint-Pierre
entries.what: a Touraine cheese.

entries.heading: Tourrée de l'Aubier
entries.what: A commercial soft cheese, sold under a trademark, from Bénestroff in Moselle.

entries.heading: Trabzon sarı tereyağı (Trabzon yellow butter)
entries.what: a traditional yellow butter from Trabzon's Black Sea region, sold fresh or salted for storage.

entries.heading: Tracle
entries.what: strong cheese spread of Bugey and parts of Savoie (Ain and Savoie).

entries.heading: Traditional fermented milk (unnamed, from lactic acid bacteria study)
entries.what: A traditional Moroccan fermented milk studied as a source of lactic acid bacteria (Enterococcus durans and Lacticaseibacillus casei isolates).

entries.heading: Traditional goat cheese (Serbian household goat cheese, Pajsijević village, central Serbia)
entries.what: a traditional goat cheese made by a countryside household in central Serbia (Pajsijević village, spring 2021)

entries.heading: Traditional Welsh Caerphilly (Caerffili Traddodiadol; Caws Cenarth "Thelma's Original")
entries.what: A pale, almost white, crumbly cheese with a mild, lemon-tinged taste and 45–55% fat. Named for the Caerphilly area, where it was made to feed coal miners. It is Wales's only native cheese, under PGI.

entries.heading: Trappe de Bricquebec
entries.what: named in the French Normandy cuisine article as a Normandy cheese, from the Bricquebec area (Manche). No description opened.

entries.heading: Trappe de la Coudre (trappiste de Laval)
entries.what: Monastic-style cheese, sold alongside the Monastic brand. Made by a dairy company in Entrammes; aged by hand by the Trappist nuns of Notre-Dame de la Coudre in the cellars of their abbey in Laval.

entries.heading: Trappiste de Campénéac
entries.what: a cow's-milk cheese made by the monks of the Abbaye de la Joie Notre-Dame at Campénéac.

entries.heading: Traungold (Schärdinger / Berglandmilch brand)
entries.what: a cheese brand listed for Schärdinger in the 1970s and in the Berglandmilch cheese list

entries.heading: Trecce / Treccia (dura)
entries.what: braided stretched-curd cheese; treccia dura from Basilicata.

name: Treccia di Santa Croce di Magliano

entries.heading: Treccia di Santa Croce di Magliano (treccia; Italian)
entries.what: A traditional Molisan pasta filata cheese made mainly in Santa Croce di Magliano (CB). Its texture is like scamorza. Production is small, about 1,000 kg per year.

entries.heading: Trentingrana (Grana del Trentino)
entries.what: A grana-style cheese from the Province of Trento. It has no DOP of its own; it is a recognised sub-denomination within DOP Grana Padano, with a dedicated mark on the rind.

entries.heading: Triangle cheese (processed cheese; local name not given)
entries.what: a processed cheese, called "triangle cheese" in the source, described as the only cheese found in the Saharawi refugee camps. It was 30.5% of recorded dairy occasions among the surveyed women.

entries.heading: Triantafyllo (τριανταφυλλο; rose cordial)
entries.what: A thick rose syrup, a sweet summer cordial, poured over mahalepi.

entries.heading: Trileçe (three-milk sponge cake)
entries.what: sponge cake soaked in a mixture of three milks until it has a pudding-like texture; topped with caramel, cream or fruit

entries.heading: Triple Cream Brie (King Island Dairy, Tasmania)
entries.what: A King Island Dairy brie product, listed as "Triple Cream Brie".

entries.heading: Trnič
entries.what: Traditional shepherds' cheese shaped like a squat onion, with decorative stamped patterns; very hard, dried and lightly smoked.

entries.heading: Trois cornes
entries.what: A cheese of Poitou and Charentes.

entries.heading: Tronchetto
entries.what: tronchetto alpino (Piacenza), tronchetto di capra (Langhe), tronchetto stagionato (Lombardy).

entries.heading: Truffe de Ventadour
entries.what: A cheese of the Ventadour area, Corrèze.

entries.heading: Trugole
entries.what: a Vicenza cheese.

entries.heading: Tryffel Pecorino (Gotland)
entries.what: A pecorino-type sheep's-milk cheese from Gotland, made with Gotland truffle.

entries.heading: Tsagaan tos (цагаан тос; white butter, "white oil")
entries.what: The first butter of the white foods, churned from cream, used in tea and on bread and in ceremonies.

entries.heading: Tsötsgii (tsötsgii; residue of butter-making)
entries.what: The residue left after white oil is separated; recently eaten mixed with cane sugar and fried millet.

entries.heading: Tude (Xilin Gol, "Mongolian Tude")
entries.what: A dense solid made from Mongolian butter, the dreg from butter-making, and wheat flour; about 21% fat and 8% protein.

entries.heading: Tulum peyniri (tulum; Erzincan Tulum; Kargı Tulum; Ödemiş and İzmir tulum)
entries.what: Traditional Anatolian cheese ripened in a goatskin sack ("tulum"). Regional variants with different character exist (İzmir, Ödemiş, Elazığ, Erzincan). Erzincan Tulum is a PDO.

entries.heading: Tuma (Tuma sicula)
entries.what: Piedmontese tuma and a Sicilian tuma sicula.

entries.heading: Tumazzu
entries.what: a Sicilian cheese with variants di pecura, di vacca.

entries.heading: Tumazzu di vacca (fiore sicano; tumazzu di vacca ccu pipi)
entries.what: a Sicilian cow's-milk cheese, wheels about 30 cm across and 20 cm high, 5–20 kg; often flavoured with chili or black pepper.

entries.heading: Tupí (Formatge de tupí; queso de tupí)
entries.what: A very soft, spreadable, spicy cheese made from serrat-style fresh curd, fermented in an earthenware pot (the tupí) and named after the pot.

entries.heading: Turmada (Cúcuta)
entries.what: A dish from Cúcuta made with cheese, milk and natas (cream), per the Spanish cuisine article.

entries.heading: Túró Rudi (túrórudi)
entries.what: Bar of sweetened túró coated in cocoa coating; developed in Hungary from a Soviet chocolate-coated curd bar (glazirovannij syrok).

entries.heading: Túrógombóc (curd dumplings)
entries.what: Sweet túró dumpling served with sour cream and icing sugar.

entries.heading: Turoš (turoš)
entries.what: a cone-shaped cottage-cheese cheese from Međimurje in northern Croatia

entries.heading: Túrós csusza (curd and noodles)
entries.what: Boiled noodles with curd, crisp bacon and sour cream; sweet version uses sugar.

entries.heading: Turrialba (queso Turrialba; "Turrialba cheese"; "Turrialba type")
entries.what: The most popular cheese of Costa Rica, from Turrialba canton in Cartago province, Valle Central. Mild, slightly salty, unripened. Its origin is protected (denominación de origen, 2012). Its history starts with a Spanish family from La Manch

entries.heading: Turunmaa (Valio)
entries.what: A Finnish cheese type from the Turku archipelago; a lighter version was developed in 1992 at Iisalmi.

entries.heading: Tuwon madara (milk sweet)
entries.what: A firm milk-and-sugar sweet from Hausa cooking, cut into shapes.

entries.heading: Tvarozhny syr, dried curd (тварожны сыр; dried hard curd)
entries.what: Traditional preserved curd, dried until hard, eaten mostly on holidays. It was the main way to preserve milk in the past, and was crumbled with a knife or sucked like candy.

entries.heading: Twaróg (twaróg; Polish quark or farmer's cheese)
entries.what: Polish fresh white curd cheese, the Polish name for quark or tvorog. Used in pierogi, kluski leniwe, pyry z gzikiem and cheesecake.

entries.heading: Tybo
entries.what: a Danish semi-hard cheese named after the Thy district; resembles a mild Samsø.

entries.heading: Tykmælk (thick milk, cultured whole milk)
entries.what: one of the most popular cultured milk products in Denmark; said to have been made in Denmark for hundreds of years. Fat about 3.5–3.6%.

entries.heading: Tyri tis trygias (τυρί της τρυγίας; Nisyros)
entries.what: a Nisyros cheese from the grape-harvest season, kept in wine.

entries.heading: Tyri tis trygias Nisyrou
entries.what: "cheese of the grape harvest" from Nisyros, submerged and kept in red wine and lees.

entries.heading: Tyrogalo / Tsiros (τυρόγαλο; τσίρος)
entries.what: the whey-based cheese that myzithra is made from on Naxos.

entries.heading: Tyrogiliata Agrinio (Τυρογιλιάτα Αγρινίου)
entries.what: Agrinio (Aetolia-Acarnania) cheese; no details.

entries.heading: Tyromalama Kritis (Τυρομάλαμα Κρήτης)
entries.what: Cretan cheese; no details.

entries.heading: Tyrozouli (Τυροζούλι)
entries.what: a traditional cheese of the home-kept goat and sheep flock on Crete.

entries.heading: Tyrozouli Kritis (Τυροζούλι Κρήτης)
entries.what: Cretan cheese; no details.

entries.heading: Tzatziki
entries.what: a dip of seasoned, strained yogurt, mainly eaten in Greece with souvlaki. Greece and Turkey both claim it.

entries.heading: Tzfatit (Tzfat cheese; Hebrew גבינה צפתית, gvina tzfatit; also "safed cheese")
entries.what: A salty, semi-hard Israeli cheese first made in Safed (Tzfat) in the Upper Galilee, now sold in wedges with varying fat and salt levels.

entries.heading: U Muntagnolu
entries.what: Corsican cheese from Haute-Corse, listed on the French cheese list.

entries.heading: Ubriaco (Veneto)
entries.what: a Veneto cheese, also made with Traminer grape-marc in a goat version.

entries.heading: Uglich cheese (Угличский сыр)
entries.what: Semi-hard cheese developed in the late 1930s at the Uglich cheese laboratory (now VNIIMS); based on Tilsit; production from 1939, spread to 19 plants by 1940.

entries.heading: UHT-mælk (long-life milk)
entries.what: long-life milk heat-treated at 135–150 °C; fat content varies by product.

entries.heading: Ukrainskyi (Український)
entries.what: a generic Ukrainian hard cheese listed under its Ukrainian name, per the List of cheeses.

entries.heading: Ulpo (toasted-flour drink, with water or milk)
entries.what: A non-alcoholic drink of toasted flour mixed with water or milk.

entries.heading: Umbuzada (imbuzada)
entries.what: A typical drink of Northeast Brazil made from umbu fruit (from the umbuzeiro tree), slightly sour, mixed with milk and sugar.

entries.heading: Umvubo
entries.what: Sour milk mixed with dry pap (maize porridge). Eaten by Zulu, Xhosa and Sotho speakers.

entries.heading: Unash (unaş; milk noodle soup)
entries.what: Traditional Turkmen soup made with milk and noodles (or with beans and noodles).

entries.heading: Undanrenna (skim milk)
entries.what: Skim milk, the liquid left after cream is removed. Skyr is made from skimmed milk.

entries.heading: Unexpected Cheddar (Trader Joe's)
entries.what: A supermarket cheddar, variants include a spread, shredded cheese and a hatch chile spread.

entries.heading: Uniekaas
entries.what: A Dutch cheese brand for Goudse kaas. Produced from 1965 for KaasUnie, a 1956 buying group of thirty cheese merchants. Later several types were sold under the name.

name: Unnamed raw cheese, small Burundian business

entries.heading: Unnamed raw cheese, small Burundian business (1988 report)
entries.what: a cheese made by a small Burundian business, per a 1988 news item from the Technical Centre for Agricultural and Rural Cooperation; the item says it was made without industrial processes and was profitable

entries.heading: Unnamed surplus-milk cheese (Nuer)
entries.what: A cheese made from surplus herd milk when a herd gives more than the family needs, per the Nuer article.

entries.heading: Urda / izvara (урда, извара; Bulgarian whey cheese)
entries.what: a high-protein curd made in households since ancient times; in western Bulgarian dialects "urda" means izvara.

entries.heading: Urner Alpkäse (Urner Alpkäse; Alpkäse)
entries.what: The most important cheese of the canton of Uri by economic weight. It is a round alp cheese weighing about 6–8 kg and about 30 cm in diameter, with sparse holes. It is sold in mild, savoury and mature forms.

entries.heading: Urner Bergkäse
entries.what: Named as a Uri cheese that sells far behind Urner Alpkäse.

entries.heading: Urubu (Kirundi; soured milk)
entries.what: a household milk product of Burundi, named in a review of Burundian traditional fermented foods and in the Wikipedia fermented-milk table.

entries.heading: Uunijuusto (oven cheese)
entries.what: A traditional Finnish dish of colostrum set in an oven, served as dessert with cloudberries, other berries or jam; also as a starter with anchovies or roe.

entries.heading: Vacherin des Bauges
entries.what: cheese of the Aillon valley in the Bauges area.

entries.heading: Vaise (Stagionato de Vaise, Vàise; Liguria)
entries.what: a Ligurian cheese named "Stagionato de Vaise" in the English list; also "Vàise" in the Italian cuisine article.

entries.heading: Vājpiens (low-fat milk)
entries.what: Milk with reduced fat content.

entries.heading: Val de Taus (Tauste)
entries.what: a cheese made in Tauste (Zaragoza), named in the regional guide.

entries.heading: Valle d'Aosta Fromadzo (Fromadzo Valle d'Aosta, Fromadzo DOP)
entries.what: A PDO cow's-milk cheese of the whole of Valle d'Aosta. Young cheese is eaten as a table cheese; longer-aged cheese is sometimes grated. "Fromadzo" is the Valdostan patois word for cheese.

entries.heading: Vallée d'Ossau
entries.what: A cheese of the Béarn Ossau valley, Pyrénées-Atlantiques.

entries.heading: Vaniljukrem (vanilla cream)
entries.what: A vanilla cream used on fruit, in desserts and with ice cream; keeps 3–4 days chilled once opened. Per 100 g: 10 g fat, 3.6 g protein.

entries.heading: Vanilla ice cream (glace à la vanille)
entries.what: Ice cream served in French Guianese restaurants and with flambéed banana (banane flambée au rhum et glace à la vanille).

name: Vanilla ice cream and frozen milk desserts

entries.heading: Vanilla ice cream and frozen milk desserts (is)
entries.what: vanilla ice cream served with pancakes and apple pie; ice cream served as dessert.

entries.heading: Varm kakao (hot chocolate with milk)
entries.what: hot chocolate served in most cafés and often given to children at home; topped with whipped cream on the page's example.

entries.heading: Varškė (curd, fresh curd)
entries.what: a high-protein sour dairy product made from soured milk, with part of the whey removed. Made in fat grades of 2, 5, 9 and 18% and as lean curd, plus curd snacks (sūreliai) and curd cheeses.

entries.heading: Varškėčiai (curd pancakes)
entries.what: fried pancakes made from curd, flour, eggs and sugar, sometimes with vanilla. Crisp outside, soft inside; served with sour cream, jam or honey.

entries.heading: Vastedda palermitana
entries.what: a fresh stretched-curd cheese from the Palermo area, shaped as an oval loaf of about 1 kg.

entries.heading: Västerbottensost (Västerbotten cheese)
entries.what: Hard cow's-milk cheese from Västerbotten, with tiny holes, a firm granular texture and a salty, slightly bitter, Parmesan-like taste.

entries.heading: Veilcheneis (violet ice cream)
entries.what: an Austrian ice cream speciality of the 19th century

entries.heading: Velveeta
entries.what: A soft block processed cheese product.

entries.heading: Venaco (also Venachese; Muntanacciu is a related mountain cheese)
entries.what: Farmhouse tomme, a "tome carrée à bords arrondis" about 12 cm across and 3–5 cm thick, ivory paste; named after the commune of Venaco in central Corsica.

entries.heading: Vendôme bleu ou cendré
entries.what: a Vendôme (Loir-et-Cher, Orléanais) cheese in blue or ash-ripened form.

entries.heading: Vermont cheddar (white cheddar)
entries.what: A Vermont cheddar, often sharp, the standard of local creameries.

entries.heading: Vershkove maslo (вершкове масло; sweet and sour butter)
entries.what: Butter made by churning fresh or sour milk, cream, or high-fat cream. Sweet butter uses pasteurised cream; sour butter uses cream soured with pure lactic cultures. Salted varieties exist.

entries.heading: Vesterhavsost (Vesterhavs cheese)
entries.what: a hard Danish cheese aged in caves, with a slightly nutty flavour.

entries.heading: Victoria Thessalonikis (Βικτώρια Θεσσαλονίκης)
entries.what: Thessaloniki cheese; no details.

entries.heading: Vidiago (Queso de Vidiago)
entries.what: cheese from Vidiago, in the Llanes municipality.

entries.heading: Vieux Pané (Le Vieux Pané)
entries.what: Square industrial cheese, 25 cm a side, 3.5 cm thick, about 2.3 kg, 25% fat; a Savencia trademark.

entries.heading: Vieux-Boulogne (Sablé du Boulonnais)
entries.what: An unpasteurised, unpressed cow's-milk cheese from around Boulogne-sur-Mer, Pas-de-Calais, developed in the 19th century.

entries.heading: Vignelait (Vignelait)
entries.what: a cheese listed for Seine-et-Marne.

entries.heading: Villageois
entries.what: A cheese of Poitou and Charentes.

entries.heading: Villisveppaostur (wild-mushroom cheese)
entries.what: A mushroom-flavoured cheese sold by Mjólkursamsalan in a 150 g pack.

entries.heading: Vindino (dairy dessert; pudinzi)
entries.what: a Vindija dairy dessert named Vindino, under the "Pudinzi" category.

name: Virgin Islands bread with butter and milk

entries.heading: Virgin Islands bread with butter and milk (dumb bread)
entries.what: A yeast-free bread from the Virgin Islands made from flour, sugar, baking powder, salt, butter and milk, sometimes with shredded coconut or cornmeal. Cheddar cheese is used as a filling in some versions.

entries.heading: Vispgrädde (whipping cream)
entries.what: A high-fat cream for whipping into stable foam, used for garnish, fillings and desserts (buns, cakes, waffles, pancakes).

entries.heading: Vispipuuro (vispipuuro; lappapuuro; marjapuuro)
entries.what: A fluffy, whipped porridge, mostly made with semolina and berries, usually lingonberries or redcurrants. Usually served cold with sugar and milk, sometimes warm.

entries.heading: Vit caprin
entries.what: Swedish goat cheese with a camembert-type white mould rind, developed in the 1970s.

entries.heading: Vitamina (milk and fruit blend)
entries.what: Milk blended with one or more fruits, served cold; in Brazil the term distinguishes fruit vitamina from milk blended with ice cream. Common fruits: avocado, açaí, banana, carambola, coconut, apple, papaya, melon, strawberry.

entries.heading: Vla (vla; blanke vla, chocoladevla, hopjesvla and others)
entries.what: A thick Dutch dairy dessert from fresh cow's milk with thickeners. Legally at least 50% cow's milk, at least 2.6% milk fat, and starch must be a characteristic ingredient. Variants include vanilla, blanke (plain), chocolate, hopjes (coffee

entries.heading: Vla / vla-crème dessert (Campina)
entries.what: A thick Dutch dairy dessert of fresh cow's milk, thickened so it is firmer than pudding. Campina launched it in Belgium in 2013 as "vla / crème dessert"; in Flanders "pudding" is often used for it.

entries.heading: Vlădeasa (soft buffalo cheese)
entries.what: A Romanian soft cheese named in the buffalo article's list of buffalo-milk cheeses.

entries.heading: Vlašić cheese (Vlašićki sir; Travnički sir; Travnik cheese; Travnički sir)
entries.what: A white, brined cheese from Mount Vlašić near Travnik in central Bosnia, named for the mountain and sold mainly in Travnik. Now made across Bosnia and the wider region.

entries.heading: Vlaskaas (flax cheese)
entries.what: A Dutch "flax cheese" with a firm but creamy texture and a sweet, sharp flavour.

entries.heading: Vlora (goat cheese, named origin)
entries.what: one of the named traditional goat-cheese origins sampled for hygiene.

entries.heading: Vltavín (Vltavin)
entries.what: traditional Czech blue-veined cheese, creamy, melting, slightly sour and mushroomy.

entries.heading: Võie (reduced-fat butter-like spread)
entries.what: a reduced-fat butter-like product that may contain plant fats; under EU rules any butter-like product under 82% milk fat is called võie, not butter; fat ranges under 39%, 41–60% and 62–80% are named

entries.heading: Võiõli (butter oil)
entries.what: the base used to make reconstituted butter

entries.heading: Volaki Androu
entries.what: a cheese of Andros, named in the Greek cheese study table.

entries.heading: Vorarlberger Alpkäse (PDO, PDO-AT-1413)
entries.what: Alpine heritage cheese from Vorarlberg, produced only during the summer grazing season.

entries.heading: Vorarlberger Bergkäse (PDO)
entries.what: Artisanal hard cheese from Vorarlberg, the westernmost Austrian state, made in the Bergkäse family.

entries.heading: Vorí vorí morotî (vegetarian milk and squash dish)
entries.what: A vegetarian dish made with milk.

entries.heading: Vtáčie mlieko (vtáčie mlieko; bird's milk; zupa nic; floating island)
entries.what: a dessert of whipped egg-white "snow" (snehové halušky or pusinky) floating on a vanilla custard, served at room temperature or chilled. Named in Slovak Wikipedia with a region list of Poland, Slovakia, Austria and Germany; origin given as

entries.heading: Vurda (урда, вурда)
entries.what: whey cheese made from the whey left after making other cheeses, including budz and brynza.

entries.heading: Wa Cheese (和チーズ, wasabi cheese)
entries.what: A bite-sized cheese snack from Yutaka Co., Ltd., made with Tokachi mountain wasabi.

entries.heading: Waddengoudkaas (Waddengoudkaas; Hoogeland cheese)
entries.what: A cheese the Groningen regional-products list calls "kaas van het Hoogeland", i.e. from Het Hoogeland, the north-eastern Groningen area.

entries.heading: Walliser Raclette (Raclette du Valais, AOP) and Raclette variants
entries.what: Swiss raclette cheese from Valais; the melting method originated there.

entries.heading: Wanka (Mantaro de Huancayo, "Quesos de Autor")
entries.what: A matured Andean-style cheese from Mantaro de Huancayo's author-cheese line, coated in powdered rosemary.

entries.heading: Warbat (وربات)
entries.what: layered phyllo pastry filled with custard, eaten during Ramadan

entries.heading: Wät'ät (seasoned yoghurt drink)
entries.what: a seasoned yoghurt drink, usually served with borasaame.

entries.heading: Water kefir (kéfir de agua; sugary kefir)
entries.what: a sweet fermented drink made by Argentine small producers. The 2025 study says the Food Code did not cover it, and that a joint resolution (7/2024, published 12 August 2024) was made to add it to the Code.

entries.heading: Waterloo
entries.what: An English semi-soft cheese from Riseley, Berkshire.

entries.heading: Watermelon milk (西瓜牛乳)
entries.what: A milk drink of over 50% milk, blended with concentrated watermelon juice. Creamy, lightly sweet, light pink.

entries.heading: Wędzony ser podpuszczkowy dojrzewający (smoked farm rennet cheese, cow and goat)
entries.what: The smoked version of the farm rennet cheese above, sold by small Polish farms.

entries.heading: Welsh butter
entries.what: butter made from cows' milk, with salt as an important ingredient.

entries.heading: Wheel pie custard cream filling (車輪餅 卡士達醬)
entries.what: Wheel pie (車輪餅), a Taiwanese pastry, with a custard-cream filling among the sweet options. The wheel pie is linked to the Japanese imagawayaki, introduced under Japanese colonial rule (1895–1945).

entries.heading: Whey and buttermilk (medieval England)
entries.what: the shepherd's due in medieval England included a bowl of whey or buttermilk all summer, valued alongside milk, wool and meat.

entries.heading: Whey and whey powder (ホエイ・乳清, hoei / nyūsei)
entries.what: The liquid left when curd is separated in cheese or acid/enzyme curdling; sold as concentrated whey (濃縮ホエイ), whey powder (ホエイパウダー) and protein-concentrated whey powder (lactose removed). Also produced in strained yogurt.

entries.heading: Whey and whey protein concentrate
entries.what: Whey protein concentrate, sold as an ingredient, and whey used to make bioethanol.

entries.heading: Whey sourdough
entries.what: A sourdough from whey, sampled as a source of Lactiplantibacillus plantarum in a study of traditional Moroccan food products.

entries.heading: Whipped cream and custard (in a sponge or jelly-roll dessert)
entries.what: Whipped cream and custard used as the filling and topping of a sponge or jelly-roll cake, served with fruit and chopped nuts and soaked in sherry.

entries.heading: White cheese, feta-style (fetta; Dairy Khoury)
entries.what: A soft, crumbly white cheese in brine. The product page describes it as "soft, wet, and crumbly with a slightly grainy texture and a fresh lemony taste in brine".

entries.heading: White Rabbit milk candy (大白兔奶糖)
entries.what: A well-known Chinese milk candy listed in the dairy-products section of the Chinese cuisine article.

entries.heading: White soft cheese (soft white cheese)
entries.what: A soft white cheese was one of the four milk and cheese products collected from Kuwaiti hospitals and tested for antibiotic residues (50 samples).

entries.heading: Whole milk powder
entries.what: Dried whole milk, NZ's largest dairy export by volume and value.

entries.heading: Whole milk with starchy staples
entries.what: Cassava, millet, maize, or sweet potatoes served in whole milk, occasionally with crushed peanuts, in the arid south and west.

entries.heading: Wicklow Farmhouse range (Wicklow Blue, Wicklow Bán, Wicklow Gold, St Kevin's Brie)
Wiesenglück (fresh milk, Schärdinger)
entries.what: a fresh milk brand from Schärdinger

entries.heading: Wodaabe milk and yoghurt (diet)
entries.what: The everyday diet of the Wodaabe (a Fulani subgroup), recorded in English Wikipedia as milk and ground millet, yoghurt, sweet tea and sometimes goat or sheep meat. Cameroon is named among the countries they live in.

entries.heading: Würchwitzer Milbenkäse
entries.what: A low-fat fresh cheese seasoned with salt and caraway, shaped into sticks or hand-sized balls with an elderflower panicle inserted so the mites can enter.

entries.heading: Xaintray
entries.what: A goat cheese of Poitou and Charentes (Xaintray, Deux-Sèvres).

entries.heading: Xerosfeli (Ξεροσφέλι; non-PDO artisanal variant)
entries.what: A non-PDO artisanal variant of Sfela, studied with the PDO industrial cheese.

entries.heading: Xinomizithra Kritis (Ξινομυζήθρα Κρήτης; PDO)
entries.what: a Cretan whey cheese, made mainly on Crete with some production elsewhere in Greece.

entries.heading: Xınalıq pendiri (Khinalug cheese; Xınalıq, Khinalug)
entries.what: A named cheese of the Khinalug people, listed as among Azerbaijan's most popular cheeses.

entries.heading: Xuehua bing / milk-based shaved ice (雪花冰; 雪花氷)
entries.what: A fine, snow-like shaved ice where the ice itself is made from milk rather than water, served with condensed milk and toppings.

entries.heading: Xwante (sour milk and maize porridge)
entries.what: a Tanzanian dish listed with sour milk as its main raw material.

entries.heading: Xygalo Siteias (Ξύγαλο Σητείας; PDO)
entries.what: a creamy cheese made only in Sitia (Lasithi), with a rich, slightly sour, fresh taste similar to xinomizithra and Pichtogalo.

entries.heading: Xygalo Sitias (Ξύγαλο Σητείας; Π.Ο.Π.)
entries.what: Sitia (Crete) cheese; PDO.

entries.heading: Xynomizithra (Ξινομυζήθρα; Π.Ο.Π. Crete and Cyclades)
entries.what: Mizithra that has been salted and aged: drier, denser, saltier and more sour; usually grated.

entries.heading: Xynomyzithra (ξινομυζήθρα; sour myzithra)
entries.what: a sour fresh cheese that must be eaten within a few days.

entries.heading: Xynotyro / Xynotyri (ξυνότυρο)
entries.what: xynomyzithra dried for several weeks until hardened.

entries.heading: Y Fenni
entries.what: A Welsh cheese named after Abergavenny (Y Fenni in Welsh), in Monmouthshire. It is a firm cheese made from cow's milk.

entries.heading: Yachi Yanagi (Japanese name not in sources; dusted with Dutch myrtle)
entries.what: A Kyodo Gakusha Shintoku Farm cheese dusted with locally harvested Dutch myrtle.

entries.heading: Yaghnob kurut (Yaghnobi hard goat cheese; kurut)
entries.what: hard cheese made by the Yaghnobis of the Upper Zarafshan valley, Tajikistan, named "kurut" in the source, alongside fermented goat milk.

entries.heading: Yak and chauri milk (fresh)
entries.what: Fresh milk from yaks and chauri, the raw material of Himalayan dairy in Nepal, including hard chhurpi (cheese) and butter.

entries.heading: Yak butter tea (gur gur cha / cha su-kan) (ཇ་མར།)
entries.what: Tibetan-style butter tea, drunk in Ladakh and other Himalayan areas; Key Monastery in Spiti is pictured.

entries.heading: Yak Cheddar-style cheese (Nepal)
entries.what: A cheddar-style cheese made from yak milk, listed by the Nepal yak-milk review as a current product.

name: Yakumo Sakeru Cheese
names: 牛乳の華 さけるチーズ

entries.heading: Yakumo Sakeru Cheese (牛乳の華 さけるチーズ, Kumaishi deep-sea water)
entries.what: A pull-apart fresh cheese from the Yakumo Handmade Association, made with Kumaishi deep-ocean water.

name: Yakumo 牛乳の華 Semi-Hard
names: 牛乳の華 セミハード

entries.heading: Yakumo 牛乳の華 Semi-Hard (牛乳の華 セミハード)
entries.what: A semi-hard cow's-milk cheese from the Yakumo Handmade Association (NPO, Yakumo, Hokkaido), sold under the 牛乳の華 (Milk Blossom) brand.

entries.heading: Yaourt / degue (yoghurt eaten with millet couscous; French "yaourt", Togo name "degue" for the dish)
entries.what: Yoghurt served with millet couscous, the northern dish called degue; the yoghurt is the accompanying dairy product.

entries.heading: Yaourt aux fruits (Tiviski, fruit yoghurt)
entries.what: Fruit yoghurt in the Tiviski dairy range.

entries.heading: Yaourt et glace industriels (industrial yoghurt and ice cream, FAN MILK)
entries.what: Yoghurts and ice cream made by FAN MILK, which leads the industrial dairy sector in Togo.

entries.heading: Yayık ayranı (churned ayran)
entries.what: a frothy ayran made by churning, from eastern Türkiye; also a salted, diluted buttermilk.

entries.heading: Yazoo (flavoured milk drink)
entries.what: milk-based drink in banana, chocolate, strawberry and vanilla flavours, sold in the UK.

entries.heading: Yeghegnadzor / Horats panir (Հորատս պանիր, "buried" cheese; also husats panir)
entries.what: A semi-soft cheese from the town of Yeghegnadzor, mixed with local herbs and seeds and aged underground in clay pots.

entries.heading: Yema (candy)
entries.what: A sweet Filipino custard confection made from egg yolks, milk and sugar; modern versions often include chopped nuts. Name comes from the Spanish word for egg yolk.

entries.heading: Yemeni cheese (Taiz cheese; Arabic جبنة تعز / الجبن التعزي; English article also gives the local name "Jubn baladi" for the local cheese)
entries.what: a traditional rural cheese of Yemen, especially Taiz Governorate. Round and flat, about 20 cm across, 4 cm thick, about 1 kg. Smoking gives it a brown colour and a flavour that varies with the smoking plant.

entries.heading: Yepadz madzoun (եփած մածուն; cooked yoghurt)
entries.what: Strained yoghurt boiled with water until it is solid, then stored for use in winter soups. Named by Baboian's cookbook (Armenian cuisine, English Wikipedia).

entries.heading: Yezhegei (ежегей; ежигей)
entries.what: Sheep-milk curd mixed with butter, salt and crushed qurt.

entries.heading: Ylette
entries.what: a lighter version of ymer ("Ymer-light").

entries.heading: Ymer (Ymer; surmælksprodukt)
entries.what: a Danish concentrated sour milk product, usually sold plain and unsweetened, eaten at breakfast or as a yoghurt alternative. Launched commercially in the 1930s; registered by dairyman E. Larsen in 1937.

entries.heading: Ymerdrys (ymer sprinkle)
entries.what: a breakfast topping for ymer made of lightly toasted rye bread (rugbrød) crumbs with brown sugar.

entries.heading: Ymerfromage
entries.what: dessert from ymer.

entries.heading: Yo-ho-ho! (children's dairy, Emil)
entries.what: A children's line of dairy products from the Emil dairy.

name: Yoghurt / curd
names: ဒိန်ချဉ် dein kyin

entries.heading: Yoghurt / curd (ဒိန်ချဉ် dein kyin)
entries.what: a liquid or semi-solid food made by souring milk with bacteria cultures.

entries.heading: Yoghurt / 酸奶 (suānnǎi, 老酸奶)
