entries.what: Mainland China's common word for yoghurt; 老酸奶 is the semi-solid kind and 酸奶 the liquid kind. Defined as fermented with Lactobacillus bulgaricus and Streptococcus thermophilus; a yoghurt drink has less than 1% protein while yoghurt has more

name: Yoghurt and cheese of the Bukavu hinterland

entries.heading: Yoghurt and cheese of the Bukavu hinterland (unnamed)
entries.what: dairy products that farmers in the Bukavu hinterlands make from their milk, as stated in the paper.

entries.heading: Yoghurt and cultured dairy (Clover Botswana)
entries.what: Yoghurts and other cultured dairy items made by Clover Botswana from fresh milk.

entries.heading: Yoghurt and drinking yoghurt
entries.what: Cultured milk products including drinking yoghurt (Anchor Uno for children), dessert yoghurt (De Winkel, Fresh 'n Fruity) and custard yoghurt.

entries.heading: Yoghurt and goat-milk paste (لبن; laban)
entries.what: the everyday yoghurt that accompanies most meals and is an ingredient in many dishes; thick goat-milk yoghurt pastes are tied to Jordan and Palestine in the Bedouin cuisine article

entries.heading: Yoghurt and ice cream (processed, urban market)
entries.what: packaged yoghurt and ice cream sold in Tanzanian supermarkets, mainly in Dar es Salaam.

name: Yoghurt and other fermented milk, industrial

entries.heading: Yoghurt and other fermented milk, industrial (йогурт, кефир, ряженка)
entries.what: Factory yoghurt, kefir and ryazhenka, reported as one group.

entries.heading: Yoghurt and pasteurised milk, Cimory (Bogor, Semarang, Pasuruan)
entries.what: Cimory pasteurised milk from 2006 and yoghurt from 2007; low-fat yoghurt and Greek yoghurt added in 2020.

entries.heading: Yoghurt and petit-suisse (industrial, yaourt; yogurt in jars)
entries.what: Factory-made yoghurt and liquid yoghurt, sold in jars, plus petit-suisse, in supermarkets and convenience shops.

entries.heading: Yoghurt drinks (drinkable yoghurt; Arabic مشروبات الزبادي)
entries.what: A yoghurt-based beverage listed among popular drinks in Omani cuisine, alongside laban.

entries.heading: Yoghurt, flavoured/fruit-based (imported)
entries.what: Flavoured or fruit-based yoghurt, appearing as an imported food line in Vanuatu trade data.

entries.heading: Yoghurt, kefir and buttermilk (imported)
entries.what: Yoghurt, kefir and buttermilk imported into Bermuda, valued at US$2.89 million from the United States in 2025.

entries.heading: Yogur bebible (drinkable yogurt, fruit flavours)
entries.what: a yogurt sold as a drink in many fruit flavours, widely drunk in Ecuador.

entries.heading: Yogur griego (Greek-style yoghurt, Conaprole)
entries.what: Conaprole's "Nuevo Yogur Griego", sold in a natural flavour with no added sugar; and "Nuevo Yogur +Proteína", with 15 g of protein per serving.

entries.heading: Yogurt de borojó (yogurt with borojó jam; Cooproleche)
entries.what: a trial new flavour of yoghurt, made with borojó jam, developed at Cooproleche in the second half of 2014 as the subject of the thesis. The thesis says borojó was a newly introduced fruit in Nicaragua and was not widely eaten.

entries.heading: Yogurt mousse (sheep's yogurt mousse)
entries.what: a mousse made from sheep's yogurt, listed as a Greek dessert.

entries.heading: Yogurt natural (yogurt; Cooproleche, El Almendro)
entries.what: plain yoghurt made by the dairy Cooproleche in the Comarca El Triunfo, municipio El Almendro, Nicaragua. A 2015 agro-industrial thesis calls it "Yogurt natural" and has a photo of "Yogurt de COOPROLECHE".

entries.heading: Yogurt tradizionale (traditional yoghurt)
entries.what: plain yoghurt made with only L. bulgaricus and S. thermophilus.

entries.heading: Yomitan Tyrí (Japanese name not in sources; marinated version)
entries.what: A Greek-style fresh cheese made at a Greek restaurant in Nagahama, Yomitan Village, Okinawa, which entered the 2018 Japan Cheese Awards.

entries.heading: Yoo-hoo
entries.what: A chocolate-flavoured drink created in 1928 in Garfield, New Jersey.

entries.heading: Yoplait (Canada)
entries.what: Agropur held the Canadian licence to manufacture and market Yoplait products from 1971; its yogurt operations merged into Ultima Foods in 1993, and in December 2020 Agropur sold its Canadian yogurt activities to Lactalis.

entries.heading: Yoplait Greek-style yoghurt ("Yoplait en Grec")
entries.what: a rich, creamy Greek-style yoghurt sold in the fresh-dairy section for breakfast or dessert.

entries.heading: Yoplait yoghurt, "Dahi" (Yoplait brand)
entries.what: Yoplait-brand yoghurt sold in Gabon. The national food safety agency AGASA withdrew a Yoplait "Dahi" batch (lot 160) from the market.

entries.heading: Yotvata dairy milk
entries.what: Dairy at Kibbutz Yotvata in the Arava, described as a milk products factory and the kibbutz's main source of income. Founded in 1962 with four cows; 700 cows by 2008. Milk also comes from the dairies of kibbutzim Yahel, Lotan and Ketura.

entries.heading: Zaanlander
entries.what: A fantasy-named Gouda-type cheese, made exclusively for Albert Heijn since 1919. Sold at different ages, from young to old, and also as komijnekaas (cumin cheese).

entries.heading: Zabady (zabadi, زبادي)
entries.what: Yoghurt-like fermented milk, described as the most popular fermented milk beverage in Egypt.

entries.heading: Zabaglione (Piedmontese sambajon)
entries.what: light custard of egg yolks, sugar and sweet wine, from Piedmont, with the Piedmontese name sambajon.

entries.heading: Zagorje cottage cheese (sir i vrhnje)
entries.what: cottage cheese from Zagorje eaten with cream (vrhnje)

entries.heading: Zaklížený tvaroh (kližák)
entries.what: named Czech curd product on the Tvaroh page.

entries.heading: Zakynthian myzithra (Μυζήθρα Ζακύνθου)
entries.what: a white cheese made on Zakynthos, named in the el.wikipedia article on the Zakynthos islets Μικρή and Μεγάλη Μυζήθρα.

entries.heading: Zămătișe
entries.what: A type of cottage cheese named in the Romanian cuisine article.

entries.heading: Zatsirka with milk (зацірка; zatsirka)
entries.what: A peasant dish of hand-rubbed noodles, eaten with milk in peasant households alongside lokshyna and halushki (per the Belarusian cuisine source).

entries.heading: Zdenka
entries.what: a cheese named on the Croatia list

entries.heading: Zebu milk, fresh and raw (ronono, zebu milk)
entries.what: Fresh zebu milk is a major part of the diet of pastoralists in the arid south and west. Fresh milk is described as a luxury for most people, not an everyday drink.

entries.heading: Žemaitiškas kastinys (Samogitian kastinys, cultured cream spread)
entries.what: a traditional Samogitian product made from cream, soured milk and butter, with garlic, salt and spices. Firm at room temperature, crumbly when cold, quick to melt in the mouth; cream or pale yellow in colour, with sour and garlic notes.

entries.heading: Žemlovka (baked roll and milk pudding)
entries.what: Baked layers of rolls, apples and milk or egg, served with cinnamon and raisins.

entries.heading: Žetica (Жетица; Žetica)
entries.what: a Montenegrin cheese listed in the cheese section of Montenegrin cuisine.

entries.heading: Żętyca (żentyca, sheep whey drink)
entries.what: A whey drink from sheep's milk. The liquid left after milk is curdled with rennet. It is a by-product of making oscypek and bundz cheeses.

entries.heading: Zhazhi (Kurdish; script not given in source)
entries.what: A "unique farmhouse traditional fermented dairy" of the Kurdistan Region, described as homemade Kurdish cheese.

entries.heading: Zigerkrapfen (Zigerkrapfen; Ziger filling)
entries.what: Fritters with a sweet, flavoured filling made from Ziger, a whey-based fresh cheese. Known as a specialty of central Switzerland, made since the 18th century.

entries.heading: Zlatarski sir (Zlatar cheese)
entries.what: a full-fat white cheese from the Zlatar mountain area of south-western Serbia

entries.heading: Zlatna kap (Tešanj cheese)
entries.what: A cheese from Tešanj, recognised by the producers' association (name means "golden drop").

entries.heading: Zlatni sir (Golden cheese; Foča)
entries.what: A cheese from Foča, recognised by the producers' association (name means "golden cheese").

entries.heading: Zoetay (ze-te, Dzongkha; also zoety, zoeti)
entries.what: Datshi left at room temperature for days to develop a pungent smell and gelatinous outer layer; regarded as a delicacy and added in small amounts to curry.

entries.heading: Zopilotillo (sour-milk dessert)
entries.what: A dessert made from leche agria, with dulce de tapa and cinnamon.

entries.heading: Zsiadłe mleko (kwaśne mleko, soured milk)
entries.what: Raw milk left to sour on its own, separating into thick curd and whey. Eaten as a drink or with food.

entries.heading: Zufi / Zuvi
entries.what: a fermented ricotta from Val Formazza, Novara province, Piedmont.

entries.heading: Zupa mleczna (milk soup)
entries.what: A sweet or savoury soup of milk and starchy foods; a staple of milk bars in Poland for decades.

entries.heading: Zuppa inglese
entries.what: Italian layered dessert with savoiardi or sponge soaked in alchermes, with crema pasticcera and chocolate custard.

entries.heading: Γκερεμέζι (Gkeremezi; Greek script; also Γκερεμέζι Αίγινας; cross-region, Epirus and Aegina)
entries.what: a cheese the Greek Wikipedia list gives as coming from Epirus and from Aegina, so it is one of the cheeses made in Attikí's island part as well as on the mainland.

entries.heading: Φράτσια (Frátsia; Greek script; Kythira)
entries.what: a cheese the Greek Wikipedia list gives as coming from Kythira (Κύθηρα). Kythira is administratively part of the Attikí region.

entries.heading: Биено сирење (Bieno sirenje; also тепано сирење, tepano sirenje; Bieno siren̂e in English Wikipedia)
entries.what: An autochthonous Macedonian cheese from the Mariovo area, made in mountain dairy huts for centuries. The name comes from the curd being beaten or whipped during making.

entries.heading: 바나나맛 우유 (banana milk)
entries.what: A South Korean flavoured milk, sold in a small bottle, launched by Binggrae in June 1974.

entries.heading: 불가리스 (Bulgaris; fermented milk drink)
entries.what: A fermented milk (발효유) product of Namyang Dairy, launched 1991.

entries.heading: 빙수 (bingsu; milk-based shaved ice; 팥빙수)
entries.what: Korean shaved-ice dessert. The modern version took condensed milk, syrup and chocolate from the US after the Korean War, and was later joined by ice cream and whipped cream. 팥빙수 (red-bean) is the most common.

entries.heading: 아이스크림 / 빙과 (ice cream and ice confections)
entries.what: Korean ice cream and bar-style ice confections (빙과). 서울우유 says ice confections began in 1952. Examples: 투게더 (1974), 더위사냥 (1989), 메로나 (1992), 캔디바 (1985), 빵또아 (1992), and many bars such as 쌍쌍바, 누가바, 부라보콘, 비비빅 (no years given).

entries.heading: 아인슈타인 우유 (DHA-added milk)
entries.what: A Namyang Dairy milk with DHA added, marketed from 1994.

entries.heading: 요구르트 (plain yogurt; Binggrae)
entries.what: Plain yogurt from Binggrae; the fermented-milk business began May 1977, producing about 200,000 bottles a day.

entries.heading: 요플레 (spoonable yogurt; 떠먹는 요구르트)
entries.what: Korea's first spoon-eaten yogurt, a Binggrae brand launched September 1983.

entries.heading: 칼피스 맛 빙과 (Calpis-flavoured ice confection; Lotte)
entries.what: A Korean ice bar with a Calpis flavour, made and sold by Lotte Confectionery. The Calpis brand itself is Japanese.

entries.heading: 타락죽 (tarak-juk; uyu-juk 우유죽; 駝酪粥)
entries.what: A Korean porridge of milk and finely ground glutinous rice. The word 타락 (tarak) once covered several dairy foods; the Mongolian or Turkic link is disputed.
